title: Designation of the Teiaiagon-Baby Point Heritage Conservation District under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage preservation; heritage districts; historic areas, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council designate the Teiaiagon-Baby Point area as a Heritage Conservation District under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act and adopt the Teiaiagon-Baby Point Heritage Conservation District Plan by by-law. The designation would manage change in the district through place-based policies and guidelines to conserve its cultural heritage value. The study was led by Heritage Planning staff with EVOQ Architecture Inc.

title: 307 Sherbourne Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve an Official Plan amendment and zoning by-law amendment to allow a 3-storey addition to the approved and under-construction 15-storey private student residence at 307 Sherbourne Street. The resulting 18-storey building would have 223 student resident units, an increase of 23 units over the previous approval. The Official Plan amendment is needed to raise the maximum permitted height, and the zoning amendment to increase gross floor area, unit count and adjust the approved built form.

title: 325 Gerrard Street East (Regent Park Phases 4 and 5) - City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a City-initiated zoning by-law amendment for Phases 4 and 5 of the Regent Park revitalization at 325 Gerrard Street East. The amendment would change development permissions for Blocks 4B and 5C/5D to create setbacks from critical City infrastructure and allow additional building massing elsewhere on the blocks to create more housing opportunities.

title: Implementation of Permit Parking on Shuter Street between Parliament Street and Sumach Street, Permit Area 7C
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: This item asks Council to skip the usual petition and polling requirements under Municipal Code Chapter 925 to add existing unsigned parking spaces on Shuter Street between Parliament Street and Sumach Street into permit area 7C for overnight parking. A local resident flagged the discrepancy with nearby spaces, and Transportation Services agreed to review adding them. The exemption would last until Toronto and East York Community Council considers a formal request for permit parking there.

title: 536-538 St. Clair Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a zoning by-law amendment to permit a 124.8-metre (30-storey, excluding mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building at 536-538 St. Clair Avenue West. The building would contain 355 dwelling units and at least 200 square metres of commercial-retail space. Staff consider the proposal an appropriate built form for the existing and planned context.

title: King Street at Bathurst Street Taxi Stand Adjustment
topics: taxicab stands, transportation; taxi stands, transportation services
brief: Frontage on the south side of King Street West just east of Bathurst Street is being reapportioned among the Ontario Line King-Bathurst Station construction site, a TTC eastbound stop and an Oretta CafeTO patio. Council is asked to rescind the existing taxi stand for 6 taxis and designate a stand for 5 taxis from December 17, 2024 to November 30, 2029. The adjustment accommodates the overlapping uses during construction.

title: 45 St. Clair Avenue West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve an Official Plan amendment and zoning by-law amendment to permit a 161.5-metre (51-storey, excluding mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building at 45 St. Clair Avenue West. The building would contain 461 residential units and 43,250 square metres of gross floor area, with a minimum of 1,800 square metres for non-residential uses.

title: 452 Bathurst Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application and City-Initiated Official Plan Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve an Official Plan amendment and zoning by-law amendment to permit a 22-metre (6-storey, excluding mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building at 452 Bathurst Street. The building would have a maximum gross floor area of 7,500 square metres, with a minimum of 250 square metres for non-residential uses.

title: Reduction of length of Accessible Loading Zone at 90 Dunn Avenue (formerly 150 Dunn Avenue) to accommodate Wheel Trans service
topics: accessibility, loading zones; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones
brief: This item amends the accessible loading zone at 90 Dunn Avenue (formerly 150 Dunn Avenue), originally approved in 2022 to accommodate Wheel Trans service. Wheel Trans vehicles have been modified and now need only 26 metres of manoeuvring space instead of 36, so Council is asked to rescind the old prohibition and amend the loading zone, freeing space for on-street parking while still meeting Wheel Trans needs.

title: Turn Prohibition - Donlands Avenue and O'Connor Drive
topics: traffic regulations, turn prohibitions (traffic);
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to prohibit northbound left turns at all times at the intersection of Donlands Avenue and O'Connor Drive. The restriction, combined with adjustments to the northbound lane alignments, is intended to improve traffic flow and reduce delays for through traffic in both directions. TTC service operates on Donlands Avenue, so Council approval is required.

title: Metrolinx Ontario Line - Temporary Parking By-law Amendments on Church Street
topics: by-laws, parking regulations, traffic regulations; bylaws, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Staff ask City Council to temporarily rescind existing timed parking and no-stopping prohibitions and implement a no-stopping rule at all times on both sides of Church Street between Queen Street East and Adelaide Street East, from October 15, 2024 to November 30, 2027. The change is needed to improve road capacity and transit flow on Church Street, which has been affected by the TTC 501 Queen streetcar diversion and Metrolinx Ontario Line work. TTC service operates on Church Street, so Council approval is required.

title: Parking Amendments - Yonge Street
topics: parking machines, parking regulations, traffic regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws, pay and display machines; pay-and-display machines
brief: Transportation Services recommends on-street parking amendments on Yonge Street tied to a new pedestrian refuge island being installed just north of the Mount Pleasant Cemetery entrance, about 106 metres north of Glen Elm Avenue. The changes adjust pay-and-display, no-parking and no-stopping regulations on both sides of the street near the island. TTC service operates on Yonge Street, so Council approval is required.

title: Realignment of Permit Parking - Area 7L to Exclude the Developments Located at 100 and 130 River Street
topics: parking, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Toronto and East York Community Council directed staff to review the realignment of the new overnight Permit Parking Area 7L to exclude the developments at 100 and 130 River Street, which are on streets with TTC service. A companion report introduces Area 7L and excludes various developments on streets without TTC service. The Director, Permits and Enforcement recommends City Council approve the revised Area 7L map by amending Schedule B of Municipal Code Chapter 925, Permit Parking.

title: Accessible Parking Space - December 2024 (Non-Delegated)
topics: accessibility, parking spaces; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, parking spots
brief: This is a procedural item: as TTC service operates on the subject streets, City Council approval is needed to remove one on-street accessible parking space for persons with disabilities at the location in Attachment 1 to the December 2024 report. The Director, Traffic Management recommends Council authorize the removal.

title: 363-391 Yonge Street - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, parking regulations, traffic regulations; building, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Concord Properties Developments Corp is building an 87-storey condominium at 363-391 Yonge Street, at the southeast corner of Yonge Street and Gerrard Street East. Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize closing a 6.6-metre-wide portion of O'Keefe Lane, between a point 38.1 metres south of Gerrard Street East and a point 33.5 metres further south, from December 18, 2024 to January 31, 2028, for construction staging. The existing one-way southbound lane operation would be temporarily converted to two-way to maintain local access.

title: 31 and 33 Parliament Street - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, parking prohibitions, stopping prohibitions, traffic regulations; building, no parking, no stopping
brief: Lanterra Developments and Laughlin Solutions are building a 32-storey and a 41-storey condominium at 31 and 33 Parliament Street, north of the Lake Shore rail corridor. Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize closing the east sidewalk and a 3.6-metre-wide portion of the northbound curb lane on Parliament Street, between a point 140 metres north of Lake Shore Boulevard East and a point 45 metres further north, from October 10, 2024 to March 31, 2027, for construction staging.

title: 952 King Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a zoning by-law amendment to permit a 17-storey mixed-use building with 227 dwelling units at 952 King Street West, including six affordable rental units. The proposal includes about 182 square metres of ground-floor non-residential space and 50 parking spaces in two levels of underground parking. Staff say the development is an appropriate built form that adds both market and affordable housing and improves the public realm.

title: 81 Isabella Street - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council add 81 Isabella Street (including entrance address 83 Isabella Street) to the City's Heritage Register for its cultural heritage value. The property in the Church-Wellesley neighbourhood contains The Merlan, an early-20th-century brick apartment building designed by architect Norman Alexander Armstrong and built in 1927. The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning recommends inclusion in accordance with the listing statement.

title: 53 Strachan Avenue - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council add 53 Strachan Avenue (including entrance addresses 715, 801, 805, 805A and 805B Wellington Street West) to the City's Heritage Register for its cultural heritage value. The property at the southeast corner of Strachan Avenue and Wellington Street West, just north of the Lakeshore West rail corridor, contains a three-storey, late-19th-century brick factory and warehouse building.

title: Designation of the West Queen West Heritage Conservation District Plan under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage preservation; heritage districts; historic areas, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council designate the West Queen West area as a Heritage Conservation District under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act and adopt the West Queen West Heritage Conservation District Plan by by-law. The designation would manage change in the district through place-based policies and guidelines to conserve its cultural heritage value. The study was led by Heritage Planning staff and began on Council direction in 2015.

title: 2400-2440 Dundas Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a zoning by-law amendment for three mixed-use towers at 2400-2440 Dundas Street West, at heights of 25, 37 and 42 storeys, with two towers sharing a podium. The proposal includes 1,214 dwelling units, 6,371 square metres of non-residential floor area, and 447 purpose-built rental units including 11 affordable rental units secured through a Community Benefits Charge and 56 affordable rental units required by Site and Area Specific Policy 796.

title: Council Mid-term Member Appointments to Committees, Boards and External Bodies
topics: appointments, governance; governance structure; municipal governance
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Clerk recommends the Striking Committee consider members' preferences and recommend Council members for appointment to the committees, advisory bodies, boards and external bodies listed in Attachment 1, for terms ending November 14, 2026. The appointments fill the council's mid-term slate.

title: 2102 Lawrence Avenue East - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property and Demolition of a Building Under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: easements, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council alter the designated heritage property at 2102 Lawrence Avenue East to integrate the church and cemetery into a new affordable housing complex with an L-shaped building of 12-storey and 6-storey components. Post-war additions to the historic church would be demolished, while a community garden and publicly accessible playground would be added and the former church used as a community gathering space. Council is asked to consent to the alterations under the Ontario Heritage Act and authorize a heritage easement agreement.

title: Review of Zoning Regulations for Nightclubs in Ward 20, Scarborough Southwest - Final Report
topics: nightclubs, regulations; dance clubs; dance halls; discos; night clubs
brief: This is a monitoring report: Council is asked to direct the Chief Planner to monitor the implementation and effectiveness of zoning permissions for nightclubs in Ward 20, Scarborough Southwest, and to report monitoring outcomes to the Scarborough Community Council. Council enacted city-wide nightclub zoning permissions in December 2023 as part of the Night Economy Review, complemented by an updated licensing framework. The report is the final review of the Ward 20 nightclub zoning study.

title: 4158 to 4180 Kingston Road and 8 to 12 Overture Road - Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: redevelopment, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: A zoning by-law amendment application for 4158 to 4180 Kingston Road and 8 to 12 Overture Road proposed a 20-storey mixed-use building with retail at grade and 320 dwelling units, with 21,211.8 square metres of gross floor area including 415 square metres of non-residential space. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on September 4, 2024 after Council did not decide within the Planning Act timeframes. Staff recommend Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the application in its current form.

title: 123 Bellamy Road North - Zoning Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A zoning by-law amendment application for 123 Bellamy Road North proposed three residential buildings of 44, 35 and 9 storeys with a combined gross floor area of 75,251 square metres (97,115 square metres with the existing 12-storey apartment building) and a floor space index of 5.16. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, and staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the application in its current form while continuing to discuss outstanding issues.

title: 3174, 3176, 3178, 3180 and 3182 Eglinton Avenue East and 1 and 7 Centre Street - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, mixed use areas, official plan amendments; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve an amendment to the Official Plan and the Zoning By-law to allow redevelopment of the site at 3174 to 3182 Eglinton Avenue East and 1 and 7 Centre Street with a 23-storey mixed-use building. The proposal includes 335 dwelling units and 21,167 square metres of gross floor area, including 386 square metres of first-floor retail and commercial space. Staff find it consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement (2024) and the general intent of the Official Plan, and say it will intensify a well-served major street.

title: Lawrence Avenue East and Valia Road/Private Driveway - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic control systems, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize the installation of traffic control signals at the intersection of Lawrence Avenue East and Valia Road / private driveway. Staff say the signals would improve safety for all road users and are justified by the assessment. TTC bus service operates on Lawrence Avenue East, so Council approval is required.

title: Metrolinx Scarborough Subway Extension - Long-term Temporary Road Closures and Public Highway Dedication - Kennedy Station Connection, Emergency Exit Building-1, and Lawrence East Station
topics: road closures, subway routes; street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Construction of the Scarborough Subway Extension's Kennedy Station connection, Emergency Exit Building-1 and Lawrence East Station requires long-term temporary road closures and traffic by-law amendments, plus temporary realignment of road segments on Eglinton Avenue East, Midland Avenue, McCowan Road and Lawrence Avenue East. Staff ask City Council to authorize the closures, including the continued temporary closure of the east sidewalk on McCowan Road between Sheppard Avenue East and Nugget Avenue from January 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026. TTC service operates in the area, so Council approval is required.

title: Permanent Road Closure - Agincourt Drive, north of Sheppard Avenue East and Road Dedication - Sheppard Avenue East, east of Reidmount Avenue
topics: road closures, traffic regulations; street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Staff recommend that City Council permanently close an unused portion of Agincourt Drive between Sheppard Avenue East and a point 30 metres north, and dedicate lands east of Reidmount Avenue as part of the public highway Sheppard Avenue East. The moves resolve remnant parcels created by the Sheppard Avenue East grade separation and Agincourt GO Station improvements: the closed road portions would transfer to Metrolinx to support the GO station, and Metrolinx lands would transfer to the City for dedication as highway.

title: 615 Kennedy Road - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction; building
brief: Times Group Construction Inc. is building a 12-storey residential building at 615 Kennedy Road, at the southeast corner of Kennedy Road and Corvette Avenue. Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize the temporary closure of the northbound curb lane and the east sidewalk on Kennedy Road, between a point 36 metres south of Corvette Avenue and a point 28.5 metres further south, with a 2.1-metre covered protected pedestrian walkway, for 13 months from November 14, 2024 to November 30, 2025. Kennedy Road is a major arterial, so Council approval is required.

title: 2102 Lawrence Avenue East and 1 Ellington Drive - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve an Official Plan amendment and zoning by-law amendment to permit a 12-storey building at 2102 Lawrence Avenue East and 1 Ellington Drive. The building would contain 148 residential rental units, including 46 affordable units, with 10,158 square metres of gross floor area at a density of 1.96 times the site area. The proposal integrates the designated heritage church and cemetery into the development.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will review the Order Paper. No other decision is attached.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions and announcements will be made at the City Council meeting. No decision is attached.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council may file petitions. No other decision is attached.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council will declare interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act. No other decision is attached.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports, New Business and Business Previously Requested from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will introduce the committee reports, new business and business previously requested from City officials. The reports include those of the Executive Committee, Audit Committee, Board of Health, Civic Appointments Committee and Corporations Nominating Panel, among others. No decision beyond introduction is attached.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will confirm the minutes from the regular meeting held on November 13 and 14, 2024. No other decision is attached.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will open its meeting with O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is attached.

title: Commuter Parking Opportunities for 777 Victoria Park Avenue
topics: commuters;
brief: City Council asked staff in July 2024 to identify off-site Green P commuter parking options to offset the loss of parking at 777 Victoria Park Avenue from the Housing Now project, and to explore parking opportunities at 781 Victoria Park Avenue. The Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management recommends Council ask CreateTO and the Toronto Parking Authority to undertake a parking utilization study and identify options for additional commuter parking. The report seeks direction on next steps.

title: Toronto Green Standard: Net Zero Transition Study Update
topics: buildings, green standards, sustainable development; environmental sustainability; green development; sustainability; sustainable; sustainable buildings; sustainable cities; sustainable design; sustainable energy; sustainable transportation, green development standards; sustainable development standards; toronto green standards
brief: Staff update City Council on the Net Zero Transition Study, which examines the feasibility of accelerating greenhouse gas emission limits in the Toronto Green Standard in 2025 and 2028 so that buildings constructed in or after 2030 are near zero emissions. The study responds to Council's December 2021 TransformTO Net Zero Strategy commitment to reach net-zero emissions in Toronto by 2040. The Interim Chief Planner recommends Council direct staff to continue the work with relevant divisions.

title: Relaunch of the Home Ownership Assistance Program to Support New Non-Profit Affordable and Attainable Home Ownership Housing
topics: affordable housing, homeowners, housing; affordable homes; housing projects, home owners, homes; residences
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the general terms and conditions for a relaunched Home Ownership Assistance Program to support new non-profit affordable and attainable home ownership housing. The report responds to Toronto's dual housing crises: a lack of deeply affordable homes for low-income and vulnerable residents, and rising costs pushing ownership out of reach for middle-income earners and key workers. Council has pledged to meet the provincial target of 285,000 housing starts in Toronto by 2031.

title: Exempting Dwelling Rooms in a Multi-tenant House from Parkland Dedication and Clarifications to Exemptions in Article III of Chapter 415 - Development of Land
topics: multi-unit dwellings; multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings
brief: Staff ask City Council to exempt dwelling rooms in a multi-tenant house from parkland dedication requirements in Article III of Municipal Code Chapter 415, the Parkland By-law, and to clarify other exemptions. The report responds to the 2023 Housing Action Plan's new multi-tenant housing framework, which recognizes this rental stock as a critical affordable housing option and brought incentives and licensing supports city-wide. Council is asked to amend Article III as set out in Attachment 1.

title: Establishing a Framework to Address Excessive Indoor Temperatures in Leased Residential Premises
topics: housing, temperature; heat, homes; residences
brief: Excessive indoor temperatures are a growing health concern for tenants in leased homes without air conditioning, intensified in multi-unit buildings and built-up areas with limited greenspace. The Executive Director of Municipal Licensing and Standards, the Executive Director of Environment and Climate, and the Medical Officer of Health recommend City Council amend Municipal Code Chapter 497, Heating, including revising the date range for the requirement that landlords maintain a minimum temperature of 21 degrees Celsius in all areas. The item would establish a framework to address excessive indoor temperatures in leased residential premises.

title: 50 Wilson Heights Boulevard (Block 1) - City Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: condominium housing, rezoning, zoning bylaws; condominiums; condos, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a City-initiated zoning by-law amendment to modify development standards for a 10-storey residential building with 209 market condominium units at 50 Wilson Heights Boulevard. The amendment would provide non-commercial uses on the ground floor (minimum 275 square metres), protect lands known as Block 9 for Toronto Water infrastructure, and remove previously approved office uses.

title: Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods - Neighbourhood Retail and Services Study Phase Two Final Report
topics: affordable housing, stores; affordable homes; housing projects, retail stores; shops
brief: This is the final report for Phase Two of the Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods neighbourhood retail and services study. Staff recommend zoning by-law amendments to permit certain small-scale retail, service and office uses on residentially zoned properties within Neighbourhoods city-wide, with a broader list of uses on major streets and more limited permissions on interior streets. Changes to home occupation permissions and a monitoring approach are also recommended.

title: 94 Cortleigh Boulevard - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 94 Cortleigh Boulevard under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The Lytton Park property between Avenue Road and Cortleigh Boulevard includes a substantial two-storey house built in 1914 on an oversized lot, with the rear of the property including part of a ravine. The Interim Chief Planner recommends the designation in line with the statement of significance.

title: 358-360 Dufferin Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the former Dominion Radiator Company factory complex at 358-360 Dufferin Street (including the structure at 350 Dufferin Street) under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The properties sit on the west side of Dufferin Street between Milky Way Lane and Melbourne Avenue in South Parkdale. The Interim Chief Planner recommends the designation in line with the statement of significance and heritage attributes.

title: 2451 and 2489 Bayview Avenue - Proposed Amendment to Designating By-law under Part IV, Section 30.1 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: change, heritage designation, heritage properties; amendments; conversion; modification, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council amend the 1992 By-law 31874 designating the City-owned Windfields Estate at 2489 Bayview Avenue under the Ontario Heritage Act. The amendment would revise the reasons for designation to current standards, expand the legal description to include the entire historic 20-acre property, and protect the archaeological sites known as the Whitney Site (AkGu-77) and the Whitney 2 Site (AkGu-82). The property sits on the east side of Bayview Avenue, south of York Mills Road.

title: Community Improvement Plan for the Economic Development and Growth in Employment (EDGE) Incentive Program
topics: community improvement plans, economic development; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: Staff recommend that City Council adopt a new city-wide Community Improvement Plan for the Economic Development and Growth in Employment (EDGE) Incentive Program. The plan follows Council direction from September 2023 to evaluate the effectiveness of financial incentives under the Imagination, Manufacturing, Innovation and Technology (IMIT) program, and further direction from the February 2024 IMIT program review. The recommended plan would provide a more targeted incentive for employment space development, replacing the existing city-wide Community Improvement Plan (By-law 1207-2018).

title: 2801 Keele Street, 6 Paxtonia Boulevard - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: Official Plans, official plan amendments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: An application for 2801 Keele Street and 6 Paxtonia Boulevard proposed an 11-storey (44.3-metre) mixed-use building with 186 units, 615 square metres of at-grade commercial space and 324 square metres of privately owned publicly accessible space. The applicant has appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal. Staff recommend Council authorize the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal hearing in opposition to the proposal in its current form while continuing to discuss outstanding issues with the applicant.

title: 2346 Yonge Street - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: official plan amendments, residential properties, zoning; residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse an Official Plan and zoning by-law amendment application for 2346 Yonge Street, which proposed a 56-storey (177.1-metre, plus 8.8-metre mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building with 407 residential units and 272.2 square metres of at-grade commercial space, at a density of 29.5 floor space index. Staff recommend refusal because outstanding issues could not be resolved within the legislated 120-day decision timeline, and discussions with the applicant will continue.

title: 131 Lyon Court and 836, 838 Roselawn Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, housing, rentals; homes; residences
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the rental housing demolition application to demolish 53 rental units at 131 Lyon Court and 836, 838 Roselawn Avenue. The units would be replaced as part of a new development on the site, with a tenant relocation and assistance plan giving existing tenants the right to return to a replacement unit of the same type at similar rent. The site is also the subject of a zoning by-law amendment application that was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, where Council endorsed a settlement offer.

title: 849 Eglinton Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning Amendment, and Subdivision Applications - Appeal Report
topics: accessible permit parking, multi-unit dwellings, official plan amendments; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled), multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings
brief: The applications for 849 Eglinton Avenue East proposed a three-building development: a 40-storey residential mixed-use building (129.02 metres), a 21-storey residential building (74.55 metres), a 6-storey office building (31.82 metres), plus a new private road, a privately owned publicly accessible space, and two road widenings to create new north-south public streets connecting Eglinton Avenue East to Vanderhoof Avenue. The applicant appealed the Official Plan, zoning and subdivision applications on July 18, 2024. Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the current applications.

title: Steeles Avenue East and Bayview Avenue; Steeles Avenue East and Leslie Street - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: [people in public safety and protection], pedestrians, transportation; pedestrianization, transportation services
brief: As part of a 2024 road resurfacing project on Steeles Avenue East from Bayview Avenue to Townsend Road, Transportation Services included pedestrian crossing improvements at right-turn channels. Staff recommend City Council authorize three pedestrian crossovers at the northeast, northwest and southeast corners of Steeles Avenue East and Bayview Avenue, plus two more at the Steeles Avenue East and Leslie Street intersection. TTC service operates on these streets, so Council approval is required.

title: 1181 Sheppard Avenue East - Public Art Plan
topics: art galleries (facilities), public art, sculpture gardens; art facilities, outdoor art; outdoor sculptures; outdoor statues
brief: This is a procedural item: staff ask City Council to approve the Public Art Plan for 1181 Sheppard Avenue East, which sets out how the owner will commission four new public art installations on the site. The plan covers the project description, planning context, art opportunities, objectives, budget, artist selection process and schedule, and meets the City's Percent for Public Art Guidelines. The Director, Urban Design recommends approval.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plans 66M-2551 and 66M-2553, Adra Grado Way Subdivision, North York
topics: agreements, assumption of services, subdivision (land); subdivision of land, tenancy agreements
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is asked to formally assume the municipal services and roads in the Adra Grado Way subdivision (Registered Plans 66M-2551 and 66M-2553), built under subdivision agreements dated May 29, 2018 between the Toronto Community Housing Corporation and the City. The Acting Director, Engineering Review recommends the assumption, which would make Adra Grado Way and Okra Tomar Crescent public roads maintained by the City.

title: Easement from Parc Downsview Park for a Sanitary Sewer to Service the Stanley Greene Subdivision, Registered Plan 66M-2520
topics: construction, easements, sanitary sewers; building
brief: This is a procedural item: staff ask City Council to authorize the City Solicitor to register an easement conveyed by Parc Downsview Park for a sanitary sewer on its lands that currently services the Stanley Greene Subdivision (Registered Plan 66M-2520). The Acting Director, Engineering Review recommends the registration on terms satisfactory to that office.

title: 1747, 1751, 1759, 1763, 1767, 1771, 1773 and 1775 Bayview Avenue - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: cultural facilities, heritage conservation districts, heritage properties; art centres; arts centres; cultural attractions; cultural centres, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage districts; historic areas
brief: Staff recommend that City Council add eight properties at 1747, 1751, 1759, 1763, 1767, 1771, 1773 and 1775 Bayview Avenue to the City's Heritage Register for their cultural heritage value. The properties sit on the east side of Bayview Avenue, south of Eglinton Avenue East and north of the properties at 1779-1787 Bayview. Council had directed heritage staff to prioritize research on these properties by November 2024.

title: Renew Sheppard East Secondary Plan - Final Report
topics: development, organizational structure, replacement; administrative structure; divisions; reporting relationship; reporting structure, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Staff recommend that City Council adopt the Renew Sheppard East Secondary Plan and associated Official Plan Amendment 777 to guide development north and south of Sheppard Avenue East between the west side of Bayview Avenue and the east side of Leslie Street. The new secondary plan replaces part of the 1999 Sheppard East Subway Corridor Secondary Plan with an updated framework supporting a mix of land uses and policy directions.

title: 120 - 128 Sheppard Avenue West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve an Official Plan amendment and zoning amendment to permit a 7-storey (21.75-metre) residential building with 30 dwelling units at 120 and 128 Sheppard Avenue West. The proposal includes 3,160.57 square metres of gross floor area (a floor space index of 2.97), 26 underground vehicle parking spaces and 24 bicycle parking spaces. The Official Plan amendment would amend the Sheppard Lansing secondary plan area policies.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the CreateTO Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Corporations Nominating Panel will interview candidates and recommend one public member for appointment to the CreateTO Board and to the Boards of Directors of Build Toronto and the Toronto Port Lands Company. The City Clerk recommends Council appoint the recommended candidate at pleasure of Council for a term ending March 28, 2028. No candidate names are given in the excerpt.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Toronto Hydro Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Corporations Nominating Panel will interview candidates and recommend one public member for appointment to the Toronto Hydro Board, plus a nominee for Board Chair. The City Clerk recommends Council appoint the recommended candidate at pleasure of Council for a term ending June 27, 2026. No candidate names are given in the excerpt.

title: Turn Off the Lights: Requesting a Review of the Nuisance Lighting By-law - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: light pollution; building lighting; office lights; urban night lighting
brief: Existing nuisance-lighting rules under the Property Standards by-law can only be enforced where light shines directly into a dwelling unit, leaving residents with no recourse against extremely bright lights from neighbouring properties. Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe, recommends Council direct Municipal Licensing and Standards to include recommendations on strengthening nuisance lighting provisions in its fourth-quarter 2025 report back on the Property Standards review.

title: Authorization to Accept the Donation of a Public Sculpture at the Guild Park and Gardens - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: donation, garden parks; bequest; toy drive
brief: This motion asks Council to authorize accepting the donation of War Horse, a larger-than-life bronze bust of a bridled horse head by German/Canadian sculptor Emanuel Hahn (1881-1957), for re-installation at the Guild Park and Gardens as part of the City's Public Art and Monuments Collection. Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends Council authorize the General Manager, Economic Development and Culture, to execute a donation agreement with the Estate of Emanuel Hahn.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from 225 Birmingham Street for Second Street Junior Middle School Schoolyard Improvement - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: funding, schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, financing
brief: Second Street Junior Middle School needs to replace its more than 40-year-old wooden play structure, and the Toronto District School Board will support full schoolyard upgrades, including new basketball nets, a soccer pitch, a sand pit, an outdoor classroom, an enhanced community garden and a new playground, if external funding is secured. Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, recommends Council increase the 2024 Operating Budget by $75,000, fully funded by Section 37 benefits from the 225 Birmingham Street development, for the schoolyard improvements.

title: Increasing Green Space, Park Amenities and Local Active Transportation Connections - East-West Hydro Corridor Linear Park - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: parks and open space areas; green spaces; open spaces
brief: The East-West hydro corridor between Islington Avenue and Royal York Road is a large under-used green space in Ward 3 Etobicoke-Lakeshore, currently used informally for trails and dog exercise, while the area faces growing park pressure from development and population growth. Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends Council direct Parks, Forestry and Recreation, with Transportation Services and the local Councillor, to explore the feasibility of a linear park with local active transportation connections in the corridor.

title: More Great Eats - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: licences, operating licences; licenses; licensing, operating licenses
brief: Since 2002 the city has had a moratorium on sidewalk vending permits in downtown wards including Ward 11, making it difficult to buy from or start a food cart downtown, even though affordable street food supports small businesses and residents. Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, recommends Council direct Municipal Licensing and Standards, with Transportation Services, Toronto Public Health and the Ward 11 Councillor, to report back to the February 26, 2025 Economic and Community Development Committee on easing mobile food vending rules.

title: Wonscotonach Parklands Naming Review - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: Council adopted the name Wonscotonach for the Lower Don River parkland system in 2018 after consultations, but language circles and community engagement found no clear consensus on the name's meaning, spelling and connection among Indigenous language speakers. Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, recommends Council ask Parks, Forestry and Recreation and the Indigenous Affairs Office to engage an Indigenous Naming Circle to review the naming.

title: The Night’s Watch - Ensuring Appropriate Oversight and Review of City-Wide Zoning By-law Changes for Nightclub Permissions - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: nightclubs, zoning bylaws; dance clubs; dance halls; discos; night clubs, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A review of zoning rules for nightclubs on Lake Shore Boulevard West found no rationale to rescind nightclub permissions there and recommended a monitoring program once three nightclubs are licensed and operating in the study area for a year. Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends Council direct the Chief Planner and Municipal Licensing and Standards to monitor the implementation and effectiveness of the new nightclub zoning permissions city-wide.

title: 321 Laird Drive - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: appeals;
brief: The applicant for 321 Laird Drive is appealing the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of four minor variances (Application A0406/23NY) needed to construct a new building. Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends Council direct the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the appeal, retain outside consultants as necessary, and resolve the matter after consulting the ward councillor and planning staff.

title: Declaring Food Insecurity an Emergency - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: emergency plans, food banks; building evacuation plans; business continuity plans; fire escape plans; fire safety plans, foodshare
brief: Food bank visits in the Greater Toronto Area are up 51 per cent as the cost of living soars, and children are going to school hungry in one of the country's most prosperous cities. Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, recommends Council declare food insecurity an emergency in the City of Toronto and direct the City Manager to factor the declaration into ongoing and future food insecurity work, including the Poverty Reduction Strategy.

title: Youth Violence Interventions - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
topics: at risk youth, youth; adolescents, high risk youth; youth at risk
brief: There is growing need for community-based youth violence intervention, interruption and prevention, particularly in Ward 7 Humber River-Black Creek and Ward 1 Etobicoke North, with TO Wards Peace working through SafeTO on place-based local solutions. Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, recommends Council authorize the Executive Director, Social Development, Finance and Administration, to negotiate and enter into funding agreements with non-profit, community-based organizations.

title: City Council Authorization for City to Accept Grants on Behalf of The Atmospheric Fund - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
brief: This motion asks Council to authorize the City to receive a $150,000 grant from the Montreal-based Trottier Family Foundation on behalf of The Atmospheric Fund. The funds would support the fund's development of an integrated, actionable and resourced plan to accelerate public electric vehicle charging on non-City public and private properties, complementing the City-operated charging network. Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, recommends the authorization.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for a Heritage Plaque to Recognize the Extinct Passenger Pigeon and its Connection to Mimico - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: The extinct passenger pigeon, one of the most abundant birds in what is now Toronto, congregated around Mimico Creek; the name Mimico comes from the Algonkian word omiimiikaa, meaning resting place of wild pigeons. Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends Council increase Heritage Toronto's 2024 operating budget by $10,000, fully funded by Section 37 benefits from the 2151-2155 Lake Shore Boulevard West development, for a heritage plaque.

title: Enhanced Water Taxi Access to Toronto Island - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: Toronto Island Park draws about 1.4 million visitors a year, and privately operated water taxis carried an estimated 486,066 passengers in 2023, with five operators and 53 boats licensed to dock at the island in 2024. Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, recommends Council authorize Parks, Forestry and Recreation to negotiate licence agreements letting private water taxi operators dock at designated island locations for annual terms at market rates.

title: Engaging the Canadian Infrastructure Bank to Support Housing Supply - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: The City has pledged actions toward 285,000 homes by 2031, but challenging market conditions and upfront infrastructure costs are delaying projects and blocking key growth areas. Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends Council ask the City Manager, with the CFO and the Deputy City Manager for Development and Growth Services, to identify potential projects for the Canadian Infrastructure Bank, which offers competitive financing rates and flexible repayment schedules.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.EC11.1 - Mount Dennis "Community for All Action Plan" - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: development, housing; developing land; development (land); land development, homes; residences
brief: Council adopted the Mount Dennis Community for All Action Plan in April 2024, including $35,000 to the Learning Enrichment Foundation to plan and co-host the Mount Dennis for All symposium, now scheduled for April 2025. The foundation has advised more funding is needed. Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends Council re-open the decision and raise the amount to $50,000.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Bridge Contract with Kodiak Group Holdings Co. Operating as Work Authority for Various Safety Footwear - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: employees, safety; public safety, staff
brief: The City's contract with Kodiak Group Holdings Co. operating as Work Authority for safety footwear, occupational footwear and galoshes for city employees expired June 30, 2023, but supply must continue to meet legislated health and safety obligations while a new competitive solicitation is delayed. Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends Council grant authority under the financial control code for Toronto Fire Services to negotiate and enter into an amending bridge agreement with the company.

title: Amending Item 2023.SC2.1 - 1625, 1633 and 1641 Kingston Road and 52 Birchcliff Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Amendment - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
brief: Council's 2023 approval of the rental housing demolition at 1625, 1633 and 1641 Kingston Road and 52 Birchcliff Avenue required site plan approval conditions and excavation and shoring permits before the 33 rental units could be demolished. Because the existing buildings are deteriorating with health and safety issues, the applicant wants to demolish sooner. Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng, recommends Council re-open its 2023 decision and delete those preconditions.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.CC23.8 - 2079-2111 Yonge Street, 9-11, 21, 31, 35 and part of 37 Hillsdale Avenue East, and 12-18 and part of 20 Manor Road East - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: The application for a 29-storey mixed-use building at 2079-2111 Yonge Street, with 486 residential units including 31 replacement rental units and 2,000 square metres of non-residential space, was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after Council failed to decide. Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends Council re-open its earlier decision to authorize the City Solicitor to retain outside consultants to support the City's position at the tribunal.

title: 3350 Weston Road - Technical Amendment to By-law 345-2024 - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
brief: Council approved a 15-storey residential building at 3350 Weston Road and enacted By-law 345-2024, but an error in the maximum storey count needs correcting. Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends Council amend the by-law to clarify that the mezzanine level and elevator penthouse are excluded from the storey calculation, and authorize the City Solicitor to make technical changes.

title: Authority to Enter into Agreement with Scarborough Health Network for the Alteration of City’s Watermain and Sewer - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainsle
topics: hospitals;
brief: Scarborough Health Network is renovating and expanding the Centenary Hospital Emergency Department at 2863 Ellesmere Road and needs to relocate or alter existing city sewers and a watermain on the site. Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, recommends Council authorize the General Manager, Toronto Water, to enter into an agreement letting the health network, through its contractor, relocate and alter the city water and sewer infrastructure.

title: Authorization for exemptions from delegated authority limits to provide nominal easement to homeowners of 603 Caledonia Road - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: easements;
brief: The shared garage at 603 Caledonia Road straddles the property line with city-owned 601 Caledonia Road and must be demolished so the City can use its property, but the homeowners will consent only if the portion on their lot is replaced and they get legal access over city-owned Part 3 for a driveway. Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, recommends Council authorize an exemption from the real property code's general conditions so the nominal driveway easement can be granted.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.TE13.7 - 1117 Danforth Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Amendment - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
brief: The 1117 Danforth Avenue application by a non-profit housing provider will build new social housing units plus rental replacement units, with all existing units vacant and tenants relocated, but the applicant needs preliminary rental demolition approval to start construction and demolition without delays that would raise costs. Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, recommends Council re-open its 2024 decision and amend the demolition approval so the social housing project can proceed on time.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Queensway Market Gardens Heritage Plaque - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: The Queensway Market Gardens once ran along the Queensway from the Humber River to west of Kipling Avenue, where family farms supplied the city with food and flowers, including an informal farmers' market at Park Lawn Road from 1915 to 1918. Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends Council increase Heritage Toronto's 2024 operating budget by $7,833.61, fully funded by Section 37 benefits from the 689 the Queensway development, to produce a heritage plaque.

title: Guns, not Fentanyl and Aliens, is our threat - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: international trade; exports; imports
brief: Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, argues that the real cross-border threat is the proliferation of firearms driving violent crime, not fentanyl or border security as stated by President-elect Trump in announcing 25 per cent tariffs on Canadian and Mexican goods. In the spirit and language of the proposed tariffs, the motion recommends Council ask the Canadian government to respond in kind with strategic tit-for-tat tariffs on imported U.S. goods.

title: 30 Charles Street East- Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: appeals, committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: The Committee of Adjustment refused a variance to allow an additional rental unit at 30 Charles Street East, and the owner has appealed to the Toronto Local Appeal Body. Tenants report the owner has a history of failing to provide vital services like heat and plumbing, failing to comply with city orders, and trying to force tenants out, and they have asked for the City's support. Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers, recommends Council direct the City Solicitor to seek party status and oppose the appeal.

title: Stating in the Strongest Terms Possible, that Proposed Arbitrary Tariffs on Canadian Exports Entering the United States Will Severely Damage Our Respective Economies and Should Be Reconsidered - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: President-elect Donald Trump has mused about placing 25 per cent tariffs on Canadian exports, and Toronto as Canada's economic engine would be severely harmed, likely triggering retaliation and a trade war. Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends Council express its objection to the arbitrary and draconian tariffs and forward the item to the U.S. Consul General in Toronto for information.

title: Continuing to Support Small Businesses Through Partnership with Digital Main Street - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: Digital Main Street, started by the City and the Toronto Association of Business Improvement Areas in 2016, helps main street businesses grow through technology, including Digital Service Squads that have provided hyperlocal support to small businesses since 2018. Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends Council authorize funding of up to $250,000 in 2024 and a further $200,000 in 2025 through the BIA association.

title: 579 Glencairn - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: On November 7, 2024 the Committee of Adjustment refused the consent to sever and two minor variance applications for 579 Glencairn Avenue, where the owner wants to demolish the existing dwelling, sever the lot into two and build two new detached dwellings, against planning staff's recommendation. Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, recommends Council authorize the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to uphold the refusal.

title: 4050 Yonge Street - Amendment to Section 37 Agreement - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: The site at the north-west corner of Yonge Street and Wilson Avenue, including portions of the Don River, was approved in 2022 (By-law 788-2022) for two residential towers in a mixed-use development with office and retail and a connection to the York Mills subway station pedestrian tunnels. The zoning secured conveyance of conservation land. Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends Council authorize the City Solicitor to support the applicant's request at the Ontario Land Tribunal to revise the Section 37 provisions for the conservation land conveyance.

title: Toronto-New York Corridor High-speed Train - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas, expresses strong support for a high-speed rail connection between Toronto and New York City, echoing New York State Senator Jeremy Cooney's recent backing for the link. The motion argues the project aligns with the City's commitment to sustainable transportation and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Council is asked to express its support for the Toronto-New York connection.

title: Clarence Square Park Improvements - Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: Clarence Square Park, one of downtown's oldest parks with a mature tree canopy, benches and an enclosed off-leash area, is an area of Special Identity in the King-Spadina Secondary Plan described as unique in Toronto. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, recommends Council direct Parks, Forestry and Recreation to engage community stakeholders and the local Councillor on the feasibility of enhancing recreational uses and undertaking park improvements.

title: 187 Oakridge Drive - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: appeals, committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: The Committee of Adjustment approved demolishing the existing dwelling at 187 Oakridge Drive and building a new two-storey dwelling (Application A0215/24SC) with 457.25 square metres of floor space, well above the 341.44 square metres permitted by the by-law. Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng, recommends Council direct the City Solicitor to appeal the decision and attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body hearing.

title: Opportunities to Advance Wider Waterfront Initiatives - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: development, waterfronts; developing land; development (land); land development, lakefronts; waterfront trail
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, asks staff to report back by the third quarter of 2025 on opportunities to advance waterfront initiatives beyond the Central Waterfront and Designated Waterfront Area projects. The report would cover City and Toronto and Region Conservation Authority joint projects on the Scarborough and Etobicoke Lake Ontario waterfront that could attract senior-government funding, informing intergovernmental discussions and the 2026 budget deliberations.

title: Investing In Youth, Empowering Our City’s Potential: Creation of a Toronto Youth Employment Program - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: Youth unemployment in Toronto is at crisis levels, the highest since 2014 excluding the pandemic years, hitting equity-deserving groups such as Black and Indigenous youth hardest, while youth firearm arrests have spiked 161 per cent in two years. Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers, proposes creating a Toronto Youth Employment Program and recommends Council ask the federal government to add investment through the Canada Summer Jobs program and the province to invest in the program.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2023.TE6.22 - 88 Isabella Street - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: demolitions, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: Council's 2023 approval of the rental housing demolition at 88 Isabella Street required excavation and shoring permits before the 82 rental units could be demolished, but the applicant wants to demolish before those permits issue. Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow, recommends Council re-open its 2023 decision and delete the excavation and shoring permit precondition so demolition can proceed.

title: Amending Item 2019.MM8.42 - Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 20 to 26 Lombard Street to the Old Town Business Improvement Area for Capital Improvements to Front Street East and Jarvis Street - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: In 2019 the Old Town Toronto Business Improvement Area received $125,000 in Section 37 funds for an art installation in Farquhars Lane but lost the ability to install it there and has since found an alternative location. Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, recommends Council amend its 2019 decision to move the artwork to Front Street East and Jarvis Street.

title: Authorization to Release Sections 37 Funds for Yorkville Library - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: funding, library branches; branches, financing
brief: The Yorkville Library at 22 Yorkville Avenue is the oldest branch in the Toronto Public Library network, opened in 1907 with a Carnegie grant and listed as a heritage property in 1973, serving a community of 61,000. Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, recommends Council increase the library's 2024-2033 Capital Budget by $1,000,000, fully funded by Section 37 community benefits from nearby developments, to enhance capital upgrades including accessibility.

title: Supporting a Fire Fighters Burn Victim Care Centre - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
brief: The city-owned former fire hall at 641 Eglinton Avenue West, most recently used by Metrolinx for the Eglinton Crosstown, could house a Home Away Program for burn victims treated at Sunnybrook or The Hospital for Sick Children, run by Toronto Fire Fighters Charities Inc. Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends Council ask the City Manager to report in the second quarter of 2025 on the feasibility of leasing the building to the charity at a nominal cost.

title: Toward Municipal Autonomy and Effective Local Governance - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: Citing provincial overreach into municipal jurisdiction, Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers, argues that Toronto delivers and funds major services like transit, roads and social housing while the province can overturn council decisions at will, which threatens local democracy and civic engagement. The motion recommends Council ask the City Manager to establish a Program Advisory Body on Municipal Autonomy and Effective Local Governance.

title: Requesting By-law Exemptions for Toronto Spring Festival on Nathan Phillips Square - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: The Toronto Spring Festival, a Lunar New Year celebration uniting diverse communities, missed inclusion in the normal Nathan Phillips Square event approvals because its application arrived in the November 2024 call for 2025 use. Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, recommends Council grant a one-time exemption so the Canada International Dance Culture Association can solicit donations and use special effects pyrotechnics for the festival.

title: Preservation of Architectural Character in Guildwood Community - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
brief: The Guildwood community, founded by Rosa and Spencer Clark as Canada's first artists' community and home to the Guild Inn and Guild Park and Gardens with its saved architectural artefacts, faces development pressure. Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas, recommends Council direct City Planning and Development Review to undertake a thorough review of existing development guidelines and zoning regulations in Guildwood to preserve its architectural character.

title: Ontario Line Vehicle Exemption along King Street West at Portland Street - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: General traffic must turn right off King Street within the Transit Priority Corridor at most major intersections, with exemptions for streetcars, buses, Wheel-Trans, airport shuttles, crisis service vehicles and bicycles, plus late-night taxis. With the Ontario Line King-Bathurst Station under construction, Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends Council let Metrolinx vehicles transporting materials or equipment proceed through King Street West at Portland Street when through travel is restricted.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Boulevard Improvements to Roehampton Avenue fronting North Toronto Collegiate Institute - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: The green boulevard on the north side of Roehampton Avenue fronting North Toronto Collegiate Institute needs significant upkeep from heavy pedestrian use, and staff and local residents have designed improvements adding tree canopy, perennial planting, a protective low fence and benches, with construction planned for 2025. Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, recommends Council increase the Transportation Services capital budget by $90,000, fully funded by Section 37 benefits from the 89-101 Roehampton Avenue and 75 Broadway Avenue developments.

title: Exploring the Feasibility of Expanding Eligibility Criteria to Increase Food Bank Access to the Charities, Institutions and Religious Organizations (CIROs) Waste Collection Fee Waiver Program - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: food banks, waste collection; collection (activity); collection routes, foodshare
brief: Food banks are serving record numbers of users, with 1 in 10 Toronto residents relying on them, yet they pay for city waste collection, diverting scarce operating budgets to disposal costs. Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends Council direct the General Manager, Solid Waste Management Services, to assess the feasibility of expanding eligibility for the Charities, Institutions and Religious Organizations waste collection fee waiver to include food banks.

title: 10 Ternhill Crescent - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
brief: On November 7, 2024 the Committee of Adjustment approved five zoning variances (Application A0480/24NY) to allow a new dwelling at 10 Ternhill Crescent, but the councillor's office has outstanding concerns about lot coverage and related matters. Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng, recommends Council direct the City Solicitor to appeal the decision and authorize the solicitor and staff to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body hearing.

title: Residential On-Street Parking for Cargo Bikes
topics: bicycles, on-street parking, transportation; bikes, curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, transportation services
brief: This is an information item: staff explored options for cargo bike parking in residential permit parking areas at the Infrastructure and Environment Committee's request. Staff examined exempting cargo bike owners from buying a permit and offering a voluntary unique licence plate that would let owners buy a permit, and found neither option to be a viable solution. The General Manager, Transportation Services recommends the committee's report be received for information.

title: Corporate Emission Budgets for 2026 - 2030
topics: city initiatives, climate, greenhouse effect; city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, greenhouse gas emissions
brief: This is an information item: the Executive Director, Environment and Climate reports on corporate emission budgets for 2026-2030, adopted under the Climate Change Goals and Governance chapter of the Municipal Code in May 2023. The corporate emissions budget is set at 2,016,471 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (about 2 megatonnes) for the period, letting the City allocate sector budgets for corporate buildings and transportation and track emissions against them. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Mississauga Boundary Facilities Agreement
topics: agreements, maintenance, service boundaries; community council boundaries, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff ask City Council to renew the cost-sharing and maintenance agreement with the City of Mississauga for boundary facilities shared by both municipalities. The previous agreement ran from January 1, 2012 to December 31, 2022, and the proposed renewal is substantially similar, with a new clause acknowledging that Mississauga may assume the Queensway Bridge, currently shared between Peel Region and Toronto under a separate agreement.

title: Granting Shared By-Law Authorities During Transition of Urban Forestry Branch
topics: by-laws, environment (sc), urban forestry; bylaws, forestry; tree health
brief: This is a procedural item: as the Urban Forestry branch transitions, staff ask City Council to amend Municipal Code Chapters 813, 658, 608, 632, 743, 918 and 441 to grant the Executive Director, Environment and Climate equal authority with the General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation over shared by-law authorities. The General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation and the Executive Director, Environment and Climate recommend the amendments as described in Attachment 1.

title: Feasibility of Requiring Side Guards on All Commercial Trucks Operating in the City of Toronto, Including Retrofitting the City's Fleet
topics: pickup trucks (fleet), retrofits, transportation equipment; building renewals; building retrofits; energy retrofits
brief: Staff report to City Council on the feasibility of requiring side guards (lateral protective devices) on all commercial trucks operating in Toronto, including retrofitting the City's fleet. Research from the United Kingdom, Australia and the Netherlands suggests side guards could cut cyclist fatalities by about 62 percent and pedestrian fatalities by 20 percent. Staff recommend Council direct Fleet Services to retrofit suitable City-owned commercial vehicles with side guards, subject to securing $5,675,560 net of HST through the 2025 budget process.

title: Ship Channel Bascule Bridge Rehabilitation Project and Unwin Avenue Bailey Bridge Replacement Study - Update
topics: bridge rehabilitation, funding, transportation; bridge reconstruction; bridge repair, financing, transportation services
brief: Staff ask City Council to authorize up to an additional $15 million from the approved 2024-2033 capital budget for the rehabilitation of the Ship Channel bascule bridge in the Port Lands, through an amended funding agreement with PortsToronto. The City is funding the rehabilitation of the bridge's approach spans and superstructure, while PortsToronto funds the mechanical and electrical work on the bridge that carries Cherry Street over the Ship Channel. The report also updates the Unwin Avenue Bailey Bridge replacement study.

title: Compressed Natural Gas Environmental Attributes
topics: conservation, diesel fuel, natural gas; environmental conservation; environmental improvements; environmental management; environmental protection; environmental stewardship; greening
brief: Solid Waste Management Services has moved its residential waste collection fleet to natural gas, with 96 percent of in-house trucks now using it, and owns compressed natural gas fuelling stations at three of its sites. That ownership creates an opportunity to create and sell compliance credits under the federal Clean Fuel Regulations. Staff ask City Council to authorize the General Manager to negotiate and execute agreements, including by non-competitive procurement, related to the compressed natural gas environmental attributes.

title: Update to Parking Bylaws Associated with Accessible Parking Permit Exemptions
topics: accessible permit parking, by-laws, exemptions; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled), bylaws, exceptions
brief: Staff ask City Council to amend Municipal Code Chapter 903, Parking for Persons with Disabilities, to let the City enforce against larger vehicles classified as commercial or recreational that use an accessible parking permit while parked on city streets. Under current bylaws, vehicles displaying a valid provincial accessible parking permit are exempt from certain parking regulations. Council is asked to add a new subsection to clarify that the exemption applies only when the permit is displayed as required.

title: Non-Competitive Bridge Contract with Kemira Water Solutions Canada for Toronto Water
