topics: chemicals, contracts, water quality, water treatment, water treatment plants; filtration plants; water filtration plants; water treatment and supply plants; water treatment facilities, water filtration; water purification, water quality reports
brief: Toronto Water seeks authority to enter a non-competitive bridge contract with Kemira Water Solutions Canada Inc. for the supply and delivery of iron salts (ferrous chloride), used by wastewater treatment plants to remove phosphorus, for one year starting January 1, 2025. The bridge contract would extend the existing contract 47023307, since Council approval is required where the commitment exceeds the Chief Procurement Officer's authority. The General Manager, Toronto Water and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend the extension.

title: Authority to Enter Into an Agreement with Parkrun Canada for Nominal Fee Permits to Hold a Community Running Pilot on the Martin Goodman Trail
topics: agreements, fitness trails, permits; exercise trails; vita parcours, permit renewal, tenancy agreements
brief: Parkrun is a free, volunteer-led 5-kilometre run, jog and walk event held every Saturday morning around the world, with no cost to register. Councillor Gord Perks recommends City Council authorize Parks, Forestry and Recreation to negotiate an agreement with Parkrun Canada for non-exclusive nominal fee permits for a community running pilot on the Martin Goodman Trail at Budapest Park, Sunnyside Park, and a third trail location. The pilot would promote healthy, active lifestyles for participants of all abilities and economic backgrounds.

title: Natural Resources Canada’s Codes Acceleration Fund for The Atmospheric Fund
topics: energy efficiency, environmental conditions, funding; alternative energy; electricity usage; energy use; sustainable energy, environmental health; environmental quality; environmental sensitivity; state of the environment, financing
brief: In April 2023 the City and The Atmospheric Fund applied to Natural Resources Canada's Codes Acceleration Fund to support building emissions performance standards, codes performance evaluation and knowledge sharing with other municipalities. On February 7, 2024, the City entered a non-repayable contribution agreement. Councillor Jennifer McKelvie recommends Council authorize the Executive Director, Environment and Climate to execute an agreement with The Atmospheric Fund to transfer the federal funds.

title: Toronto Islands' Environmentally Significant Areas
topics: Master Plans, parks, wetlands; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, marshes; ponds; swamps
brief: This is an information item: the General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation reports on Environmentally Significant Areas and Provincially Significant Wetlands on Toronto Island, the highest-quality ecological assets of the city's Natural Heritage System. The report describes ongoing investment in erosion infrastructure, park use management, invasive species control and native planting. Council is asked to receive the report through the Infrastructure and Environment Committee.

title: Updates on Vision Zero Road Safety Plan
topics: budgets, greenhouse effect, road safety; budgets and accounts, greenhouse gas emissions
brief: This report updates City Council on the Vision Zero Road Safety Plan, which has aimed since 2016 to eliminate serious injuries and fatalities on Toronto streets. The General Manager, Transportation Services recommends Council designate Community Safety Zones at the locations in Attachment 1 and delete Subsection (3) of section 950-400B of Municipal Code Chapter 950, Traffic and Parking. The report covers trends in serious injuries and fatalities and new countermeasures.

title: Regarding the Cost of Toronto Fire Services Operations on the Toronto Island
topics: fire and rescue services; fire fighting; fire services; fire suppression; firefighting; rescue; rescue operations; search and rescue
brief: This is an administrative inquiry from Councillor Jon Burnside under Municipal Code S27-7.11, asking the City Manager for information on Toronto Fire Services costs on Toronto Island. The request covers the average cost per incident city-wide in 2023, the average cost per incident on the Toronto Islands in 2023, and the island figures for peak and off-peak periods. No decision is attached; it is a request for information.

title: Action Plan to Keep Toronto Safe from Hate
topics: culture (sc), safety; public safety
brief: Councillor James Pasternak has submitted an administrative inquiry under the Municipal Code seeking information, updates and details of actions taken since May 2024, when Council asked the City Manager to develop an action plan to keep Toronto safe from hate and protect places of worship, faith-based schools and daycares, and other vulnerable institutions. Council adopted the original motion on May 23, 2024 in a 13-11 vote. The item seeks information and carries no recommendation.

title: Appointment of Acting Medical Officer of Health
topics: appointments, health; health coverage
brief: This is a procedural item: the Medical Officer of Health Hiring Committee recommends to the Board of Health that City Council appoint the Associate Medical Officer of Health named in Confidential Attachment 1 as Acting Medical Officer of Health for the City of Toronto Health Unit, effective January 1, 2025. The individual's name is confidential in the report.

title: Strengthening and expanding the Into Kids' Health program
topics: children, health, youth programs; child, health coverage, leadership programs
brief: The Medical Officer of Health asks City Council to authorize ongoing agreements with Toronto's four school boards (TDSB, TCDSB, Mon Avenir and Conseil scolaire Viamonde) to transfer funds for the Into Kids' Health program. The evidence-informed collaboration between Toronto Public Health and schools in equity-deserving communities gives participating schools up to $7,500 over two years to create healthy school environments. No decision details beyond the authorization are given.

title: Authority to Receive Grants in Support of Public Health Initiatives
topics: boards of health, health, public health; health coverage
brief: The Medical Officer of Health asks City Council for standing authority to accept grants from governments, agencies, community organizations, private entities or individuals to support Toronto Public Health programs and services. A recent example is a one-time $100,000 transfer from the Urban Public Health Network to boost HPV vaccination rates among high school students in the 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 school years. The recommended delegation would let the Medical Officer of Health enter such funding agreements.

title: Contracts and Purchase Order Amendments Process
topics: change, contracts, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, amendments; conversion; modification
brief: Councillor Vincent Crisanti recommends that City Council ask the Chief Financial Officer, in consultation with the Chief Procurement Officer, to review the historic use of contract and purchase order amendments and report to the General Government Committee in the third quarter of 2025. The motion notes that this meeting alone has 15 amended items totalling over $55 million, with more than $31 million attributed to unforeseen items, and that 60 amended items have come forward since January.

title: Award of Doc4553928310 to GFL Environmental Inc., for Curbside Collection Services in District 2 for Solid Waste Management Services
topics: contracts, purchasing, solid waste management; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, solid waste management planning; swm; waste management
brief: City Council referred this item back to the General Government Committee in October 2024. The report advises on the results of Request for Quotation Doc4553928310 for the collection, transportation and off-loading of garbage, bulky items, organic materials and yard waste from curbside single-family homes and multi-residential locations in District 2, with a recommendation to award the contract to GFL Environmental Inc. The item summary gives no recommendation text or contract value.

title: Temporary Suspension of Duron Ontario Ltd.
topics: contracts, purchasing, suppliers, suspension; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders
brief: Staff ask City Council to suspend Duron Ontario Ltd.'s eligibility to bid on or be awarded any City contracts for four months, for contraventions of the Supplier Code of Conduct on supplier performance in Chapter 195 of the Municipal Code. Duron is currently suspended under the Chief Procurement Officer's authority, and the officer recommends a longer Council-imposed suspension covering Duron and affiliated persons as suppliers or subcontractors.

title: Expropriation of Business Improvement Area Land and Potential Compensation
topics: business associations, business improvement areas, expropriations, payment, taxes; bia; business improvement associations, compulsory purchase; eminent domain, industry associations; marketing alliances; trade associations, levies, paying; payment information; payment methods; payment options; pre-authorized payment plans; pre-authorized plans; preauthorized payments
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to receive, for information, a report from Revenue Services explaining how the city would determine and collect payments in lieu of taxes for businesses Metrolinx has expropriated and closed in Business Improvement Areas, and how the city would make up the BIA levies on those properties. Council ordered the report in October 2024. No decision or policy change is proposed.

title: 2022 - 2023 Annual Human Rights Office Report
topics: annual reports, human rights, policies and procedures; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, guidelines; policies
brief: This is an information item: the Chief People Officer presents the 2022-2023 annual report of the City's Human Rights Office, as required by the City's Human Rights and Anti-Harassment / Discrimination Policy. The Office received 1,294 inquiries in 2022 and 1,190 in 2023, a 43 percent increase since 2019, and undertook program initiatives to prevent human rights breaches and promote equity and inclusion. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Occupational Health and Safety Report - End of Year 2023
topics: annual reports, injuries, safety; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, public safety
brief: This is an information item: the Chief People Officer reports on the City's health and safety system performance in 2023. Lost-time injuries fell 16.4 percent compared to 2022, while recurrences rose 5.5 percent and medical aid injuries rose 28 percent. Invoiced costs under the City's Workplace Safety and Insurance Board firm number rose from $49.5 million in 2022 to $57.3 million in 2023, mainly from mental and emotional illness claims. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: 101 Cedarvale Avenue (Carpark 20) - Future De-designation as a Municipal Parking Facility - Toronto Transit Commission's Line 2 Capacity Enhancement Program
topics: municipal facilities, parking, public transit; city facilities; municipal buildings, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: This is a housekeeping item: City Council is asked to de-designate 101 Cedarvale Avenue (Carpark 20) as a municipal parking facility once the TTC gives 90 days' notice that the building permit is approved. The site has been identified as the ideal location for the new Danforth Traction Power Substation, part of the TTC's Line 2 Capacity Enhancement Program. The change requires amending Municipal Code Chapter 950, Traffic and Parking.

title: 33 Queen Street East - Toronto Parking Authority Settlement Proposal with Dakin West Inc.
topics: legal matters, parking, parking authorities; legal issues, parking authority
brief: The City Solicitor and the Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management ask City Council to approve a proposed conditional settlement between the Toronto Parking Authority and Dakin West Inc. at 33 Queen Street East, set out in Confidential Attachment 1. Council is also asked to adopt the confidential instructions to staff and keep the confidential information sealed. No public details of the settlement terms are given.

title: Amendment to By-law Governing the City-sponsored Pension Plan - Toronto Fire Department Superannuation and Benefit Fund
topics: funding, governance, pensions; financing, governance structure; municipal governance
brief: This is a procedural item: the Executive Director, Finance Shared Services asks City Council to amend the by-law governing the Toronto Fire Department Superannuation and Benefit Fund to raise the Plan Committee Chair's honorarium from $7,500 to $15,000 per year.

title: Largest Property Tax Debtors with Tax Arrears Greater than $500,000 as at June 30, 2024
topics: arrears, debt, property taxes, taxes; levies, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts, outstanding balances; outstanding bills; outstanding charges; overdue; past due; unpaid balances; unpaid bills
brief: This is an information item: the Executive Director, Finance Shared Services reports on property tax accounts with outstanding receivables of $500,000 or more as of June 30, 2024. Thirty properties meet that threshold, 27 owned by corporations and 3 by individuals, an increase from the number reported as of December 31, 2023. Council is asked to direct that the confidential information in Confidential Attachment 3 remain confidential.

title: Amendments to Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 217, Records, Corporate (City)
topics: archives (records), conservation (archival), municipal codes, records; conservators
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Clerk asks Council to amend the records retention by-law (Municipal Code Chapter 217) to add three new retention schedules, including for declarations of office executed by members of council before they take office. The by-law provides the legal basis for destroying city records once retention periods expire. Council is asked to amend Schedule A of Chapter 217 as set out in Appendix 1.

title: 50 Richmond Street East - Nominal Lease Agreement with Unity Health Toronto
topics: agreements, contracts, health, leasing, public health; health coverage, leases, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff ask City Council to authorize an up to ten-year nominal lease agreement with Unity Health Toronto for the property at 50 Richmond Street East. The lease, with a future service level agreement, would let Unity Health, in partnership with Toronto Public Health, run clinic programming to meet urgent health needs in the downtown core, as Toronto Public Health relocates some clinical services following the approved sale of 277 Victoria Street.

title: 26 Gerrard Street East - Designation of the Property Used by Toronto Shelter and Support Services as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: facility naming, property (sc), supportive housing; alternative housing; special needs housing; supported housing, park naming
brief: Staff ask City Council to pass a by-law under Section 252 of the City of Toronto Act, 2006 to designate the property at 26 Gerrard Street East, owned by Aura Hotel Group Inc. and leased to the City, as a municipal capital facility. The designation would exempt about 26,500 square feet leased to Toronto Shelter and Support Services from municipal property taxes and education taxes. The site helps meet unprecedented demand for shelter and 24-hour respite services since the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Non-Competitive Procurement with Computacenter TeraMach Technologies Inc., for Change Management Consulting Services for Housing Secretariat
topics: housing, information and communication technology, management (sc), technology acquisition; homes; residences, ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it, information technology acquisitions; it acquisitions
brief: Staff ask City Council to authorize a new non-competitive contract with Computacenter TeraMach Technologies Inc. for change management consulting services for the Housing Secretariat, from the date of award to December 31, 2026, for $442,478 ($450,266 net of HST recoveries). The work supports a new phase of the Housing Secretariat's modernization project, with a focus on digital equity for housing applicants who lack access to technology.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Esri Canada Limited for Proprietary Geographic Information System Software Licenses, Cloud Subscriptions and Related Maintenance
topics: application software, contracts, geographic information systems, maintenance, software, software licences; computer programs, geospatial layers; gis, software licenses
brief: Staff ask City Council to authorize a non-competitive contract with Esri Canada Limited for proprietary Geographic Information System software licences, cloud subscriptions and related maintenance. Council gave initial authority in April 2024 (2024.GG11.10) for continuity of GIS services while Technology Services assessed future capability needs; with the assessment complete, staff return to seek authority for future staff capability requirements and long-term GIS capability goals. The Chief Technology Officer and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend the contract.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order Number 6047137 with North Tunnel Constructors ULC for the Construction of the Coxwell Bypass Tunnel between Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant and Coxwell Ravine Park
topics: contracts, legal matters, water treatment, water treatment plants; filtration plants; water filtration plants; water treatment and supply plants; water treatment facilities, legal issues, water filtration; water purification
brief: Staff ask City Council to approve a proposed settlement of claims that North Tunnel Constructors ULC is pursuing against the City over costs from the Coxwell Bypass Tunnel project between the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant and Coxwell Ravine Park. Council is also asked to amend Purchase Order 6047137 to fund the proposed settlement. The recommendations involve claims for significant compensation under the contract awarded through Request for Tender 221-2017.

title: Non-Competitive Contracts with Various Suppliers for the Supply of Proprietary Parts and Maintenance Services at Various Wastewater and Water Treatment Plants for Toronto Water
topics: contracts, wastewater, wastewater treatment, wastewater treatment, wastewater treatment plants, watermains; mains; water mains, sanitary sewage; sewage; waste water, sewage treatment plants; treatment plants; waste water treatment plants, sewage treatment; waste water treatment; wastewater management, sewage treatment; waste water treatment; wastewater management
brief: Staff ask City Council to authorize the General Manager of Toronto Water to negotiate five separate non-competitive contracts for proprietary parts and maintenance services at water and wastewater treatment plants. The contracts would run to December 31, 2025, with an option to extend for up to six one-year periods, for a total of $9,575,064 ($9,743,585 net of HST recoveries). The suppliers include Automated Logic Ltd. and Biorem Technologies Inc., among others named in the report.

title: Metro Hall (55 John Street) - Non-Competitive Contract with Siemens Canada Limited for Building Automation System Upgrades
topics: building plans, heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, system software; air conditioning; air conditioning systems; boilers; climate control systems; cooling systems; furnaces; heat; heating systems; hvac; ventilation; ventilation systems, building records
brief: Staff ask City Council to authorize a non-competitive contract with Siemens Canada Limited to upgrade the pneumatic (compressed air) controls on the central heating and cooling plants and basement to the existing Siemens Apogee building automation system at Metro Hall, 55 John Street. The contract is worth $1,042,800 ($1,061,154 net of HST recoveries) over ten months and is the second and final phase of the building automation system upgrades at Metro Hall.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Moore Canada Corporation for the Provision of Renewal Forms and Parking Permits
topics: parking, permits, redevelopment; permit renewal, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Staff ask City Council to authorize a non-competitive contract with Moore Canada Corporation for Speedimailer renewal forms and permits, plus printing and sealing services, for the on-street permit parking program. The contract would run two years from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2026, with an option for one more year, for a total potential value of $772,488 net of HST recoveries. The Speedimailer product is proprietary to Moore Canada and needs its specialized equipment.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with HP Canada for Supply and Provision of Single and Multi-function Printers, Plotters, and Related Maintenance and Services
topics: computer equipment, contracts, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, computer hardware; computer-related equipment
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Technology Officer and the Chief Procurement Officer ask City Council to authorize a two-year non-competitive bridge contract with HP Canada Ltd. for printers, plotters and related maintenance and services. The current contract expires January 15, 2025, and the bridge would continue under the same terms and conditions as the 2019 request for proposal, leveraging the remaining contract value of about $8.99 million. The recommended amount is $8,836,630.25 net of taxes ($8,992,154.94 net of HST recoveries).

title: Non-Competitive Contract with 1313135 Ontario Inc., operating as Lands and Forests Consulting for Prescribed Burn Services in 2025-2029 for Parks, Forestry and Recreation
topics: parks, recreation centres, urban forestry; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, forestry; tree health, rec centers; rec centres; recreation centers
brief: Staff ask City Council to authorize a new non-competitive contract with 1313135 Ontario Inc., operating as Lands and Forests Consulting, for planning and implementing the prescribed burn program in parks for one year from the date of award, with an option to renew for up to four additional one-year terms covering 2026 to 2029. The total potential contract value is $214,820 net of taxes ($218,601 net of HST recoveries). The firm has planned and implemented 73 prescribed park burn units with zero incidents since 2000.

title: Review of Zoning Regulations for Nightclubs on Lake Shore Boulevard West - Final Report
topics: nightclubs, zoning; dance clubs; dance halls; discos; night clubs
brief: This is a monitoring report: Council is asked to direct the Chief Planner to monitor the implementation and effectiveness of zoning permissions for nightclubs along Lake Shore Boulevard West between Palace Pier Court and Forty Third Street. Council enacted city-wide nightclub zoning permissions in December 2023 as part of the Night Economy Review, complemented by an updated licensing framework. The report is the final review of the Lake Shore Boulevard West nightclub zoning study.

title: 220, 230 and 240 Lake Promenade and 21 and 31 Park Boulevard - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment, and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Combined Official Plan, zoning and subdivision applications for 220, 230 and 240 Lake Promenade and 21 and 31 Park Boulevard proposed phased demolition of five seven-storey rental apartment buildings to build five new buildings of 12 to 30 storeys with 2,021 residential units (577 rental, including 548 replacement rentals, and 1,444 condominiums). The applicant has appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal. Staff recommend Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the applications in their current form.

title: 4875 Dundas Street West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: buildings, development, rental housing; developing land; development (land); land development, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse an Official Plan and zoning by-law amendment application for 4875 Dundas Street West, which proposed a 45-storey (150-metre) mixed-use building with 488 residential units (56 rental replacement and 432 condominium units) and 461 square metres of at-grade retail, at a density of 11.7 times the lot area. Staff find the proposal not consistent with Official Plan policies. A related rental housing demolition application has also been submitted.

title: 530 The East Mall - Rental Housing Demolition Application- Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, development, rental housing; developing land; development (land); land development, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the rental housing demolition application to demolish a seven-storey rental apartment building with 110 rental units at 530 The East Mall. The 110 units would be replaced as part of a new development on the site, which is also the subject of a zoning by-law amendment application. The proposal includes a tenant relocation and assistance plan giving existing tenants the right to move directly to a replacement unit of the same type at similar rent.

title: 530 The East Mall - Zoning By-law Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a zoning by-law amendment and draft plan of subdivision to allow three residential apartment buildings at 530 The East Mall: a 14-storey building, two 22-storey towers on an eight-storey base, and a 22-storey tower with an eight-storey base, plus a public park at the south of the site. The proposal includes 1,095 residential units (including 110 replacement rental units), 868 vehicle parking spaces and 822 bicycle parking spaces, with 84,098 square metres of gross floor area.

title: 82 Buttonwood Avenue - Temporary Use Zoning By-law - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning;
brief: West Park Healthcare Centre has redeveloped its campus at 82 Buttonwood Avenue and opened a new main hospital building, but the Ministry of Health has asked that the former hospital building and its central utility plant be retained and used temporarily. Staff recommend a temporary use zoning by-law to allow the former buildings to remain in use, since the existing zoning expects them to be demolished. Council is asked to amend former City of York By-law 1-83 to permit the temporary use.

title: Church Street - Removal of Traffic Calming Islands
topics: traffic calming;
brief: Traffic calming islands were installed on Church Street between Grattan Street and Cypress Street after residents petitioned about speeding, but the islands have proven ineffective at slowing traffic and have become a safety concern. Councillor Frances Nunziata recommends Council authorize removing the islands and ask the Director of Traffic Management to assess vehicle speeds on that stretch.

title: Humberwood Boulevard and Kingsplate Crescent - Traffic Control Signals
topics: public transit, traffic control systems; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize the installation of traffic control signals at the intersection of Humberwood Boulevard and Kingsplate Crescent / private access. Staff say the signals would improve safety for all road users and are justified by the assessment. TTC bus service operates on Humberwood Boulevard, so Council approval is required.

title: 2200 Islington Avenue - Traffic Control Signal Modifications (Non-Delegated)
topics: traffic control systems, traffic signal timing; advanced green; amber light phase; coordination of traffic signals; left turn arrow phase; left turn phase; pedestrian crossover timing; signal timing; traffic light timing; traffic signal operations; traffic signal phases; traffic signal synchronization, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to amend the by-law to reflect changes to traffic control signals at Rexdale Boulevard and Islington Avenue and at Rexdale Boulevard and Bergamot Avenue / Vetiver Drive. Council is also asked to rescind the existing eastbound left-turn prohibition and reflect dual eastbound-to-southbound right-turn lanes and dual northbound-to-westbound left-turn lanes. TTC bus service operates in the area, so Council approval is required.

title: Marine Parade Drive - Parking Amendments
topics: parking, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Transportation Services recommends prohibiting stopping at all times on the east side of Marine Parade Drive opposite Silver Moon Drive, between a point 23 metres south and a point 12 metres north of the intersection, to deter parking near the intersection. Council is asked to rescind the existing pay-and-display parking regulation for that section. A companion report proposes an all-way stop at Marine Parade Drive and Silver Moon Drive. TTC service operates on Marine Parade Drive, so Council approval is required.

title: 2422, 2428 and 2434 Islington Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: An application to amend the Official Plan, Zoning By-law 569-2013 and former Etobicoke By-law 11,737 for 2422, 2428 and 2434 Islington Avenue proposed demolishing the existing commercial plaza (Elmhurst Plaza), a Tim Hortons and a detached dwelling to build a mid-rise mixed-use building with two blocks of stacked townhouses. The amendment would redesignate the site from Neighbourhoods to Mixed Use Areas. The Director, Community Planning recommends Council approve the amendments.

title: 2050 Weston Road - Application for a Clothing Drop Box Location Permit
topics: clothing drop boxes; clothes donation boxes; clothing bins
brief: This is a procedural item: Municipal Licensing and Standards refused an application for a clothing drop box location permit at 2050 Weston Road. Staff report the refusal to City Council, which is asked to either deny or approve the application for the proposed clothing drop box permit.

title: 1-20 Adriatic Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve an Official Plan amendment (OPA 758) to redesignate 18 properties at 1-20 Adriatic Road, each with a detached dwelling, from Neighbourhoods to Apartment Neighbourhoods to allow a more intense form of development. The amendment would also redesignate the southeast corner of the block as parks and open space, recognizing on-site parkland dedication, and as natural areas for sensitive land in the Natural Heritage System. The rezoning would set regulations and performance standards for the intensified development.

title: 2025 Interim Water and Wastewater Consumption Rates and Service Fees
topics: wastewater, water rates; residential water rate, sanitary sewage; sewage; waste water
brief: Staff recommend that City Council adopt interim 2025 water and wastewater consumption rates and service fees, effective January 1, 2025, so staff have authority to implement them before the 2025 budgets are adopted. The recommended interim rates include a 3.75 percent increase to combined water and wastewater consumption rates for metered consumers. The rates may be amended when the 2025 rate-supported budgets are adopted.

title: 2025 Tax and Rate Supported Interim Operating and Capital Spending Authorities
topics: capital budgets, operating budgets, projects, taxes; levies
brief: Staff ask City Council to approve interim spending authorities for 2025 so City programs and agencies can keep delivering current services, meet contractual commitments and continue previously approved capital projects until the 2025 budgets are adopted in February 2025. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends approving interim operating spending authorities totalling $7.352 billion. No funding for new or enhanced services or new capital projects is included.

title: Toronto Membership in the Association of Municipalities of Ontario
topics: members, municipal associations; memberships
brief: This report addresses the intergovernmental and financial considerations of Toronto rejoining the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), which would reinforce Toronto's leadership in the municipal sector and support fiscal sustainability, knowledge sharing and municipal collaboration. The City Manager recommends Council direct the City Manager to facilitate Toronto's membership and negotiate any required agreements, while retaining Toronto's direct government-to-government relationships. No membership cost is stated in the excerpt.

title: Assessment of Scarborough Rapid Transit Adaptive Reuse and Next Steps
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, capital budgets; ttc
brief: Following Council's March 2024 request, this report assesses the scope, feasibility, costs and risks of adaptively reusing the decommissioned Scarborough Rapid Transit Line 3 right-of-way, infrastructure and stations. Line 3 ceased operation in July 2023 and was replaced by rapid bus service, while the Scarborough Subway Extension is planned for completion in 2030. The City Manager recommends Council ask the TTC Board to direct the Interim CEO to report in Q1 2025 on which SRT assets are no longer required.

title: Analysis of Driver Wages in the Vehicle-for-Hire Industry
topics: drivers, wages; earnings; pay; pay scale; salary; wage rate
brief: This is an information item: researchers Dr. Mischa Young, Dr. Steven Farber and Dr. Mashrur Rahman were retained to assess driver wages in the vehicle-for-hire industry, which includes taxicabs, limousines and private transportation companies. The academic assessment was requested to inform Council about the current state of driver wages. The Executive Director, Municipal Licensing and Standards recommends the Executive Committee receive the report for information.

title: Updating the Code of Conduct for Public Members of City Council’s Advisory Bodies
topics: advisory committees, behaviour standards, public appointments; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups, behavior standards; behaviour; code of conduct; codes of behaviour; codes of conduct; standards of behavior; standards of behaviour
brief: Councillor Chris Moise recommends that City Council direct the City Manager, in consultation with the City Clerk, the City Solicitor and the Integrity Commissioner, to develop a Code of Conduct for public members of Council advisory bodies. The report notes that a 2022 review updated codes of conduct for Members of Council, local board members and adjudicative board members, but created no code for Council appointees to advisory bodies, who are currently guided only by general standards in the Public Appointments Policy.

title: Authority to Accept Monetary and In-kind Archival Donations to Toronto Archives
topics: archives (records), donation; bequest; toy drive
brief: Staff ask City Council to accept archival donations to Toronto Archives valued over the $50,000 acceptance threshold: in-kind donations from photographers Vid Ingelevics ($122,600), Robert Burley ($86,500) and Ted Yarwood (estimated $50,000), plus a monetary donation of $34,074.07 from the Estate of Katherine Anne Hartley, for a total of $197,037.03. Council approval is required under the City's donations policy and Municipal Code Chapter 71.

title: 29 Basin Street - Ground Lease Amendments and Strengthening the Toronto Port Lands Company Mandate
topics: business & industry (sc), development, film and television industry; cinema industry; film and television cluster; film production; movie industry; television industry, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: City Council is asked to approve amendments to the ground lease between Toronto Port Lands Company and Basin Media Studios GP Inc. for the Basin Studios project at 29 and 75 Basin Street. The tenant requested the changes in response to extraordinary market and economic pressures since 2021; the project is an approximately $300 million film, television and digital media hub with over 485,000 square feet of new studio space in the Port Lands. The report also recommends strengthening the Toronto Port Lands Company's mandate.

title: Proposed Land Lease with the Community Music Schools of Toronto at 1785 Finch Avenue West
topics: land, leasing; leases, property
brief: Staff ask City Council to authorize an Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management, on behalf of the City as landlord, to negotiate a nominal land lease with the Community Music Schools of Toronto for part of 1785 Finch Avenue West. The leased premises cover part of the parking surface and an unused loading dock at the Toronto Public Library's York Woods Branch, where the tenant would design, build, finance and operate a new not-for-profit music school.

title: St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts - Enhanced State of Good Repair Strategy
topics: arts and culture organizations, performing arts; art councils; art organizations; arts councils; arts groups; cultural organizations
brief: This report responds to Council's request for an enhanced State of Good Repair plan for the St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts, with advice from Corporate Real Estate Management and Financial Planning to TO Live on a 10-year plan with a reasonable projected spend. The Deputy City Manager, Corporate Services recommends the Executive Committee direct Corporate Real Estate Management, working with TO Live and Financial Planning, to support implementing the enhanced repair plan. No capital amount is stated in the excerpt.

title: Next Phase of Waterfront Revitalization - Update
topics: development, waterfronts; developing land; development (land); land development, lakefronts; waterfront trail
brief: Following Council's 2022 in-principle approval of a Next Phase of Waterfront Revitalization, staff report back on intergovernmental discussions with provincial and federal officials. The Deputy City Manager recommends Council endorse the first set of priority projects in Attachment 1, subject to satisfactory cost-sharing from Ontario and Canada, which would advance complete communities in Ookwemin Minising (formerly Villiers Island) and Quayside.

title: Update on Co-development of First Nations, Inuit and Métis Procurement Policy
topics: First Nations, policy development; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples, policy making
brief: This is an information item: staff report on progress toward co-developing an Indigenous procurement strategy, as directed by Council in May 2023. A dedicated Policy Development Officer was hired in April 2024 to lead the work with Indigenous businesses and communities, and progress has been made since then. The Chief Procurement Officer recommends Council receive the progress report for information.

title: Social Procurement Policy Review
topics: programs, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders
brief: Staff report the results of a review of the Social Procurement Program, implemented in 2017 to leverage City purchasing power for workforce development and supply chain diversity, summarizing program output data from 2017 to 2023. The Chief Procurement Officer recommends City Council amend the Social Procurement Policy as set out in Attachment 1, effective January 1, 2025, and direct continued engagement with divisions, businesses and the community.

title: Arena Boards of Management Settlement of Operating Results for the year Ended 2022; and 2021 specifically for North Toronto Memorial Arena
topics: arenas, boards of management, financial reports, operating budgets; annual financial reports; financial statements, boards of directors; boards of governors, indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: The City annually settles operating surpluses and deficits with eight Arena Boards of Management based on their audited financial statements, paying or clawing back amounts to balance the results. The 2021 and 2022 operating surpluses total $450,458 from six arenas: George Bell, William H. Bolton, McCormick, Forest Hill, Ted Reeve, and North Toronto for 2021 and 2022. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends these surpluses be paid to the City and used in part to fund arena operations.

title: City of Toronto Reserve and Reserve Fund Balances as at September 30, 2024
topics: [activities in finance], reserve funds; reserves and reserve funds
brief: This report summarizes the City's reserves and reserve funds for the nine months ended September 30, 2024. Balances totaled $5,857.7 million, up $566.0 million from $5,291.7 million at December 31, 2023. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends City Council direct a transfer of $211.1 million from the Tax Rate Stabilizing Reserve to the Budget Bridging and Balancing Reserve Fund, consistent with the multi-year budget strategy.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2024
topics: budgets, operating budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: This report gives City Council the operating budget variance for the nine months ended September 30, 2024, with year-end projections to December 31, 2024, for tax-supported operations. It also asks Council to approve amendments to the 2024 Approved Operating Budget that have no impact on the City's net budget. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends the budget adjustments and associated changes detailed in the report's appendices.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2024
topics: capital budgets, financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer reports City capital spending for the nine months ended September 30, 2024, with projected 2024 year-end expenditures. Council is asked to approve in-year budget adjustments to the 2024-2033 Approved Capital Budget and Plan, including reallocations of funding sources for prior approved budgets, as detailed in Appendix 3.

title: City of Toronto Investment Report for the Six Month Period Ending June 30, 2024
topics: investment, reserve funds; reserves and reserve funds
brief: This report covers the performance of the City's investment funds for the six months ending June 30, 2024, along with a market update and compliance with the Council-adopted investment policy. The General Fund, which holds working capital plus the reserves and reserve funds, had a book return of 4.8 per cent and generated $247.6 million. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends Council receive the report for information.

title: 2025 Interim Solid Waste Management Services Rates and Fees
topics: fees, management (sc), solid waste; administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees, commercial waste; municipal solid waste; refuse
brief: Staff recommend Council adopt interim 2025 Solid Waste Management Services rates and fees effective January 1, 2025, in advance of the 2025 Tax and Rate Supported Operating and Capital Budgets expected in February 2025. The report recommends a 3.75 per cent increase in rates and fees so staff have authority to implement them on time. Council may amend the interim rates when the full 2025 budgets are approved.

title: Strengthening the City of Toronto's Housing Development Capacity to Deliver Housing Faster
topics: development, housing; developing land; development (land); land development, homes; residences
brief: Toronto faces an unprecedented housing affordability crisis, with too few deeply affordable and supportive homes for low-income residents and high rents for middle-income earners. Building on Council's 2023 housing delivery decisions, the City Manager recommends that Council, as sole shareholder, ask the Toronto Community Housing Corporation board to direct its CEO to work with the Deputy City Manager, Development and Growth Services to advance housing development projects under the City's housing plans.

title: Proposed Cedarbrae Markham Lawrence Village Business Improvement Area Poll Results
topics: business improvement areas, polling; bia; business improvement associations
brief: The City Clerk conducted a poll under Municipal Code Chapter 19 on designating the Cedarbrae Markham Lawrence Village Business Improvement Area, and the required benchmark number of ballots to validate the poll was received. The proposed BIA covers the area along Lawrence Avenue East bounded by Bellamy Road, Greenholm Court, Markham Road from Lawrence to the south, and Painted Post Drive. The General Manager, Economic Development and Culture recommends Council designate the area as a BIA.

title: Implementation of the Canada-wide Early Learning and Child Care System and 2025 to 2029 Child Care and Early Years Service Plan: Update
topics: child care, early childhood education; childcare, early education; ece; kindergartens; pre-school education; preschool education; preschool learning
brief: This is an information item: staff update City Council on implementing the Canada-wide Early Learning and Child Care system in Toronto, including the Province's new cost-based funding approach, recently announced program changes, and the development of the 2025-2029 Child Care and Early Years Service Plan. The General Manager, Children's Services recommends Council ask the federal and provincial governments to increase capital funding to meet child care targets in the not-for-profit and public sector for Toronto.

title: Shelter Safety Action Plan and Contract Amendments related to Lodging for Asylum Seekers and Refugees, and Community Safety Team Services
topics: women; shelters for women
brief: Staff ask City Council to adopt a 36-month Shelter Safety Action Plan advancing the recommendations of the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health Shelter Safety Study, developed with people with lived experience, shelter providers and the Housing Rights Advisory Committee. The report also seeks contract amendments related to lodging for asylum seekers and refugees and community safety team services. Council is asked to adopt the plan, which prioritizes safety for shelter staff and clients.

title: Addressing Reconciliation and Equity via Community Funding
topics: equity, funding; employment equity; fair wage; pay equity, financing
brief: Staff recommend that City Council adopt the Indigenous Funding Framework in Appendix 1 of the report, following work with not-for-profit leaders to support Indigenous, Black and equity-deserving communities hit hardest by the pandemic's aftermath and the affordability crisis. The report focuses on increasing financial resources, streamlining processes and reducing administrative burden to make funding more inclusive and accessible. Council is also asked to request a follow-up report through the Economic and Community Development Committee.

title: A Partnered Approach to Inclusive Economic Development
topics: economic development, economic indicators; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: Staff put forward a definition of Inclusive Economic Development with guiding principles to direct the City's efforts to advance it, responding to findings that Toronto's economic success has not been shared equitably. The definition and principles would form the basis for co-developing an Inclusive Economic Development Framework with community partners. Council is asked to adopt the definition and guiding principles.

title: Ombudsman Toronto Housing Unit Status Report 2024
topics: housing, ombudsman; homes; residences, ombudspersons
brief: This is an information item: the Ombudsman reports on the activities of Ombudsman Toronto's Housing Unit since its creation in July 2023. In less than a year, the unit was fully staffed, built its infrastructure, launched two investigations, consulted City staff, and met with more than 170 people through its engagement work. City Council referred the item to the Economic and Community Development Committee for consideration in July 2024.

title: 4800 Yonge Street - Request for Further Directions
topics: appeals, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning
brief: The applicant for 4800 Yonge Street sought to redevelop the site with a 49-storey (160-metre) mixed-use building with 497 dwelling units, a five-storey base with retail and office uses, and a five-level underground garage with 318 parking spaces, then appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal when Council did not decide in time. Council accepted a settlement offer on February 26, 2019. The City Solicitor now asks Council to adopt the recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 and authorize the public release of the confidential recommendations and appendices if adopted.

title: 145 Sheppard Avenue East - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a procedural legal item: the proposal for 145 Sheppard Avenue East, an 11-storey mixed-use building with at-grade retail and 47 underground parking spaces, has been before the tribunal since the applicant appealed in 2018 after Council refused the Official Plan Amendment. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 and authorize their public release if adopted.

title: 2453-2469 Bloor Street West - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a procedural legal item: Council approved a modified 10-storey development at 2453-2469 Bloor Street West through by-law 488-2024 after the applicant proposed 13 storeys with 91 units and 260 square metres of retail, and the applicant appealed that by-law to the Ontario Land Tribunal on May 27, 2024. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 and authorize their public release if adopted.

title: 390-400 Woodsworth Road- Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a procedural legal item: the applicant for 390-400 Woodsworth Road, proposing three 8-storey mid-rise residential buildings with two later raised to 9 and 10 storeys, appealed Council's failure to decide to the Ontario Land Tribunal on December 18, 2023. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 and authorize their public release if adopted. The site plan application was also appealed.

title: 4001 Steeles Avenue West, 5000 Jane Street and 360 Hullmar Drive - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a procedural legal item: the applicant for infill development at 4001 Steeles Avenue West, with three new towers of 45, 45 and 35 storeys, appealed Council's failure to decide to the Ontario Land Tribunal on March 13, 2023. The hearing was adjourned from November 2024 to May 2025. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 and authorize their public release if adopted.

title: Legal Review of Bike Lane Amendments to Highway Traffic Act, formerly Bill 212
topics: bike lanes; bicycle lanes; on street bike lanes
brief: Bill 212 became law on November 25, 2024, amending the Highway Traffic Act to require prescribed municipalities to get provincial approval before installing certain bike lanes that reduce vehicle lanes, and directing the Minister to remove existing bike lanes on University Avenue, Yonge Street and Bloor Street. The City Solicitor recommends Council keep the information in Confidential Attachment 1 confidential, as it contains solicitor-client privileged advice about litigation or potential litigation.

title: Canada Post Labour Disruption and Councillor Newsletter Entitlement
topics: municipal officials; city officials
brief: Councillors receive an annual Newsletter Entitlement to produce and distribute communications to ward households, but the Canada Post strike that began November 15, 2024 has prevented them from sending end-of-year 2024 mailings. The City Clerk recommends Council authorize councillors impacted by the disruption to spend their unspent 2024 Newsletter Entitlement, as of December 31, 2024, in 2025.

title: SmartTrack Stations Program - Update
topics: public transit, transit networks; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: The SmartTrack Stations Program, five stations on three GO rail corridors with a $1.689 billion budget including $878 million from the City, has received notice from the province of cost pressures exceeding the approved budget. The City Manager recommends Council confirm the priority for delivering three stations, East Harbour, Bloor-Lansdowne and St. Clair-Old Weston, within the current $1.689 billion program budget.

title: Policy Framework - City Response to Demonstrations
topics: protests; demonstrations; protest marches
brief: Council directed the City Manager in February 2024 to develop a policy framework for managing and monitoring rallies and protests, aligned with the City's Human Rights and Anti-Harassment Policy. The resulting Policy Framework - City Response to Demonstrations notes that Toronto Police Service is the primary responder and enforcement agency for demonstrations. The City Manager recommends Council adopt the framework and direct the City Manager to keep it current.

title: Advancing Phase One of the Purpose-built Rental Housing Incentives Stream
topics: rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: On November 13-14, 2024 Council adopted a new purpose-built rental housing incentives stream and directed staff to launch a Quick Start Call for Applications supporting 7,000 new rental homes, including at least 1,400 affordable rental homes. The call opened November 18 and closed November 29, 2024, and staff are reviewing submissions. The Executive Director, Housing Secretariat recommends Council receive this update for information.

title: 789-793 Don Mills Road and 10 Ferrand Drive - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Request for Direction Report
topics: official plan amendments;
brief: This is a procedural legal item: the application to redevelop 789-793 Don Mills Road and 10 Ferrand Drive would build four residential towers of 56, 49, 45 and 22 storeys in three phases, plus a privately-owned publicly accessible space and a public park at Ferrand Drive and Rochefort Drive. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 and authorize their public release if adopted.

title: 595 Bay Street, 304 - 316 Yonge Street and 14 - 40 Dundas Street West - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a procedural legal item: the applicant for a 34-storey mixed-use building at 595 Bay Street, 304-316 Yonge Street and 14-40 Dundas Street West, with 317 dwelling units and 2,998 square metres of non-residential space, appealed Council's failure to decide to the Ontario Land Tribunal on January 12, 2024. The City Solicitor needs directions for hearings scheduled June 9-13, 2025, and recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release if adopted.

title: 417-419 Burnhamthorpe Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural legal item: the application for a four-storey townhouse building with 10 residential units at 417-419 Burnhamthorpe Road was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on January 31, 2024 after Council failed to decide within the Planning Act timelines. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 and authorize their public release if adopted.

title: 33-51 Walsh Avenue and 2717-2745 Weston Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a procedural legal item: the application for 33-51 Walsh Avenue and 2717-2745 Weston Road, with six mixed-use towers of 14 to 40 storeys, a public park and 766 square metres of retail fronting Weston Road, was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on November 14, 2023 after Council failed to decide. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their public release if adopted.

title: 1245 and 1285 Dupont Street, 1260 Dufferin Street, and 213 Emerson Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a procedural legal item: the application for 1245 and 1285 Dupont Street, 1260 Dufferin Street and 213 Emerson Avenue would add 2,966 dwelling units across 8 buildings of 18 to 48 storeys, about a 30 per cent increase in height and residential floor area over the already-approved Reimagine Galleria development, including purpose-built and affordable rental units. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release if adopted.

title: 2350-2352 Yonge Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a procedural legal item: the application for a 50-storey residential building at 2350-2352 Yonge Street, with 323 dwelling units and 20,562 square metres of floor area, was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on July 10, 2023 after Council failed to decide. The summer 2024 hearing was adjourned for without-prejudice discussions. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their public release if adopted.

title: Ombudsman Toronto Report - An Investigation into the City's Decision to Stop Allowing Refugee Claimants into Base Shelter System Beds
topics: ombudsman; ombudspersons
brief: Ombudsman Toronto investigated the City's decision to stop allowing refugee claimants into base shelter system beds not specifically designated for them, marking the first investigation by the Ombudsman's Housing Unit, and issued 14 recommendations. The Ombudsman recommends City Council adopt the December 10, 2024 investigation report and direct the City to implement its recommendations, including following proper process for shelter standards amendments.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Lakeshore Arena Corporation Board
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Clerk recommends Council appoint the candidate in Confidential Attachment 1 to the Lakeshore Arena Corporation Board at pleasure of Council, for a term ending May 24, 2026, with the attachments remaining confidential. The candidate's name is not public in the report.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Board of Directors of TO Live
brief: This is a procedural item: the Civic Appointments Committee will interview candidates and recommend four of them to City Council for appointment to the Board of Directors of TO Live. The City Clerk recommends the Committee recommend four candidates at pleasure of Council for a term ending December 20, 2028, and asks that confidential attachments remain sealed.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Housing Rights Advisory Committee
brief: This is a procedural item: the Civic Appointments Committee must select candidates to interview for appointment to the Housing Rights Advisory Committee. The City Clerk recommends the Committee select five candidates from Confidential Attachment 1a to interview at its next meeting, with one candidate ultimately recommended to City Council for appointment. The confidential attachments would remain sealed.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will introduce General Bills and Confirming Bills. No details of the bills are given in the item.

title: Business Improvement Areas - Update on 2023 Audited Financial Statements
topics: business improvement areas, committees of council, financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements, bia; business improvement associations, council committees
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer presents the 2023 audited financial statements and management letters of 71 Business Improvement Areas for City Council's approval. All received unqualified audit opinions and were approved by their respective boards of management; one BIA, ShoptheQueensway.com, received minor recommendations to strengthen internal controls, which its management accepted. There are 83 active BIAs in the city.

title: Audit of Parks Branch Operations - Phase 1: December 2024 Status Update
topics: audits, maintenance, park maintenance, parks, parks and open space areas; auditors; auditors, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, green spaces; open spaces, parks maintenance
brief: This is a status update on the Auditor General's October 2024 audit of Parks Branch Operations, which found the branch needed better oversight of day-to-day parks maintenance to keep parks clean, safe and beautiful. City Council adopted recommendations in November 2024, including that Parks, Forestry and Recreation report back in December 2024, July 2025 and November 2025. The General Manager recommends Council receive this first status update for information.

title: Status Update on the Information Technology Disaster Recovery Program
topics: disasters, emergency management, information and communication technology; crisis management; disaster planning; disaster supply kits; emergency preparedness; emergency procedures; emergency supply kits; survival kits, ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it, major incident
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Technology Officer, the Chief Information Security Officer and the Executive Director of Toronto Emergency Management report progress on the City's Enterprise Information Technology Disaster Recovery Program, including business continuity and cyber major incident management and the status of disaster recovery plans across divisions, agencies and corporations. Council is asked to direct that Confidential Attachment 1 remain confidential, as it involves the security of City property.

title: Cybersecurity Audit of Toronto Community Housing and Toronto Seniors Housing Corporations - Phase Two: User Access Management and Event Logging
topics: assessment, audits, computer networks, housing, security; auditors; auditors, homes; residences
brief: This is an information item: on October 18, 2024, the Toronto Community Housing Corporation board adopted recommendations from the Auditor General's phase two cybersecurity audit of Toronto Community Housing and Toronto Seniors Housing Corporations, covering user access management and event logging. The board forwarded the report to City Council through the Audit Committee. Council is asked to authorize the public release of Confidential Attachment 1 at the Auditor General's discretion.

title: Audit of Software Acquisition and Licence Management: Managing and Optimizing Value from Software Licences
topics: audits, software licences, technology acquisition; auditors; auditors, information technology acquisitions; it acquisitions, software licenses
brief: The Auditor General audited how the City acquires and manages software: in 2023 the City spent $44 million on software acquisitions and $34 million on maintenance, about $235 million in total from 2019 to 2023, across more than 7,500 software titles. The audit assessed whether tracking and management practices deliver value from these licences. The Auditor General recommends Council ask the Chief Technology Officer to evaluate whether the cost of unused software licences identified in the report can be reduced or deferred.

title: Auditor General’s Office 2025 Work Plan and Budget Highlights
topics: audits, budgets, work plans; auditors; auditors, budgets and accounts
brief: The Auditor General presents the 2025 Work Plan, covering audit projects in progress or starting in 2025 and new projects slated for late 2025 or 2026, identified through a City-wide risk and opportunities assessment that is updated annually. The report also includes budget highlights for the Auditor General's Office, and the plan may be amended if new priorities arise. The Auditor General recommends City Council receive the report for information.

title: Investment Manager Updates

brief: This is an information item: the Director, Capital Markets updates the Toronto Investment Board on activities involving investment managers and related parties, including changes to mandates, contracts and funding. The update notes that Fiera Capital has closed the Fiera Global Equity Common Contractual Fund and all city fund assets were transferred in-kind to a new Canadian pooled fund, the Fiera Global Equity Focused Pooled Fund, with the trade settled September 11, 2024. The Board is asked to keep Confidential Attachment 1 confidential.

title: Presentations from Investment Managers
topics: investment;
brief: Presentations will be given to the Toronto Investment Board by two investment managers: Pier 21 / C WorldWide on global equity, and Legal & General Investment Management on global equity. No decision is attached.

title: Environmental, Social, and Governance Reporting Update
brief: This is an information item: the Director, Capital Markets reports that the Board engaged MSCI Inc. and MSCI ESG Research as its ESG ratings service provider, in response to Council's request to monitor and report on external investment firms' performance on ESG factors under the Investment Policy. The agreement includes MSCI's Carbon Portfolio Analytics reporting to help investors understand climate data and analytics. The Board is asked to direct that four confidential attachments remain confidential.

title: Extending the Mandate of Chief Information Security Office - Cyber Risk
brief: This is an information item: Maneesh Agnihotri, Chief Information Security Officer, and Andree Noel, Deputy Chief Information Security Officer, will give a presentation to the Toronto Investment Board on extending the mandate of the Chief Information Security Office for cyber risk. No decision is attached.

title: Personal Trading Policy - Toronto Investment Board
brief: This is a procedural item: members of the Toronto Investment Board are required to sign an annual compliance statement on the Board's personal trading policy and return it to the Clerk for filing with the City Clerk's Office. No decision is attached.

title: Hotel X Phase 2 Development - Minutes of Settlement Extension with IATSE Local 58
topics: employment & labour (sc), labour relations, unions; collective bargaining; employee relations; labor relations; union-management relations, labour unions; trade unions
brief: The Chief Executive Officer asks the Board to approve a multi-party Minutes of Settlement Extension Agreement covering the completion and operation of the E-Sport Performance Venue, following negotiations between Princes Gate Hotel Limited Partnership (Hotel X), Overactive Media Corporation and IATSE Local 58. The Board is asked to authorize the public release of some confidential information from Confidential Attachment 1 and to approve the agreement, with remaining attachments staying confidential.

title: Exhibition Place Hotel X Development - Phase 2 Lands
topics: development; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: This is an information item: the report describes the Hotel X development at Exhibition Place, where the City and the Board leased lands to Princes Gate Hotel Limited Partnership under a 49-year Phase 1 lease, with two 25-year renewal options. The first phase of Hotel X opened March 20, 2018, and the tenant has an option to lease additional lands to the west for a second hotel tower. The Chief Executive Officer recommends the Board receive the report for information.

title: Exhibition Place Financial Report - 3rd Quarter September 30, 2024
topics: financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Executive Officer provides the detailed financial report for the third quarter ending September 30, 2024, with appendices summarizing all Exhibition Place program areas. The Board is asked to receive the report for information and to direct that Confidential Attachment 1 remain confidential, as it contains financial information belonging to the Board with monetary value.

title: Employee and Corporate Policies 2024 Review and Update
topics: employees, human resources, labour force; labor force; workforce, staff
brief: This is a procedural item: the Chief Executive Officer asks the Board to approve the new or revised Exhibition Place employee and corporate policies and guidelines set out in Appendices A and B. The item recommends approval of the 2024 policy review and update.

title: Exhibition Place Management Report - 3rd Quarter September 30, 2024
topics: management (activity);
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Executive Officer provides the third quarter management report for the period ending September 30, 2024. The Board is asked to receive the report for information.

The roadmap is being promoted on Exhibition Place's social media channels and website. The Chief Executive Officer recommends the Board receive the report for information.

title: Business Travel for UFI Executive Committee Meetings and UFI Board of Directors Meetings in 2025
topics: business travel (municipal); corporate travel
brief: The Chief Executive Officer of Exhibition Place asks the Board to authorize business travel expenses for General Manager Laura Purdy to attend UFI Executive Committee and Board of Directors meetings in 2025. UFI is the global association of the exhibition industry, and Purdy was appointed inaugural Chair of its new North American chapter in November 2023. The cost of each trip is not expected to exceed $7,000 plus HST for registration and related expenses.

title: Event Revenue and Receivables Review 2024

brief: This is an information item: the Chief Executive Officer of Exhibition Place asks the Board to receive for information the City Internal Audit review of event revenue and receivables for 2024. The review assessed whether adequate processes and controls support efficient, effective and sustainable delivery of Exhibition Place's events, conventions and tradeshow business. No decision is attached.

title: Toronto Seniors Strategy
topics: accessibility, seniors; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, elderly; geriatric; older adults; senior citizens
brief: Liv Mendelsohn recommends the Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee ask the Executive Committee to direct the Toronto Seniors' Strategy team to present at the Committee's February 28, 2025 meeting. The City is developing a third Toronto Seniors Strategy to support aging in place, particularly for seniors who are Indigenous, Black or belong to equity-deserving groups, and the recommendation says the strategy should be designed with an accessibility lens and treat people with disabilities as a specific priority group for consultations.
