title: West Toronto Railpath Extension Cost Estimate Peer Review
topics: railways, transportation; rail fares; railroads, transportation services
brief: This is an information item: staff report on the West Toronto Railpath Project, a fully off-street pedestrian and cycling pathway, in response to Council's direction to examine the capital budget and plan and to report on due diligence and an independent third-party estimate review. The existing Railpath runs 2.1 km north of Dupont Street. The General Manager, Transportation Services recommends the Executive Committee receive the report for information.

title: 2024 Review of the Vehicle-for-Hire By-Law and Industry
topics: drivers, municipal codes, vehicle emission testing; drive clean tests
brief: This report reviews Toronto's vehicle-for-hire industry, covering taxicabs, limousines and private transportation companies licensed under Municipal Code Chapter 546. The City Manager, the Executive Director of Municipal Licensing and Standards and the General Manager of Transportation Services recommend capping the number of Private Transportation Company drivers, with an exemption for zero emission and wheelchair accessible vehicles. The Executive Committee is asked to recommend that Council amend Chapter 546 to implement the cap.

title: Listening to Toronto Survey
topics: customer satisfaction surveys, customer service, non emergency municipal services; 3-1-1; 311; 311 calls; non-emergency city services
brief: This item forwards Service Excellence Committee recommendations on the Listening to Toronto survey, a public opinion poll conducted by Ipsos from August 28 to September 18, 2024. The poll gathered resident feedback on city services such as parks and social services, quality of life such as cleanliness and public safety, and priorities for the City's budget. The Committee recommends the Executive Committee ask staff to analyse and report on alignments or contrasts between 311 customer experience data and the survey results.

title: 311 Toronto - Framework for Reporting and Dashboards: Update
topics: customer service, non emergency municipal services; 3-1-1; 311; 311 calls; non-emergency city services
brief: On November 25, 2024, the Service Excellence Committee considered a report from the Executive Director, Customer Experience on work since May 2024 on a prototype ward dashboard and additional reporting features for 311 data. The Committee recommends the Executive Committee ask the Executive Director to review extending access and training on the 311 Business Intelligence Tool to the offices of the Mayor and all Councillors, and to consult those offices on potential modifications or enhancements to reporting features.

title: Guild Park and Gardens Revenue New Source
topics: funding, gardens, investment, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, financing
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie recommends that Council ask the Mayor to consider, in the 2025 budget, increasing the Parks, Forestry and Recreation capital budget so that revenues from the Guild Inn Estates sublease are reinvested in Guild Park and Gardens as a new long-term funding source. The letter describes the park as a significant cultural and historical landmark and argues that reinvesting its revenues is a sustainable way to preserve its long-term vitality. The Executive Committee is asked to consider the recommendation.

title: Consolidated Human Resources Management and Ethical Framework for Members' Staff
topics: discrimination, harassment, human resources;
brief: This is an information item: the City Clerk presents a consolidation of the Human Resource Management and Ethical Framework for members' staff, incorporating past Council decisions. The report responds to Council's direction on the Integrity Commissioner's report on workplace harassment and discrimination, which had noted that various Council decisions were not reflected in the framework. The Executive Committee is asked to receive the report for information.

title: 2023 Development Charge Deferred Revenue Activity and Balances
topics: development charges, projects, redevelopment; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer reports development charge activity for 2023 as required by the Development Charges Act, 1997. The City collected $801.3 million in development charge contributions and earned $57.7 million in interest, offset by $466.9 million in earned revenue recognized for growth-related capital spending. As a result, the deferred revenue balance increased by $391.2 million from the prior year. The Executive Committee is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Deferred Revenue Report at September 30, 2024
topics: budgets, financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements, budgets and accounts
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer reports deferred revenue balances as at September 30, 2024, and related earned revenue for the nine months then ended. Deferred revenue represents monies received from external parties that must be set aside for specific purposes under provincial legislation or third-party agreements. The Executive Committee is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Responding to the Safer Streets, Stronger Communities Act
topics: [activities in health], health, public health; health coverage
brief: On November 18, the provincial government tabled Bill 223, which includes the Community Care and Recovery Act banning supervised consumption sites within 200 metres of schools and child care centres. The bill would force the closure of at least five supervised consumption facilities in Toronto, putting lives at risk and burdening first responders. Councillor Chris Moise recommends the Board of Health direct the Medical Officer of Health, in consultation with the City Solicitor, to submit comments on Bill 223 before December 18, 2024.

title: Appointment of Medical Officer of Health
topics: appointments, boards of health, public health;
brief: The Medical Officer of Health hiring committee, working with Phelps Group, has conducted an extensive search and interview process to find Toronto's next Medical Officer of Health ahead of Dr. Eileen de Villa's departure at the end of the year. The Board of Health is asked to consider a recommendation to appoint the new Medical Officer of Health. The item summary gives no further detail, and no recommendation text is attached.

title: Update on Action Plans - KPMG Management Letter Recommendations
topics: audits, finance (sc), financial reports, management (sc); annual financial reports; financial statements, auditors; auditors
brief: This is an information item: the Director, Internal Audit reports on the status of action plans for the 55 recommendations in KPMG's December 15, 2021 Management Letter, as directed by Council and the Audit Committee. The Audit Committee is asked to receive the update for information, with no decision attached.

title: KPMG Management Letter for the City of Toronto with Management Responses for Period Ended December 31, 2023
topics: audits, financial reports, management (sc); annual financial reports; financial statements, auditors; auditors
brief: This is an information item: KPMG LLP, appointed in 2020 as the auditor licensed under the Public Accounting Act, 2004 for the City and certain local boards, submits its Management Letter with management responses for the period ended December 31, 2023. The item presents the letter for the Audit Committee's consideration, with no recommendation text included.

title: Status Update on Enterprise Risk Management
topics: application software, audits, management (sc); auditors; auditors
brief: This is an information item: the Director, Internal Audit reports on the development of the City-wide Enterprise Risk Management program, including the completion of an Enterprise Risk Management Framework. The next phases cover communication and training on the framework, then formal integration of risk management into strategic planning, decision making and reporting. The Audit Committee is asked to receive the update for information.

title: 20 Shirley Crescent - Application to Remove a Private Tree
topics: applications, tree removal; application process
brief: This is a procedural item: the owner of 20 Shirley Crescent is appealing the denial of a permit to remove a privately owned tree, a 153-centimetre silver maple cited for concerns about its health and the potential for failure and property damage. City staff found the tree healthy and maintainable, so the Tree By-laws do not support its removal. The Acting Director of Urban Forestry recommends Scarborough Community Council deny the removal permit.

The Acting Director of Urban Forestry recommends Scarborough Community Council deny the removal permit.

title: 2771 and 2773 Victoria Park Avenue - Residential Demolition Applications
topics: demolitions, residential properties; residential real estate

topics: councillors, street names; aldermen; alderwomen; city councellors; city councillors; council members; councilors; members of council, renaming; road names; street naming
brief: Councillor Jamaal Myers proposes renaming Rosebank Park, at 1051 Progress Avenue, to Cynthia Lai Park in honour of the late Councillor Cynthia Lai, who represented Ward 23 - Scarborough North. The proposal cites her legacy of service and inclusion, and comes with her family's permission and a community petition of support. The Community Council is asked to direct the City Manager to review the name "Cynthia Lai Park" and have Parks, Forestry and Recreation report back.

title: Our Plan Toronto: Recommendations on the East Harbour Employment Area Conversion Request - Final Report
topics: development, land use, official plan amendments; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: This item is the fourth in a series of final reports recommending staff positions on Employment Area conversion requests under the Municipal Comprehensive Review of the Official Plan, known as Our Plan Toronto, which Council started on August 4, 2020. It addresses the East Harbour Employment Area conversion request, and City Council referred it back to the Planning and Housing Committee on October 11 and 12, 2023. The summary of the staff report is truncated, so only the referral and the subject matter are established.

title: Developing a Missing Middle Action Plan informed by Lessons Learned from the Beaches-East York Missing Middle Pilot Project
topics: housing, meetings; homes; residences
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford recommends that the Planning and Housing Committee direct staff to report back in the second quarter of 2025 with a Missing Middle Action Plan. The plan would draw lessons from the Beaches-East York Missing Middle Pilot Project at 72 Amroth Avenue, a City-owned demonstration site approved by Council on November 13, 2024 as part of the Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods initiative. The action plan would set out timing and considerations for missing middle housing city-wide.

title: Our Plan Toronto: Draft Delineations - Protected Major Transit Station Areas and Major Transit Station Areas (9 Stations) - Proposals Report
topics: transit networks, transit stops; stops (public transportation)
brief: Staff ask the Planning and Housing Committee to authorize City Planning to use draft delineations of 7 Major Transit Station Areas and 2 Protected Major Transit Station Areas as the basis for consultation toward a final Official Plan amendment. The delineation work is part of the Growth Plan conformity and Municipal Comprehensive Review started in June 2020, which identified about 180 potential station areas; a subset was identified as protected areas where the Council-approved inclusionary zoning framework can apply. The Committee is asked to approve the draft delineations for consultation.

title: Official Plan Review - Office Replacement Policies - Status Report
topics: Official Plans, official plan amendments;
brief: This is a status report on the Office Space Needs Study, which the City launched as office vacancies rose with hybrid work after the COVID-19 pandemic. The report follows the Committee's July 11 endorsement of proposed policy directions on office replacement and requests further analysis. The Interim Chief Planner recommends the Committee ask the City Solicitor to report back on implementation through OPA 231 in the first quarter of 2025.

title: Minor Variances for Additional Height and Density on Related Zoning By-law Amendments
topics: minor variances, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, variance
brief: This is an information item: staff report back on whether the City should adopt a by-law under Section 45 of the Planning Act to limit what counts as a minor variance when applicants seek extra height and density for large multi-storey proposals that already have site-specific zoning from a private zoning by-law amendment. The report explains the Committee of Adjustment's role in reviewing minor variance applications and summarizes minor variances related to site-specific zoning permissions. The Chief Planner recommends the Planning and Housing Committee receive the report for information.

title: Housing Accelerator Fund: Expanding Permissions in Neighbourhoods for Six Units and Four Storeys - Preliminary Report
topics: [buildings by height], housing, neighbourhoods; cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods, homes; residences
brief: As part of the City's application to the federal Housing Accelerator Fund, Council directed staff to report on allowing as-of-right zoning for residential buildings with up to six units and four storeys city-wide, building on the recent multiplex permissions for up to four units. This preliminary report outlines the policy context and work so far, including the Scarborough North multiplex study. The Interim Chief Planner recommends the Committee direct staff to bring back a proposals report in the fourth quarter of 2025 to expand zoning for six-unit buildings city-wide.

title: Housing Action Plan: Mid-Rise Building Design Guidelines
topics: development, housing, mid rise buildings; developing land; development (land); land development, homes; residences
brief: Staff present updated Mid-Rise Building Design Guidelines dated November 2024, which they will apply when evaluating mid-rise development applications. The update follows the Committee's November 30, 2023 request to consolidate guidelines incorporating mid-rise monitoring results, public and stakeholder consultation, and analysis. The Chief Planner recommends the Committee ask that the guidelines be published on the City Planning website and used by staff.

title: Traffic Calming at Macpherson Avenue/Yonge Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic, traffic calming measures; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Vehicles parked and stopped at the intersection of Yonge Street and Macpherson Avenue are causing major congestion, and the community petitioned for changes to loading and parking rules. Councillor Dianne Saxe recommends that Toronto and East York Community Council amend the permit parking regulation on the even (north) side of Macpherson Avenue, changing the stretch covered between Avenue Road and Yonge Street to end 38 metres west of Yonge Street, to deter blockages while keeping loading nearby.

title: Changes to Danforth Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: boards of management, public appointments; boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: Toronto and East York Community Council has delegated authority to appoint and remove directors of BIA boards within its boundaries. The item asks the Community Council to remove directors from the Danforth Mosaic and Danforth Village BIA Boards of Management, including Enza Lorefice of the Danforth Mosaic board, and make the removed directors ineligible to serve on a board for four years, in accordance with the Public Appointments Policy and Municipal Code Chapter 19.

title: Re-Installing a Traffic Control Personnel (TCP) at the intersection of Yonge Street and Heath Street West
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: pedestrians, traffic control systems; pedestrianization, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: The Deer Park community has raised concerns about traffic at Yonge Street and Heath Street West, an intersection that caretakers and children cross to reach Deer Park Public School. A traffic control officer previously installed there drew positive feedback from school administration and parents. The councillor asks Toronto and East York Community Council to re-install traffic control personnel for one month, in addition to the existing school crossing guard, to help pedestrians cross safely.

title: Addressing Traffic Concerns on Austin Terrace
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking regulations, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: following a new sidewalk installation on Austin Terrace, Transportation Services recommends parking changes to address resulting traffic concerns. The motion asks Toronto and East York Community Council to rescind the existing parking regulations on Austin Terrace and prohibit parking at any time on the north side between points near Lyndhurst Avenue and on the south side near Lyndhurst Court. The Community Council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Traffic Calming - Barrington Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: The councillor recommends that Toronto and East York Community Council approve four speed humps on Barrington Avenue between Secord Avenue and Lumsden Avenue. Residents report that speeding has become a major concern, especially given the proximity to Secord Elementary School, and a petition in support was successful. The Community Council is also asked to direct the City Solicitor to prepare the by-law to alter the roadway.

title: Installation of Backlit Chevrons Signs in Order to Increase Safety at Woodbine Avenue and Lake Shore Boulevard East Curve
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: safety, traffic signs; public safety, traffic regulatory signs
brief: The curve where Woodbine Avenue meets Lake Shore Boulevard East has been the site of numerous accidents over the years, almost exclusively in the evening. The councillor recommends installing six backlit chevron signs on the south side of the curve on a pilot basis for up to 24 months, at an estimated cost of about $35,000, with vehicle speeds and collisions monitored before and after. Funding is included in the proposed 2025 operating budget for Transportation Services. Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to direct the installation.

title: Additional Speed Hump - Victor Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher recommends adding one more speed hump on Victor Avenue between Broadview Avenue and Howland Road. Residents noted a significant gap between the existing humps, and polling showed 69 percent support for the original installation of six speed humps in 2015. Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to authorize the installation and direct the City Solicitor to prepare the by-law.

title: Implementing Traffic Calming in Regent Park - Nicholas Avenue and Sumach Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: safety, speed humps, traffic calming; public safety, sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Staff working with community members identified Nicholas Avenue and Sumach Street in Regent Park for traffic calming to address pedestrian safety. Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to authorize speed humps on Nicholas Avenue between Shuter Street and Wyatt Avenue and on Sumach Street between Shuter Street and Dundas Street East, and to direct the City Solicitor to prepare the by-law. Further calming measures will be considered as Regent Park phases 4 and 5 move forward.

title: Commercial Loading Zone - Jordan Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, loading zones; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, ttc
brief: King Station is getting three new elevators under the TTC Easier Access Project, with construction running from January 2023 to June 2026. Sidewalk and lane closures on Melinda, Yonge and Colborne Streets have reduced the loading spaces that downtown businesses rely on. The motion asks Toronto and East York Community Council to rescind an existing parking prohibition on the east side of Jordan Street south of King Street West and designate that section as a commercial loading zone.

title: Traffic Calming Measures on Hector Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Residents on Hector Avenue report that vehicles use their residential street as a cut-through to and from Davenport Road at unsafe speeds, and the community submitted an overwhelming petition for speed humps. Councillor Josh Matlow recommends that Toronto and East York Community Council authorize two speed humps on Hector Avenue between Melita Avenue and Davenport Road and direct the City Solicitor to prepare the by-law.

title: Amending Parking Restrictions on Chiltern Hill Road
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Residents along Chiltern Hill Road between Eglinton Avenue West and Dewbourne Avenue submitted an overwhelming petition asking for more on-street parking opportunities. The councillor asks Toronto and East York Community Council to rescind the parking prohibition in effect from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday to Saturday, on the east side of Chiltern Hill Road between Dewbourne Avenue and a point 44 metres south of Eglinton Avenue West, and to amend the existing maximum parking regulation. The change is meant to let visitors and community members enjoy what the community has to offer.

title: Ward Street - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, permit parking; no parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: On Ward Street, which runs from Wallace Avenue to Lappin Avenue, alternate side parking days force residents to move their vehicles to the east side, where there are far fewer spaces. A survey by the councillor's office found most residents support removing alternate side parking and keeping parking on the east side in front of homes. Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to rescind the existing Thursday seasonal parking prohibition on the east side of Ward Street.

title: McRoberts Avenue - Road Safety Review
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: road safety, traffic calming measures; traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: A 2022 traffic safety survey found most McRoberts Avenue residents feel unsafe because of dangerous driving and speeding, with drivers using the local street to avoid traffic on St. Clair Avenue West and Caledonia Road. The councillor asks Toronto and East York Community Council to request that Transportation Services conduct a comprehensive road safety review of McRoberts Avenue between St. Clair Avenue West and Rogers Road, considering changes such as directions that reduce cut-through traffic while maintaining access.

title: Harrison Street - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, permit parking; no parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: A pick-up and drop-off zone was installed on Harrison Street for parents of children at the daycare at Harrison Street and Ossington Avenue, but the daycare has since closed and the property was listed for sale. Transportation Services found there is no longer a need for the short-term parking zone and recommends converting the spaces to permit parking for residents and visitors. Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to rescind the 15-minute maximum parking regulation on the north side of Harrison Street.

title: Installation of Speed Humps on Westport Avenue, between Old Weston Road and the public lane east of Old Weston Road and south of Davenport Road
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Residents on Westport Avenue have advocated for traffic calming for several years, reporting that drivers cut through the street and the nearby laneway at dangerous speeds to avoid Davenport Road and Old Weston Road. Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to authorize a speed hump on Westport Avenue between Old Weston Road and the public lane east of Old Weston Road south of Davenport Road, which will connect with speed bumps planned for the laneway. The Community Council is also asked to direct the City Solicitor to prepare the by-law.

title: Installation of Speed Humps on Rusholme Road, between Dundas Street West and College Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Drivers use Rusholme Road as a shortcut to avoid major intersections between Dundas Street West and College Street, leading to speeding, running stop signs, racing and aggressive driving on a street where many young children live and walk. A neighbourhood survey found strong support for speed humps. Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to authorize six speed humps on Rusholme Road between Dundas Street West and College Street and direct the City Solicitor to prepare the by-law.

title: Installation of Speed Humps on Harrison Street, between Dovercourt Road and Ossington Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Residents on Harrison Street report near accidents with speeding vehicles using their street to avoid traffic off Ossington Avenue. A poll by the councillor's office found nearly 90 percent of participating residents support speed humps. Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to authorize four speed humps on Harrison Street between Dovercourt Road and Ossington Avenue and direct the City Solicitor to prepare the by-law.

title: Installation of Speed Humps on Gladstone Avenue, between Hallam Street and Dupont Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Residents along Gladstone Avenue between Hallam Street and Dupont Street report concerns about speeding, and many children and parents use the street to walk to Dovercourt Public School, whose field sits on the west side. A survey by the councillor's office found overwhelming support for speed humps. Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to authorize five speed humps on Gladstone Avenue between Hallam Street and Dupont Street and direct the City Solicitor to prepare the by-law.

topics: parking machines, parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws, pay and display machines; pay-and-display machines

body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: road safety, traffic calming;
brief: The City committed to improvements under the Geary Avenue Mobility and Public Realm Strategy, but progress on its ten strategic directions has slowed even as the street has added small businesses, restaurants and cultural spaces drawing thousands of visitors. Residents and businesses remain concerned about pedestrian safety and intersection conditions. Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to direct Transportation Services to develop a comprehensive implementation plan for the strategy as outlined in the Geary Avenue Works Planning Study.

topics: pavement markings, signs, traffic; arrows (markings); centre lines (pavement markings); edge lines; lane lines; road markings, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, signage
brief: Residents of the Pelham Park and Carleton Village area report pedestrian and cyclist safety problems at the jogged intersection of Davenport Road and Osler Street, including illegal turns, vehicles stuck in the intersection, near collisions and rush-hour backlogs on Osler Street. The councillor asks Toronto and East York Community Council to request that Transportation Services conduct a comprehensive intersection safety review, including signage and signal timing changes.

body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: road safety, traffic calming measures; traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Alberta Avenue runs between St. Clair Avenue West to the north and Davenport Road to the south, and residents report speeding and dangerous driving on the local street that many neighbours use to walk to school or connect to transit. Residents have asked for more traffic calming, but the street's grade limits how many additional speed humps can be installed. The councillor asks Toronto and East York Community Council to request that Transportation Services conduct a comprehensive road safety review of Alberta Avenue, considering measures such as directional changes to reduce cut-through traffic and local-traffic-only signage.

brief: This is a procedural item: a resolution will be passed to confirm the amendments to By-law No. 1-2022. The source provides no further detail on the amendments or their subject.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order Number 6042899 with DTAH for Professional Landscape Architecture Services during Design and Contract Administration of the Phase 2 of Lower Don Trail Improvements for Parks, Forestry and Recreation
topics: recreation centres, services, urban design; civic improvements, rec centers; rec centres; recreation centers
brief: The General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve amending purchase order 6042899 with DTAH for Phase 2 of the Lower Don Trail improvements. The $333,455 amendment covers redesigning the sloped path foundation, a structural assessment of the sewer chamber crossing the trail, and additional contract administration. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order 6053869 with Montgomery Sisam Architects Inc., for the Long-Term Care Redevelopment Project for Seniors Services and Long-Term Care
topics: long term care homes, redevelopment, services; homes for the aged; long term care centers; long term care centres; long term care facilities; nursing facilities; nursing homes, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: The interim General Manager, Seniors Services and Long-Term Care and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve amending purchase order 6053869 with Montgomery Sisam Architects Inc. for the new long-term care home at 4610 Finch Avenue East. The $1,324,205 increase raises the total design and contract administration contract to $5,780,808 net of taxes. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Contract 47024899 with Gordon Food Services for the Supply and Delivery of Groceries for Seniors Services and Long-Term Care
topics: long term care homes, purchasing, service delivery; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, homes for the aged; long term care centers; long term care centres; long term care facilities; nursing facilities; nursing homes
brief: The interim General Manager, Seniors Services and Long-Term Care and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve amending the non-competitive grocery supply contract 47024899 with Gordon Food Services Canada Ltd. The $3,157,730 increase covers groceries, produce, frozen foods, seafood, dairy, meat, and poultry for the city's long-term care homes. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contracts 47024891 with CBV Collection Services Ltd., 47024892 with Gatestone & Co Inc., and 47024893 with Partners in Credit Inc., for the Collection Services for Provincial Offences Act Fines for Court Services
topics: courts, fines, services;
brief: The Director, Court Services and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve amending three blanket contracts - with CBV Collection Services Ltd., Gatestone and Co Inc., and Partners in Credit Inc. - for collection of defaulted Provincial Offences Act fines. The amendments address underestimated contract values for the collection agency services. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contract Number 47022502 with Redflex Traffic Systems (Canada) Limited for the Provision of Automated Speed Enforcement Cameras
topics: traffic, traffic cameras, traffic speed; compass cameras; rescu cameras; rescu equipment, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: The General Manager, Transportation Services and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve amending blanket contract 47022502 with Redflex Traffic Systems (Canada) Limited for automated speed enforcement cameras. The $11,240,779 amendment funds 75 additional speed cameras for the program, as requested by City Council. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: Introduction of By-law
topics: by-laws, draft by-laws; bylaws, draft bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the General Government Committee will introduce a confirming bill. No substantive decision is attached.

title: Status of iOS AirDrop Functionality on City Devices
topics: computer equipment, information & communication (sc), mobile application software; computer hardware; computer-related equipment, mobile app; smartphone app
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Information Security Officer and Chief Technology Officer ask the General Government Committee to receive the report on the city's decision to keep AirDrop disabled on city devices. The report was requested by the committee in September 2024. No decision beyond receiving it is attached.

title: 2023 Update on Fire and Life Safety Compliance at the City of Toronto
topics: fraud, programs, safety; public safety, waste (fraud)
brief: This is an information item: the Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management asks the General Government Committee to receive the 2023 annual update on fire and life safety compliance across city properties. The report compares 2023 compliance rates against 2018-2022 baselines, showing continued improvement since the Safety and Compliance team was established. No decision is attached.

title: Non-Union Separation Costs for 2023
topics: costs, employment & labour (sc), grade separations;
brief: This is an information item: the Chief People Officer asks the General Government Committee to receive the 2023 report on non-union employee separation costs for information. The report covers employer-initiated exits where payments exceed legislative minimums, informed by factors such as length of service and age that courts consistently consider. No decision is attached.

title: Cancellation, Reduction or Refund of Property of Taxes or Payment in Lieu of Taxes - November 20th, 2024
topics: appeals, hearings, property taxes; municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: The Executive Director, Finance Shared Services recommends that the General Government Committee approve individual tax appeal applications under the City of Toronto Act, 2006. The appeals cover properties that were destroyed by fire or demolished, became exempt from taxation, or were reclassified due to a change in use, with tax reductions listed in Appendix A. The Committee is asked to approve the applications.

title: Award of Province of Ontario's Vendor of Record Tender Number 19514 to Qualified Manufacturers, their Authorized Dealers and Upfitters, for Supply and Delivery of Various Vehicles under Category 1, 2 and 3 - General Vehicle Acquisition and Upfitting Services for Fleet Services Division
topics: city vehicles, manufacturing industry, records, vendors; city owned vehicles; city-owned vehicles; corporate fleet
brief: The General Manager, Fleet Services and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve using the Province of Ontario's Vendor of Record tender 19514 for city vehicle acquisitions and upfitting. The arrangement covers Ford, General Motors, FCA Canada, and Toyota Canada and their authorized dealers under vehicle categories 1, 2, and 3. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Duracut Machine Knife Company Limited for the Servicing of Ice Resurfacer Blades for Parks, Forestry and Recreation
topics: parks, urban forestry; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, forestry; tree health
brief: The General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve a non-competitive contract with Duracut Machine Knife Company Limited for servicing ice resurfacer blades. The $499,999 contract before taxes covers supply, pickup, delivery, and sharpening for one year from November 21, 2024 to November 20, 2025, with an option to renew for four additional years. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: Award of Doc4752600161 to Flow-Kleen Technology Ltd., for Catch Basin Inspection and Cleaning Services on Arterial, Collector and Local Roads City Wide for Toronto Water
topics: catchbasins, roads, water; catch basins; catch-basins, circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads)
brief: The General Manager, Toronto Water and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve awarding quotation Doc4752600161 to Flow-Kleen Technology Ltd. for catch basin inspection and cleaning services on arterial, collector, and local roads city-wide. The one-year, non-exclusive contract went to the lowest compliant bidder, with an option for the city to extend. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: Award of Doc4534714002 to J.C. Rock Ltd., for the Supply and Delivery of Quarried Crushed Stone Aggregates, Sand and Gravel
topics: purchasing, service delivery, water; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders
brief: The General Manager, Toronto Water and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve awarding quotation Doc4534714002 to J.C. Rock Ltd. for quarried crushed stone aggregates, sand, and gravel. The one-year, non-exclusive supply contract serves Toronto Water, Parks, Transportation Services, and Solid Waste Management; J.C. Rock was the lowest compliant bidder. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: Amendment to Various Blanket Contracts and Purchase Order for Fire and Life Safety, Inspection, Test and Maintenance Services for Fire Alarm, Sprinkler, Standpipe, Special Suppression, Fire Extinguisher, and Fire Hydrants
topics: fire alarms, fire extinguishers, fire hydrants; hydrants; water hydrants, smoke alarms; smoke detectors
brief: The Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve amending several blanket contracts and a purchase order for fire and life safety inspection, testing, and maintenance services. The vendors include Tyco Integrated Fire and Security, JD Collins Fire Protection, Onyx Fire Protection, Eurotech Safety, Greater Toronto Fire Protection, and Building Reports Canada Inc. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: Amendment to UBA Inc. Blanket Contract 47025391 for the Supply and Delivery of Sodium Hypochlorite for Toronto Water
topics: chlorination, contracts, water, water supply systems, water treatment; chlorine; liquid chlorine, water distribution systems; water pumping systems; water storage systems; water transmission systems, water filtration; water purification
brief: The General Manager, Toronto Water and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve amending blanket contract 47025391 with UBA Inc. for sodium hypochlorite supply and delivery. The $4,005,000 amendment is needed because significant rain events drove higher wastewater flows and chemical usage than planned. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order Number 6054441 with OJCR Construction Ltd., for General Sewer and Watermain Construction Related Activities for Residential Service Connections for Toronto and East York Districts
topics: sewers, underground services, watermains; mains; water mains, sewage systems; sewerage, underground service networks; underground utilities
brief: The General Manager, Toronto Water and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve amending purchase order 6054441 with OJCR Construction Ltd. for general sewer and watermain construction for residential service connections in the Toronto and East York districts (Wards 4, 9, 11 and 12). The amendment addresses an unforeseen increase in work volume under the contract. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: 40 College Street - Amendment to Purchase Order Number 6054325 with 1246175 Ontario Limited operating as Active Mechanical Services for the Replacement of Building Automation Systems
topics: buildings, services, traffic control systems; traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: The Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve amending purchase order 6054325 with Active Mechanical Services for replacing the building automation systems at 40 College Street. The $400,000 amendment revises the purchase order for work scheduled for completion at the end of July 2025. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order Number 6051765 with CS&P Architects Inc., for Design and Construction Professional Services for the new Davisville Community Aquatic Centre, a Net Zero Facility for Parks, Forestry and Recreation
topics: construction, designers (buildings), services; building, building designers; designers
brief: The General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation and the Chief Procurement Officer ask the General Government Committee to approve amending purchase order 6051765 with CS and P Architects Inc. for the new net-zero Davisville Community Aquatic Centre. The amendment adds $393,750 net of taxes ($400,680 net of HST recoveries) for design and construction professional services. The Committee is asked to grant the authority.

title: Apportionment of Property Taxes - November 20, 2024 Hearing
topics: appeals, hearings, property taxes; municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: The Executive Director, Finance Shared Services recommends that the General Government Committee approve five property tax apportionment applications under section 322 of the City of Toronto Act. The apportionments split unpaid taxes onto newly created parcels where land was severed, in the amounts listed in Appendices A and B, following the required public meeting. The Committee is asked to approve the apportionments.

title: Award of Sourcewell Solicitation Number 011723-VCE to Strongco Limited Partnership for the Supply and Delivery of Volvo L150H Articulated Loaders with Related Accessories, Attachments and Supplies for Fleet Services
topics: city vehicles, contracts; city owned vehicles; city-owned vehicles; corporate fleet
brief: This is a routine contract award: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel award Sourcewell solicitation 011723-VCE to Strongco Limited Partnership for Volvo L150H articulated loaders with accessories and attachments for Fleet Services. The city would piggyback on the Sourcewell cooperative contract with Volvo. Eighteen bids were received under the solicitation. The Panel is asked to grant the award.

title: Award of Doc4744087267 to Gannett Fleming Canada ULC for Engineering Services for the Detailed Design of the F.G. Gardiner Expressway for Engineering and Construction Services
topics: contracts, engineering, road construction, road reconstruction; road alterations; road narrowing; road widening
brief: This is a routine contract award: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel award proposal Doc4744087267 to Gannett Fleming Canada ULC for detailed design engineering of the F.G. Gardiner Expressway and the Lake Shore Boulevard East realignment from Cherry Street. Four bids were received; two did not meet the minimum technical threshold. The Panel is asked to grant the award.

title: Award of Doc4641009724 to Concept Fiatlux Inc. for the Provision of Non-Exclusive Design, integration, Supply, Delivery and Cleanup of Pyrotechnic and or Autonomous Aerial Light Show - Event Series 2 for Economic Development and Culture
topics: [activities in culture], contracts;
brief: This is a routine contract award: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel award proposal Doc4641009724 to Concept Fiatlux Inc. for design, supply, delivery, and cleanup of pyrotechnic and aerial light shows (Event Series 2) for Economic Development and Culture. Six bids were received, with scores ranging from 80.7 to 91.2. The Panel is asked to grant the award.

title: Award of Doc4619018927 to Quadra Chemicals Ltd. and SNF Canada Ltd.  for the Supply and Delivery of Water-Soluble Polyelectrolyte for Sludge Thickening and Sludge Dewatering for Toronto Water
topics: [water management equipment], contracts;
brief: This is a routine contract award: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel award quotation Doc4619018927 to Quadra Chemicals Ltd. and SNF Canada Ltd. for water-soluble polyelectrolyte used in Toronto Water's sludge thickening (Lot 1) and sludge dewatering (Lot 2), effective January 1, 2025. Quadra's bid of $2,297,883.75 won Lot 1 and SNF's bid of $2,650,500 (including contingency) won Lot 2. The Panel is asked to grant the awards.

title: Attendance and Revenue Report - October 2024
topics: boards of management, revenue generation, zoos; boards of directors; boards of governors, revenue tools
brief: This is an information item: the Director of Finance, Technology and Innovation asks the Zoo Board of Management to receive the October 2024 attendance and revenue report for information. The report covers the period ending October 31, 2024 and includes a dashboard of key 2024 metrics. No decision beyond receiving the report is attached.

title: Modifications to Exhibit Design, Welding and Paint Shops - Tender Award
topics: awards, boards of management, exhibits, zoos; boards of directors; boards of governors, exhibitions; exhibitors
brief: This is a routine contract award: the Director, Facilities and Infrastructure recommends that the Zoo Board of Management award the tender for modifications to the exhibit design, welding, and paint shops to Norfield Construction Inc. for $1,241,678.75 before HST. The CEO would be authorized to negotiate and enter into the contract. The Board is asked to approve the award.

title: Toronto Zoo Operational Update
brief: This is an information item: Toronto Zoo CEO Dolf DeJong will give a verbal operational update to the Zoo Board of Management. No decision is attached.

title: Conservation Science Presentation
topics: conservation, zoo animals, zoos; environmental conservation; environmental improvements; environmental management; environmental protection; environmental stewardship; greening
brief: This is an information item: Dr. Gabriela Mastromonaco, the Toronto Zoo's Senior Director of Wildlife and Science, will present to the Zoo Board of Management on the Zoo's role in the Canadian Conservation Strategy. No decision is attached.

title: Proposed 2025 Schedule of Board of Health Meetings
topics: boards of health, committee meetings, schedules; project schedules; scheduling; timing
brief: This is a procedural item: the Board Secretary, in consultation with the Chair, recommends that the Board of Health approve its 2025 meeting dates at 9:30 a.m., including January 20, February 10, April 1, May 5, June 2, July 7, and September 15. The schedule aligns with the 2025 Council and committee calendar approved in July 2024 and must be publicly available by the Board's first meeting of the year. The Board is asked to approve the dates.

title: Addressing Routine Immunization Rates Among School-Aged Children and Youth
topics: boards of health, catholic schools, children, immunizations, public health, public schools, youth; adolescents, child, flu shots; shots; vaccinations; vaccines
brief: The Medical Officer of Health recommends that the Board of Health urge the Ministry of Health to create a provincial immunization registry with real-time access for individuals and health care providers, including sociodemographic data. Toronto Public Health is working to keep vaccination rates high among school-aged children under the Immunization of School Pupils Act to prevent outbreaks. The Board is asked to adopt the recommendation.

title: Our Health, Our City: Annual Progress Report 2024
topics: health, mental health care and counselling, public health; health coverage, mental health agencies; mental health centres; psychiatric treatment; pyschiatry
brief: The Medical Officer of Health asks the Board of Health to receive the 2024 annual progress report on Our Health, Our City, the five-year mental health, substance use, harm reduction and treatment strategy adopted in November 2023. The recommendations ask the Board to continue recognizing the drug toxicity epidemic as a public health crisis and recommit to evidence-based actions aligned with the strategy. The Board is asked to endorse the report and its directions.

title: Appointment of Medical Officer of Health
topics: appointments, boards of health, public health;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Board of Health is bringing forward a recommendation to appoint Toronto's next Medical Officer of Health, following Dr. Eileen de Villa's departure at the end of 2024. The Medical Officer of Health Hiring Committee worked with the Phelps Group on an extensive search and interview process. A report naming the recommended appointee goes to the November Board meeting for consideration.

title: Presentation on Amendments to the Sign By-law
brief: This is an information item: the Project Director, Business Transformation and Citywide Priorities, will present to the Sign Variance Committee on amendments to the city's Sign By-law adopted by City Council in spring 2024. The presentation focuses on how the amendments affect variance requests and applications. No decision is attached.

title: 2025 Schedule of Meetings for the Sign Variance Committee
topics: by-laws, schedules, signs; bylaws, project schedules; scheduling; timing, signage
brief: This is a procedural item: the Deputy Secretary recommends that the Sign Variance Committee approve its 2025 meeting schedule. The proposed dates are Fridays: February 7, March 21, May 2, June 13, September 5, October 17, and November 28, 2025. The schedule follows City Council's approved calendar and virtual meeting availability.

title: 2026-2040 Queen Street East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments for a six-storey mixed-use mid-rise building at 2026-2040 Queen Street East, with 60 dwelling units and 1,140 square metres of non-residential space.

title: 985 Woodbine Avenue and 2078, 2086, 2100, 2102 and 2106 Danforth Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rental housing, zoning bylaws, zoning designations; permitted use requests; permitted uses, rental properties; rental units, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the zoning amendment and rental housing demolition for a mixed-use development at 985 Woodbine Avenue and 2078–2106 Danforth Avenue: a 10-storey residential building and a 35-storey tower sharing a non-residential base, next to the Woodbine TTC station.

title: 150-164 Eglinton Avenue East, and 134 and 140 Redpath Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments for two 61-storey mixed-use towers at 150-164 Eglinton Avenue East and 134 and 140 Redpath Avenue. The proposal has 1,329 residential units, 89,018.9 square metres of floor area and 2,680 square metres of publicly accessible space.

title: Main Street - Parking Amendments
topics: parking regulations, stopping prohibitions; no stopping, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: City Council is asked to amend parking on Main Street, between Danforth Avenue and Doncaster Avenue, so the 1-hour maximum extends to 6:00 p.m. instead of 4:00 p.m. The original request was adjusted for an existing stopping prohibition; residents now ask for the later time.

title: Kingston Road and Columbine Avenue - Traffic Control Signals
topics: safety, traffic control systems, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, public safety, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: City Council is asked to approve traffic control signals at Kingston Road and Columbine Avenue. Residents in the Beach Triangle neighbourhood report a lack of safe pedestrian crossings on the major arterial, and a community petition showed strong support.

title: 90-110 Eglinton Avenue East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments for two 58-storey mixed-use towers at 90-110 Eglinton Avenue East, connected at floors 5 to 10 by a bridge element. The proposal has 1,035 residential units, 93,096.6 square metres of floor area and 2,375 square metres of public space.

title: Crawford Street Community Safety Zone
topics: safety, traffic regulations; public safety
brief: City Council is asked to designate a community safety zone, in effect at all times, on both sides of Crawford Street, between Queen Street West and Dundas Street West. Residents and staff raised road safety concerns along Crawford Street, parallel to Trinity Bellwoods Park.

title: Permit Parking (Amendments and Variances) - Annette Street
topics: parking regulations, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to implement overnight on-street permit parking on Annette Street, between Jane Street and Keele Street, at the request of residents through Councillor Gord Perks' office. The proposal amends the existing 12:01–7:00 a.m. permit parking regulation. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Annette Street.

title: 555 University Avenue, 110 Elm Street and 170-180 Elizabeth Street - Official Plan Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments;
brief: Staff recommend City Council amend the Official Plan to allow an expansion of SickKids hospital at 555 University Avenue, 110 Elm Street and 170-180 Elizabeth Street, including a 32-storey institutional building with patient care space. The amendment would permit the building to be partially visible behind the protected silhouette view of City Hall.

title: Temporary Adjustments to Traffic and Parking Regulations for 2024 Distillery Winter Village (Non-delegated)
topics: parking regulations, traffic regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: City Council is asked to authorize temporary traffic and parking regulations on streets near the Distillery District for the annual Distillery Winter Village, from November 13, 2024 to January 5, 2025, to improve traffic operations and pedestrian safety. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Parliament Street, Mill Street and Front Street East.

title: Pay-and-Display Parking - Various Streets (Non-Delegated)
topics: parking, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to approve new on-street paid parking in Ward 13, identified with the Toronto Parking Authority to support local businesses and encourage turnover of on-street parking. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates on the affected streets.

title: 100-104 Beverley Street - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the zoning amendment for a 4-storey apartment building with 12 dwelling units at the rear of 100-104 Beverley Street. The existing 3-storey building with 9 units would be retained, for 21 units total on the site.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - October 2024 (Non-Delegated)
topics: accessible permit parking, persons with a disability; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled), disabled; disabled persons; handicapped persons; people with disabilities; persons with disabilities; persons with special needs; physical disabilities; physically challenged; physically disabled; physically impaired; special needs; the physically disabled
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to approve the installation of on-street accessible parking spaces for persons with disabilities at the location in the report's attachment. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates on the affected street.

title: Maintenance of Bike Lanes around Construction Projects
topics: bike lanes, safety; bicycle lanes; on street bike lanes, public safety
brief: Transportation Services reports on maintaining bike lanes around construction projects, following the council's July 10, 2024 direction to implement a protocol keeping bike lanes clear and safe from debris. City Council is asked to receive the report.

title: Construction Staging Area - 7 Hart House Circle
topics: construction, road closures, sidewalks; building, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Pomerleau Inc. is renovating the University of Toronto's Hart House academic building at 7 Hart House Circle, and City Council is asked to authorize closing the southbound curb lane, sidewalk and cycle track on the west side of Queens Park Crescent West. City Council approval is required because Queens Park Crescent West is a major arterial.

title: 3524 Dundas Street West - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: construction, road closures; building, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Maple Reinders Constructors Ltd. is building a six-storey self-storage building at 3524 Dundas Street West, and City Council is asked to extend the closure of the north sidewalk and westbound curb lane on Dundas Street West for construction staging. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Dundas Street West.

title: 40-44 Mitchell Avenue - Demolition of Designated Heritage Buildings under Section 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: demolitions, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend City Council refuse the application to demolish the designated heritage cottages at 40-44 Mitchell Avenue under Section 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The pair of single-storey semi-detached workers' cottages are rare, early surviving examples of the type in Toronto.

title: 148-158 Avenue Road and 220-234 Davenport Road - Community Benefits Charge In-kind Contribution Value Report
topics: community benefits;
brief: This is an information item: the community benefits charge in-kind contribution report for 148-158 Avenue Road and 220-234 Davenport Road. Council approved a 35-storey, 330-unit mixed-use building in July 2023, including conveyance of 207 and 209 Avenue Road as off-site parkland expanding Ramsden Park.

title: 2461-2475 Dundas Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council refuse the zoning amendment for a 29-storey mixed-use building with 288 residential units at 2461-2475 Dundas Street West. The proposal would demolish the existing buildings, including nine rental units proposed for replacement, and a rental housing demolition application is under review.

title: 2915 St. Clair Avenue East - Zoning Amendment   Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the zoning amendment to allow additions to the existing legal non-conforming vehicle service shop at 2915 St. Clair Avenue East. The proposal adds a canopy over the gas pumps, an expanded retail store and a take-out eating establishment.

title: 3051 to 3079 Pharmacy Avenue and 10 to 30 Calamint Lane - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: part lot control;
brief: Staff recommend City Council enact a Part Lot Control exemption by-law for 3051–3079 Pharmacy Avenue and 10–30 Calamint Lane, to divide the property into stratified parcels for residential and commercial units. The exemption would create 85 Parcels of Tied Land under the site's zoning and site plan approval.

title: 2740 Lawrence Avenue East- Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: part lot control, planning approvals; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals
brief: Staff recommend City Council enact a Part Lot Control exemption by-law for part of 2740 Lawrence Avenue East, to create and convey 65 three-storey townhouse units with maintenance easements. The subdivision plan with a public street was registered in April 2023.

title: 673 Warden Avenue - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300) - Decision Report - Approval
topics: noise control, planning approvals; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals, noise barriers; sound barriers
brief: Staff recommend City Council designate 673 Warden Avenue as a Class 4 Noise Area under the provincial NPC-300 guidelines. Council adopted a settlement in May 2024 for a 27-storey mixed-use building with a 6-storey podium on the site.

title: Kingston Road and Audrey Avenue - Left Turn Prohibition
topics: traffic control systems, traffic direction; one way operations; one way streets; one way traffic; two way operations; two way streets; two way traffic, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Councillor Parthi Kandavel recommends City Council prohibit eastbound left turns from 4:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday to Friday (bicycles excepted), at Kingston Road and Audrey Avenue. A petition showed 68 percent of residents support the restriction to address afternoon cut-through traffic.

title: Village Green Square and Kennedy Road - Traffic Signal Concerns
topics: pedestrian crossovers, traffic signals; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations
brief: Councillor Nick Mantas recommends City Council prohibit pedestrian crossings on Kennedy Road between Village Green Square and a point 30.5 metres south. Community members report the traffic signals at Village Green Square and Kennedy Road cause congestion and confusion; staff would direct pedestrians to the north side of the intersection.

title: 1925 Victoria Park Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments for a 12-storey mixed-use building at 1925 Victoria Park Avenue. The building is organized around a central courtyard, with the 12-storey massing fronting Victoria Park Avenue and lower heights along Greylawn Crescent, Lynvalley Crescent and the east side, with non-residential uses at grade.

title: Morningside Avenue at Finch Avenue East/Staines Road - U-Turn Prohibition
topics: traffic regulations, turn prohibitions (traffic);
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council prohibit westbound U-turns at all times on Morningside Avenue at Finch Avenue East/Staines Road, to address traffic safety concerns in the area. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Morningside Avenue.

title: Meadowvale Road and Rotary Drive - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic, traffic control systems; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council NOT install traffic control signals at the intersection of Meadowvale Road and Rotary Drive, because the warrant criteria were not met. City Council approval is required since the TTC operates transit service on Meadowvale Road.

title: 1151 Markham Road - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: redevelopment, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the zoning amendment for a 44-storey mixed-use building at 1151 Markham Road, with 455 residential units, ground-floor retail and a 266-square-metre privately owned public space. The existing structures would be demolished.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council reviews the Order Paper, the list of business before the meeting.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions and announcements are made at the City Council meeting.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council may file petitions.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council declare interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from the Mayor and City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: the Mayor and committee chairs introduce their committee reports and new business to City Council, including reports from the Executive Committee, Audit Committee, Economic and Community Development Committee, and General Government Committee.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council confirms the minutes of the October 9 and 10, 2024 regular meeting.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Council meeting opens with O Canada and a moment of silence.

title: Tenancy Update: Beech Hall Housing Co-operative and Alexandra Park Housing Co-operative
topics: co-operative housing, tenants; co-op housing; coop housing; cooperative housing, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize ground lease actions for the Beech Hall and Alexandra Park housing co-operatives. Council's June 2024 Community Housing Sector Modernization strategy approved a policy framework for ground leases with community housing providers, who operate a vital part of Toronto's affordable housing stock.

title: Authority to Enter into Municipal Housing Facility Agreements under the Community Housing Partnership Renewal Program
topics: housing providers; community housing corporations
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize the Executive Director, Housing Secretariat, to negotiate and enter into municipal housing facility agreements under the Community Housing Partnership Renewal Program. The program, approved in 2019, gives former federal non-profit housing providers property tax exemptions in exchange for keeping rental housing affordable.

title: Implementing a Rental Renovation Licence By-law to Address Renovictions
topics: tenancies legislation, tenants; renters; tenancy agreements, tenancy legislation
brief: Staff recommend City Council establish a new rental renovation licence by-law to address renovictions, responding to Council's June 2024 directive for a Hamilton-style by-law. A renoviction is when a landlord illegitimately evicts a tenant by claiming the unit must be vacated for renovations.

title: Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods - Beaches-East York Pilot Project - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendments - Decision Report - Approval
topics: [housing by physical form], neighbourhoods (planning), pilot projects;
brief: Staff recommend City Council amend the Official Plan and zoning by-law for the Beaches-East York missing middle pilot project at 72 Amroth Avenue. The pilot, part of the Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods initiative, would build a demonstration project on city-owned land in Ward 19.

title: Low-Rise Residential Lands in the Toronto and East York District of the City of Toronto, to Zoning By-law 569-2013
topics: residential properties, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend City Council amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 to incorporate low-rise residential lands in the Toronto and East York District into the city-wide zoning by-law. The standards would be consistent with the applicable former municipal by-laws and recent city-wide zoning changes.

title: Building More Missing Middle - Addressing Gaps in Multiplex Permissions
topics: housing, zoning; homes; residences
brief: Staff recommend City Council ask the Chief Planner to clarify multiplex permissions in semi-detached buildings as part of the Multiplex Monitoring Program and report back. Council legalized multiplexes city-wide in May 2023, and gaps remain in the permissions for semi-detached homes.

title: City Comments on Proposed amendment to Ontario Regulation 299/19 ADDITIONAL RESIDENTIAL UNITS, made under the Planning Act
topics: planning, zoning;
brief: The Chief Planner submitted comments to the Province on the proposed amendment to Ontario Regulation 299/19 on additional residential units, with comments due October 23, 2024. Staff recommend City Council receive the report on the city's comments.

title: 630 Spadina Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation;
brief: Staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate 630 Spadina Avenue (Knox Presbyterian Church) under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The property sits on the west side of Spadina Avenue, about 30 metres south of Harbord Street.

title: 28 Halton Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, planning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate the property at 28 Halton Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The property sits on the north side of Halton Street at Givins Street, southeast of Ossington Avenue and Dundas Street West.

title: Housing Action Plan: As-of-Right Zoning for Mid-rise Buildings on Avenues and Updated Rear Transition Performance Standards - Final Report
topics: mid rise buildings, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve as-of-right zoning for mid-rise buildings on Avenues, one of 54 Housing Action Plan initiatives to enable more housing along major streets. The final report also updates rear transition performance standards for the zoning by-law.

title: 99 and 109 Cartwright Avenue and 130 Bentworth Avenue - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: parking spaces, redevelopment, zoning; parking spots, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Staff recommend City Council amend the former North York zoning by-law for 99 and 109 Cartwright Avenue and 130 Bentworth Avenue to permit a two-storey, 15-metre addition to Sterling Hall School, with indoor classrooms and a rooftop terrace. The addition totals 2,440.63 square metres with 106 vehicle spaces.

title: 444 - 466 Eglinton Avenue West  - Official Plan and Zoning Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: buildings, parking spaces, zoning; parking spots
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize the City Solicitor and staff to appear before the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the 19-storey residential building proposed at 444–466 Eglinton Avenue West. The application, submitted March 2023, proposes 15,063 square metres with retail at grade.

title: 3140, 3170, and 3180 Dufferin Street, and 60 and 68 Apex Road - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning Amendment, Subdivision, and Site Plan Applications - Appeal Report
topics: multi-residential properties, official plan amendments, subdivision (land); subdivision of land
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing in opposition to the Dufferin Plaza proposals at 3140 and 3170 Dufferin Street and 60 and 68 Apex Road. The applications propose a 9-storey residential building and an 11-storey mixed-use building with 606 units total.

title: 150 - 160 Cactus Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, development, rental housing; developing land; development (land); land development, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the rental housing demolition application for 150–160 Cactus Avenue, demolishing 60 townhouse rental units. The units would be replaced in two blocks of back-to-back stacked townhouses, with a tenant relocation plan giving existing tenants the right to return at similar rents plus financial compensation.

title: Bayview Avenue - On-Street Pay-and-Display Parking
topics: parking, parking receipts, parking spaces; parking spots
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to approve new on-street paid parking in Ward 15, identified with the Toronto Parking Authority to support local businesses and encourage parking turnover. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Bayview Avenue.

title: Leslie Street and the Wilket Creek Trail - Pedestrian Refuge Island
topics: pedestrian islands, pedestrians, transportation; pedestrian refuge islands, pedestrianization, transportation services
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council NOT install a pedestrian refuge island on Leslie Street at the northerly intersection with the Wilket Creek Trail, because the technical criteria were not met. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Leslie Street.

title: 4696 Yonge Street - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: construction, development, metered parking spaces; building, developing land; development (land); land development, metered street parking; parking stalls
brief: Staff recommend City Council refuse the Official Plan and zoning amendments for a 40-storey mixed-use building with 536 units at 4696 Yonge Street. The proposal is not consistent with the Provincial Policy Statement.

title: 1800 Sheppard Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: buildings, official plan amendments, redevelopment; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Staff recommend City Council amend the Official Plan for the multi-phase redevelopment of the 18.8-hectare site at 1800 Sheppard Avenue East: 14 new buildings of 24 to 52 storeys, about 6,200 residential units, 9,500 square metres of parkland, a multi-use path, and new public streets.

title: 230 and 240 The Donway West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, official plan amendments, zoning; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments for a 6-storey apartment building with a ground-floor place of worship at 230 and 240 The Donway West. The 21-metre building would have 308 residential units and a 734-square-metre place of worship, replacing the existing worship buildings.

title: 7 - 11 Rochefort Drive - Zoning By-law Amendment and Plan of Subdivision Applications - Appeal
topics: buildings, rezoning, subdivision (wards); re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, voting subdivisions
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the applications for 7–11 Rochefort Drive.
