The proposal includes three towers of 30, 41 and 46 storeys with 1,322 units, demolishing two buildings with 128 rental units; the applicant appealed in June 2024.

title: 10 Elmwood Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, accessible permit parking, zoning designations; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled), permitted use requests; permitted uses
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments to allow a single-storey restaurant with an outdoor patio at 10 Elmwood Avenue, replacing a surface parking lot. The proposal has a gross floor area of 197.86 square metres, a height of 8.61 metres, and no parking or loading spaces.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.NY12.8 - 680 and 688 Sheppard Avenue East - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends that City Council re-open and amend its April 17, 2024 approval of the rental housing demolition application for 680 and 688 Sheppard Avenue East. The site holds 47 rental units approved for demolition, and the amendment would delete the part authorizing preliminary approval of the demolition permits. Council is asked to amend the earlier decision.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.IE14.6 - New Golden Mile Environmental Assessment - Interim Report  - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
brief: Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, recommends that City Council re-open its June 2024 decision on the ReNew Golden Mile environmental assessment and push the staff reporting deadline from December 17, 2024 to February 5, 2025. The report covers phases 3 and 4 of the municipal class environmental assessment and any required planning amendments. Council is asked to amend the earlier decision.

title: Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) Financing Tools - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends that City Council ask the Executive Director, Environment and Climate, to consider Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy as a voluntary financing tool. The tool would help commercial building owners fund energy and water retrofits, supporting housing supply, construction, economic development, and Toronto's climate targets. Council is asked to direct staff to explore it.

title: Proclaiming December as Christian Heritage Month - by Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, recommends that City Council proclaim December as Christian Heritage Month. The motion notes that Christianity is the most followed religion in Canada, that the Charter of Rights and Freedoms mentions God in its first sentence, and that December marks Christmas celebrations. Council is asked to adopt the proclamation.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for a Pedestrian Refuge Island on Leslie Street at Wilket Creek - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends City Council increase the Transportation Services capital budget by $31,500, fully funded by Section 37 funds, for a pedestrian refuge island on Leslie Street at the Wilket Creek Trail. Leslie Street is a four-lane arterial carrying about 25,000 vehicles daily.

title: Toronto Community Crisis Service Vehicle Exemption along King Street Priority Corridor - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, recommends City Council allow Toronto Community Crisis Service vehicles to proceed through intersections along the King Street priority corridor, like streetcars, buses, Wheel-Trans and bicycles. The crisis service operates 24 hours a day.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.CC20.26 - 10 Huntley Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends that City Council re-open and amend its July 2024 decision on item 2024.CC20.26, which accepted a without-prejudice offer to settle the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal over 10 Huntley Street in Ward 13. Parts 3(b)(iv) and 4 misstate the July 9, 2024 settlement offer on the timing of on-site parkland dedication. Council is asked to correct the decision.

title: Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario Liquor Licence Application - 142 George Street File 2847929 - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends that City Council direct the City Clerk to tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that the liquor licence application for 142 George Street (operating as 6ix Iron Indoor Golf) is not in the public interest. The 28-person-capacity premises previously operated as an unlicensed nightclub, drew resident complaints about noise and safety, and the operator was convicted on bylaw charges. Council is asked to oppose the licence.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.TE13.42 - Keeping Dundas Street Streetcar Moving Through Chinatown: Temporary Adjustments to Parking Regulations on Dundas Street West - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, recommends that City Council re-open and amend its earlier decision on keeping the Dundas Street streetcar moving through Chinatown. The amendment would extend the temporary parking regulation adjustments on Dundas Street West from January 1, 2025 to March 31, 2025. Council is asked to approve the extension.

title: Appointment of Fire Chief and General Manager, Toronto Fire Services - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: This is a procedural item: Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends that City Council direct the City Manager to run reference checks and contract negotiations with the confidential candidate to become the next Fire Chief and General Manager of Toronto Fire Services. Previous chief Matthew Pegg left October 4, 2024, and Larry Cocco serves as interim. The appointment depends on the checks and negotiations.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.MM22.36 - Alternative Space for Recreation Programming at Carmine Stefano Community Centre - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, recommends that City Council amend its 2024.MM22.36 decision to authorize a lease extension for the Carmine Stefano Community Centre building, soccer fields, and surrounding green space. The city's lease expires November 30, 2024, so the amendment is urgent to keep recreation programming running. Council is asked to authorize the extension agreement.

title: 80 Guestville Avenue - Revoking a Building Permit - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends that City Council ask the Chief Building Official to investigate the building permits at 80 Guestville Avenue and consider revoking them. The landlord issued 26 N13 eviction notices claiming renovations were needed, but no work has started, suggesting a renoviction tactic to raise rents. Council is asked to authorize the investigation and possible permit revocation.

title: Partial Reimbursement of Permit Fees for Toronto Music, Arts and Nature Alliance - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends that City Council direct parks staff to refund 25 percent of permit fees - $13,319.51 before HST - to the Toronto Music, Arts and Nature Alliance on a one-time basis. The not-for-profit ran its Promise Cherry Beach arts and music series on eleven ticketed dates in summer 2024, a series now in its 24th year. Council is asked to approve the refund.

title: Year-Round Non-Motorized Watercraft Storage Pilot - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends that City Council direct parks staff to negotiate amending agreements with existing non-motorized watercraft licence holders, including Toronto SUP & Kayak Inc., to allow year-round storage. Current licences for rentals, lessons, and public storage run seasonally from June to September on four-year terms with market licence fees. Council is asked to authorize the negotiation.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Glen Road Pedestrian Bridge and Tunnel Project - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, recommends City Council increase the Transportation Services capital budget for the Glen Road Pedestrian Bridge and Tunnel Project, which replaces the bridge across the Rosedale Valley Ravine and the tunnel under Bloor Street East connecting Rosedale and North St. James Town. The project would be funded by Section 37 funds.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Items 2024.IE10.1 and 2024.IE16.3 - Administrative Penalty System for Red Light Camera and Automated Speed Enforcement Violations - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends that City Council amend its earlier decisions to delay the new Administrative Monetary Penalty System for red light camera and automated speed enforcement tickets from December 9, 2024 to January 20, 2025. Court Services asked for six more weeks to finish a privacy impact assessment, cybersecurity checks, testing, and staff training. Council is asked to approve the new date.

title: Showing Toronto’s Pride - 50 Years with the City of Toronto’s Flag - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: congratulatory messages, municipal flags; city flag, letter of greeting; proclamations; scrolls
brief: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, recommends that City Council ask the Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management, to report by the third quarter of 2025 on opportunities to fly or display the City of Toronto flag at more city facilities. Toronto recently marked 50 years since the flag - designed by George Brown College student Rene DeSantis - was adopted on November 7, 1974. Council is asked to order the report.

title: Authority to Negotiate and Enter Operation and Maintenance Agreement with Toronto and Region Conservation Authority to Realize Meadoway, by Deputy Mayor McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: conservation, maintenance; environmental conservation; environmental improvements; environmental management; environmental protection; environmental stewardship; greening
brief: Deputy Mayor McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, recommends that City Council direct parks staff to negotiate and execute an operation and maintenance agreement with the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority for the Meadoway. The 16-kilometre hydro-corridor park in Scarborough links downtown Toronto to Rouge National Urban Park and will become one of Canada's largest linear urban parks. Council is asked to authorize the agreement.

title: Toronto Transit Commission Environmental Report for the Conversion of the Scarborough Rapid Transit Right-of-Way, Busway Project - Tara Avenue and Mooregate Avenue Bus Stop - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: bus stops, environmental impacts, light rail transit, public transit; environmental effects; environmental footprint; environmental impact, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, lrt
brief: Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas, recommends that City Council ask the Toronto Transit Commission to remove the proposed bus stop at Tara Avenue and Mooregate Avenue from the Line 3 busway conversion project. The stop was included in the TTC's environmental project report, whose public comment period closed November 4, 2024, and the community opposed its placement. Any cost savings would go to other TTC capital priority projects.

title: Downsview Community Recreation Centre: Intent to Enter into Lease Agreement - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
topics: news releases, recreation centres; rec centers; rec centres; recreation centers
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, recommends that City Council authorize negotiation of a nominal land lease among the city, Parc Downsview Park, and Northcrest Developments for a new Downsview Community Recreation Centre. The centre, identified in the city's facilities master plan and Downsview Secondary Plan, would sit within Downsview Park on Parc Downsview Park lands. Council is asked to authorize the lease negotiation.

title: Exemption to the Policy for Policy for Accepting Potentially Contaminated Lands to be Conveyed to the City as a Condition of a Development Application Approval - Fedex Block - by Deputy Mayor Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: Deputy Mayor Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, recommends that City Council exempt city-bound land on the Fedex Block from the policy on accepting potentially contaminated lands. The parcels (Parts 3, 4, and 5 on Reference Plan 66R-32887) would be conveyed to the city for a new east-west road in the block bounded by Lake Shore Boulevard East, Queens Quay East, Richardson Street, and Lower Sherbourne Street. Council is asked to grant the exemption.

title: Re-Opening and Amending the decision on Item 2024.NY17.11 - 7 St. Dennis Drive and 10 Grenoble Drive - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends that City Council re-open and correct its October 2024 decision on item 2024.NY17.11, covering 7 St. Dennis Drive and 10 Grenoble Drive. The correction deletes the part attributing a parkland over-dedication value of 4 percent of the land value, so the decision matches the revised staff recommendations. Council is asked to amend the earlier decision.

title: Parkland obligations at 29, 35, 41 and 75 Basin Street - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Malik
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Malik, recommends that City Council allow the on-site parkland conveyance for the Basin Media Hub project (29, 35, 41 and 75 Basin Street) to proceed despite the usual timing rules. The $300 million film, television, and digital media hub spans 52,649 square metres, with 576 square metres of on-site parkland shown on the site drawings. Council is asked to approve the timing exception.

title: Implementation of Permit Parking on John Perkins Bull Drive, William Duncan Road, Franco Basille Grove and Maria Iacampo Gardens, Permit Area 18A - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends that City Council exempt four streets - John Perkins Bull Drive, William Duncan Road, Franco Basille Grove, and Maria Iacampo Gardens - from the usual requirements for implementing permit parking within Permit Area 18A. The streets in the Stanley Green neighbourhood were not yet fully developed when the permit area was created in 2019. Council is asked to approve the exemption.

title: Renewal of Below Market Rent Lease Agreement with Toronto Azzurri Soccer Club - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
topics: soccer, sports clubs; badminton clubs; baseball associations; baseball leagues; bowling clubs; cross-country ski clubs; curling clubs; gymnastic clubs; hockey associations; hockey leagues; karate clubs; lacrosse clubs; lawn bowling clubs; ride clubs; rifle clubs; slo-pitch leagues; soccer clubs; soccer leagues; softball associations; softball leagues; swim clubs; tennis clubs; volleyball clubs
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, recommends that City Council authorize negotiation of a 10-year nominal lease renewal with the Toronto Azzurri Soccer Club for the city-owned property at 4995 Keele Street. The not-for-profit club holds a 20-year below-market lease since January 1, 2006, built a field house on site, and runs recreational, competitive, and other soccer programming. Council is asked to authorize the renewal.

title: 75 Glendora Avenue - Request for the City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body in support of the Committee of Adjustment's refusals at 75 Glendora Avenue. The applications seek to sever the property into two lots and build two new homes.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.PH13.6 - Strategic Opportunity at 267 and 275 Merton Street - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, recommends that City Council re-open its 2024 decision on item 2024.PH13.6, which authorized a municipal housing facility agreement for affordable housing at 267 and 275 Merton Street. The amendment would add a reference to a revised Confidential Attachment 1 with updated key terms of the contribution agreement. Council is asked to amend the earlier decision.

title: Protecting Tenants from Price-Fixing on Rental Apartments - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends that City Council ask the City Manager to report to the Planning and Housing Committee by the second quarter of 2025 on software that landlords and rental managers may use to fix rental prices, and on possible policy responses. The motion cites vacancy decontrol, the province's removal of rent control on post-2018 buildings, and double-digit rent increases. Council is asked to order the report.

title: Authorization of a Private Family Mausoleum within the Mount Pleasant Cemetery at 375 Mount Pleasant Road - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends that City Council find that a private family mausoleum at Mount Pleasant Cemetery (375 Mount Pleasant Road, Plot AA) is in the public interest. The Mount Pleasant Group of Cemeteries proposes building it on an existing interment right under the provincial Funeral, Burial and Cremation Services Act. Council is asked to make the public-interest finding.

title: 171 Pendrith Street - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councilor Parthi Kandavel
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor to appeal the Committee of Adjustment's October 2, 2024 approval of minor variance application A0475/23TEY at 171 Pendrith Street. The City Solicitor would attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the proposed development, retain outside consultants if needed, and negotiate a settlement. Council is asked to authorize the appeal.

title: Exploring Vacant City of Toronto/Toronto Parking Authority Property at 1220 Wilson Avenue as Potential Park - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside, recommends that City Council direct parks staff to work with the Toronto Parking Authority on assessing a potential park at 1220 Wilson Avenue and report back in the first quarter of 2025. The vacant parking authority land sits across from Humber River Hospital and could serve hospital staff and patients, nearby students, and the neighbourhood. Council is asked to approve the assessment.

title: Provincial Overreach and Toronto’s Infrastructure - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, recommends that City Council direct the City Manager to write to the Premier of Ontario and all Ontario municipalities protesting the overreach in Bill 212. The letter would ask the province to respect municipalities' jurisdiction over their own infrastructure and to withdraw the overreach. Council is asked to approve sending the protest letters.

title: Providing Safety and Convenience for Midtown Residents: Moving Forward with a Pedestrian Scramble at Yonge and Eglinton - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends that City Council ask the General Manager, Transportation Services, to report by the second quarter of 2025 on the feasibility of a pedestrian scramble at Yonge and Eglinton. A city count on May 24 found 40,372 pedestrians crossing in one day, the highest of any Toronto intersection from 2020 to 2024, with crowding that forces long waits. Council is asked to order the report, following resolution of Eglinton Crosstown matters.

title: 16 Martindale Road - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: appeals;
brief: Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe, recommends that City Council authorize the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to uphold the Committee of Adjustment's September 18, 2024 refusal of application A0174/22SC at 16 Martindale Road. The refused application sought six variances to demolish the existing home and build a new two-storey detached dwelling. Council is asked to authorize defending the refusal.

title: Managing Sustainable Growth in the School Crossing Guard Program - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
brief: Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends that City Council direct Transportation Services to review alternative delivery models for the School Crossing Guard Program. Options could include partnerships, volunteer-supported or technology-assisted models, since costs have grown since the city took over the program from Toronto Police in 2017. Council is asked to order the review.

title: Analyzing the Compensatory Aspects of a Councillor's Office - Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends that City Council ask the City Manager and Chief People Officer to report to the December 17-19, 2024 Council meeting with an updated comparison of councillor compensation and recommendations to adjust it. The motion cites the province's 2018 cut of Council from 44 to 25 seats and the resulting workload change. Council is asked to order the report.

title: Declaring Toronto a Paid-Plasma-Free Zone - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: health; health coverage
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council declare Toronto a paid-plasma-free zone, opposing private for-profit blood collection companies. The motion cites Canada's tainted blood crisis, which claimed about 8,000 lives, and the Krever Commission's call for a fully voluntary donation system.

title: Community Sport and Recreation Investment Fund Application: Stream 1 - Repair and Rehabilitation for the Jack Goodlad Park Basketball Court Rehabilitation Project
topics: basketball, funding, improvement; enhancement; rehabilitation (property), financing
brief: Councillor Michael Thompson recommends City Council endorse the city's application under the Province's Community Sport and Recreation Investment Fund, Stream 1 (Repair and Rehabilitation), for the Jack Goodlad Park basketball court rehabilitation. Each municipality may advance one project per stream under the cost-shared program.

title: Enhanced Nighttime Security at Green P Parking Facilities
topics: carparks, parking, security; car parks; car-parks; city parking lots; municipal parking lots; parking lots; public parking
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, as the city's Nighttime Economy Champion, recommends City Council ask the Toronto Parking Authority board to review a universal security protocol for its garages and parking lots and report back. Businesses have asked for stronger nighttime security at Green P facilities.

title: Parkside Drive Study Final Report
topics: capital budgets, infrastructure, road safety;
brief: Staff recommend City Council endorse, in principle, the road safety project on Parkside Drive, the eastern boundary of High Park. The study, directed by Council in November 2021, explored design changes to improve safety and mobility for people walking, cycling and other vulnerable road users.

title: Temporary Street Closure for Eastbound F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Northbound Don Valley Parkway - 2025 Toronto Triathlon Festival
topics: highways, races, road closures; freeways; motorways; parkways, marathons; runs; walkathons, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize closing the eastbound lanes of the F.G. Gardiner Expressway, from the Humber River to the Don Valley Parkway, and the northbound lanes of the Don Valley Parkway for the 2025 Toronto Triathlon Festival. The proposed 2025 route is the same as 2024.

title: Meter Transmission Units Emergency and Emergency Non-Competitive Contract with Aclara Technologies LLC to Obtain Supply of Replacement Water Meter Transmission Units
topics: purchasing, water, water meters; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, remote water meters
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize Toronto Water to negotiate an emergency non-competitive contract with Aclara Technologies LLC for replacement water meter transmission units. Over 150,000 of the city's 470,000 units are failing prematurely, threatening accurate water billing and customer service.

title: Award of Collaborative Procurement Contract from Ontario Education Collaborative Marketplace Master Agreement OECM-2023-441-11 to Outdoor Outfits Ltd., for Toronto Paramedic Services via City Stores
topics: agreements, contracts, education (sc), paramedics, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize Toronto Paramedic Services to enter into an agreement with Outdoor Outfits Ltd. for apparel and related products through the Ontario Education Collaborative Marketplace, from the award date to May 5, 2030, in the amount of $3,385,353.

title: Non-Competitive Contracts with Intergraph Canada Ltd., and Quatro Group Software Systems Inc., for the Provision of Proprietary Fire Services Information and Technology Systems for Toronto Fire Services
topics: contracts, fire and rescue services, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, fire fighting; fire services; fire suppression; firefighting; rescue; rescue operations; search and rescue
brief: Staff recommend City Council enter into non-competitive contracts with Intergraph Canada Ltd. for computer-aided dispatch — the core of Toronto Fire Services' emergency response — at $508,800 over five years, plus a contract with Quatro Group Software Systems Inc. for fire services information technology systems.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Rocket Software for Proprietary Court Management Software Licences, Professional Services and Related Maintenance
topics: application software, contracts, licences, software, software licences, system software; computer programs, licenses; licensing, software licenses
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize a non-competitive contract with Rocket Software Inc. for proprietary court management software licences, professional services and maintenance. The current contract expires December 31, 2024, and Rocket is the sole supplier of the Mobius View software.

title: Expropriation of Easements to Construct the Black Creek Sanitary Trunk Sewer Relief System - Stage 2
topics: construction, expropriations, sanitary sewers, sewers, trunk sewers; building, compulsory purchase; eminent domain, main sewers; sewer mains, sewage systems; sewerage
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the stage 2 expropriation of property interests for Toronto Water's Black Creek Sanitary Trunk Sewer Relief System. Council authorized the first stage in April 2024 for properties including 37 Downsview Avenue, 200 Chalkfarm Drive, 1570 Wilson Avenue, 2208 Jane Street and 2210 Jane Street.

title: 21 Western Battery Road - Below Market Lease Agreement with Network Child Care Service for Child Care Services
topics: agreements, child care, child care facilities, contracts, leasing; child care agencies; child care centres; day cares; day nurseries; home care agencies; home child care providers; nursery schools, childcare, leases, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize a ten-year nominal lease with Network Child Care Services for child care at the newly built centre at Unit 1, 21 Western Battery Road. The tenant was selected through an expression of interest process run by Children's Services.

title: Litigation Arising from the Construction of Ethennonnhawahstihnen' Community Recreation Centre and Library
topics: community centres, construction, legal matters, library branches; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, branches, building, legal issues
brief: The City Solicitor recommends City Council adopt confidential recommendations on the litigation arising from the construction of the Ethennonnhawahstihnen' Community Recreation Centre and Library. The general contractor and subcontractors sued the city over alleged damages and extra costs from the 2018–2023 construction.

title: 100 Ethennonnhawahstihnen Lane - Below Market Lease Agreement with Petit Pearson Child Care North York for Child Care Services
topics: agreements, child care, child care facilities, contracts, leasing; child care agencies; child care centres; day cares; day nurseries; home care agencies; home child care providers; nursery schools, childcare, leases, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize a ten-year nominal lease with Petit Pearson Child Care North York for child care at the newly built centre at 100 Ethennonnhawahstihnen Lane. The tenant was selected through an expression of interest process run by Children's Services.

title: Renaming of Rainbow Park
topics: naming, parks and open space areas; green spaces; open spaces
brief: Councillor Frances Nunziata recommends City Council approve renaming Rainbow Park to Ernie Lustig – Rainbow Park, notwithstanding the property naming policy. Ernie Lustig was a lifelong Toronto resident and volunteer in the Jewish community who advocated against racism and for an inclusive society.

title: 1828-1844 Weston Road - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, high rise buildings, mixed use areas, rezoning; developing land; development (land); land development, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, tall buildings
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the zoning amendment and rental housing demolition for a 45-storey mixed-use building at 1828–1844 Weston Road, with 565 residential units including nine replacement rental units and 428 square metres of non-residential space.

title: Audley Street and Newcastle Street - Pay-and-Display Parking
topics: on-street parking, parking, parking regulations; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to approve new on-street paid parking on Audley Street and Newcastle Street in Ward 3, identified with the Toronto Parking Authority to serve the local community and area businesses. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates on both streets.

title: 230 Royal York Road - Construction Staging Area
topics: [buildings by height], construction, residential properties; building, residential real estate
brief: Leader Lane Developments is building a 9-storey residential building at 230 Royal York Road, and City Council is asked to authorize closing the west sidewalk, part of the southbound bike lane and part of the southbound curb lane on Royal York Road for construction staging. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Royal York Road.

title: 5359 Dundas Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the zoning amendment for a 50-storey mixed-use building at 5359 Dundas Street West, with 600 dwelling units and 743 square metres of commercial space, totalling 37,975 square metres. The Etobicoke Zoning Code would also be amended to permit use of the retained parking garage.

title: Property Taxes: 2025 Interim Levy By-Law
topics: property taxes, taxes; levies, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: Staff recommend City Council adopt the by-law for the 2025 interim property tax levy, based on 50 percent of the total 2024 taxes billed per property. The interim levy will raise about $2.85 billion for city purposes until the 2025 budget and final levy are approved.

title: GO Expansion Program - 2024 Update
topics: rail transportation, transportation; railway transport; railway transportation, transportation services
brief: Staff recommend City Council amend the temporary highway closing by-law to support Metrolinx's GO Expansion Program. The report updates Council on the program's three work packages: Enabling Works, Off-Corridor and On-Corridor Works.

title: CaféTO Business Improvement Area (BIA) Pilot Programs Update and Toronto Municipal Code Amendments for 2025
topics: municipal codes, pilot projects;
brief: Staff recommend City Council amend the Municipal Code for the 2025 CaféTO program, which supports outdoor dining for bars and restaurants from May 1 to October 15. The report covers the BIA pilot programs and code amendments for sidewalk cafés, parklets and marketing displays.

title: 2024 Chief Information Security Officer’s Report on Agencies and Corporations
topics: corporations, information, security;
brief: The Chief Information Security Officer recommends City Council receive the 2024 report on agencies and corporations' cyber security responses and compliance rates. Council directed the officer to extend the mandate to city agencies and corporations and report annually.

title: ModernTO: Selection of Proponent for 610 Bay Street and 130 Elizabeth Street
topics: boards of management, redevelopment; boards of directors; boards of governors, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: The CreateTO board recommends City Council approve the preferred development proponent for 610 Bay Street and 130 Elizabeth Street. The redevelopment prioritizes affordable housing, a Paramedics Multi-Hub, medical-sciences commercial space, and adaptive reuse of a heritage building.

title: Ookwemin Minising and Biidaasige Park: Naming the New Island and Park in the Port Lands
topics: parks, report requests; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Staff recommend City Council name the new island and park in the Port Lands Ookwemin Minising and Biidaasige Park. The names came from an Indigenous community engagement process led with the MinoKamik Collective, responding to Council's reconciliation directions for the Port Lands.

title: Build More Homes: Expanding Incentives for Purpose Built Rental Housing
topics: buildings, development, rental housing; developing land; development (land); land development, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend City Council endorse developing a new purpose-built rental homes incentives stream, responding to the housing crisis and Council's pledge to meet the provincial target of 285,000 homes. The report addresses both deeply affordable homes for low-income residents and rising rents for middle-income earners.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Revenue Opportunities to Support Hosting Obligations, Procurement Plan Revisions, and Social Procurement and Community Workforce Development Updates
topics: financial reports, sports, sports tournaments; annual financial reports; financial statements, tournaments
brief: The FIFA World Cup 2026 Subcommittee asks City Council to approve a temporary increase to the Municipal Accommodation Tax from 6 percent to 8.5 percent, effective June 1, 2025 to July 31, 2026, with the extra revenue going toward World Cup hosting costs. The report also covers a revenue strategy to offset hosting expenses, community workforce development, and business opportunities for local and diverse suppliers through World Cup procurements. Council is also asked to approve revisions to the procurement plan.

title: Good Roads Board of Directors Meetings Update September 26 - September 27, 2024
topics: conferences, roads; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), conference travel
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie recommends City Council receive his update on the September 26–27, 2024 Good Roads Board of Directors meetings, where he serves as Toronto's representative and Third Vice President. The meetings covered road infrastructure policy updates and future direction.

title: Establishment of Ontario Rural Road Safety Program
topics: infrastructure, road safety;
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie recommends City Council support Good Roads' request to the Province to establish an Ontario Rural Road Safety Program, and forward Council's decision to the Province. Ontario saw 616 road deaths and 36,090 injuries in 2023, with fatalities up nearly 20 percent over a decade.

title: Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) Report to City Council
topics: board members, municipalities; boroughs; cities; counties; regional municipalities; towns
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, as a Toronto appointee to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities Board of Directors, recommends City Council receive his summary of the September 18–19, 2024 board gathering in Ottawa. Key topics included reconciliation and FCM's fall and winter preparations.

title: Updating All of City of Toronto Relationship Frameworks to include Gender Inclusive Language
topics: sex and gender; gender identity; sex
brief: The 2SLGBTQ+ Advisory Committee recommends the Executive Committee ask City Council to direct the City Manager to update all city relationship frameworks with gender-inclusive language. The motion calls for replacing gender-specific language and reviewing assumptions that reinforce binary ideas about gender.

title: Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee - Proposing Amendments to the Terms of Reference and Committee Procedures
topics: aboriginal services, advisory committees, committee meetings; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups
brief: The Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee recommends the Executive Committee ask City Council to amend the committee's terms of reference to include a minimum of six members. The committee discussed its preferred approach to terms of reference and procedure changes at its October 8, 2024 meeting.

title: Reporting Noise Exemptions and Noise Complaints Transparently
topics: liquor sales licences, noise control; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, noise barriers; sound barriers
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie recommends City Council direct staff to create a dedicated web page reporting noise exemption permits and noise by-law complaints transparently, including a map of exemption locations for businesses and residents.

title: Changes to Fairbank Village Business Improvement Area Board of Management
topics: board members, business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: Staff recommend City Council remove two directors from the Fairbank Village Business Improvement Area Board of Management. The BIA falls within two community council boundaries, so the change goes to Council.

title: Update on Outstanding Directives Related to the Noise By-law
topics: by-laws, noise complaints; bylaws
brief: Staff recommend City Council amend the Noise By-law, including options to reduce noise from waste collection, a fee waiver for noise exemption permits for grassroots cultural organizations, and assessment of amplified sound levels above ambient levels. The report also updates implementation of the June and September 2023 noise by-law amendments.

title: Update on Actions to Address Dangerous Dogs
topics: dogs, public safety & protection (sc);
brief: Staff recommend City Council re-iterate its request to the Ontario government to amend the Dog Owners' Liability Act to provide a faster process for dangerous dog orders. The city has increased education and enforcement after a rise in dangerous dog service requests since 2022.

title: Sidewalks to Skylines: An Action Plan for Toronto’s Economy (2025-2035)
topics: sidewalk repairs; roadside repair; sidewalk brick installation; sidewalk brick maintenance; sidewalk maintenance; sidewalk ramping; sidewalk replacement; sidewalks maintenance; walkway maintenance; walkway repair
brief: Staff recommend City Council adopt Sidewalks to Skylines: An Action Plan for Toronto's Economy (2025–2035), the city's first economic development plan in over a decade, focused on job creation and growth amid new global and local trends.

title: Culture Connects: An Action Plan for Culture in Toronto (2025-2035)
topics: [activities in culture], culture (sc);
brief: Staff recommend City Council adopt Culture Connects: An Action Plan for Culture in Toronto (2025–2035), a 10-year vision positioning Toronto as a global cultural capital where everyone can discover, experience and create culture.

title: Extending Voting Opportunities in City Polls to 16- and 17-Year-Olds - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: electoral reform, youth; adolescents, campaign finance reform; voting reform; voting system reform
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng, recommends City Council ask the City Clerk to report on reducing the minimum voting age to 16 in neighbourhood polls. Fourteen Canadian municipal councils and school boards have passed motions supporting votes at 16 or studying the policy.

title: 4800 Yonge Street - Request for Further Directions
topics: appeals, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council for further directions on the long-running 4800 Yonge Street file. The applicant's plan was a 49-storey, 497-unit mixed-use building with a five-storey retail and office base and a five-level underground garage; appeals went to the tribunal after Council missed the decision deadline, and Council accepted a settlement offer on February 26, 2019. Council is asked to adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their later public release.

title: 2079-2111 Yonge Street, 9-11, 21, 31, 35 and part of 37 Hillsdale Avenue East, and 12-18 and part of 20 Manor Road East - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council for confidential directions for an Ontario Land Tribunal proceeding. The case concerns a 29-storey (98-metre) mixed-use building proposed for 2079-2111 Yonge Street and nearby Hillsdale Avenue East and Manor Road East addresses, with 486 residential units including 31 replacement rental units, 2,000 square metres of non-residential floor area, and partial retention of the heritage building at 2111 Yonge Street. The applicant appealed after Council failed to decide the zoning and Official Plan amendments, which were filed September 15, 2023. Council is asked to adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their later public release.

title: 2111 Yonge Street - Alteration to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes at a Designated Property under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement - Request for Directions
topics: appeals, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The City Solicitor recommends City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the heritage alterations and demolition at 2111 Yonge Street, part of the proposed 29-storey mixed-use building at 2079-2111 Yonge Street with 486 residential units. The designated heritage building was proposed to be partially retained.

title: 272, 284, 286, 288, 290, and 296 Lawrence Avenue West and 1507, 1525, 1537, 1539, 1545, and 1549 Avenue Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: appeals, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning
brief: The Ontario Land Tribunal hearing for the 14- and 10-storey mixed-use buildings with 455 units proposed at 272–296 Lawrence Avenue West and 1507–1549 Avenue Road is the subject of a confidential legal report. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release after the matter concludes.

title: Sherway Area Secondary Plan - City-initiated Official Plan Amendment and 25 The West Mall (Sherway Gardens Mall) - Official Plan Amendment Application - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearings - Request for Directions
topics: hearings, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council for confidential directions on ongoing Ontario Land Tribunal appeals of the Sherway Area Secondary Plan (Official Plan Amendment 469, adopted in October 2019) and the Official Plan amendment application for 25 The West Mall (Sherway Gardens Mall). Most of the nine appeals have been resolved or narrowed through earlier Council instructions to the City Solicitor. Council is asked to adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their later public release.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the CreateTO Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Corporations Nominating Panel recommends that City Council appoint two public members, Mark Bonham and Marni Dicker, to the CreateTO Board. The appointments would run until March 28, 2028, at Council's pleasure, or until successors are appointed.

title: Updates on Addressing Workplace Harassment and Discrimination
topics: discrimination, harassment;
brief: The Integrity Commissioner recommends that City Council ask the Commissioner to review any provincial amendments addressing workplace harassment and discrimination by members of Council and local boards, and report back if appropriate. This follows Council's October 2023 request that the province amend the City of Toronto Act, 2006 on this issue, with no provincial action yet indicated. Council is asked to authorize the review.

title: 26 Millwood Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend City Council state its intention to designate 26 Millwood Road under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. Council stated its intention to designate the property in May 2024, but the designation must be re-stated.

title: 53-63 Sheppard Avenue West and 62-68 Bogert Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Applications - Request for Direction
topics: redevelopment; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: The redevelopment proposal for a 15-storey mixed-use building at 53-63 Sheppard Avenue West and 62-68 Bogert Avenue, previously before Council and appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, still has outstanding matters. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt confidential instructions to staff and authorize their release after the matter concludes.

title: Council Member Appointments to the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority
topics: conservation; environmental conservation; environmental improvements; environmental management; environmental protection; environmental stewardship; greening
brief: This is a procedural item: the Mayor recommends that City Council appoint council members to the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority board for January 1, 2025 to November 14, 2026, based on members' preferences. The Authority wants its 2025-26 appointments in November so new members can be onboarded before the January annual general meeting. Council is asked to make the appointments.

title: 3374 Keele Street - Zoning Amendment Application - Request for Direction
topics: condominium housing, zoning bylaws; condominiums; condos, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council to adopt confidential instructions on the 3374 Keele Street zoning file. The application started as a 12-storey, 158-unit condo building and was revised on March 21, 2023 to a 29-storey building with 296 units and about 20,761 square metres of floor area. Council is asked to adopt the confidential instructions and authorize their later public release.

title: 50 Eglinton Avenue West - Alterations to a Designated Property under Sections 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The owner of 50 Eglinton Avenue West appealed Council's refusal of the Official Plan and zoning amendments for 50-90 Eglinton Avenue West and 17-41 Henning Avenue — proposing 46- and 58-storey towers with about 1,206 units plus a 34-storey building. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt confidential instructions to staff on the heritage alterations.

title: 50 - 90 Eglinton Avenue West and 17 - 41 Henning Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council for confidential instructions on Ontario Land Tribunal proceedings over planning applications at 50-90 Eglinton Avenue West and 17-41 Henning Avenue. The applicant appealed after Council refused the Official Plan and zoning amendments within the Planning Act timeline; 50 Eglinton Avenue West is a heritage-designated property under Part IV, Section 29. Council is asked to adopt the confidential instructions and authorize their later public release.

title: 49-59 Lawrence Avenue East - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: multi-unit dwellings, zoning bylaws; multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council for confidential directions for an Ontario Land Tribunal proceeding. The case concerns a 9-storey, 40-unit residential building with two levels of underground parking at 49-59 Lawrence Avenue East; the applicant appealed Council's failure to decide the application on April 23, 2024. Council is asked to adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their later public release.

title: 40 Walmer Road - Zoning By-law Amendment - Request for Direction Report
topics: multi-unit dwellings, zoning bylaws; multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The Ontario Land Tribunal hearing for the 35-storey, 365-unit residential building proposed at 40 Walmer Road, including 33 replacement rental units, is the subject of a confidential legal report. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release after the matter concludes.

title: 710 The West Mall - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: hearings, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor asks City Council for confidential directions for the February 10, 2025 Ontario Land Tribunal case management conference. The case concerns a refused zoning amendment application for 710 The West Mall, where the applicant wants to build a 22-storey residential building with 282 new homes; the applicant appealed Council's refusal to the Tribunal on March 6, 2024. Council is asked to adopt the confidential instructions and authorize their later public release.

title: 69 Yorkville Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning tribunals, rezoning; omb; ontario municipal board, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council for confidential directions for a December 2, 2024 Ontario Land Tribunal hearing. The case concerns a refused Official Plan and zoning amendment for a 29-storey, 143-unit mixed-use building at 69 Yorkville Avenue; the applicant appealed Council's refusal on February 23, 2023. Council is asked to adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their later public release.

title: 685 Lake Shore Boulevard East - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: construction, residential properties; building, residential real estate
brief: The Ontario Land Tribunal hearing for the two residential towers of 38 and 43 storeys proposed at 685 Lake Shore Boulevard East, on a 4-storey commercial base, is the subject of a confidential legal report. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release after the matter concludes.

title: 4630 Kingston Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: appeals, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning
brief: The Ontario Land Tribunal hearing for the 13-storey mixed-use building with 417 units proposed at 4630 Kingston Road is the subject of a confidential legal report. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release after the matter concludes.

title: 38 Walmer Road and 188 Lowther Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: buildings, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council for confidential directions for an Ontario Land Tribunal hearing. The file concerns a 20-storey, 162-unit mixed-use building at 38 Walmer Road and 188 Lowther Avenue, including altering the Walmer Road Baptist Church and demolishing its Sunday School building; the applicant appealed to the Tribunal on May 31, 2023. Council is asked to adopt the confidential instructions and authorize their later public release.

title: Respecting Local Democracy and Cities
topics: municipalities; boroughs; cities; counties; regional municipalities; towns
brief: This is an information item: the Mayor reports that provincial Bill 212 would overturn work and decisions of Toronto City Council at great taxpayer cost and without collaboration, and that she is working with city staff to review the city's options. The Mayor recommends that City Council receive the report for information. No further decision is requested.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will introduce General Bills and Confirming Bills. No substantive decision is attached; these are the routine by-laws that give effect to Council's actions.

title: Award of Doc4681367135 to HUB International Ontario Ltd. for the General Benefits Consulting Services, for the Pension Payroll and Employee Benefits Division
topics: contracts, purchasing, quotations; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, bids; quotes; request for quotation; rfq
brief: This is a routine contract award: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel award proposal Doc4681367135 to HUB International Ontario Ltd. for general benefits consulting services for the Pension, Payroll and Employee Benefits Division. The fee-for-service contract covers subject-matter expertise during collective bargaining, underwriting reviews, and related benefits work. HUB was the highest-scoring of six bidders.

title: Award of Doc4669795916 to Timbel Limited for Transmission Watermain Abandonment, Road Resurfacing and Storm Sewer Replacement for Engineering and Construction Services
topics: contracts, purchasing, quotations; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, bids; quotes; request for quotation; rfq
brief: This is a routine contract award: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel award Tender Doc4669795916 to Timbel Limited. The work covers transmission watermain abandonment on St. George Street, Boulton Drive, and other streets, plus road resurfacing and storm sewer replacement. Timbel's bid of $3,215,215 before HST was the lowest compliant bid; the cheapest bidder, Clearway Construction at $3,195,761, was found non-compliant.

title: Results of 2024 External Quality Control Review
topics: audits, external services, service quality; auditors; auditors, consultants; consulting services; professional services

title: Request to Implement Measures for Mandatory Lead Disclosure and Mitigation in Multi-Residential Housing
topics: disclosure, lead levels, multi-residential properties; additional disclosure; request for disclosure, lead in soil

brief: The Toronto Preservation Board recommends City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage property at 41-45 Spadina Road under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act, plus a heritage easement agreement. The site holds Spadina Gardens, built in 1905-1906 as one of Toronto's first six apartment buildings, with only two of the six still standing. The proposal adds a 10-storey residential tower with a mechanical penthouse, cantilevered above the existing four-and-a-half-storey building on two structural columns. Council is asked to consent to the alteration application with conditions.
