brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage property at 105 Maitland Street — the National Ballet School, with buildings at 99-113 Maitland Street dating from 1871 to 1888 — to replace the original single-pane wooden windows in line with technical standards. This matches the Toronto Preservation Board's recommendation. Council is asked to approve the alterations under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act.

title: 20 (22) Front Street West - Alterations to a Heritage Property Under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend the Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: easements, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve alterations to the heritage property at 20 Front Street West (entrance at 22 Front Street West) in the Union Station Heritage Conservation District, to allow a new mixed-use building. The site holds the 1923 Gowns-Kent Building, an eight-storey Classically influenced commercial building, and the existing heritage easement agreement needs amendment. This matches the Toronto Preservation Board's recommendation.

title: 414, 416 and 418 Church Street and 79 and 81 Granby Street - Alterations to Attributes of Designated Heritage Properties Under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: agreements, easements, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage properties at 414, 416 and 418 Church Street (the Stephen Murphy Houses and Store) and 79 and 81 Granby Street (the Robert Kidney Houses) to allow a new 32-storey mixed-use development with retail at grade. This matches the Toronto Preservation Board's recommendation. Council is also asked to authorize a heritage easement agreement.

title: 1337-1355 King Street West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment, and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, official plan amendments, rental housing, zoning bylaws; rental properties; rental units, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a 10-storey residential building with 92 affordable housing units, including 10 rental replacement units, at 1337-1355 King Street West. The existing 11-storey Phoenix Place apartment building and Parkdale United Church would be fully retained, and the project is supported by the Open Door Affordable Rental Housing Program. The report also recommends approving the rental housing demolition with a tenant relocation and assistance plan. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments.

title: 38 Walmer Road - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes and Demolition of Buildings on a Designated Property - Refusal
topics: buildings, demolitions;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the application to alter and demolish heritage attributes at the Walmer Road Baptist Church property at 38 Walmer Road (including 188 Lowther Avenue) under the Ontario Heritage Act. The related development application proposes a 20-storey mixed-use building, altering the church sanctuary and demolishing the Memorial Building and Sunday School building. City Council is asked to refuse the alteration and demolition permits.

title: 15 Elm Street - Demolition of a Designated Property
topics: demolitions, heritage properties, permits; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, permit renewal
brief: This report recommends that City Council refuse the application to demolish the designated heritage building at 15 Elm Street under the Ontario Heritage Act — the same recommendation the Toronto Preservation Board made. Council stated its intention to designate the property in May 2023, affirmed it after an objection, and passed Designation By-law 742-2023, now under appeal to the Ontario Land Tribunal. If the owner appeals the refusal, Council would defend it at the Tribunal.

title: 505 University Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: construction, zoning bylaws; building, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal report: the applicant for 505 University Avenue appealed the Zoning By-law Amendment application for a 64-storey mixed-use building with 704 units to the Ontario Land Tribunal in October 2023 after Council missed the Planning Act deadline. The designated heritage building would be demolished with some materials reused. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the appeal while continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: 505 University Avenue - Official Plan Amendment Application - Refusal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the Official Plan Amendment application for 505 University Avenue, tied to a proposal for a 64-storey mixed-use building with 704 units and 25,700 square metres of non-residential space. The designated heritage building would be demolished with some materials reused in the podium, and a February 2024 amendment sought to drop the office replacement requirement. The applicant appealed the zoning application to the Ontario Land Tribunal in October 2023.

title: 1050-1060 Eastern Avenue (Formerly 1555-1575 Queen Street East) - Extension of Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Approval
topics: by-laws, exemptions, part lot control; bylaws, exceptions
brief: Staff recommend that City Council extend the Part Lot Control exemption for the Toronto Community Housing revitalization site at 1050-1060 Eastern Avenue (formerly 1555-1575 Queen Street East) for two more years. The development has 771 residential units across a 10-storey TCHC building and 17-storey and 15-storey market buildings, with rent-geared-to-income, affordable rental, market rental and condo tenures. The extension supports implementation of the approved development.

title: 409 Front Street East - Extension of Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Centres, buildings, projects;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council extend the Part Lot Control exemption at 409 Front Street East (Block 10 of the West Don Lands) for two more years. The 2020 exemption, enacted for four years, supports an Indigenous health centre and a training, education and employment centre plus residential and commercial uses in five buildings. The extension allows time to complete the project and the associated land transfers.

title: 1650-1664 Dupont Street and 3 Osler Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal of Official Plan Amendment and Approval of Zoning By-law Amendment
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend a split decision at 1650-1664 Dupont Street and 3 Osler Street: refuse the Official Plan Amendment for 3 Osler Street, but approve the Zoning By-law Amendment for an eleven-storey mixed-use building with 159 residential units and 418 square metres of ground-floor retail at 1650, 1660 and 1664 Dupont Street. The building steps down to eight and six storeys at the rear beside Neighbourhoods. City Council is asked to approve the split recommendation.

title: 1266 Queen Street West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal of Official Plan Amendment and Approval of Zoning By-law Amendment
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend a split decision at 1266 Queen Street West: refuse the Official Plan Amendment but approve the Zoning By-law Amendment for a 24-storey mixed-use building with 331 residential units and 563 square metres of ground-floor commercial space. The Official Plan redesignation was already reviewed and recommended through Official Plan Amendment 653 in the Municipal Comprehensive Review. City Council is asked to approve the split recommendation.

title: 73, 77, 79 and 83 Woodbine Avenue and 3 Buller Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a six-storey residential apartment building with 86 condominium units at 73 to 83 Woodbine Avenue and 3 Buller Avenue. The proposal is consistent with the Provincial Policy Statement and the Growth Plan, conforms with the Official Plan, and is described as an appropriate scale compatible with the neighbourhood. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments.

title: 400 Broadview Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a non-profit long-term care home with 392 beds on a vacant lot within the Bridgepoint Health campus at 400 Broadview Avenue, serving people needing continuing and complex nursing care and personal support. The proposal responds to the urgent need for long-term care in Toronto, which has grown since the campus was established in 2006. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments.

title: 27 and 29 Parkcrest Drive - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, residential properties; residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend approving the residential infill development at 27 and 29 Parkcrest Drive in Scarborough: five blocks of stacked back-to-back townhouse units oriented along a shared private driveway and a central outdoor amenity space, with parking in a one-level underground garage. An Official Plan amendment was found not to be needed along this stretch of Kennedy Road. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendment.

title: Hupfield Trail - No U-Turn Signs
topics: traffic signs, turn prohibitions (traffic); traffic regulatory signs
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Jennifer McKelvie to prohibit northbound and southbound U-turns at all times on Hupfield Trail between McLevin Avenue and Overlord Crescent/Rovinelli Road. The request responds to concerns from Mary Shadd Public School about U-turns near the two schools on Hupfield Trail, and City staff have no objections. City Council is asked to approve the prohibition.

title: St. Clair Avenue East - Road Alteration
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, road reconstruction; road alterations; road narrowing; road widening, ttc
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council, on the TTC's behalf, to alter St. Clair Avenue East between Midland Avenue and Linden Avenue by adding westbound and eastbound queue-jump lanes for TTC buses. The lanes would let buses bypass general traffic, improving reliability and travel times for about 630 daily bus trips and 44,000 daily customers. City Council is asked to designate the lanes as reserved for transit vehicles and bicycles at all times.

title: 1161 Kingston Road - Construction Staging Area
topics: road construction, road construction;
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize closing the south sidewalk and the eastbound curb lane on Kingston Road, between Courcelette Road and a point 50 metres east, for construction staging of Windmill Developments' 8-storey mixed-use building at 1161 Kingston Road. The closures are already in place under a monthly street occupation permit and need formal authorization, with a temporary pedestrian walkway in the closed curb lane. Council approval is required because Kingston Road is a major arterial street.

title: McNicoll Avenue at Markham Road - U-Turn Prohibition
topics: traffic signs, turn prohibitions (traffic); traffic regulatory signs
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to prohibit eastbound and westbound U-turns on McNicoll Avenue at the centre medians near Markham Road, and to extend those medians by 10 metres on the east side and 35 metres on the west side of Markham Road. The changes would address safety concerns and eliminate vehicle conflicts around the medians. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on McNicoll Avenue.

title: 3291 Kingston Road and 2 and 4 Windy Ridge Drive - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, demolitions, rental housing; application process, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend approving the Rental Housing Demolition application to demolish an eight-unit rental apartment building at 3291 Kingston Road, to be replaced with eight new rental units as part of a 12-storey redevelopment with 357 units. Two of the units were previously demolished without permits and would be included in the permit. The proposal includes a tenant relocation and assistance plan. City Council is asked to approve the demolition application.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will review the Order Paper at the July 24, 2024 meeting. No decision is attached.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions and announcements will be made at the July 24, 2024 City Council meeting. No decision is attached.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council may file petitions at the July 24, 2024 meeting. No decision is attached.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council will declare any interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act at the July 24, 2024 meeting. No other business is attached to this item.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from the Mayor and City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council introduces the committee reports and new business from the Mayor and City officials for the July 24, 2024 meeting. Reports come from the Executive Committee, Audit Committee, Economic and Community Development Committee, General Government Committee, Infrastructure and Environment Committee, and Planning and Housing Committee. No decision is attached beyond introducing the reports.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will confirm the minutes from its regular meeting held on June 26 and 27, 2024. No other business is attached to this item.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Council meeting on July 24, 2024 opens with O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is attached.

title: Single Exit Stair: Ontario Building Code Feasibility Study
topics: building codes, exits; fire exits
brief: This report responds to Council's direction to study whether multi-residential buildings up to four storeys could have a single exit stair instead of two, with added life safety measures meeting the Ontario Building Code's intent. Exits are a fundamental part of a building's fire and life safety system, and some designers have argued the Code's two-stair threshold should change. The Chief Building Official asks Council to request that the provincial Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing and the national construction codes board consult directly with the City, including Toronto Building, on the issue.

title: Advancing the Construction of Affordable Rental Homes at 777 Victoria Park Avenue
topics: affordable housing, construction; affordable homes; housing projects, building
brief: This is a confidential directions item on advancing affordable rental homes at the Housing Now site at 777 Victoria Park Avenue. The Housing Now Initiative leverages City-owned land for mixed-use, mixed-income communities and has identified 22 sites so far. The Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat asks City Council to adopt the confidential staff instructions in Confidential Attachment 1 and keep the attachment fully confidential. No public details are available beyond the confidential instructions.

title: Toronto Local Appeal Body - Chair's 2023 Annual Report
topics: annual reports, appeals, courts; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards
brief: This is an information item: the report transmits the Toronto Local Appeal Body Chair's 2023 Annual Report. The Local Appeal Body is an independent quasi-judicial tribunal, established in 2017, that hears appeals of Committee of Adjustment decisions on minor variances and consents; it has 14 members including the Chair and Vice-Chair. The Director of Court Services recommends City Council receive the annual report for information.

title: Our Plan Toronto: Recommendations on Three Employment Area Conversion Requests - Decision Report - Approval
topics: employment areas, official plan amendments; employment districts; employment zones
brief: This is the sixth in a series of final reports on Employment Area conversion requests under the Municipal Comprehensive Review of the Official Plan. Toronto's Employment Areas held over 21,900 establishments and nearly 398,000 jobs in 2023 — 26 per cent of city jobs — generating about 27 per cent of the City's estimated 2021 GDP of $195.7 billion. The Interim Chief Planner asks Council to adopt Official Plan Amendment 742 on three conversion requests and seek the Minister's approval.

title: Medical - Office Facilities/Affordable-Seniors Residential Project in Continuum of Care Setting - Request for Minister’s Zoning Order at 4646 Dufferin Street
topics: medical clinics, seniors housing; health clinics; outpatient clinics
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor James Pasternak asking City Council to request a Minister's Zoning Order from the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing for 4646 Dufferin Street, at the heart of the City's Russian Jewish community. The 6.17-acre site would hold six buildings with about 432,000 square feet of medical, office, commercial and residential space — including seniors and affordable housing in a continuum-of-care setting. The proposal supports City housing initiatives and provincial goals for community-based medical facilities.

title: Expanding Permitted Uses in Laneway and Garden Suites
topics: laneways, rezoning; back alleys; mews, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: This is a member motion from Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asking City Council to have the Chief Planner study whether the Zoning By-law could allow more residential uses — such as multi-tenant homes, group homes and residential care homes — in laneway and garden suites. The request follows the House of Compassion's approved laneway suite expansion of a residential care home at 169-171½ Shaw Street. Council is asked to direct the feasibility review.

title: 770 Don Mills Road - Memorandum of Understanding with Toronto Lands Corporation
topics: land acquisition, mixed use areas; land acquisitions; park acquisition; parkland acquisition; parks acquisitions; property acquisition; property acquisitions
brief: CreateTO's board asks City Council to approve the terms of a Memorandum of Understanding with the Toronto Lands Corporation (acting for the Toronto District School Board) to put a public elementary school inside the Housing Now development at 770 Don Mills Road. The Phase 1 Housing Now site sits at the southwest corner of Don Mills Road and Eglinton Avenue. Council is asked to approve the MOU terms and direct CreateTO's CEO to finalize it.

title: Employment Area Land Use Permissions - Decision Report - Approval
topics: employment areas, land use; employment districts; employment zones
brief: This report asks City Council to adopt Official Plan Amendment 680, updating Employment Area policies to align with the provincial definition of "area of employment" under the Planning Act as amended by Bill 97. It also concludes a Council-directed study on expanding permitted Employment Area uses to include places of assembly, places of worship and sports facilities on a site- or area-specific basis. The Interim Chief Planner asks Council to adopt the amendment and have the City Solicitor hold the implementing by-law.

title: 2-56 Cather Crescent - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: exemptions, part lot control, property (sc); exceptions
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that City Council enact a Part Lot Control Exemption By-law for 2-56 Cather Crescent, Phase 1Fa of the Lawrence Heights Revitalization Project. The exemption would create 32 parcels — 26 conveyable parcels for market townhouses plus parts supporting a future common-elements condominium — along with various easements. City Council is asked to enact the exemption by-law.

title: 50-90 Eglinton Avenue West and 17-19 Henning Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-Law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: buildings, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend refusing the application to raise the approved heights at 50-90 Eglinton Avenue West and 17-19 Henning Avenue from 35 and 37 storeys (approved by the Ontario Land Tribunal) to 46 and 58 storeys. The taller scheme would have 73,305 square metres of floor area and 1,206 residential units. City Council is asked to refuse the Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments in their current form.

title: 515, 519 and 521 Coldstream Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving a two-storey institutional building with a post-secondary institution and a place of worship at 515, 519 and 521 Coldstream Avenue, with 1,547.83 square metres of gross floor area and a driveway off Coldstream Avenue. The plan includes 33 surface vehicle parking spaces and 8 short-term bicycle spaces. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendment.

title: 1265 Wilson Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, dwellings, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend approving the Rental Housing Demolition application to demolish 61 rental units at 1265 Wilson Avenue and replace them with 61 new rental units of the same types, similar sizes and similar rents, with a tenant relocation and assistance plan. The Ontario Land Tribunal approved the related zoning amendment in principle in April 2024, with the final order withheld until outstanding matters including the rental demolition are resolved. City Council is asked to approve the demolition application.

title: 665, 667, 669 and 671 Sheppard Avenue West - Official Plan and Zoning Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, official plan amendments, zoning; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Staff recommend approving an 11-storey mixed-use building with 256 dwelling units at 665, 667, 669 and 671 Sheppard Avenue West, with 16,980 square metres of gross floor area including 154 square metres of retail, and 209 underground parking spaces on three levels. The proposal fits the Sheppard West/Dublin Secondary Plan's goals for diverse commercial and residential uses along Sheppard Avenue West while protecting adjacent lower-density areas. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments.

title: 1875 Steeles Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition and Conversion Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: buildings, development, zoning bylaws; developing land; development (land); land development, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving three residential towers of 39, 33 and 14 storeys on a shared five-storey base at 1875 Steeles Avenue West, with 960 dwelling units including 120 replacement rental units on site. The proposal conforms with the Provincial Policy Statement, the Growth Plan and the City's Official Plan. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendment and the rental housing demolition and conversion.

title: North York Civic Centre 2025 - Strategic Plan
topics: civic engagement, community centres, services; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, citizen participation; civic participation; community involvement; community participation; public involvement; public participation
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Lily Cheng asking City Council to have the City Manager assess the use of space at the North York Civic Centre and explore a Strategic Plan by 2025, in line with the City's workplace modernization program. The aim is a community hub strengthening civic engagement, connectivity and economic development as North York grows, addressing local needs including not-for-profit office and programming space. Council is asked to direct the review.

title: 155 Antibes Drive - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: buildings, development, zoning bylaws; developing land; development (land); land development, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving the infill development at 155 Antibes Drive: an 8-storey, a 32-storey and a 36-storey building in addition to the existing 16-storey building on the property. The proposal is consistent with the Provincial Policy Statement and the Growth Plan and provides new and improved amenities. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendment.

title: Steeles Avenue East - Road Alteration
topics: local roads, municipal road damage deposits, road reconstruction; construction deposits; street damage deposits; tree damage deposits; tree deposits, road alterations; road narrowing; road widening
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council, on the TTC's behalf, to alter Steeles Avenue East by extending the existing reserved bus lane 295 metres west of Townsend Road, creating a continuous 500-metre queue-jump lane. The lane would let TTC buses bypass general traffic, improving reliability and travel times for about 240 daily bus trips on Steeles Avenue East. City Council is asked to designate the northerly westbound lane as a reserved transit and bicycle lane at all times.

title: 2400-2444 Yonge Street - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, industrial areas, residential properties; building, industrial districts, residential real estate
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize closing the west sidewalk and part of the southbound curb lane on Yonge Street, plus the south sidewalk on Roselawn Avenue, for 38 months (July 25, 2024 to August 1, 2027) for construction staging of 21-storey and 27-storey residential towers at 2400-2444 Yonge Street by First Capital. Council approval is required because Yonge Street is a major arterial street. City Council is asked to authorize the closures.

title: Traffic Control Signals - Bathurst Street and a Point 100 Metres South of Carpenter Road
topics: services, traffic, transportation; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, transportation services
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize installing traffic control signals on Bathurst Street about 100 metres south of Carpenter Road, justified by its safety assessment, and to remove the existing pedestrian refuge island about 60 metres south once the signals are active. The signals would improve safety for all road users. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Bathurst Street.

title: Wilson Avenue - Road Alteration
topics: development, local roads, road reconstruction; developing land; development (land); land development, road alterations; road narrowing; road widening
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council, on the TTC's behalf, to alter Wilson Avenue by extending the existing reserved bus lane 100 metres to create a continuous 420-metre queue-jump lane from the Wilson Station entrance to east of Faywood Boulevard and past the development at 480 Wilson Avenue. The change ties into road modifications already made in the area. City Council is asked to adjust the reserved lane designations on the northerly westbound lane of Wilson Avenue.

title: 101 Mason Boulevard - Alterations to a Heritage Property and Demolition of a Building
topics: demolitions, development, property (sc); developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage property at 101 Mason Boulevard — the 1928 Loretto Abbey complex — to allow a large side addition so the school can expand, plus the demolition of a small rear garage under the Ontario Heritage Act. This is the same recommendation the Toronto Preservation Board made. The approvals tie to a site plan application for the school expansion.

title: 7-17 Nipigon Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: Official Plans, dwellings, housing; homes; residences
brief: Staff recommend refusing the Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment applications for a 50-storey residential building with 620 units at 7-17 Nipigon Avenue, finding the proposal inconsistent with the Provincial Policy Statement and the Growth Plan and non-conforming with the Official Plan and the Council-adopted Yonge Street North Secondary Plan. The proposal has a density of 17.1 times the lot area. If appealed, Council would direct the City Solicitor to oppose the application at the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 6035 Bathurst Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: buildings, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a 12-storey residential building with 205 dwelling units at 6035 Bathurst Street, with 13,412 square metres of gross floor area and a floor space index of 6.18. The proposal is described as an appropriate scale for the site given the surrounding mid-rise context. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendments.

title: 1800 Sheppard Avenue East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications
topics: redevelopment, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an information item: the report responds to a February 2024 North York Community Council motion that sent the 1800 Sheppard Avenue East refusal report back so the applicant could work with staff on planning issues for the 18.8-hectare site. The applicant conceptually envisions 12 new buildings in a multi-phased redevelopment. City Planning recommends that City Council receive the report for information. No decision is attached.

title: 75 and 63 Ethennonnhawahstihnen' Lane (formerly municipally known as 1001 Sheppard Ave East (Block 9 and Block 18 on REG PLAN 66M-2518) - Official Plan and Zoning Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, residential properties, zoning; residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend approving a 44-storey and 39-storey mixed-use development with 867 residential units at 75 and 63 Ethennonnhawahstihnen' Lane (formerly 1001 Sheppard Avenue East), with about 60,809 square metres of floor area. The plan puts a Toronto Catholic District School Board elementary school in the first two storeys of the base building plus a new school yard, with 4,618 square metres dedicated to the school. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments.

title: 49-59 Lawrence Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: Official Plans, residential properties, zoning bylaws; residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal report: the applicant for 49-59 Lawrence Avenue East appealed the Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment applications for a 9-storey, 40-unit residential building to the Ontario Land Tribunal on April 23, 2024 after Council missed the Planning Act deadline. No case management conference has been held yet. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the application while continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: 1 Sandfield Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, housing, zoning bylaws; homes; residences, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a seven-unit, three-storey townhouse block fronting York Mills Road at 1 Sandfield Road, with 2,629 square metres of floor area and vehicle access from Sandfield Road. The existing detached dwelling on Sandfield Road would be demolished. An Official Plan amendment was found not to be needed. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendment.

title: 1779-1787 Bayview Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, dwellings, residential properties; residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend approving the Rental Housing Demolition application to demolish ten vacant rental units at 1779-1787 Bayview Avenue and replace them with twelve new rental units of the same types, similar sizes and similar rents. A settlement was reached with the applicant and the Ontario Land Tribunal issued an interim order in May 2024 approving the related Official Plan and zoning amendments in principle. City Council is asked to approve the demolition application.

title: Revitalization of the Historic Mimico Train Station in Coronation Park - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: historic sites, railway stations, redevelopment; heritage buildings; heritage sites; historical sites, railroad stations; train stations, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Amber Morley asking City Council to advance the restoration and activation of the historic Mimico Train Station in Coronation Park. Built around 1916 for the Grand Trunk Railway and later run by Canadian National, the station closed in the late 1960s, was abandoned in 1989, and was relocated to Coronation Park in 2007 after the community fought a demolition. The motion asks the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to start planning, including a building condition assessment and community engagement.

title: Amending Item 2023.CC5.37 - 175 Wynford Drive - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Request for Direction Report - To Authorize entering into a Section 37 Agreement - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: construction, ramps (highways), sidewalks; building, off ramps (highways); on ramps (highways)
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Jon Burnside to amend Council's earlier decision on the 175 Wynford Drive zoning application to authorize a Section 37 agreement. Wynford/Concorde residents have raised safety concerns about the Wynford Drive on/off ramp section, and without Section 37 funds there is no money to address them. The motion asks Council to require the owner to provide a phased cash contribution through the Section 37 agreement.

title: Bike Share for Everyone: Allowing Young Torontonians to access Safe, Sustainable Commutes - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
topics: bicycles, commuters, youth; adolescents, bikes
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe asking City Council to open Bike Share Toronto to younger riders. Bike Share recorded 5.7 million trips in 2023, but only riders 18 and older may ride alone — 16- and 17-year-olds need parental supervision and younger riders are banned. The motion asks the Toronto Parking Authority board to let 16- and 17-year-olds ride classic bikes unsupervised and to consider younger riders' access, so youth can use Bike Share with confidence.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 44 Jackes Avenue and 33 Rosehill Avenue for Production and Installation of a Replacement Heritage Plaque to Commemorate Glenn Gould - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: music, plaques; heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Josh Matlow to release $8,000 in Section 37 funds from the development at 44 Jackes Avenue and 33 Rosehill Avenue to Heritage Toronto for producing and installing a replacement heritage plaque commemorating Glenn Gould. Gould, one of Canada's most internationally revered musicians — his 1955 Goldberg Variations is the best-selling classical piano record of all time — remains an icon of creative innovation. The motion asks Council to increase the 2024 Heritage Toronto budget by $8,000, fully funded by the Section 37 money.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.CC18.7 - 34-70 Montgomery Avenue - Parkland Dedication Update - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: official plan amendments, parkland dedication;
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Mike Colle to reopen and amend Council's May 2024 settlement decision on the 34-70 Montgomery Avenue Ontario Land Tribunal appeal. The confidential settlement instructions did not contain the correct Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommendations on satisfying the parkland dedication requirement under Section 42 of the Planning Act. The motion asks Council to delete the part directing the General Manager to accept a payment in lieu of on-site parkland dedication.

title: City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment for Phases 4 and 5 of the Regent Park Revitalization - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: affordable housing, rezoning; affordable homes; housing projects, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Councillor Chris Moise and Councillor Paula Fletcher ask City Council to order a city-initiated zoning by-law amendment for Phases 4 and 5 of the Regent Park revitalization. In July 2023 Council approved zoning for 12 buildings of 6 to 39 storeys, but in March 2024 two conflicts were found between the proposed building footprints and critical city infrastructure. Council is asked to direct the Executive Director of Development Review to determine the appropriate zoning amendment to avoid those conflicts.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 1 Bloor Street West to St. Clare’s MultiFaith Housing for the Construction and Fit Out of a New Theatre and Rehearsal Space at 877 Yonge Street - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: development, religious diversity; developing land; development (land); land development, multi faith; spirituality
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe to release $600,000 in Section 37 funds from the development at 1 Bloor Street West to St. Clare's MultiFaith Housing for building and fitting out a new theatre and rehearsal space at City-owned 877 Yonge Street. Nightwood Theatre and Tapestry Opera will lease the sub-basement as their new theatre, office and rehearsal space, shared with other community performing arts groups. The motion asks Council to increase the 2024 Non-Program budget by $600,000, fully funded by the Section 37 money.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2024.CC19.16 - 2575 and 2625 Danforth Avenue, 2681 Danforth Avenue, and 2721 Danforth Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: rentals, tenants; renters; tenancy agreements
brief: Councillors Brad Bradford and James Pasternak ask City Council to re-open and amend its June 2024 decision on the Ontario Land Tribunal settlements for 2681 and 2721 Danforth Avenue. Council adopted the settlement offers in June, but a minor discrepancy arose between the offers and the instructions to the City Solicitor for the tribunal hearing. The corrected instructions confirm 21 affordable rental units from Canadian Tire at 2681 Danforth Avenue and the Tri-Metro terms at 2721 Danforth Avenue.

title: Release the Canada-Ontario Housing Benefits! Province Must End Delays so People Can Secure Housing - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: social assistance, transitional housing; alternative housing; short-term housing, financial assistance; income assistance; ontario works; ow; welfare
brief: Councillors Alejandra Bravo and Gord Perks ask City Council to call on the Ontario government to immediately release Toronto's Year 5 Canada-Ontario Housing Benefit allocation. The federally and provincially funded program helps people experiencing homelessness secure permanent housing, and in its fourth year helped move over 3,000 households from shelters and encampments into housing. The province closed Year 4 on March 31, 2024, and the motion also asks both orders of government to ensure Toronto's full Year 5 allocation.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds toward a new Play Area at Maurice Cody Junior Public School - By Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
topics: playgrounds, schools; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures, community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow and Councillor Parthi Kandavel ask City Council to contribute $164,811.50 in Section 37 development funds toward a new play area at Maurice Cody Junior Public School. The schoolyard serves as the neighbourhood park for eastern Davisville Village, where greenspace is scarce, and the planned features include basketball nets, an outdoor classroom, and new seating. The funds come from the development at 87-107 Davisville Avenue and 108-128 Balliol Street, at zero net cost to the city.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.NY13.6 - 501 and 503 Eglinton Avenue East and 383, 385, 387 and 389 Cleveland Street - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: zoning;
brief: Councillors Brad Bradford and James Pasternak ask City Council to re-open and amend its May 2024 approval of the zoning amendment for 501 and 503 Eglinton Avenue East and 383 to 389 Cleveland Street. Council approved a 14-storey residential building with retail at grade, but the adopting bill was never introduced and an amendment to the parking rates is now needed. The tenure also changed from condominium to rental, and the applicant has proposed reduced parking. The motion corrects the previous decision accordingly.

title: Improving Equity in the Distribution of City Cultural Funding - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: arts and culture, equity; employment equity; fair wage; pay equity
brief: Councillors Parthi Kandavel and Lily Cheng ask City Council to improve equity in how city cultural funding is distributed. The motion says non-profit arts organizations in Scarborough, Etobicoke, and North York, especially those serving vulnerable and racialized youth, are struggling to survive after the pandemic. Council is asked to direct the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture to ensure the needs of equity-deserving communities and youth outside the downtown core are considered in cultural funding.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Traffic Control Signals at Queen Street East and Sackville Street - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: pedestrians, safety; pedestrianization, public safety
brief: Councillor Chris Moise and Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik ask City Council to release Section 37 development funds for traffic control signals at Queen Street East and Sackville Street. The motion also authorizes removing the existing pedestrian crossover on Queen Street East just west of Sackville Street. Because the location is on a TTC route, the change requires City Council rather than community council approval.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds towards Public Realm and Streetscape Improvements related to "Manor Road Square" as prescribed in Official Plan Amendment 405 as a City-initiated Public Realm Move - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: road reconstruction; road alterations; road narrowing; road widening
brief: Councillors Josh Matlow and Mike Colle ask City Council to release an additional $318,600 in Section 37 development funds for the Manor Road Square public realm improvements. Council originally authorized $711,800 to Rockport Yonge and Manor Inc. in 2022, but cost escalations and design delays have pushed the revised project cost to $1,030,400 including HST. The motion amends the 2024-2033 capital budget to provide the one-time top-up.

title: Declaring April 11 to 17, 2025 as Black Maternal Health Week in the City of Toronto - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: health; health coverage
brief: Councillors Michael Thompson and Amber Morley ask City Council to formally declare April 11 to 17, 2025 as Black Maternal Health Week in Toronto. The week would raise awareness of Black maternal health, support Black-led initiatives, and encourage community involvement. The motion notes that Black Ontarians face health disparities and the province's Black Health Plan calls for equitable prenatal care and better data collection.

title: Artscape Receivership - Next Steps - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: art programs; art classes; art workshops; arts programs
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik and Councillor Gord Perks ask City Council to adopt confidential staff instructions on the next steps in the Artscape receivership. A court-appointed receiver took over Toronto Artscape Inc. on January 11, 2024, and the city has been advocating for the interests of Artscape's 390 residential and commercial tenants across 14 properties. Council is asked to adopt the confidential instructions and authorize their public release if adopted.

title: Multi-Tenant Housing Framework: Parks Levy Exemption and Framework Application - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: housing, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, homes; residences
brief: Councillors Alejandra Bravo and Chris Moise ask City Council to extend the multi-tenant housing framework's fee exemptions to parkland dedication. The 2023 Housing Action Plan legalized multi-tenant houses and directed fee exemptions, but parkland dedication was not exempted, unlike development charges for rooming-house dwelling rooms. Council is asked to direct the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to bring forward a Municipal Code amendment creating the exemption.

title: Welcome to Toronto, Taylor Swift! - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: street name signs, transportation; street signs, transportation services
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Jennifer McKelvie celebrating Taylor Swift's six Eras Tour concerts at the Rogers Centre this November. The motion asks City Council to direct Transportation Services and Economic Development and Culture to install honorary sign toppers creating a "Taylor Swift Way" route from the Rogers Centre to Nathan Phillips Square along John Street and Queen Street, with the Toronto signs' seven letters lit red in her honour. Council is asked to approve the tribute.

title: A Vital Link: Monitoring Traffic Congestion on Avenue Road - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: congestion, traffic; gridlock, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Councillors Brad Bradford and Jon Burnside ask City Council to monitor traffic congestion on Avenue Road between Bloor Street West and Dupont Street. In June 2024 Council approved a complete-street redesign with cycle tracks from Bloor to Davenport, and installation began in mid-July, removing one vehicle lane in each direction. Council is asked to direct the General Manager of Transportation Services to collect traffic data and report back on impacts to travel times compared with before installation.

title: Authority to execute agreements under section 4.1 of the Development Charges Act relating to statutory exemptions for Affordable Residential Units - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: Councillors Gord Perks and Shelley Carroll ask City Council to authorize the Deputy City Manager for Development and Growth Services to enter into agreements under section 4.1 of the Development Charges Act for statutory exemptions on affordable residential units. The motion follows provincial changes from Bill 23 and Bill 134, which made exemptions from development charges, community benefits charges, and parkland dedication mandatory for affordable units. Staff would execute the agreements in consultation with the Housing Secretariat, the Chief Financial Officer, and the City Solicitor.

title: Appointment of Director and Deputy Chief Building Official - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: appointments, buildings, municipal officials; city officials
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Gord Perks and Mayor Olivia Chow ask City Council to appoint Frank Stirpe, Tony D'Amico, and Anthony De Francesca as Deputy Chief Building Officials, effective as soon as possible. Each appointee would hold the powers and duties of the Chief Building Official in their assigned district. The motion is flagged as urgent so the appointments can meet city needs.

title: Accepting an In-Kind Donation from the East York Foundation and Leaside Baseball Association for New Scoreboards at Howard Talbot Park - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: community development, sports; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development
brief: Councillors Mike Colle and James Pasternak ask City Council to accept an in-kind donation of up to $180,000 from the East York Foundation for new scoreboards at Howard Talbot Park. The donation benefits the Leaside Baseball Association, which serves over 850 youth players a year, and covers replacing the east diamond scoreboard and adding a new free-standing scoreboard for the west diamond at the park near Eglinton Avenue and Bayview Avenue. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to accept the donation.

title: Waiving Road Occupancy Fees to Support the Construction of the Affordable Housing Building at 1141 Bloor Street West (Bloor-Dufferin) - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: affordable housing, construction; affordable homes; housing projects, building
brief: Councillors Alejandra Bravo and Paula Fletcher ask City Council to waive all road occupancy and temporary street occupation permit fees for the affordable housing building at 1141 Bloor Street West. The Block F development on the Bloor-Dufferin site includes 56 affordable rental units approved for Open Door fee exemptions in 2019, but road occupancy fees were not covered. The motion notes the construction staging area also blocks access to two other blocks on the site.

title: Reducing Runoff and Mitigating Flooding - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: climate change, flooding, wet weather flow; climate protection, floods, storm drainage; storm water; stormwater; stormwater pollution; stormwater runoff; surface drainage; surface flow
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow and Councillor Jennifer McKelvie ask City Council to order a report on reducing runoff and mitigating flooding. The motion points to more frequent and severe storms flooding roads, transit, homes, and businesses, and asks the City Manager, working with Toronto Water, the Chief Financial Officer, and the environment and climate office, to report back no later than the fourth quarter of 2024 on existing efforts and investment priorities.

title: Limiting Distance Agreement for 128 Havelock Street - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: Councillors Alejandra Bravo and Mayor Olivia Chow ask City Council to exempt the limiting distance agreement for 128 Havelock Street from the rule that city property deals reflect fair market value. The site is an affordable housing project by the Neighbourhood Land Trust with YWCA Toronto as operator, already approved for Open Door incentives in December 2023. The exemption covers the agreement between the city, as owner of the adjacent Dufferin Grove lands, and the developer.

title: A Traffic Action Plan for Liberty Village - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: public transit, traffic; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik and Councillor Gord Perks ask City Council to order a traffic action plan for Liberty Village. The motion says congestion has worsened with Gardiner Expressway rehabilitation and King Street water main work, leaving residents with unreliable car and transit trips and some drivers breaking road rules, endangering cyclists and pedestrians. Council is asked to direct the General Manager of Transportation Services, working with other city and TTC staff, to develop the plan.

title: Protecting Youth from Vapour Product Harms - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: harm reduction, public health, students, treatment (health); crack kits; methadone clinic; methadone maintenance; methadone treatment; needle exchanges; safer crack kits; safer crack smoking materials; safer injection, health treatments; therapeutics; therapy
brief: Councillors Alejandra Bravo and Paula Fletcher ask City Council to strengthen action against illegal vapour-product sales to youth. The motion cites Toronto Public Health data showing 11.4 percent of GTA students in grades 7 to 12 used a vapour product in the past year, and concerns from local schools about youth access despite the under-19 sales ban. Council is asked to direct the Medical Officer of Health and the Executive Director of Municipal Licensing and Standards to improve coordinated enforcement, compliance, and education and outreach.

title: Jurisdictional Research on Municipal Fiscal Frameworks - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: budgets, economic development; budgets and accounts, business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng and Mayor Olivia Chow ask City Council to order jurisdictional research on how comparable cities around the world fund themselves. The motion notes Toronto generates over 20 percent of Canada's GDP yet its operating budget rests mainly on property taxes, and frames the research as support for Toronto's push for a new fiscal framework. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer, with the City Manager, would report back with findings in advance of the 2025 budget.

title: Weston Charrette - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: development; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Frances Nunziata on a community-led design charrette for parks in Weston, which is growing fast with more residents in tall buildings. A developer, Weston Park Baptist Church and a consultant team propose leading the engagement with the Weston Residents' Association and arena management. The motion asks City Council to have Parks, Forestry and Recreation join the design exercise, since its 2024-2033 capital projects could be shaped by the community input.

title: Parking Amendment - Danforth Avenue Between Sibley Avenue and Thyra Avenue - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
topics: parking, transportation; transportation services
brief: Councillors Brad Bradford and Parthi Kandavel ask City Council to reinstate pay-and-display parking on the south side of Danforth Avenue between Sibley Avenue and Thyra Avenue. Parking there was removed in 2022 when cycle tracks were installed; Transportation Services identified an opportunity to bring it back after local businesses in the Danforth Village business improvement area asked for more parking. Council is also asked to approve adjustments to the cycle track and related parking and traffic regulations.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto District School Board for Public Realm Improvements at Inglenook Community School - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: improvement, school boards; enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise to release $816,000 in Section 37 funds from the development at 46-48 Power Street and 113-125 Parliament Street to the Toronto District School Board for public realm improvements at Inglenook Community School at 19 Sackville Street. The work centres on a new decorative fence with student-designed art panels and lighting along Sackville Street, Eastern Avenue and Virgin Place. The motion asks Council to increase the 2024 Non-Program budget by $816,000, fully funded by the Section 37 money.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 495- 517 Wellington Street West and 510- 532 Front Street West for The Waterfront School Playground Improvements - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: improvement, playgrounds, schools; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures, community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: This is a member motion from Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik to release $419,345.09 in Section 37 funds from the development at 495-517 Wellington Street West and 510-532 Front Street West for The Waterfront School playground improvements at 635 Queens Quay West. The school sits on leased City land and its playground doubles as a public park outside school hours; the school board has developed a Playground Master Plan. The motion asks Council to increase the 2024 Non-Program budget by $419,345.09, fully funded by the Section 37 money.

title: Accepting an In-Kind Donation from Moore Park Tennis Club and Central Tennis Club to Refurbish the Tennis Courts at Moorevale Park and Tom Riley Park - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: donation, tennis; bequest; toy drive
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe to accept an in-kind donation of up to $300,000 from Moore Park Tennis Club to refurbish the tennis courts at Moorevale Park in 2024. Community Tennis Clubs are partners in delivering tennis programming and maintain capital reserve funds for court repairs under the City's 2004 community tennis policy. The motion asks Council to authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to accept the donation.

title: Elm Street Streetscape - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: landscaping, transportation, urban design; civic improvements, landscapers, transportation services
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe on the Elm Street streetscape between Yonge Street and Bay Street, a downtown block with heritage character — landscaping, public seating, low-rise heritage buildings and sidewalk cafés — now facing severe development and traffic pressure. A consolidated streetscape vision is needed to maintain the block's character while accommodating new development and heritage alteration applications. The motion asks the Chief Planner and Transportation Services to prepare the vision and report back.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.CC16.25 - 619-637 Yonge Street and 1-9 Isabella Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: building plans, development; building records, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise to reopen and amend Council's March 2024 settlement decision on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 619-637 Yonge Street and 1-9 Isabella Street. The applicant has since proposed revised settlement plans dated July 2, 2024 with a 5.5-metre setback, which City Planning staff consider appropriate for the site. The motion asks Council to delete the part accepting the March 5, 2024 settlement offer and adopt the revised plans.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto District School Board for Fairbank Public School Playground and Schoolyard Revitalization - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: playgrounds, school boards; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Josh Matlow to release $300,000 in Section 37 funds from the development at 859, 861 and 875 Eglinton Avenue West and 2020 Bathurst Street to the Toronto District School Board for the Fairbank Public School playground and schoolyard revitalization. The schoolyard is well used by the school and community; the project adds new playgrounds and outdoor areas that are safe, accessible and support outdoor learning. The motion asks Council to increase the 2024 Non-Program budget by $300,000, fully funded by the Section 37 money.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Toronto District School Board for Humewood Community Schoolyard Master Plan - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: playgrounds, school boards; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Josh Matlow to release $300,000 in Section 37 funds from the development at 1443, 1445 and 1451 Bathurst Street and 501 St. Clair Avenue West to the Toronto District School Board for the Humewood Community Schoolyard Master Plan. The schoolyard is well used by the school and community; the plan adds new outdoor play areas, a relocated baseball diamond and soccer pitch, treed areas and seating. The motion asks Council to increase the 2024 Non-Program budget by $300,000, fully funded by the Section 37 money.

title: Improving Access to Outdoor Ovens in City Parks - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: accessibility, parks; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Brad Bradford asking City Council to improve access to the ten outdoor bake ovens in City parks, which are community focal points run with volunteer groups. Ovens are available by permit for occasional use or through longer-term agreements for charities and not-for-profits, under the 2011 Outdoor Ovens in City Parks Policy. The motion asks the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to review the policy for customer service and equity barriers.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Conseil Scolaire Viamonde for schoolyard improvements at École élémentaire Charles-Sauriol - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: landscaping, schools, tree planting; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, landscapers, reforestation; tree advocacy
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Alejandra Bravo to release $500,000 in Section 37 funds from the developments at 386-394 Symington Avenue, 485 Perth Avenue and 17 Kingsley Avenue to the Conseil Scolaire Viamonde for schoolyard improvements at École élémentaire Charles-Sauriol. The work includes soft landscaping, tree planting, a new bus bay and a new soccer field, with the schoolyard open to the public during community access hours. The motion asks Council to increase the 2024 Non-Program budget by $500,000, fully funded by the Section 37 money.

title: Putting the Brakes on Auto Theft: Immediate Action Needed to Keep our Neighbourhoods Safe - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: automobiles, safety, theft; cars; used automobiles; used cars, public safety
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Josh Matlow on the surge in auto theft and home invasions affecting neighbourhoods, with Toronto topping Ontario cities for auto theft claim values. The motion asks City Council to request that the federal government update vehicle security standards and expedite port screenings, and to ask the provincial Minister of Transportation to act. The Insurance Bureau of Canada estimates auto theft costs Ontarians hundreds of millions a year in claims and premiums.

title: Building a Permanent Safety Barrier Along the Leaside Bridge to Prevent Suicide Attempts
topics: bridges, safety barriers, suicide; suicide barriers
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor James Pasternak asking City Council to have Transportation Services report on the feasibility of a permanent safety barrier on the Leaside Bridge to prevent suicide attempts. On June 16, 2024, a man fell from the bridge onto a vehicle on the Don Valley Parkway, killing both him and a passenger; several similar cases are on record. The 2003 Bloor Viaduct barriers proved highly effective at deterring such attempts.

title: Options to Fund and Expand the HTO To Go Water Trailer program
topics: [events in community and life], funding, mobile water trailers; financing, h20 to go water trailer; h2o to go water trailer; hto to go water trailer; htotogo water trailers; water on wheels
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor James Pasternak asking City Council to have Toronto Water explore options to fund and expand the HTO To Go Water Trailer program, which provides free tap water at public events from May 1 to September 30 and reduces single-use plastic bottle waste. The motion asks the General Manager of Toronto Water, with the Chief Financial Officer, Parks and Solid Waste staff, to report back on expansion options.

title: Review of Standard Operating Procedure for Off-Road Vehicles in Parks
topics: parks, parks vehicles, policies and procedures; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, guidelines; policies, park vehicles
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Alejandra Bravo asking City Council to review the standard operating procedure for off-road vehicles in parks. Residents report that frequent vehicle use in green areas damages fields and turf, dominates pedestrian paths and blocks accessible routes, making park users feel unsafe. The motion asks the General Managers of Parks, Forestry and Recreation and Fleet Services to report to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee in the first quarter of 2025.

title: Annual Winter Maintenance Report
topics: annual reports, road maintenance, winter; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, roads maintenance; sidewalk maintenance; sidewalks maintenance; summer maintenance; winter maintenance
brief: This is the first Annual Winter Maintenance Report, starting a planned yearly cycle on winter operations transparency. It reviews the 2023-2024 winter season and outlines improvements for 2024-2025, including pilot testing, training, better contract administration and community events. City Council is asked to endorse in principle a Major Snow Event Response Plan and confirm updated winter maintenance service levels for cycling facilities. The report also updates on advances in winter operations.

title: Toronto Island Park Master Plan
topics: First Nations, Master Plans, attractions; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples, cultural attractions; places of interest; tourist attractions; tourist sites
brief: Staff ask City Council to adopt the Toronto Island Park Master Plan as the general direction for improvements to the 242-hectare park over the next 25 years. The park, established in 1956 and known to Indigenous communities as Mnissing, comprises 15 islands and waterways, hosts millions of visitors a year and is home to over 600 residents. The General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends adopting the plan to coordinate the park's complex needs and challenges.

title: Developing a Rat Reduction Plan for Toronto
topics: city initiatives, prevention, rodents; city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, gophers; mice; rats; squirrels
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Alejandra Bravo and Deputy Mayor Amber Morley asking City Council to develop a rat reduction plan for Toronto. Residents report growing rat populations in neighbourhoods, a multifaceted problem needing collaboration across City divisions, following examples like New York City's rat mitigation zones and Alberta's rat control plan. The motion asks the City Manager, with the Medical Officer of Health and other division heads, to develop an upstream prevention and action-focused plan.

title: Serving Climate-friendly Meals through City Services - Cool Food Pledge Commitment and Food-related Greenhouse Gas Emissions
topics: greenhouse effect, long term care homes, municipal services; city services, greenhouse gas emissions, homes for the aged; long term care centers; long term care centres; long term care facilities; nursing facilities; nursing homes
brief: This report outlines the food-related greenhouse gas emissions from meals the City serves, in relation to its Cool Food Pledge commitment. In 2019 Toronto pledged to cut corporate food procurement emissions by 25 per cent by 2030, and is exploring a shift to climate-friendlier meals; the City is also a C40 Good Food Cities signatory. The Executive Director of Environment and Climate asks Council to direct staff across Children's Services, Shelter and Support Services, and Seniors Services to work on the shift.

title: 39 Dundalk Drive Modular Housing
topics: housing, housing services; homes; residences
brief: This is an administrative inquiry from Councillor Michael Thompson about the 39 Dundalk Drive modular housing project in Scarborough Centre. Council's 2023.AU2.7 adopted the Auditor General's 19 recommendations to strengthen planning, oversight and cost tracking of Phase One and Phase Two modular housing projects, and a future work plan would examine whether supportive housing meets tenants' needs. The 39 Dundalk Drive project, part of Phase Two, opened 57 units. No decision is attached.

title: Introduction of By-law
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the General Government Committee introduces a confirming bill. A confirming bill formally records decisions the committee has already made. No new decision is attached.

title: Process for Award of Negotiable Request for Proposal Document Number 4053424337 for the Construction of Two New Fully Electric Ferry Vessels
topics: contracts, ferries, proposals, transportation; bids; request for proposal; rfp, ferry boats; ferryboats, transportation services
brief: This is an information item: the report sets out the process for awarding the negotiable request for proposals for two new fully electric Toronto Island ferry vessels — a passenger-and-vehicle vessel and a passenger vessel — under the Ferry Fleet Replacement Strategy. The new vessels would add over 400 and nearly 1,000 passengers per trip of capacity respectively. The General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends the report be received for information.

title: Supporting the Learning Enrichment Foundation by Identifying Community Space in York South - Weston

The Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management recommends that Council direct staff to keep working with the Foundation to find future space opportunities, with City Planning and Social Development involved.

Notices were served in Stage 1 and owners had 30 days to respond under the Expropriations Act. The Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management asks Council, as approving authority, to approve the expropriation of the property interest.

This is Stage 1: staff would serve and publish the Notice of Application for Approval to Expropriate on each registered owner, who can request a hearing under the Expropriations Act. City Council is asked to authorize the negotiations and the Stage 1 process.

title: Claim for Damages - Toronto Paramedic Services Vehicle Components

brief: This is a confidential directions item: the City bought vehicle components meant to improve the environmental and fuel efficiency of Toronto Paramedic Services vehicles and alleges the components were defective. The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 on legal action and authorize their later public release at the Solicitor's discretion. No public details are available beyond the confidential legal advice.

title: 245 Bartley Drive - Designation of a Portion of the Property used by the Toronto Transit Commission as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, by-laws, exemptions, properties (real estate), taxes; bylaws, exceptions, levies, property; real estate, ttc
brief: This is a tax item: staff ask City Council to designate the TTC-leased portion of 245 Bartley Drive (unit 2, about 46,000 square feet, owned by 245 Bartley Inc.) as a Municipal Capital Facility, exempting it from municipal and education property taxes. The designation would be made through a by-law and a Municipal Capital Facility agreement with the landlord. City Council is asked to pass the by-law.

title: Sale of 120 Grangeway Avenue to Metrolinx - Scarborough Subway Extension Project
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, council items, regional transportation agencies, subways, transportation projects; clauses; items (council); items before council, commuter rail systems; go transit; intercity transportation; interregional public transit systems; interregional transit systems; interurban transit organizations; metrolinx; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; regional transit authorities; regional transportation authorities; transit agencies; transit operating agencies, ttc, underground
brief: This report asks City Council to authorize selling part of the City-owned property at 120 Grangeway Avenue to Metrolinx and conveying a temporary easement over another part of the property. Metrolinx needs the land to build the new TTC Scarborough Centre subway station as part of the Scarborough Subway Extension, delivered by Metrolinx for the Province. City Council is asked to authorize accepting Metrolinx's offer to purchase.

title: Revenue Sharing Agreement for 14 Topiary Signs near the F.G. Gardiner Expressway
topics: agreements, maintenance, neighbourhoods; cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods, tenancy agreements
brief: This report asks City Council to authorize a revenue-sharing agreement with Hillside Media Communications Limited for 14 topiary signs in the rail corridor beside the F.G. Gardiner Expressway. Hillside already has a 10-year revenue-sharing agreement with the City under which it pays the City a share of revenues and maintains the "Toronto Sign" topiary for the City's use. City Council is asked to authorize negotiating and executing the new agreement.

title: Redevelopment of St. Lawrence Market North - Emergency Non-Competitive Contract and Purchase Order Amendment for Contract Administration Services
topics: [materials in management], by-laws, contracts, purchasing, redevelopment; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, bylaws, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization, resources
