Staff also ask Council to amend the purchase order with Adamson Associates Architects by an additional amount for contract administration services. City Council is asked to authorize the purchase order amendment.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Canadian Red Cross for Emergency Social Services
topics: agreements, contracts, emergency management, emergency services, purchasing; 9-1-1; 911; 911 calls; emergency assistance; emergency response, acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, crisis management; disaster planning; disaster supply kits; emergency preparedness; emergency procedures; emergency supply kits; survival kits, tenancy agreements
brief: This is a procurement item: the Executive Director of Toronto Emergency Management asks City Council to authorize a non-competitive five-year agreement with the Canadian Red Cross for emergency social services, starting January 1, 2025. The initial two-year term would have options to renew for another two years and one final year. An environmental scan found the Red Cross to be the local, scalable provider able to meet the immediate short-term needs of residents affected by emergencies.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Hootsuite Inc., for Enterprise Social Media Management Platform
topics: communication, contracts, management (sc), purchasing, social media; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, communicating; communications, facebook; twitter
brief: This is a procurement item: staff ask City Council to authorize a non-competitive contract with Hootsuite Inc. for the City's enterprise social media management platform, after a competitive procurement was unsuccessful. The initial three-year term runs to August 27, 2027 with an option to renew for two more years, totalling $853,343. City Council is asked to authorize the agreement.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Trojan Technologies Group ULC for the Supply of Proprietary Parts and Maintenance Services at Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant for Toronto Water
brief: This is a procurement item: staff ask City Council to authorize a non-competitive contract with Trojan Technologies Group ULC for $1,111,867 for proprietary parts and maintenance services for the ultraviolet disinfection system at the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant, running from award to March 31, 2027. Only the manufacturer can supply the proprietary parts. Council approval is required because the request exceeds the Chief Procurement Officer's authority.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order Number 47015457 with Bell Canada for Integrated Telecommunications Infrastructure

brief: This is a procurement item: staff ask City Council to amend the Bell Canada integrated telecommunications infrastructure contract by $17,492,138, raising its value from $146,407,475. The original 2010 contract expires September 30, 2025 and did not account for the pandemic-driven increase in reliance on the City's telecom systems, which support daily operations, state-of-good-repair projects and network cabling. City Council is asked to authorize the amendment.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order 6050005 with Yardi Canada Ltd., to Integrate a Centralized Affordable Rental Housing Access System into Existing Web-Based System and to Renew the Existing Licence Agreement
topics: affordable housing, agreements, official plan amendments, purchasing, rental housing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, affordable homes; housing projects, rental properties; rental units, tenancy agreements
brief: This is a procurement item: staff ask City Council to amend purchase order 6050005 with Yardi Canada Ltd. to add Affordable Rental Housing Program units into the City's integrated housing management system (MyAccesstoHousingTO) and renew the existing licence agreement. The City piggybacked on Toronto Community Housing's 2019 five-year Yardi software agreement. City Council is asked to authorize the amendment under the Financial Control By-law.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Blanket Contract 47023317 and Non-Competitive Procurement for the Provision of Warranty and Non-Warranty Service Bulletins, Safety Recalls, Services, Tools, Subscriptions, and Training on Cummins Engines
topics: contracts, purchasing, safety, services, taxes; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, levies, public safety
brief: This is a procurement item: staff ask City Council to amend the non-competitive blanket contract with Cummins Canada ULC for warranty and non-warranty parts and services for Cummins engines. The amendment would extend the term by one year to November 30, 2025, with an option to renew for four more years, add $685,175 to the budget, and expand the scope to cover service bulletins, safety recalls, tools, subscriptions and training. City Council is asked to authorize the amendment.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contract Number 47022859 of the Existing Property Management Agreement with Kipling Realty Management Inc., at Canoe Landing Facility for Parks, Forestry and Recreation
topics: agreements, contracts, management (sc), purchasing, taxes; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, levies, tenancy agreements
brief: This is a procurement item: staff ask City Council to amend the property management agreement with Kipling Realty Management Inc. for the Canoe Landing Facility at 20 Brunel Court, extending it seven months beyond the original five-year term and increasing the contract value by $90,118, from $996,482 to about $1,086,600. The request exceeds the Chief Procurement Officer's authority, so Council approval is required. City Council is asked to authorize the amendment.

title: 7-17 Locust Street - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: multi-unit dwellings, official plan amendments, rezoning; multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend refusing the application for a 48-storey residential building with 517 units at 7-17 Locust Street in Mount Dennis, finding it lacks supportable zoning standards for setbacks, tower stepbacks and separation distances. The proposal is inconsistent with the Provincial Policy Statement, does not conform with the Official Plan or have regard for the Mount Dennis Secondary Plan, and misses the intent of the Tall Building Design Guidelines. If appealed, Council would defend the refusal at the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 1175-1181 Weston Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: applications, official plan amendments, rezoning; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend refusing the application for a 38-storey mixed-use building with 382 units at 1175-1181 Weston Road in Mount Dennis, finding it lacks supportable zoning standards for setbacks, tower stepbacks and separation distances. The proposal is inconsistent with the Provincial Policy Statement, does not conform with the Official Plan or have regard for the Mount Dennis Secondary Plan, and misses the intent of the Tall Building Design Guidelines. If appealed, Council would defend the refusal at the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 37 Shorncliffe Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: industrial properties, office buildings, rezoning; industrial real estate, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend approving the redevelopment of 37 Shorncliffe Road with a five-storey self-storage warehouse building plus three one-storey buildings divided into 28 industrial and office condominium units. The proposal conforms with the Official Plan and is appropriate for an Employment Area. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendment.

title: 12-20 Cordova Avenue - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, residential properties; building, residential real estate
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize closing the west sidewalk and the southbound curb lane on Cordova Avenue, south of Dundas Street West, for 35 months (September 1, 2024 to August 1, 2027) for construction staging of a 24-storey residential building at 12-20 Cordova Avenue by Minto Cordova LP. A 2.1-metre covered pedestrian walkway would be maintained. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Cordova Avenue.

title: Lake Shore Boulevard West - Pay-and-Display Parking
topics: on-street parking, parking machines; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, pay and display machines; pay-and-display machines
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to approve new on-street pay-and-display parking on Lake Shore Boulevard West in Ward 3, replacing the existing unpaid one-hour parking to encourage turnover and support local businesses. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Lake Shore Boulevard West. City Council is asked to authorize the parking regulation amendments.

title: Mimico GO Station Area - Newcastle Street and Audley Street - Parking Amendments
topics: parking regulations, public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to amend parking on Newcastle Street and Audley Street near Mimico GO Station: allowing parking on the north/west sides between Windsor Road and Portland Street under the city-wide three-hour rule, while prohibiting parking at all times on the south/east sides where the TTC bus operates. The changes provide overflow parking for the station area. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on both streets.

title: 955-975 Weston Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mid rise buildings, official plan amendments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend approving a mixed-use development at 955-975 Weston Road with 984 residential units, community space and an on-site public park. The plan includes two residential towers of 34 and 24 storeys plus a seven-storey mid-rise along Weston Road, with 60,687 square metres of residential floor area and 465 square metres of community space. The Official Plan would change from Neighbourhoods to Mixed Use Areas and Parks. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments.

title: Bloor Street West - St. Clement Catholic School - Speed Limit Amendment
topics: assessment, speed limits;
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to replace the flashing 40 km/h School Speed Zone on Bloor Street West near St. Clement Catholic School with a 40 km/h speed limit in effect at all times. The change would allow Automated Speed Enforcement, which provincial legislation bars within flashing school zones. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Bloor Street West.

title: Metrolinx Eglinton Crosstown LRT - Traffic Control Signals at Eglinton Avenue West and Keelesdale Road
topics: regional transportation agencies, traffic control systems; commuter rail systems; go transit; intercity transportation; interregional public transit systems; interregional transit systems; interurban transit organizations; metrolinx; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; regional transit authorities; regional transportation authorities; transit agencies; transit operating agencies, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to approve the new Metrolinx-installed traffic signals at Eglinton Avenue West and Keelesdale Road (about 148 metres west of Black Creek Drive) for the Eglinton Crosstown LRT project. Council approval enables inspections, acceptance and activation of the signals. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Eglinton Avenue West.

topics: assumption of services, municipal services; city services

City Council is asked to approve the assumption.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2533, Longbranch Avenue and Eastwood Park Gardens, Lakeshore EMPC Two Limited, 2226704 Ontario Incorporated, Minto 3600 Lakeshore Commercial Incorporated, Stockton 3600 Lakeshore GP Incorporated, 3600 Lakeshore GP Incorporated
topics: assumption of services, municipal services; city services

The developers were Lakeshore EMPC Two, 2226704 Ontario, Minto 3600 Lakeshore Commercial, Stockton 3600 Lakeshore GP and 3600 Lakeshore GP. City Council is asked to approve the assumption.

title: 1575 Lawrence Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend approving an 11-storey mid-rise mixed-use building at 1575 Lawrence Avenue West, with 10,014 square metres of gross floor area, 118 residential units and two ground-floor retail units. The proposal provides an appropriate level of intensification for the site. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendment.

title: Association of Community Centres Settlement of Operating Results for Year Ended 2022
topics: community centres, operating budgets; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes
brief: This is a finance item: the City annually settles operating results with its ten Association of Community Centres based on their audited financial statements. For 2022, five centres ran operating surpluses totalling $228,451 — Community Centre 55, Central Eglinton, Scadding Court, Swansea Town Hall and Waterfront — which the Chief Financial Officer asks Council to direct be paid to the City, with deficits handled per the usual settlement. City Council is asked to approve the settlement.

title: 100 Thorncliffe Park Drive - Development Charges Complaint
topics: development, projects; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: This is a procedural item: the report responds to a development charges complaint filed under the Development Charges Act by 2613815 Ontario Inc. for a two-storey, 1,502.95 square metre expansion at 100 Thorncliffe Park Drive. The complainant says $400,147.13 in development charges should be refunded because the new first-floor space is industrial. City staff reviewed the complaint and the Chief Financial Officer recommends Council find the charges were properly applied and dismiss the April 2, 2024 complaint.

title: Transmittal of the 519 Board of Management General By-law No.2
topics: boards of management, by-laws; boards of directors; boards of governors, bylaws
brief: This is a governance item: the City Manager transmits General By-law No. 2 of The 519 Church Street Community Centre Board of Management for Council approval, as required by the Relationship Framework with the Association of Community Centres boards. The framework provides that Council consider board requests to amend Chapter 25, by-laws or governance structures. City Council is asked to approve the by-law and authorize technical changes to the framework.

title: Ontario Science Centre Update
topics: Centres, science & technology (sc);
brief: This is an information item: following Council's June 2024 direction (MM19.25), the City Manager will report to the Executive Committee before its July 16, 2024 meeting with an update on staff's preliminary work on the future of the Ontario Science Centre. The City Manager recommends the Executive Committee receive the report for information. No decision is attached.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026: Toronto Host City Procurement Plan
topics: [events in recreation and tourism], sports;
brief: This report presents the procurement plan for Toronto's hosting of the FIFA World Cup 2026, covering the planning, execution and obligations tied to the games. The FIFA World Cup 2026 Subcommittee considered it on July 5, 2024 and recommends that City Council direct the City Manager, the Executive Director of FIFA World Cup Hosting 2026 and the Chief Procurement Officer to proceed under the procurement plan. The plan sets out when procurement decisions come to the Executive Committee for financial oversight.

title: Refreshing the Parks and Recreation Facilities Master Plan and Building a Cricket Strategy
topics: cricket, school boards, structures;
brief: This is a committee recommendation item: the City-School Boards Advisory Committee asks Council to encourage Councillors to explore outdoor school improvements like shade structures and misting stations, and asks the Executive Committee to have the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation report on refreshing the Parks and Recreation Facilities Master Plan and building a cricket strategy, including opportunities with school boards. City Council is asked to endorse the recommendations.

title: Community Safety and Well-being and Schools
topics: community safety, school boards;
brief: This is a committee recommendation item: the City-School Boards Advisory Committee asks the Executive Committee to have the Executive Director of Social Development and the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation advance youth violence prevention opportunities for the summer months, including recreation programs. The request follows a presentation on community safety, well-being and schools highlighting City, school board and partner efforts under SafeTO, the City's ten-year community safety plan. City Council is asked to endorse the recommendation.

title: Subway Agreement in Principle and Update on Metrolinx Subway Program - Third Quarter 2024
topics: subways, transit routes; surface routes, underground
brief: This is an information item: the report updates City Council on the Subway Agreement in Principle and the Province's Metrolinx-delivered subway program — the Ontario Line, Scarborough Subway Extension, Eglinton Crosstown West Extension and Yonge North Subway Extension — in the third quarter of 2024. The 2020 Preliminary Agreement set out City and Province roles, and further agreements are being developed as the program advances. Council is asked to receive the update for information.

title: Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation Annual General Meeting and 2023 Audited Financial Statements
topics: audits, financial reports, seniors housing; annual financial reports; financial statements, auditors; auditors
brief: This is a procedural shareholder item: the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation board asks City Council to treat part of the Council meeting as the corporation's Annual General Meeting of the Shareholder, receive the board-approved 2023 audited financial statements, and handle the other AGM business required by the shareholder direction. City Council is asked to approve the shareholder actions.

title: Toronto Port Lands Company - Annual General Meeting and 2023 Audited Financial Statements
topics: board members, financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is a procedural shareholder item: the Toronto Port Lands Company board asks City Council to treat part of the Council meeting as the company's Annual General Meeting of the Shareholder and receive the board-approved 2023 audited financial statements. The company, managed by CreateTO, is the largest landowner in the Port Lands and is advancing the area's long-term vision as a sustainable community, working port and film studio district. City Council is asked to approve the shareholder actions.

title: Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre Annual General Meeting and 2023 Audited Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, boards of management, budgets, financial reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements, boards of directors; boards of governors, budgets and accounts
brief: This is a procedural shareholder item: the Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre board asks City Council, as a shareholder, to adopt and authorize the City Manager to sign the shareholder resolutions attached to its 2023 annual general meeting materials, covering the 2023 operating highlights, financial statements, auditor appointment and board composition. City Council is asked to adopt the resolutions.

title: Toronto Hydro Corporation Annual General Meeting and 2023 Audited Financial Statements
topics: audits, boards of management; auditors; auditors, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural shareholder item: the Toronto Hydro Corporation board asks City Council to treat part of the Council meeting as the corporation's Annual General Meeting of the Shareholder and to approve and adopt the shareholder resolution in Attachment 2. The report, with the 2023 Annual Report attached, satisfies staff's request for key financial highlights and meets the corporate law requirement to hold the annual meeting. City Council is asked to approve the shareholder actions.

title: Toronto Community Housing Corporation - Annual General Meeting and 2023 Audited Consolidated Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, financial reports, social housing; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements, community housing; housing allowance; housing projects; low income housing; non profit housing; non-profit housing; public housing; rent geared to income assistance; rent geared to income housing; rent subsidies; rent supplement; subsidized housing; subsidized rent; subsidized units
brief: This is a procedural shareholder item: Toronto Community Housing's board asks City Council to treat part of the Council meeting as the corporation's Annual General Meeting of the Shareholder, receive its 2023 Annual Report and audited consolidated financial statements, and appoint the 2024 auditor. KPMG audited the 2023 statements and gave an unqualified opinion. City Council is asked to approve the shareholder actions.

title: Lakeshore Arena Corporation - Annual General Meeting and 2023 Audited Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, financial reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is a procedural shareholder item: the Lakeshore Arena Corporation board asks City Council to treat part of the Council meeting as the corporation's Annual General Meeting of the Shareholder, receive its 2023 Annual Report and audited financial statements, and appoint the 2024 auditor. Welch LLP audited the 2023 statements and gave an unqualified opinion that they present fairly. City Council is asked to approve the shareholder actions.

title: Build Toronto Inc. 2023 Annual General Meeting and Audited Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, audits, financial reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements, auditors; auditors
brief: This is a procedural shareholder item: the Build Toronto Inc. board asks City Council to treat part of the Council meeting as the corporation's Annual General Meeting of the Shareholder and receive the board-approved 2023 audited financial statements. Build Toronto supports CreateTO's city-wide real estate mandate, developing City buildings and lands for municipal purposes and advancing Council's public policy goals. City Council is asked to approve the shareholder actions.

title: Governance, Community Benefits Plan, Legacy and Program Advisory Framework, FIFA Fan Festival
topics: community benefits, festivals and special events; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals
brief: This report covers FIFA World Cup 2026 governance, the community benefits plan, legacy and program advisory framework, and the FIFA Fan Festival. Toronto, announced as a host city in June 2022, will stage six matches starting June 12, 2026, including the first-ever men's World Cup match on Canadian soil with Canada's national team. The Executive Director of FIFA World Cup Hosting asks Council to authorize the City Manager to enter agreements with donors and organizations to receive FIFA 2026 funds and report quarterly.

title: Delegation of Development Review Related Authorities
topics: development, housing, zoning bylaws; developing land; development (land); land development, homes; residences, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This report proposes delegating development review approval authorities, building on the 2019 End-to-End Review of the Development Review Process which recommended a new operating model for managing growth. Development review approvals are critical to delivering affordable housing, parkland, economic growth and complete communities. The Interim Chief Planner, General Manager of Toronto Water, Chief Engineer and Executive Director of Development Review ask Council to amend Municipal Code Chapter 41 and delegate the specified authorities.

title: Update on the Reallocation of Funding from the Provincial Upload of the F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Don Valley Parkway
topics: expressways, funding; financing, municipal highways
brief: This is a finance item: the report updates City Council on reallocating funding freed up by the Province's upload of the F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Don Valley Parkway under the December 2023 Ontario-Toronto New Deal. The upload lets about $1.9 billion be reinvested in existing and unfunded City infrastructure priorities over the coming years. The Chief Financial Officer asks Council to endorse the reallocation plan and direct staff to prioritize capital investments.

title: Toronto Water 2024 Capital Budget and 2025-2033 Capital Plan Adjustments
topics: capital budgets, projects;
brief: This is a finance item: the General Manager of Toronto Water asks City Council to authorize reallocating $29.405 million in cashflows and funding within Toronto Water's 2024 Capital Budget and 2025-2033 Capital Plan, to match project accelerations and deferrals. The adjustments have zero net impact on the budget and plan and let Toronto Water keep delivering its capital projects. City Council is asked to authorize the reallocations.

title: 2024 Heads and Beds Levy on Institutions
topics: colleges, correctional institutes, hospitals, taxation, universities; detention centres; jails; penal institutions; penitentiaries, educational institutions, educational institutions
brief: This is a tax item: staff ask City Council to adopt a by-law levying the 2024 "Heads and Beds" tax on colleges, universities, public hospitals and correctional facilities, estimated at about $19.8 million at the legislated rate of $75 per student, bed or resident place — a rate unchanged since 1987. Had the rate kept pace with inflation, it would be $177.81 and raise an extra $27.2 million. The Interim Controller asks Council to authorize the levy.

title: 2024 Levy on Railway Roadways and Rights-of-Way and on Power Utility Transmission and Distribution Corridors
topics: electric distribution utilities, power plants, railways, taxes; electricity distribution utilities; electricity retailers, generation stations; power stations, levies, rail fares; railroads
brief: This is a tax item: staff ask City Council to authorize the 2024 levy on railway roadways and rights-of-way and on power utility transmission and distribution corridors, totalling about $6,996,373 in tax revenue — $6,487,844 municipal and $508,529 provincial education share. The rates are unchanged from 2023, when the levy totalled $6,996,832. The Interim Controller asks Council to authorize the levy and collection under the City of Toronto Act.

title: City of Toronto Reserve and Reserve Fund Balances as at December 31, 2023
topics: reserve funds; reserves and reserve funds
brief: This is a finance item: the report summarizes the City's reserve and reserve fund balances as at December 31, 2023 — funds set aside for future capital needs, obligations, fiscal pressures and revenue shortfalls to smooth tax rate changes. The Chief Financial Officer asks City Council to approve establishing a Toronto Shelter and Support Services Stabilization Reserve in the Municipal Code to fund shelter system pressures. City Council is asked to approve the new reserve.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Four Months Ended April 30, 2024
topics: operating budgets, programs;
brief: This is a finance item: the operating variance report for the four months ended April 30, 2024 gives year-to-date results and year-end projections for the City's tax-supported operations. The Chief Financial Officer asks City Council to approve budget adjustments to the 2024 Approved Operating Budget with no impact on the net budget, and to amend the Fees and Charges by-law. City Council is asked to approve the adjustments.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Four Months Ended April 30, 2024
topics: capital budgets;
brief: This is a finance item: the capital variance report for the four months ended April 30, 2024 gives the City's actual capital spending versus the approved 2024 capital budget and projected year-end expenditures. The Chief Financial Officer asks City Council to approve in-year budget adjustments to the 2024-2033 Capital Budget and Plan and a reallocation of funding sources for the 2022 and 2023 budgets, as detailed in Appendix 3.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Year-Ended December 31, 2023
topics: finance (sc), operating budgets;
brief: This is a finance item: the operating variance report for the year ended December 31, 2023 summarizes the year-end position of the City's tax-supported operations — City operations came in $94.3 million favourable, agencies $60.3 million favourable, and corporate accounts $746.4 million unfavourable. With no further 2023 intergovernmental funding, the Chief Financial Officer asks Council to approve a one-time $739.3 million withdrawal of COVID-19 backstop funding from the Tax Rate Stabilization Reserve to cover the shortfall.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Twelve Months Ended December 31, 2023
topics: capital budgets, financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements
