topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a five-storey stacked townhouse building with 34 residential units and 34 parking spaces at 10-22 Pauline Avenue, replacing a place of worship and surface parking. The proposal is described as appropriately scaled residential intensification. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments.

title: Avenue Road Study - Interim Update and Proposed Site-Specific Road Safety Improvements
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, road safety; ttc
brief: This is an interim update on the Avenue Road Study between Bloor Street West and St. Clair Avenue West, which City Council ordered in 2019 to improve pedestrian safety. Transportation Services has made several changes to the roadway over the past four years and now proposes site-specific near-term measures, including a median between the northbound left-turn lane and centre through lane on Avenue Road between Dupont Street and a point 46 metres south. City Council is asked to endorse the proposed improvements.

title: Construction Staging Area - Richmond Street East and Ontario Street (261-285 Queen Street East, 384-410 Richmond Street East and 90 Ontario Street)
topics: construction, road closures; building, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Transportation Services requests authorization to temporarily close a portion of the southbound curb lane on Ontario Street and part of the cycle track on Richmond Street East for construction staging. Tricon Residential is building 24-storey and 33-storey buildings at 261-285 Queen Street East, 384-410 Richmond Street East and 90 Ontario Street. The closures would run for 19 months, from June 27, 2024 to December 31, 2025.

title: 2161 Yonge Street (Yonge Street and Soudan Avenue) - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
brief: Transportation Services recommends extending the construction staging area closure at 2161 Yonge Street (Yonge and Soudan), where Tribute Communities is building a 35-storey mixed-use building. The closures of parts of the sidewalks and curb lanes on Yonge Street and Soudan Avenue would continue from July 1, 2024 to December 31, 2025. City Council approval is required because Yonge Street is a major arterial street.

title: 309 Cherry Street - Alterations to Heritage Attributes on a Designated Heritage Property Under Part IV, Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage properties, zoning bylaws; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving alterations to the designated heritage property at 309 Cherry Street under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act, with conditions, in connection with a redevelopment that includes four new buildings. The site holds a two-storey 1920 bank building and a 1941 industrial oil storage warehouse. City Council is also asked to authorize entering into a heritage easement agreement.

title: 135 Roxborough Drive - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage districts; historic areas
brief: This is a heritage item: the Acting Senior Manager, Heritage Planning asks City Council to refuse approval for painting the masonry on the east and west facades at 135 Roxborough Drive. The property is C-rated in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District, and the painting does not comply with the district plan or Parks Canada conservation standards. City Council is asked to refuse the alterations.

title: 98 Highland Avenue - Refusal of Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District
topics: heritage properties, planning, urban design; civic improvements, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: This is a heritage item: the Acting Senior Manager, Heritage Planning asks City Council to refuse retroactive approval for windows already installed at 98 Highland Avenue. The property is B-rated in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District, and the new windows detract from the building's character and do not comply with the district plan or Parks Canada conservation standards. City Council is asked to refuse the alterations.

title: 263 Adelaide Street West - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Property Under Part IV, Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, ttc
brief: Staff recommend approving the alteration and partial demolition of heritage attributes at the designated property at 263 Adelaide Street West, under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act, to allow a 49-storey mixed-use building approved by the Ontario Municipal Board in 2017. The plan conserves and alters the front facade of the historic Purman Building. City Council is also asked to approve amending the existing heritage easement agreement.

title: 40 Wabash Avenue - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend including 40 Wabash Avenue (including entrance address at 50 Wabash Avenue) on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register. The property is an early-twentieth century factory and warehouse complex with Edwardian Classical detailing, built in phases between 1910 and 1947 and acquired by the City in 2000. City Council is asked to approve the heritage listing.

title: 321-355 Symington Avenue and 350 Campbell Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal report: the applicants for 321-355 Symington Avenue and 350 Campbell Avenue appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after City Council did not make a decision within the Planning Act timeframe. The proposal is two towers of 36 and 39 storeys with 817 dwelling units, including an Official Plan redesignation from employment to mixed-use lands. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the appeals at the Tribunal in their current forms.

title: 9 Benlamond Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, natural environment, residential properties, rezoning, zoning bylaws; application process, environment; natural heritage systems, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a four-storey residential apartment building with 16 units, nine underground parking spaces and 20 bicycle parking spaces at 9 Benlamond Avenue. The rear portion of the site would be rezoned from Residential to Open Space and Natural Zone, and the building is set back from the Glen Davis Ravine and Environmentally Significant Area. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendment.

title: 135 Isabella Street - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rental housing, zoning bylaws; rental properties; rental units, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a 69-storey residential building with 814 dwelling units at 135 Isabella Street, along with the Rental Housing Demolition application to demolish 80 existing rental units. The proposal includes 80 replacement rental units and a tenant relocation and assistance plan addressing return rights and financial compensation. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law and rental demolition amendments.

title: 191-199 College Street and 74-76 Henry Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a land-use item: the Director, Community Planning, Toronto and East York District asks City Council to approve an Official Plan and zoning amendment for a 31-storey mixed-use building at 191-199 College Street and 74-76 Henry Street. The proposal includes 490 dwelling units with 408 affordable units under the Open Door Affordable Rental Housing Program, plus partially retained three-storey dwellings at 74 and 76 Henry Street. City Council is asked to adopt the amendments.

title: 191-199 College Street and 74-76 Henry Street - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties under Part IV, Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: This is a heritage item: the Acting Senior Manager, Heritage Planning asks City Council to approve alterations to the designated heritage properties at 191-199 College Street and 74-76 Henry Street, with authority to enter into a heritage easement. The Victorian-era semi-detached houses support the historic character of College Street across from the University of Toronto. The alterations would allow construction of a new 31-storey tower on the lands.

title: 25 Borough Drive, Scarborough- Public Art Plan
topics: arts and culture, public art; outdoor art; outdoor sculptures; outdoor statues
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the Public Art Plan for 25 Borough Drive in Scarborough, which sets out how the owner will commission public art within the site's privately owned publicly accessible space. The plan covers the art consultant role, selection strategy, jury composition, mentorship opportunities and budget. Council approval of the plan is required under the Section 37 agreement.

title: 1680 Brimley Road - Public Art Plan
topics: arts and culture, public art; outdoor art; outdoor sculptures; outdoor statues
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the Public Art Plan for 1680 Brimley Road, which sets out how the owner will commission public art within a new privately owned public space on the site. The plan covers the project overview, consultation, location, selection process, mentorship program, budget and schedule. The plan meets the City's Percent for Public Art objectives.

title: 4201 to 4203 Kingston Road and 120 Galloway Road -  Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: multi-unit dwellings, zoning; multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings
brief: Staff recommend approving a 4-storey apartment building with 68 affordable rental units (54 one-bedroom and 14 two-bedroom) at 4201 to 4203 Kingston Road and part of 120 Galloway Road. The site includes 2,076 square metres of Toronto District School Board land added through a consent application. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendment.

title: 3000, 3004, 3008, 3012 and 3020 Kennedy Road - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: townhouses, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend approving the construction of 171 residential units in three-storey stacked and back-to-back townhouse buildings at 3000, 3004, 3008, 3012 and 3020 Kennedy Road, with approximately 17,950 square metres of gross floor area. The plan includes 175 surface parking spaces and 48 bicycle parking spaces across nine blocks. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendment.

title: 528 and 530 Birchmount Road, and 118 and 120 Newlands Avenue - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: residential properties, zoning; residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend amending the Zoning By-law to allow four existing single detached homes at 528 and 530 Birchmount Road and 118 and 120 Newlands Avenue to be redeveloped into nine new single detached dwellings on smaller lots, subject to a future consent application to sever the lands. The proposal is consistent with the Provincial Policy Statement and the City's Official Plan. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendment.

title: Dedication as Public Highway of Starfire Drive Extension (25 Starfire Drive and 50 Scarboro Road) and Authority to Allocate Funds to Complete Road Works
topics: development, residential properties; developing land; development (land); land development, residential real estate
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Jennifer McKelvie to dedicate the Starfire Drive extension (at 25 Starfire Drive and 50 Scarboro Road) as a public highway and authorize funds to complete the remaining road works. The extension was required under a 2012 consent agreement, but the former owner did not finish the topcoat asphalt, curbs and sidewalks. City Council is asked to approve the dedication and funding.

title: Lawrence Avenue East and Danielle Moore Circle/Private Driveway - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic control systems, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Services supports installing new traffic control signals at the new intersection of Lawrence Avenue East and Danielle Moore Circle/Private Driveway, required as a condition of the development approval at 2740 Lawrence Avenue East. The existing midblock signals on Lawrence Avenue East, 55 metres west of Marcos Boulevard, would be removed. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Lawrence Avenue East.

title: Brimley Road and McNicoll Avenue - Intersection Safety Review
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, intersections, road operations, safety; public safety, road services, ttc
brief: Transportation Services recommends prohibiting eastbound right turns on a red signal at all times at the intersection of Brimley Road and McNicoll Avenue, along with refreshed signs and pavement markings. Scarborough Community Council had directed a safety and operations review of the intersection. City Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on both streets.

title: 2265 Victoria Park Avenue - Application for a Clothing Drop Box Location permit
topics: applications, clothing drop boxes; application process, clothes donation boxes; clothing bins
brief: This is a permit decision item: Municipal Licensing and Standards refused a Clothing Drop Box Location permit for 2265 Victoria Park Avenue, and the matter is before City Council. City Council can either deny the application, upholding the refusal, or approve the permit. The decision rests with City Council.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will review the Order Paper at the June 26, 2024 meeting. No decision is attached.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions and announcements will be made at the June 26, 2024 City Council meeting. No decision is attached.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council may file petitions at the June 26, 2024 meeting. No decision is attached.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council will declare any interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act at the June 26, 2024 meeting. No other business is attached to this item.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from the Mayor and City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council introduces the committee reports and new business from the Mayor and City officials for the June 26, 2024 meeting. Reports come from the Executive Committee, Board of Health, Economic and Community Development Committee, General Government Committee, Infrastructure and Environment Committee, and Planning and Housing Committee. No decision is attached beyond introducing the reports.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will confirm the minutes from its regular meeting held on May 22 and 23, 2024. No other business is attached to this item.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Council meeting on June 26, 2024 opens with O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is attached.

title: Community Housing Sector Modernization and Growth Strategy
topics: affordable housing, community & life (sc), social housing; affordable homes; housing projects, community housing; housing allowance; housing projects; low income housing; non profit housing; non-profit housing; public housing; rent geared to income assistance; rent geared to income housing; rent subsidies; rent supplement; subsidized housing; subsidized rent; subsidized units
brief: Staff propose a Community Housing Sector Modernization and Growth Strategy, creating a new regulatory and funding framework for the non-market housing sector (non-profit housing, co-ops, Indigenous housing providers, TCHC and the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation). The strategy would modernize service agreements and funding for Part VII.1 housing projects under Ontario Regulation 367/11. City Council is asked to authorize the Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat to enter into the new agreements.

title: Launching the Rental Housing Supply Program
topics: affordable housing, rental housing; affordable homes; housing projects, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff propose launching a Rental Housing Supply Program to address Toronto's two housing crises: a shortage of deeply affordable and supportive housing for low-income residents, and rising rents pushing middle-income earners and key workers out of the city. The program would help the City hit its approved rent-controlled, affordable and rent-geared-to-income rental housing targets. City Council is asked to approve the program and authorize the Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat to implement it.

title: Renovictions Policy Implementation: Review of Hamilton Renovation Licence and Tenant Relocation By-law and developing a Toronto Renovictions By-law
topics: housing, rental housing; homes; residences, rental properties; rental units
brief: This report starts work on a Toronto renoviction by-law: staff are asked to review Hamilton's Renovation Licence and Tenant Relocation By-law and develop a Toronto version. The HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan commits the City to protecting tenants and preserving affordable rental homes, and renovictions are eroding the existing affordable rental supply. City Council is asked to direct the Chief Building Official and Housing Secretariat staff to develop the by-law.

title: Strategic Opportunity at 267 and 275 Merton Street
topics: city-owned properties, rental housing, strategic plans; city owned properties; city properties, rental properties; rental units, strategic planning; strategy
brief: Staff report a strategic opportunity to leverage City-owned land at 275 Merton Street to create new purpose-built rental homes, with a minimum target of 30% affordable rental homes. CreateTO has negotiated a development partnership with Collecdev-Markee Limited Partnership covering both the City site and the adjacent privately owned 267 Merton Street. City Council is asked to authorize the Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management to negotiate and execute the agreement of purchase and sale.

title: Modular Housing Initiative Phase 2: Update Report, and Amendments to Purchase Order Numbers 6052027 and 6052881 issued to NRB Inc. for Design-Build Services for Supportive Housing
topics: affordable housing, housing; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences
brief: This is an update on the Modular Housing Initiative Phase 2, launched in April 2020 to rapidly create at least 250 rent-geared-to-income and supportive homes using modular construction. Staff request authority to amend purchase orders 6052027 and 6052881 issued to NRB Inc. so the City can restart and complete the projects at 175 Cummer Avenue and 39 Dundalk Drive. Four of the five projects have already been tenanted.

title: 2444 Eglinton Avenue East - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: high rise buildings, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, tall buildings
brief: Staff recommend approving a three-tower mixed-use development at 2444 Eglinton Avenue East: a 31-storey condominium with 307 units, plus two co-op buildings of 19 and 41 storeys with 612 co-op units (306 market co-op and 306 affordable co-op). The towers sit on podiums containing above-grade parking and ground-floor non-residential uses. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendment.

title: Villiers Island Precinct - City-Initiated Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: affordable housing, housing, rezoning; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend a City-initiated Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendment to enable the revitalization of the Port Lands, starting with Villiers Island — the first mixed-use residential community in the area, which will receive a permanent Indigenous name in fall 2024. The precinct plan covers lands on Villiers Street, Commissioners Street, Cherry Street, Polson Street and Munitions Street. The area is planned for housing at all levels of affordability, community infrastructure, and continued employment uses including film and port industries.

title: 522 University Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate 522 University Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The property holds a 15-storey Modernist office building constructed between 1971 and 1974, designed by architect John C. Parkin for the National Life Assurance Company of Canada. This is the first step in the designation process.

title: 2024 Toronto Heritage Grant Awards
topics: programs, subsidies and grants; financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs
brief: Staff recommend approving ten grants totalling $317,000 under the 2024 Toronto Heritage Grant Program, covering heritage properties such as 288 Annette Street. The grants fund up to 50% of eligible heritage conservation work on designated residential or tax-exempt properties and are expected to generate about $706,926 in private investment. City Council is asked to approve the grant awards.

title: 8 and 10 Hyde Park Circle - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: development, official plan amendments, rezoning; developing land; development (land); land development, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: This is a legal directions item: City Planning asks City Council to direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the applicant's appeal for 8 and 10 Hyde Park Circle. The applicant sought to build a 4-storey, 55-unit residential building and appealed in February 2024 after Council missed the Planning Act decision deadline. City Council is asked to authorize opposing the appeal and continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: 77 Erskine Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Application - Appeal Report
topics: demolitions, residential properties, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: This is an appeal report: the applicant for 77 Erskine Avenue appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on February 26, 2024 after City Council did not make a decision. The proposal is a 35-storey residential building with 377 units, including 37 replacement rental units. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the application while continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: 19 Poyntz Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, residential properties, zoning bylaws; residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a three-storey (11.43-metre) residential building with eight dwelling units at 19 Poyntz Avenue, with a gross floor area of 839.12 square metres. The proposal is described as missing-middle rental housing near an existing subway station. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments.

title: 1802 Bayview Avenue - Official Plan Amendment - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: development, official plan amendments, residential properties; developing land; development (land); land development, residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend refusing the Official Plan Amendment application at 1802 Bayview Avenue, which sought to move the lands from the Secondary Zone to the Station Area Core of the Yonge-Eglinton Secondary Plan to facilitate a 46-storey residential building with 419 units. City Council is asked to refuse the application and direct the City Solicitor to oppose any appeal to the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 12 - 14, 18, 20 Bentworth Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, residential properties, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend approving a 9-storey residential building with up to 136 dwelling units at 12-14, 18 and 20 Bentworth Avenue, replacing the existing buildings. The approval would come with a Holding (H) provision, meaning certain conditions must be addressed before the zoning takes effect. City Council is asked to approve the Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendments.

title: Downsview Park Boulevard at Keele Street - Exclusive Right-Turn Lane Designation
topics: high occupancy vehicle lanes, traffic calming measures, turn prohibitions (traffic); diamond lanes; hov lanes; multi-occupancy lanes, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Transportation Services recommends designating the northerly westbound lane on Downsview Park Boulevard, between Keele Street and a point 30.5 metres east, for westbound right-turns only. The TTC operates transit service on this street, so City Council approval is required. The lane designation is meant to define lane usage and reduce confusion for drivers.

title: 7 - 15 Steeles Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws, zoning designations; permitted use requests; permitted uses, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a land-use item: the Director, Community Planning, North York District asks City Council to refuse the Official Plan and zoning amendment applications for 7-15 Steeles Avenue East. The proposal would allow a 50-storey mixed-use building with 683 dwelling units at 18.93 times the lot area, which staff found inconsistent with the Provincial Policy Statement and not conforming to the Growth Plan or the Official Plan. City Council is asked to refuse the applications and authorize the City Solicitor to oppose them.

title: 172-202 Drewry Avenue - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: construction, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; building, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving 45 new three-storey townhouse units in six blocks at 172-202 Drewry Avenue, with a total gross floor area of 7,476 square metres and two parking spaces per unit. The proposal includes a new 617 square metre public park on the southeast corner of the site. City Council is asked to approve the Zoning By-law amendment.

title: Don Mills Road (The Donway in the north to The Donway in the south) - Community Safety Zone
topics: community safety, safety; public safety
brief: Councillor Jon Burnside asks City Council to designate a community safety zone on Don Mills Road between the south and north intersections of The Donway West and The Donway East, in effect at all times. Residents raised concerns about speeding near the Lawrence Avenue East intersection, close to several schools including Norman Ingram and Greenland public schools. The safety zone allows for higher fines to deter speeding.

title: Requesting Alignment of the Independent Electricity System Operator Integrated Regional Resource Plan with the City’s 2040 Target of Net Zero Greenhouse Gas Emissions - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: electricity generation utilities, greenhouse effect; greenhouse gas emissions, hydroelectricity utilities
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe asking City Council to request that the Independent Electricity System Operator align its Integrated Regional Resource Plan for Toronto's electricity system with the City's 2040 net zero greenhouse gas emissions target, adopted in 2021 through the TransformTO strategy. The City and Toronto Hydro are already engaging with the system operator on the plan. Alignment is needed so energy planning supports the City's climate goals.

title: Supporting the City of Toronto in Joining the Strong Cities Network and Hosting a Future Strong Cities Summit in October 2025 - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: municipalities, organizations; boroughs; cities; counties; regional municipalities; towns, corporate bodies
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor James Pasternak asking City Council to have the City Manager apply for Toronto to join the Strong Cities Network, a global network of more than 220 cities working against hate, extremism and polarisation. This follows Council's November 2023 endorsement of the network's summit declaration. The motion also asks Economic Development to report by the end of 2024 on hosting a Strong Cities Summit in October 2025.

title: Request to Rename an Existing or Planned Community Garden After the Late Estella Wheeler - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: community gardens, memorials; monuments; permanent memorials
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor James Pasternak to honour the late Estella Wheeler, a Toronto District School Board teacher who died in February 2024 as a victim of domestic violence. The motion asks City Council to direct Parks, Forestry and Recreation, in consultation with Economic Development and Culture, to look for opportunities to name or rename a new or existing community garden after Mrs. Wheeler, a beloved teacher at the Africentric Alternative School and other schools since immigrating to Canada in 2008.

title: Honouring the Late Councillor Jaye Robinson by Naming a Landmark or Site in Don Valley West - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: councillors, memorials; aldermen; alderwomen; city councellors; city councillors; council members; councilors; members of council, monuments; permanent memorials
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor James Pasternak to honour the late Councillor Jaye Robinson, who died May 16, 2024 after serving Don Valley West for over 14 years, including as TTC Chair from 2018 to 2022. The motion asks City Council to direct Parks, Forestry and Recreation and Transportation staff to find opportunities to name or rename an existing or planned landmark or site after Robinson, a champion of the tree canopy, parks and Vision Zero road safety.

title: Requesting the Province to Support Family Physicians - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: doctors; physicians
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe asking City Council to call on the provincial Minister of Health to act on the family physician shortage: properly compensate family doctors with fee increases and reduce the administrative burden the Province places on them. The motion notes the shortage has reached a crisis point, with hundreds of thousands of Torontonians lacking a family doctor. Health care is a provincial responsibility.

title: Seeking Council Direction to Conclude Negotiations between Ontario Tennis Association and the City of Toronto for the building of a Multi-purpose Sports Complex in the Allen East District - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor James Pasternak asking City Council to direct the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer to bring forward a Municipal Capital Facility designation for the Ontario Tennis Association's multi-purpose sports complex in the Allen East District. The 2021 Allen East District Plan contemplated the Tennis Association building the facility at its own cost on City-owned land east of Allen Road, and a land lease is being negotiated. Council direction is needed on the capital facility designation, a daycare and a public access agreement.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2023.TE6.16 - 170 Roehampton Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval to Move Forward With Rental Housing at 170 Roehampton Avenue - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Josh Matlow to amend Council's 2023 approval of the 170 Roehampton Avenue rental housing demolition, which required site plan approval and excavation permits before the 15 rental units could be demolished. The applicant wants to demolish the units sooner than the development timeline allows. The motion asks Council to delete the timing pre-conditions so demolition can move forward while the rest of the approval stands.

title: Non-Competitive Bridge Contract with Kodiak Group Holdings Co. Operating as Work Authority for Various Safety Footwear - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: This is a procurement item: Councillor Jon Burnside asks City Council to authorize an extension of the non-competitive bridging contract with Kodiak Group Holdings (Work Authority) for safety footwear, occupational footwear and galoshes for City employees. The current 12-month bridge contract, approved in May 2023, was for $1,985,502 covering June 2023 to July 2024. Council is asked to grant authority for the Fire Chief and General Manager to extend the arrangement.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.CC17.5 - 151 and 161-181 Mulock Avenue and 6 Lloyd Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Frances Nunziata to reopen and amend Council's April 17, 2024 settlement decision on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 151 and 161-181 Mulock Avenue and 6 Lloyd Avenue. The motion would delete a pre-condition requiring the owner, at its own expense, to start the Metrolinx Deviation Process with Metrolinx and AECOM before any Tribunal order is issued — a condition the applicant says may be unnecessary. City Council is asked to amend its previous decision.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Toronto Police Service Board - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded Councillor Amber Morley
topics: appointments, police services; police; policing
brief: This is an appointments item: Councillor Shelley Carroll recommends that City Council rescind the appointment of Nadine Spencer to the Toronto Police Service Board and appoint Chris Brillinger instead, for a term ending November 14, 2026. Brillinger worked for the City for 31 years, including nine as Executive Director of Social Development, Finance and Administration, and now leads Family Services Toronto. City Council is asked to approve the change.

title: Review of Traffic Impacts of Ontario Place Redevelopment and Proposed Ontario Science Centre Relocation - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: redevelopment, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: This is a member motion from Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asking for a staff analysis of traffic impacts on Lake Shore Boulevard West from the Ontario Place redevelopment, including the Therme spa, Live Nation renovations and the relocated Ontario Science Centre. Lake Shore Boulevard already carries heavy traffic and sits near Exhibition Place events like the CNE, Honda Indy and Caribbean Carnival that generate peak congestion. The motion asks Transportation Services to summarize the anticipated traffic impacts.

title: Authorization to provide property tax relief for community non-profit affordable rental housing at 26 Maynard Avenue - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: social housing, tax reduction; community housing; housing allowance; housing projects; low income housing; non profit housing; non-profit housing; public housing; rent geared to income assistance; rent geared to income housing; rent subsidies; rent supplement; subsidized housing; subsidized rent; subsidized units, tax assistance; tax decrease; tax rebate; tax refunds; tax relief
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Gord Perks to provide property tax relief for the 15-unit affordable rental building at 26 Maynard Avenue, owned by the non-profit Neighbourhood Land Trust. In 2019 Council approved financial assistance for the Trust's acquisition, renovation and operation of the property as affordable rental housing. The motion asks Council to authorize a municipal capital facility agreement granting the tax exemption.

title: 2267 Dundas Street West - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: appeals, hearings;
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Gord Perks asking City Council to authorize the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to uphold the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of the 2267 Dundas Street West application. The Committee refused the owner's request on June 5, 2024 to convert a three-storey mixed-use semi-detached building into five residential units, citing concerns including the loss of retail space. The owner appealed on June 24, 2024.

title: Construction Management Agreement for the creation of Chimney Swift Replacement Habitat in Budd Sugarman Park - 906 Yonge Street and 25 McMurrich Street - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe to protect Chimney Swifts, a species at risk, at the 906 Yonge Street and 25 McMurrich Street development site. The Ontario Land Tribunal approved the zoning change in January 2024, and the developer found the swift habitat in an existing chimney slated for removal. Under the Endangered Species Act, replacement habitat must be built first. The motion asks Council to authorize a construction management agreement to build two chimney swift habitats in Budd Sugarman Park.

title: 222 Rosedale Heights Drive - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: appeals, committees of adjustment, municipal officials; city officials, committee of adjustment
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe asking City Council to direct the City Solicitor to appeal the Committee of Adjustment's approval of minor variances at 222 Rosedale Heights Drive and oppose the development at the Toronto Local Appeal Body. On June 11, 2024, the Committee approved three variances to alter a two-storey detached dwelling. The motion also seeks authority to retain outside consultants and negotiate a settlement.

title: Direction to Install a Pride-Coloured Pedestrian Crossing near University of St. Michael’s College - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: festivals and special events, pedestrian crossovers; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals, cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe to have Transportation Services paint a rainbow Pride pedestrian crossing near the University of St. Michael's College. The University requested the crosswalk between the John M. Kelly Library and Elmsley Place on St. Joseph Street and has committed to covering all costs. The motion is urgent because Pride celebrations are approaching.

title: Toronto International Pizza Festival - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: festivals and special events, food festivals; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals, summerlicious; winterlicious
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Mike Colle proposing that the City host the first-ever Toronto International Pizza Festival to support small businesses, Business Improvement Areas and the city's food scene. Toronto's street festivals and food events already draw hundreds of thousands of visitors. The motion asks the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture to report back at the July 24-26, 2024 Council meeting on the festival idea.

title: Authorization to Repatriate Two Specified Objects from the City of Toronto’s Museum Collection to the Métis National Council - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: museums (facilities);
brief: This is a member motion from Mayor Olivia Chow to repatriate two objects from the City's museum collection to the Métis National Council, following a formal repatriation claim from August 2023. The objects are a beaded tobacco pouch in traditional Métis style dating to about 1890, and a letter from Louis Riel's era that research showed to be a period forgery but remains part of his story. The motion asks Council to direct staff to return the objects during the Back to Batoche Days event.

title: 2057 Dundas Street West - Liquor Licence Application - High Notes Coffee and Vinyl Licence 2554413 - by Councillor Gord Perks seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Gord Perks about a liquor licence application for High Notes Coffee and Vinyl at 2057 Dundas Street West, near residential units. Community concerns include noise, litter and safety. The motion asks City Council to advise the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that the licence is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing residents' concerns are attached.

title: Dogs Off Leash Area Criteria for Commercial Dog Walkers - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: dog off-leash areas, dogs; dog parks; dogs off leash parks; dogs off-leash parks; leash free areas; leash free dog walking areas; leash free parks; leash free zones; leash-free areas; leash-free dog walking areas; leash-free zones; off leash areas; off leash parks
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe asking City Council to have Parks, Forestry and Recreation develop criteria for which dogs off-leash areas should be open to commercial dog walkers, who handle multiple dogs at a time. The 2023 citywide off-leash strategy did not address commercial dog walkers, and their use of some areas can create conflicts. The criteria and list of acceptable sites would come as part of the citywide Dogs Off-Leash Area report due in the third quarter of 2024.

title: 17 Boothroyd Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: appeals;
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Paula Fletcher asking City Council to direct the City Solicitor to appeal the Committee of Adjustment's decisions on 17 Boothroyd Avenue and attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose them. The applications sought to sever the property into two undersized lots and build three-storey detached dwellings with variances on lot frontage. The motion asks the City Solicitor to oppose the severance and variances with City staff support.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from Various Developments to Community Matters Toronto for Mural Art on Bell Utility Boxes in Eglinton-Lawrence - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: funding, urban beautification; 20-minute makeover; beautification projects; clean & beautiful city; clean and beautiful city; clean city beautiful city; community clean-up days; facade improvement; mural program; neighbourhood beautification, financing
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Mike Colle to release $28,000 in Section 37 funds to Community Matters Toronto for 14 murals on Bell utility boxes in Ward 8, Eglinton-Lawrence. The Bell Box Murals Project has painted utility boxes across Toronto since 2009, replacing graffiti with original art. The motion asks Council to increase the 2024 Non-Program Operating Budget by $28,000, fully funded by Section 37 funds from various developments.

title: 65 Front St West - Temporary Outdoor Patio During "Union Summer" Event - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: street occupation permits; curblane permits; road use permits; street closure permits; streets and sidewalks
brief: This is a member motion from Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik to allow the Union Chicken patio at 65 Front Street West to take part in the Union Summer event outside Union Station. An exemption is needed from the 10-metre extended liquor licence adjacency rule because the approval process changed when responsibility transferred to the City. City Council is asked to exempt the temporary liquor licence extension application for the patio.

title: Towards a Beautiful City - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
topics: urban design; civic improvements
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Josh Matlow, titled Towards a Beautiful City, seeking unified public realm design standards across City divisions and the public portions of private developments. The motion cites broken bike lane posts, construction hoarding around patios and overflowing garbage cans as signs of a mediocre public realm. It also explores creating a City Architect and Designer position to raise design quality across the city.

title: An Update on Work to Protect the Science Centre and Support Thorncliffe and Flemingdon Park - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: public properties; public buildings; public property; public sector buildings; public streets
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Josh Matlow asking for an update on the City's work to protect the Ontario Science Centre and support Thorncliffe and Flemingdon Park. The Province announced plans to move the Science Centre to a smaller Ontario Place site without consulting local residents, who rely on it for jobs and education; the area is also expecting the Eglinton Crosstown's Science Centre station. The motion asks the City Manager to report to the July 16, 2024 Executive Committee.

title: Review of Major Events Policy - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: festivals and special events; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Paul Ainslie proposing a review of the City's financial support system for major events and attractions. The review would explore moving from the current annual application process to predictable, ongoing annual support to give organizers stability for long-term planning. The motion asks the Chief Financial Officer and the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture to report back to the October 23, 2024 meeting.

title: 290 Lake Promenade - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: appeals;
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Amber Morley asking City Council to direct the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the owner's appeal regarding 290 Lake Promenade. The Committee of Adjustment refused the owner's application on April 11, 2024 for a new detached dwelling with variances on floor space, height and balconies. The motion also seeks authority for the City Solicitor to try to negotiate a resolution.

title: 15 and 35 Trehorne Drive Encroachment Agreement - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: encroachments;
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Stephen Holyday about the former Scarlett Heights high school site at 15 Trehorne Drive, which the Toronto District School Board declared surplus and the Catholic board wants to acquire for a new high school. New property lines are being drawn to separate the former high school from Hilltop Middle School at 35 Trehorne Drive. The motion asks City Council to have Transportation Services negotiate an encroachment agreement to keep a private manhole in the municipal boulevard.

title: Fostering Belonging, Community and Inclusion, and Combating Hate in Toronto - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, Councillor Mike Colle, Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, and Councillor Amber Morley
topics: community outreach, community safety, racial discrimination; anti-racism; racism, awareness programs; community engagement; outreach; promotion (communication); public outreach
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Mayor Chow and others, to foster belonging, community and inclusion and to combat hate in Toronto. The motion cites a troubling pattern of social isolation in the Toronto Foundation's Vital Signs report and the need for all Torontonians to feel safe from hate. It asks City Council to direct the Executive Director of Social Development, the Director of Equity, Diversity and Human Rights, and the Chief Communications Officer to act on the recommendations.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from Various Developments to Support Toronto Transit Commission Station Upgrades in Ward 11, University-Rosedale - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: funding, subway stations; financing
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe to release $915,000 in dormant Section 37 funds earmarked in 1999, 2007 and 2008 for TTC subway station improvements in Ward 11, University-Rosedale. Council's May 2024 decision unlocked these forgotten funds, which can now go toward TTC station priorities. The motion asks Council to increase the 2024 TTC Operating Budget by $915,000, fully funded by the Section 37 money from the 86-100 Bloor Street West development.

title: 14 Lacewood Crescent - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: committees of adjustment, construction; building, committee of adjustment
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Jon Burnside asking City Council to authorize the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body hearing on August 26, 2024 to uphold the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of a three-storey detached dwelling proposal at 14 Lacewood Crescent. The Committee refused the application on April 25, 2024 over height and massing concerns, and the owner appealed on May 13, 2024. The motion also seeks authority to retain outside consultants.

title: Request to Implement Measures for Mandatory Lead Disclosure and Mitigation in Multi-Residential Housing - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: lead (contaminant), lead levels; lead in soil
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe asking City Council to have Municipal Licensing and Standards report on requiring landlords of multi-residential buildings to disclose and mitigate lead risks. Lead poisoning endangers children and pregnant people, and landlords currently have no obligation to replace dangerous lead pipes on their properties. The motion asks for options on mandatory lead disclosure and mitigation to be reported to the December 5, 2024 Planning and Housing Committee.

title: Ensuring Increased Access for All Toronto Residents to the Toronto Islands While Saving Toronto Taxpayers Money - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
topics: bridges, ferries, pedestrian bridges; ferry boats; ferryboats, footbridges; pedestrian overpasses
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Jon Burnside asking City staff to study a fixed link — such as a bridge — to the Toronto Islands as an alternative to replacing the City's four aging ferries, whose replacement costs have skyrocketed. An area east of Ward's Island is only 250 metres from the Port Lands and could provide reliable year-round access for pedestrians, cyclists and emergency vehicles. The motion asks two Deputy City Managers to report on the cost of a fixed link versus continuing with ferries.

title: Amending Item 2022.TE34.40 to Secure Affordable Housing at 888 Dupont Street - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: affordable housing, housing; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe to amend Council's 2022 approval of the 888 Dupont Street redevelopment to secure the 20 affordable rental housing units promised as a Section 37 community benefit. The 14-storey mixed-use building approval included the affordable units and 2,028 square metres of non-residential uses. The motion adds a condition tied to a Committee of Adjustment minor variance application to make sure the affordable housing is delivered.

title: Permitting a Seasonal Outdoor Patio at 460 Adelaide Street East - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: street occupation permits; curblane permits; road use permits; street closure permits; streets and sidewalks
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise to permit the owner or tenant of a ground-floor retail unit in Toronto Standard Condominium Corporation 2756 to operate a seasonal outdoor patio on part of the privately owned publicly accessible space at 424-460 Adelaide Street East. The patio would operate on a temporary basis until October 15, 2025, on space secured through a 2015 Section 37 agreement. City Council is asked to grant the permission.

title: Re-Opening and Rescinding Council’s Decision on Item 2024.MM16.28 - Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Revitalize Trans Flag-Coloured Pedestrian Crossings in the Village - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: funding, lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgendered, reserve funds; financing, gay community; glbt; homosexual; lgbt; queer; transexual; transgendered; two spirited, reserves and reserve funds
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise to rescind Council's earlier decision releasing Section 37 funds to revitalize the trans flag-coloured pedestrian crossings in the Village. The Church Wellesley Village Business Improvement Area no longer needs the funds because Transportation Services touched up the paint on the trans flag and rainbow crosswalks before this year's Pride Festival. Council is asked to rescind item 2024.MM16.28.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Toronto District School Board for Schoolyard Improvements at Dewson Street Junior Public School - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: funding, reserve funds, schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, financing, reserves and reserve funds
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Alejandra Bravo to contribute $100,000 in Section 37 funds from the development at 871 to 899 College Street toward the Dewson Street Junior Public School schoolyard revitalization. The improvements include a multi-use sports court, track and field, new playground and outdoor learning spaces; the schoolyard serves as the local playground for the wider community. The motion asks Council to increase the 2024 Operating Budget by $100,000, fully funded by the Section 37 funds.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 192A, 194, and 200 Bloor Street West to Support Annex Heritage Conservation - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: funding, heritage conservation districts, reserve funds; financing, heritage districts; historic areas, reserves and reserve funds
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe to release $230,895 in Section 37 funds from the development at 192A, 194 and 200 Bloor Street West to fund the West Annex Phase II Heritage Conservation Study. The funds were originally earmarked in 2010 but never released, and Council's May 2024 decision unlocked them. The motion asks Council to increase the 2024 City Planning Operating Budget by $230,895, fully funded by the Section 37 money.

title: Amending Item 2021.MM37.24 - Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 587 to 599 Yonge Street Development to the 519 Community Centre for Capital Improvements - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: community centres, funding, reserve funds; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, financing, reserves and reserve funds
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise to amend Council's earlier decision releasing Section 37 funds to The 519 Community Centre for capital improvements. The 519's board has adjusted its capital plan and wants flexibility in how the funds are used, while still honouring its commitment to move garbage storage to the back of the building. The motion asks Council to delete the specific-use wording so the centre can adjust its plans.

title: Strengthening and Improving the City-Wide Approach to Youth Violence Interventions - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: abuse, youth; adolescents, assault; domestic violence; violence
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Vincent Crisanti asking City Council to strengthen the city-wide approach to youth violence interventions, citing a troubling increase in gun violence affecting Ward 1 and other communities. The motion asks that the upcoming SafeTO Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan report include an update on multi-sector community and youth violence prevention and intervention efforts. The City is working with community partners and other governments on violence prevention, intervention, response and recovery.

title: Supporting the Special Hockey International Tournament Coming to Toronto in 2026 - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: sports, sports tournaments; tournaments
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor James Pasternak asking City Council to explore how the City can support the Special Hockey International Tournament coming to Toronto in March 2026. The tournament, previously hosted in Toronto in 2019, expects about 60 teams from Canada, the United States and England, playing at Scotiabank Pond Arena and Chesswood Arena on March 5-7, 2026. The motion asks the Deputy City Manager to report on ways the City can assist the organizers.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 905 Don Mills Road for Park Improvements at Don Mills Collegiate Institute - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: development, playground equipment; developing land; development (land); land development, park equipment; play apparatus; play equipment; play structures
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Jon Burnside to release $90,000 in Section 37 funds from the development at 905 Don Mills Road to the Toronto District School Board for stationary fitness equipment at Don Mills Collegiate Institute. The school is rejuvenating its facilities, and the equipment would serve all ages including seniors. The motion asks Council to increase the 2024 Operating Budget by $90,000, fully funded by the Section 37 funds, once the school board signs a Community Access Agreement.

title: Impact of Bill 165 and Gas Utility Use of Public Property in Toronto
topics: energy infrastructure, greenhouse effect, utilities; greenhouse gas emissions, hydro property, power utilties
brief: This is an information item: the Executive Director, Environment and Climate reports on the impact of provincial Bill 165 and natural gas utility use of public property in Toronto. Natural gas causes over half of Toronto's annual greenhouse gas emissions, and the TransformTO strategy targets rapid reductions toward net zero by 2040. City Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Circular Economy Road Map Strategy and Implementation Plan Development Update
topics: environment (sc), environmental incentive programs, solid waste management; green rebate program; toilet replacement programs; washer rebate programs; water rebate program; watersaver programs, solid waste management planning; swm; waste management
brief: This is an information item: the General Manager, Solid Waste Management Services and the Executive Director, Environment and Climate update City Council on developing a 10-year Circular Economy Road Map strategy and implementation plan. The interim report describes the project governance, building on the 2021 TransformTO Net Zero Strategy, and upcoming community engagement. City Council is asked to authorize the two divisions to share previously granted authorities.

title: ReNew Golden Mile Environmental Assessment - Interim Report
topics: Master Plans, Secondary Plans, environmental assessments; ea; ecological assessment; environmental assessment; environmental evaluation
brief: This is a transportation item: the General Manager, Transportation Services asks City Council to endorse the preliminary recommended alignments and designs for the ReNew Golden Mile Environmental Assessment. The study builds on the 2020 Golden Mile Secondary Plan and covers Eglinton Avenue East and Craigton Drive between Victoria Park Avenue and Birchmount Road. City Council is asked to endorse the designs so staff can complete the mandatory phase 3 public consultation and report back.

title: On-Street Logistics Mini-Hub on St. George Street -  Pilot Update and Next Steps
topics: mail services, pilot projects, transportation; courier services; mail rooms; mailrooms, transportation services
brief: This is a transportation item: the General Manager, Transportation Services asks City Council to make the On-Street Logistics Mini-Hub a permanent program. The 18-month pilot placed a repurposed shipping container in a St. George Street parking layby, operated by Purolator, as a redistribution centre for e-bike deliveries and customer pick-ups near the University of Toronto campus. City Council is asked to approve the permanent program concept.

title: Cycling Network Plan -  2024 Cycling Infrastructure and Missing Sidewalk Installation - Third Quarter Update
topics: cycling, sidewalks, transportation; bicycling, transportation services
brief: This is a transportation item: the General Manager, Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize 2024 bikeway installations from the Cycling Network Plan's 2022-2024 program, plus one missing sidewalk project and a by-law adjustment. The projects include a uni-directional cycle track on Avenue Road from Bloor Street West to Davenport Road and a bi-directional track on Elm Ridge Drive. City Council is asked to authorize the installations.

title: Cycling Network Plan Update (2025 - 2027)
topics: bikeway networks, congestion, cycling, road networks; bicycle facilities; bicycle routes; bike routes; bikeway routes; bikeways; cycling routes; shared roadways; signed routes, bicycling, gridlock, road infrastructure; street network
brief: This is a transportation item: the General Manager, Transportation Services asks City Council to endorse in principle the 2025-2027 Near-Term Implementation Program for the Cycling Network Plan. The plan aims to connect gaps, grow into new areas and renew existing routes for safety, building on the 2022-2024 program. City Council is asked to endorse the bikeway projects as the focus of the cycling budget.

title: Pickering Town Line Agreement
topics: agreements, road maintenance, transportation; roads maintenance; sidewalk maintenance; sidewalks maintenance; summer maintenance; winter maintenance, tenancy agreements, transportation services
brief: This is a transportation item: the General Manager, Transportation Services asks City Council to approve negotiating a new cost-sharing agreement with the City of Pickering for the Pickering Town Line road. The 2.75-kilometre road between Finch Avenue East and Steeles Avenue East is jointly shared, and the old agreement expired January 1, 2023. City Council is asked to grant authority to negotiate, enter into and execute the agreement.

title: De Havilland 'Mossie' Park Underground Storage Tank
topics: basement flooding, stormwater detention tanks, stormwater management, stormwater storage tunnels; basement flood cleanup; basement flooding response, storm water management; swm; wet weather flow management
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor James Pasternak about the De Havilland 'Mossie' Park underground storage tank project in Ward 6, stemming from the 2012 basement flooding environmental assessment. The project was found to meet the cost threshold for detailed design, but has no planned construction start year. The motion asks City Council to direct the General Manager of Toronto Water to report on when detailed design will be completed and construction will begin, and proposes an alternative solution for local basement flooding.

title: Authority to Ban Natural Gas in Toronto
topics: confidentiality, municipal officials, natural gas; city officials
brief: This is a confidential directions item: the City Solicitor asks City Council to keep confidential the solicitor-client advice in Confidential Attachment 1 on the City's authority to ban natural gas in Toronto. The item supplements the Environment and Climate Division's report on fuel utilities requested by Council in March. City Council is asked to direct that the attachment remain confidential.

title: Financial Plan for the City of Toronto's Municipal Drinking Water License Renewal
topics: licences, regulations, water; licenses; licensing
brief: This is a finance item: the General Manager of Toronto Water and the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer ask City Council to approve the Financial Plan for the City's Municipal Drinking Water System. The plan is required under Ontario Regulation 453/07 for renewal of the drinking water licence, which expires January 29, 2025. City Council is asked to approve the plan for submission to the Ontario government.

title: Revised Free-Floating Car-Share Program
topics: city drivers, municipal codes, transportation; city driver, transportation services
brief: This is a regulatory item: the General Manager, Transportation Services asks City Council to approve an expanded free-floating car-share program through Municipal Code amendments. The changes would exempt car-share vehicles from the three-hour parking rule, one-hour parking limits and winter overnight parking prohibitions on listed streets, and remove the cap on permits issued to one company. City Council is asked to approve the amendments.

title: Removal of City Symbols
topics: community & life (sc), government symbols;
brief: This is an administrative inquiry from Councillor Stephen Holyday about the removal of historical Coats of Arms from public display within the Toronto Public Service. The inquiry cites two Toronto Sun articles from May 26 and June 2, 2024 reporting on activities that led to the removals. It seeks information from staff on the circumstances. No decision is attached.

title: 9-1-1 Call Wait Times
topics: community & life (sc), emergency services; 9-1-1; 911; 911 calls; emergency assistance; emergency response
brief: This is an administrative inquiry from Councillor Jennifer McKelvie about 9-1-1 call wait times in Toronto. The Toronto Police Service's Communications Services Unit answers all emergency 9-1-1 calls, including fire and paramedic calls, and residents have reported concerns about wait times. The inquiry asks for information on the timeliness of call answering. No decision is attached.

title: The Missing Video Archive of the February 22, 2024 Toronto Transit Commission Board Meeting
topics: information & communication (sc), streaming media; streaming audio; streaming video
brief: This is an administrative inquiry item: Councillor Chris Moise asks City Council to seek information on the missing video archive of the TTC Board meeting of February 22, 2024. As a Commissioner, he received a staff explanation at the April 11, 2024 board meeting about how the archived video feed was lost the next morning. The inquiry asks Council to obtain the information under the Municipal Code. No recommendation is attached.

title: 2024 Student Nutrition Program Service Subsidies
topics: boards of health, health, nutrition, students, subsidies and grants; diet; dieting; healthy eating, financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs, health coverage
brief: This is a health item: the Medical Officer of Health asks City Council to authorize funding transfers for the 2024 student nutrition program: $4,919.3 thousand to the Angel Foundation for Learning and $14,214.9 thousand to the Toronto Foundation for Student Success. Student nutrition programs provide meals and snacks in schools, supporting children's health and learning. City Council is asked to authorize the agreements.

title: Service Agreements Awarded and Executed by the Medical Officer of Health for 2024
topics: boards of health, contracts, health; health coverage
brief: This is a health item: the Medical Officer of Health reports on 2024 purchase of service contracts awarded under delegated authority and asks City Council to authorize ongoing food security contracts with Working Women Community Centre. The agreements fund food handler training and certification, food literacy and employment skills development for low-income participants including newcomers and refugees. City Council is asked to authorize the Medical Officer of Health to award, execute and amend the agreements within the approved budget.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Blanket Contract 47022513 with Strongco Limited Partnership for Proprietary Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Parts and Services
topics: agreements, contracts, purchasing, services, taxes; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, levies, tenancy agreements
brief: This is a procurement item: the General Manager, Fleet Services and the Chief Procurement Officer ask City Council to amend the non-competitive blanket contract with Strongco Limited Partnership for proprietary equipment parts and services. The amendment would extend the term from five to ten years and increase the contract value by $7,457,061 net of HST, to a target value of $15,004,812 net of HST. City Council is asked to authorize the amendment.

title: 2023 Write-Off of Uncollectible Property Taxes and Accounts Receivable
topics: accounts receivable, financial write-offs, property taxes, provincial offences; financial write offs, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: This is a finance item: the Interim Controller asks City Council to deem uncollectible and write off $1,950,451 in unpaid property taxes from 31 accounts, covering 182 receivables from taxation years 1995 to 2023. The Executive Committee is asked to receive the report for information.

topics: economic development, governance; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing, governance structure; municipal governance

Key findings: Sankofa Square has a broader mandate including economic development, its model is similar to other North American squares, and it is mandated to be financially self-sufficient. The City Manager recommends directing the Board of Management to develop a multi-year strategic and business plan.

Most of the new spaces would replace temporary COVID-era spaces, including hotel sites, and the plan would secure up to five new shelter sites in 2024 through acquisitions. City Council is asked to amend the 2024 Capital Budget and 2025-2033 Capital Plan to create the new capital project.

City Council is asked to adopt the protocol and authorize related actions.
