brief: Councillor Brad Bradford asks City Council to review permit parking Area 9A at Danforth Avenue and Dawes Road. The 2021 removal of minimum parking requirements for new developments should not let on-street permit parking cover on-site parking shortfalls. Council is asked to direct Transportation Services to report back on excluding the Ontario Land Tribunal-approved developments at 6, 9-25 and 10-30 Dawes Road from the permit parking area.

title: Creating a Community Safety Zone on Lake Shore Boulevard East
topics: community safety, safety, transportation; public safety, transportation services
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford asks City Council to designate a Community Safety Zone on Lake Shore Boulevard East between Woodbine Avenue and 200 metres west of Lower Coxwell Avenue, in effect at all times. The area around Woodbine Beach draws heavy use, especially during the Canada Day fireworks and Winter Stations events. Council is also asked to have Transportation Services consider the zone for a permanent automated speed enforcement camera in Beaches-East York.

title: Expanding Permit Parking Area 13K
topics: parking, permit parking, traffic control systems; on-street permit parking; parking permits, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow asks City Council to expand permit parking Area 13K onto Lonsmount Drive between Don Francks Lane and Tichester Road, and onto Tweedsmuir Avenue between Heath Street West and 320 Tweedsmuir Avenue. A traffic signal installed in December 2023 at Heath Street West and Tweedsmuir Avenue extended the no-parking zone, removing resident parking. Council is asked to exempt the expansion from the permit parking by-law requirements.

title: Keeping Dundas Street Streetcar Moving Through Chinatown: Temporary Adjustments to Parking Regulations on Dundas Street West
topics: parking regulations, streetcars; parking by-laws; parking bylaws, street-cars
brief: City Council is asked to support temporary traffic and parking changes on Dundas Street West through Chinatown during the June to December 2024 closure of the 510 Spadina streetcar for Spadina Station construction. The TTC wants to keep the 505 Dundas streetcar moving through congestion between Spadina Avenue and McCaul Street. Council is asked to have the General Manager, Transportation Services report directly to the May 22, 2024 Council meeting with recommended amendments.

title: Transit Lane - Lake Shore Boulevard West, west of Yonge Street (Bus Terminal)
topics: public transit, terminals; intermodal stations; intermodal terminals; terminal stations; terminus; terminuses, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: City Council is asked to reserve the northerly westbound curb lane of Lake Shore Boulevard West, between about 70 metres west of Yonge Street and 55 metres further west, as an exclusive transit lane. The lane serves the Metrolinx bus terminal within the 45 Bay Street development, which has direct pedestrian connections to Union Station. The reservation was a condition of the site plan agreement. Council is asked to approve the lane designation.

title: 1910, 1920 and 1944 Yonge Street - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, demolitions, rental housing, zoning bylaws; application process, rental properties; rental units, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The Director, Community Planning recommends that City Council approve the zoning amendment and rental housing demolition applications for 1910, 1920 and 1944 Yonge Street. The proposal is a mixed-use building with two towers of 48 and 53 storeys (154.7 and 169.7 metres) plus a new public laneway. It includes 102 rental replacement units and a tenant relocation and assistance plan protecting tenants' right to return at similar rents. Council is asked to approve both applications.

title: Amend the existing stopping prohibition in effect at all times, on the south side of Annette Street, between a point 49 metres west of Evelyn Avenue and a point 43 metres east of High Park Avenue
topics: signs, stopping prohibitions, transportation; no stopping, signage, transportation services
brief: Councillor Gord Perks asks City Council to slightly adjust the no-stopping zone on the south side of Annette Street. The existing prohibition between 49 metres west of Evelyn Avenue and 43 metres east of High Park Avenue would shift to start at 56 metres west of Evelyn Avenue. City transportation staff reviewed the sign position and recommended the change.

title: Parking Amendment - River Street
topics: parking spaces, safety; parking spots, public safety
brief: City Council is asked to prohibit stopping at all times on the east side of River Street between Oak Street and a point 20 metres south. Residents report long-standing safety problems at the pedestrian crossover, including vehicles running through it while people cross and one recent injury. Removing the one parking space south of the crossover would improve sightlines for northbound drivers. The council is asked to approve the prohibition.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - May 2024 (Non-Delegated)
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, parking spaces; parking spots, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize an on-street accessible parking space for persons with disabilities at the location in Attachment 1 to the April 19, 2024 report. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on the subject street. The Director, Traffic Management recommends Council authorize the installation.

title: City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendments - Re allocating Section 37 funds from certain developments within Ward 11 - Decision Report   Approval
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, zoning bylaws; ttc, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The Director, Community Planning recommends that City Council amend site-specific zoning by-laws in Ward 11 to allow unspent Section 37 funds to be reallocated to new purposes. The affected sites include 86-100 Bloor Street West, 1 and 3 Sultan Street, 77 Charles Street West, 13-21 Balmuto Street, 590 Jarvis Street, 4-8 St. Thomas Street and 192A-200 Bloor Street West. Council is asked to approve the amendments so the funds can be used toward the purposes set out in the report.

title: 244-260 Church Street - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: buildings, construction, laneways; back alleys; mews, building
brief: The Director, Traffic Management asks City Council to extend the construction staging area for the 52-storey mixed-use building at 244-260 Church Street, being built by 250 Church Limited Partnership. The closure of the first north-south public laneway west of Church Street would continue from August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025. Council approval is required because Dundas Street East is a major arterial street.

title: 1404-1428 Yonge Street - Construction Staging Area
brief: Transportation Services seeks City Council approval for a construction staging area for the 50-storey condominium YSC Development Corp is building at 1404-1428 Yonge Street, on the west side between St Clair Avenue West and Farnham Avenue. Council approval is required because the Toronto Transit Commission operates transit service on Yonge Street. The report was referred from the December 2023 Council meeting; no recommendation text is visible in the source.

title: 399 Bathurst Street (Nassau Street) - Construction Staging Area
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, hospitals, sidewalks; ttc
brief: The Director, Traffic Management asks City Council to authorize a construction staging area for the new Toronto Western Hospital tower addition at 399 Bathurst Street, being built by EllisDon Corporation. The closure covers the east sidewalk and the northbound curb lane on Bathurst Street between Nassau Street and 85 metres south for 42 months, from May 31, 2024 to December 1, 2027. A temporary pedestrian walkway would be maintained in the closed lane. Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Bathurst Street.

title: Curb Lane Café - 88 Ossington Avenue, Humbert Street flankage - Appeal
topics: appeals, businesses, commercial areas, permits; commercial districts; retail areas, commercial waste collection customers, permit renewal
brief: This is a procedural item: Toronto and East York Community Council considers the appeal from Bar Koukla at 88 Ossington Avenue for a CafeTO curb lane cafe on the Humbert Street flankage. The proposed cafe contravenes the sidewalk cafes by-law, Chapter 742. The Director, Permits and Enforcement recommends the council not authorize the permit for the proposed curb lane cafe. The council is asked to decide the appeal.

title: 2991 and 2993 Dundas Street West - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Acting Senior Manager, Heritage Planning recommends that City Council include 2991 and 2993 Dundas Street West on the City's Heritage Register for their cultural heritage value. The two two-storey main street commercial row buildings sit near Pacific Avenue within the Junction Phase I Heritage Conservation District study area in Ward 4. The Toronto Preservation Board considered the same item and is asked to recommend the inclusion to Council.

title: 137-141 Isabella Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: applications, buildings, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The Director, Community Planning recommends that City Council refuse the zoning amendment for 137-141 Isabella Street. The proposal is a 69-storey residential building with 823 units, replacing a 7-storey apartment building and a 3-storey house; the 61 demolished rental units would be replaced in the new building. Refusal is recommended because outstanding issues could not be resolved within the legislated 90-day decision timeframe.

title: 1304-1318 King Street West and 143-145 Cowan Avenue - Official Plan, Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: demolitions, official plan amendments, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: The Director, Community Planning recommends that City Council refuse the Official Plan and Zoning By-law amendment applications for 1304-1318 King Street West and 143-145 Cowan Avenue. The proposal is a 21-storey mixed-use building with 263 dwelling units and 213 square metres of ground floor retail, plus a related rental housing demolition application for eight existing rental units. Staff find the proposal is inconsistent with provincial policies and does not conform with the Official Plan. Council is asked to refuse the applications in their current form.

title: Council Member Appointments to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities Board of Directors
topics: appointments, government (sc);
brief: This is an appointments item: the City Clerk recommends that the Striking Committee consider members' preferences and recommend two Council members for appointment to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities Board of Directors. The terms run from the June 2024 annual conference to the 2025 annual conference. The Striking Committee is asked to make the recommendations to Council.

title: Council Member Appointment to Fill a Vacancy on the Service Excellence Committee
topics: appointments, government (sc);
brief: This is an appointments item: the City Clerk recommends that the Striking Committee consider members' preferences and recommend one Council member to fill the vacancy on the Service Excellence Committee. The vacancy resulted from Councillor Jaye Robinson's resignation, with the term running to December 31, 2024. The Striking Committee is asked to make the recommendation to Council.

title: Council Member Appointments to the City of Toronto Long-Term Care Committee of Management
topics: appointments, government (sc);
brief: This is an appointments item: the City Clerk recommends that the Striking Committee consider members' preferences and recommend two Council members for appointment to the City of Toronto Long-Term Care Committee of Management. The terms would run until November 14, 2026. The Striking Committee is asked to make the recommendations to Council.

title: Eglinton GO Area Urban Design Guidelines - Final Report
topics: regional transportation agencies, urban design; civic improvements, commuter rail systems; go transit; intercity transportation; interregional public transit systems; interregional transit systems; interurban transit organizations; metrolinx; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; regional transit authorities; regional transportation authorities; transit agencies; transit operating agencies
brief: The Director, Community Planning and the Director of Urban Design recommend that City Council adopt the Eglinton GO Area Urban Design Guidelines. The guidelines respond to development interest around Eglinton GO station, where the Official Plan identifies a Protected Major Transit Station Area with minimum densities. Council is asked to adopt the guidelines and direct the Chief Planner to use them in reviewing development.

title: 1880-1890 Eglinton Avenue East and 1523 and 1525-1545 Victoria Park Avenue (Golden Mile) - Public Art Plan
topics: properties (real estate), public art; outdoor art; outdoor sculptures; outdoor statues, property; real estate
brief: City Planning recommends that City Council approve the public art plan for 1880-1890 Eglinton Avenue East and 1523 and 1525-1545 Victoria Park Avenue (Golden Mile). The plan outlines how the owner will commission public art in the privately owned, publicly accessible areas of the site, covering site context, art direction, public priorities, mentorship, implementation and budget. Council is asked to approve the plan.

title: 180 and 260 Brimley Road - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Appeal Report
topics: development, official plan amendments, rezoning; developing land; development (land); land development, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: The Director, Community Planning recommends that City Council oppose the appeals for 180 and 260 Brimley Road at the Ontario Land Tribunal. The applications propose 1,337 dwelling units on 15.625 hectares, including back-to-back, stacked and on-street townhouses, with new streets and a public park. The applicant appealed to the Tribunal on February 14, 2024. Council is asked to direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the hearing in opposition to the current proposal.

title: 1891 Eglinton Avenue East - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300) - Decision Report - Approval
topics: noise, noise control; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise, noise barriers; sound barriers
brief: The Director, Community Planning recommends that City Council designate lands at 1891 Eglinton Avenue East as a Class 4 Noise Area under provincial noise guidelines. The site will be redeveloped with four buildings: 48-storey, 44-storey and 44-storey towers plus a 12-storey mid-rise building, under a settlement offer Council accepted. The Class 4 designation accounts for the area's stationary noise sources. Council is asked to approve the designation.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will review the Order Paper at the May 22, 2024 meeting. The Order Paper is the formal record of Council's agenda business. No decision is attached.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions and announcements will be made at the May 22, 2024 City Council meeting. This is part of the regular order of business. No decision is attached.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council may file petitions at the May 22, 2024 meeting. Petitions are part of the regular order of business. No further decision is attached.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council will declare interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act at the May 22, 2024 meeting. Declarations of interest are part of the regular order of business. No further decision is attached.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will receive the reports of the Executive Committee, Board of Health, Civic Appointments Committee, Economic and Community Development Committee, General Government Committee, and Infrastructure and Environment Committee from their recent meetings. Introducing committee reports and new business from City officials is part of the regular order of business. No further decision is attached.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will confirm the minutes from the regular meeting held on April 17 and 18, 2024. Confirming the minutes is part of the regular order of business. No further decision is attached.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council opens its May 22, 2024 meeting with the call to order, including O Canada and a moment of silence. The call to order is the first item in the order of business. No decision is attached.

title: Request a Review of Zoning Regulations to Restrict Outdoor Parking of Commercially Licensed Vehicles on Private Property in Residential Areas
topics: commercial vehicles, residential properties, zoning bylaws; commercial motor vehicles, residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Councillor Vincent Crisanti asks the Planning and Housing Committee to recommend a review of zoning rules on commercially licensed vehicles parked outdoors on residential properties. Etobicoke North constituents raised the issue; the city-wide zoning by-law already restricts about ten vehicle types, including vehicles with more than six wheels and commercially licensed vehicles. Council is asked to have the Chief Planner, with Municipal Licensing and Standards, review the regulations.

title: City Comments on Proposed Bill 185 - Cutting Red Tape to Build More Homes Act, 2024, Provincial Planning Statement 2024, and New Minister Zoning Order Framework
topics: housing, zoning; homes; residences
brief: This is an information item: the Interim Chief Planner reports on the Province's Bill 185 (Cutting Red Tape to Build More Homes Act), the revised Provincial Planning Statement 2024, and the new Minister Zoning Order framework. Bill 185 affects 17 acts including the City of Toronto Act and Planning Act and has reached second reading. The Interim Chief Planner recommends the Planning and Housing Committee receive the report for information.

title: 26 Millwood Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Interim Chief Planner recommends that City Council state its intention to designate 26 Millwood Road under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The property is on the north side of Millwood Road, about 30 metres east of Yonge Street in the South Eglinton-Davisville neighbourhood, with a two-storey detached house built between 1880 and 1885. Council is asked to approve the notice of intention to designate.

title: Transit-Oriented Communities Status Update
topics: community & life (sc), community development, transit routes, urban transit systems; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development, local transit authorities; municipal transit authorities; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; transit agencies; transit operating agencies, surface routes
brief: The Interim Chief Planner asks City Council to authorize a Transit Oriented Communities resource agreement with Infrastructure Ontario. The agreement would have Infrastructure Ontario fund temporary City staff positions to process transit-oriented community submissions within provincial timelines. The report also updates Council on the TOC program, the provincial value allocation framework for community benefits, and proposals that progressed over the past year. Council is asked to authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement.

title: Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods: Major Streets Study - Final Report
topics: [housing by physical form], redevelopment; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: The Interim Chief Planner recommends that City Council adopt the Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods Major Streets Study final report. The study addresses Toronto's expected growth of at least 700,000 new residents by 2051 and the shortage of low-rise housing like townhouses and small apartment buildings. Council is asked to amend the Official Plan with Official Plan Amendment 727 and amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 to allow more housing types on major streets in neighbourhoods.

title: Recommended Official Plan Amendment respecting Schedule 3 Complete Application Requirements, Chapter 3 Cultural Heritage Evaluation Report and Municipal Code Amendments respecting Delegated Authority for Minor Zoning By-laws
topics: [rules in planning and development], official plan amendments, planning & development (sc);
brief: The Interim Chief Planner recommends that City Council adopt Official Plan Amendment 720 to clarify and streamline complete application requirements in Schedule 3 of the Official Plan. The amendment covers technical housekeeping changes, legislative and policy updates, and plan of condominium requirements. Council is also asked to amend the Municipal Code to update delegated authority for minor zoning by-laws and heritage evaluation reports.

title: Update Downsview: Secondary Plan, Zoning By-law, Urban Design Guidelines and Master Environmental Servicing Plan - Final Report
topics: Secondary Plans, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The Interim Chief Planner and General Manager, Transportation Services recommend that City Council adopt the comprehensive planning framework for the Downsview area over the next 30 years. The deliverables include the Downsview Secondary Plan (Official Plan Amendment 716), a zoning by-law for meanwhile uses, urban design guidelines, and a master environmental servicing plan. The framework guides resilient, sustainable and equitable complete communities on the former Downsview lands.

title: Progress Update on Toronto Community Housing Corporation's (TCHC) Tenant Advisory Committee
topics: advisory committees, tenant organizations, tenants; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: This is an information item: the Executive Director, Housing Secretariat reports on progress launching the Toronto Community Housing Corporation's Tenant Advisory Committee since spring 2023. The committee advises TCHC on tenant engagement and corporate initiatives advancing tenant priorities, with recruitment and an orientation completed in 2023. The recommendation asks Council, as shareholder, to have the TCHC board direct its CEO to submit a report by the end of 2024.

title: 298 Newton Drive - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, official plan amendments, zoning; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: The Director, Community Planning recommends that City Council amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 to permit six three-storey townhouses at 298 Newton Drive. The units would average 11.23 metres in height with 1,035 square metres of floor area, a floor space index of 1.29, and rear integral garages off a shared driveway. Staff find the infill proposal conforms with provincial and Official Plan policies. Council is asked to approve the amendment.

title: 56 Finch Avenue West - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, parking spaces, zoning; parking spots
brief: The Director, Community Planning recommends that City Council amend the former North York Zoning By-law 7625 to permit an office use in the existing building at 56 Finch Avenue West. The office use has operated since 2018 in contravention of the zoning by-law; the building footprint and 139 square metres of floor area remain unchanged. Staff find the proposal conforms with provincial and Official Plan policies. Council is asked to approve the amendment.

title: 939 Lawrence Avenue East, 966 Don Mills Road, and 169 The Donway West - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: exemptions, land use, part lot control, planning; exceptions
brief: City Planning recommends that City Council enact a part lot control exemption by-law for 939 Lawrence Avenue East, 966 Don Mills Road and 169 The Donway West. The exemption facilitates the orderly development of the lands adjoining the Shops at Don Mills. Staff find the proposal conforms with provincial and Official Plan policies. Council is asked to approve the exemption by-law.

title: 501 and 503 Eglinton Avenue East and 383, 385, 387 and 389 Cleveland Street - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: multi-residential properties, official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: City Planning recommends that City Council approve the zoning amendment for 501 and 503 Eglinton Avenue East and 383-389 Cleveland Street. The proposal is a 14-storey mixed-use building with 207 dwelling units, 468 square metres of commercial space and 83 parking spaces, at a floor space index of 7.33. Staff find it conforms with provincial policies, the Official Plan and the Yonge-Eglinton Secondary Plan. Council is asked to approve the amendment.

title: 47 Ranleigh Avenue - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: City Planning recommends that City Council approve the zoning amendment for 47 Ranleigh Avenue. The proposal would permit a new four-storey residential apartment building with 16 rental dwelling units and about 1,148 square metres of floor area. The existing two-storey building with three rental dwelling units and a rear garage would be demolished. Staff find the proposal is appropriate intensification that conforms with provincial and Official Plan policies.

title: 272, 284, 286, 288, 290, and 296 Lawrence Avenue West and 1507, 1525, 1537, 1539, 1545, and 1549 Avenue Road Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: Official Plans, official plan amendments, planning approvals, zoning, zoning bylaws; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Planning recommends that City Council oppose the Lawrence Avenue West and Avenue Road development proposal at the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing. The 2020 application proposed 14 and 10-storey mixed-use buildings with 455 residential units including 15 rental replacements, 4,680 square metres of retail and a 902.8 square metre park. The applicant appealed on December 18, 2023. Council is asked to authorize the City Solicitor and staff to attend in opposition to the current proposal while continuing discussions.

title: 824 Sheppard Avenue West, 177, 179 and 181 Cocksfield Avenue - Zoning Amendment  and Rental Housing Demolition and Conversion Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: buildings, height, residential tenants; height restrictions
brief: The Director, Community Planning recommends that City Council approve the zoning amendment and rental housing demolition and conversion application for 824 Sheppard Avenue West and 177-181 Cocksfield Avenue. The proposal adjusts the approved density for a 12-storey mixed-use building with 328 residential units and 445 square metres of non-residential space, including 15 rental replacement units, retaining the holding provision. Council is asked to approve the amendment.

title: Yonge Street and Kempford Boulevard - U-Turn Prohibition
topics: full closures (traffic calming), transportation, turn prohibitions (traffic); transportation services
brief: The Director, Traffic Management asks City Council to prohibit northbound and southbound U-turns at all times on Yonge Street at Kempford Boulevard. Transportation Services requested the prohibition to address traffic safety concerns in the area. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Yonge Street.

title: Amending the 2024-2033 Capital Budget and Plan for Parks, Forestry and Recreation for the Lower Don Trail Improvements - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: capital budgets, change, recreation & tourism (sc); amendments; conversion; modification
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, to add $2.7 million for the Lower Don Trail improvements project. Unforeseen unstable soil conditions found during construction required redesign and modified construction methods. Council is asked to amend the 2024-2033 Parks, Forestry and Recreation capital budget and plan, raising the total project cost from $3.1 million to $5.8 million.

title: Request to Enter into a Construction Funding Agreement with 712953 Ontario Limited, 591 Sherbourne Street Limited And 2370165 Ontario Incorporated for Improvements to St. James Town West Park - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: construction, development charges, funding; building, financing
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, to enter into a construction funding agreement for base park improvements at St. James Town West Park. The Section 37 agreement for the Sherbourne, Bleecker and Howard Street developments requires the developers to deliver the park improvements. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation to negotiate and execute the agreement with the three development companies.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Support The Elizabeth Fry Society at 215 Wellesley Street East - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: development, funding, housing; developing land; development (land); land development, financing, homes; residences
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, to provide $500,000 to the Elizabeth Fry Society for its affordable housing development at 215 Wellesley Street East. Elizabeth Fry is building an addition with 32 new transitional housing units plus counselling, court diversion, employment and multi-purpose spaces; construction is well underway. Council is asked to have the Housing Secretariat provide the funding from the Capital Revolving Reserve Fund for Affordable Housing.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Developments at 59 Richmond Street East and 114 and 120 Church Street for the Dixon Hall Community Hub - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: funding, social housing; community housing; housing allowance; housing projects; low income housing; non profit housing; non-profit housing; public housing; rent geared to income assistance; rent geared to income housing; rent subsidies; rent supplement; subsidized housing; subsidized rent; subsidized units, financing
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, to provide Dixon Hall with $375,000 for its community hub at 58 Sumach Street. Construction delays and inflation have significantly increased costs since Dixon Hall's earlier Section 37 funding. Council is asked to increase the 2024 Non-Program operating budget by $375,000 gross and $0 net, fully funded by Section 37 community benefits from the Richmond Street East and Church Street developments.

title: Taking Congestion Seriously - A Plan to Accelerate Construction of the Gardiner Expressway - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: construction, highways, transportation (sc); building, freeways; motorways; parkways
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside, on accelerating construction of the Gardiner Expressway. Toronto has been ranked the most congested city in North America, with Gardiner travel times doubling in recent weeks and harming businesses and quality of life. Council is asked to direct the General Manager, Transportation Services to report back by the fourth quarter of 2024 with a plan to accelerate the Strategic Rehabilitation Plan and minimize congestion impacts.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from Various Developments to Support the Construction of Blackhurst Cultural Centre - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: construction, cultural facilities, funding; art centres; arts centres; cultural attractions; cultural centres, building, financing
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers, to release $1,000,000 in Section 37 funds for the construction of the Blackhurst Cultural Centre. A Different Booklist, operating in Mirvish Village since 1995, proposes a new non-profit community cultural centre celebrating the culture and history of Canadians of African and Caribbean ancestry as part of the Honest Ed's redevelopment. Council is asked to increase the 2024 Economic Development and Culture operating budget by $1,000,000, fully funded by Section 37 money.

title: Artscape Receivership - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: art programs, arts and culture organizations; art classes; art workshops; arts programs, art councils; art organizations; arts councils; arts groups; cultural organizations
brief: This is a confidential directions item: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, asks City Council to adopt the confidential staff instructions in Attachment 1 on the Artscape receivership. A court-appointed receiver took over Toronto Artscape Inc. on January 11, 2024; staff worked on transition plans for 14 properties and 390 residential and commercial tenants. Council is asked to adopt the confidential instructions and authorize their release if adopted.

title: Safe Access to Leslie Lookout Park - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: pedestrian crossovers, safety; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, public safety
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, on safe access to Leslie Lookout Park in the Port Lands. The park opens in early summer 2024, but the multi-use trail sits across Leslie Street, which carries heavy truck traffic from Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant construction and industrial uses. Council is asked to have Transportation Services report to the July 10, 2024 community council meeting on a pedestrian crossing for the park.

title: Saulter Street Short Term Rental - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, on the short-term rental at 48 Saulter Street. Neighbours report two years of noise, building code and short-term rental by-law violations, and an armed home invasion occurred at the address this weekend. Council is asked to request the Executive Director, Municipal Licensing and Standards to consider available Toronto Police Service information when reviewing the operator's registration.

title: Support for the Relocation of the It’s Ok* Community Arts Studio - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: art galleries (facilities), community & life (sc); art facilities
brief: This is a member motion from Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, to support relocating the It's Ok* Community Arts Studio. The Black-led non-profit has operated its interdisciplinary arts space at 468 Queen Street West for two years, but the City-owned building transfers to Parks, Forestry and Recreation in April 2025 and a lease extension is not possible. Council is asked to have Economic Development and Culture prioritize finding the studio a new home.

title: Jameson On-Ramp Gate to Westbound F.G. Gardiner Expressway - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: highways, ramps (highways); freeways; motorways; parkways, off ramps (highways); on ramps (highways)
brief: This is a member motion from Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, to open the Jameson on-ramp gate to the westbound Gardiner Expressway. Contract 2 of the Gardiner rehabilitation runs to mid-2027, and construction has pushed traffic onto Lake Shore Boulevard West. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager, Transportation Services to open the on-ramp from westbound Lake Shore Boulevard West at Jameson Avenue between 2:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. on weekdays.

title: 1438-1440 Queen Street West - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, on the Toronto Local Appeal Body appeal for 1438-1440 Queen Street West. The applicant seeks variances for a rear second-storey and full third-storey addition to a mixed-use building with ground floor retail and four residential units. Council is asked to authorize the City Solicitor to attend the appeal body as a party with City staff.

title: 29 Lake Promenade - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, on the Toronto Local Appeal Body appeal for 29 Lake Promenade. The Committee of Adjustment refused the owner's variances to legalize a new detached dwelling with an attached garage in December 2023; the owner appealed. Council is asked to authorize the City Solicitor to attend the appeal body to uphold the refusal and retain outside consultants as needed.

title: Desotos Eatery/Atomic 10 (1079 St. Clair Avenue West and 145 Lauder Avenue) - Exemption of Certain Requirements under Chapter 742 - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, to exempt Desotos Eatery and Atomic 10 at 1079 St. Clair Avenue West and 145 Lauder Avenue from certain sidewalk cafe requirements. The restaurant has operated its patio since 2016 and has worked with City staff since 2022 on compliance. Council is asked to exempt its 2024 summer cafe season permit application from the notice requirements when it applies.

title: Amending Items 2023.CC5.6 and 2023.MM6.28 - Terms of Reference for the Housing Rights Advisory Committee for 2022-2026 City Council Term - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, to amend the Housing Rights Advisory Committee's Terms of Reference so public members can receive honoraria for working group meetings. The committee unanimously approved the request on May 13, 2024, recognizing that public members with lived experience of homelessness or housing precarity are otherwise uncompensated for their expertise. Council is asked to amend the Terms of Reference notwithstanding its earlier decision on advisory body honoraria.

title: Accepting an In-Kind Donation from Kew Gardens Tennis Club to Refurbish Tennis Courts at Beaches Park - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
topics: donation, tennis courts; bequest; toy drive, tennis centers; tennis centres; tennis complexes; tennis facilities
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, to accept an in-kind donation of up to $200,000 from the Kew Gardens Tennis Club to refurbish five tennis courts at Beaches Park in 2024. Community tennis clubs maintain capital reserve funds for court repairs under the City's 2004 tennis policy. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation to accept the donation.

title: Tie-Back Encumbrances - 11-25 Yorkville Avenue and 16-18 Cumberland Street - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: parks, parks and open space areas; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, green spaces; open spaces
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, on tie-back encumbrances at 11-25 Yorkville Avenue and 16-18 Cumberland Street. Council's 2019 approval of the 62-storey tower and 674-unit development did not authorize tie-backs in the park, but staff found tie-backs were installed. Council is asked to approve the acceptance of the on-site parkland dedication subject to the owner's commitments.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2023.IE9.5 to Extend the 2024 Reporting, Exemption, and Extension Deadline for Municipal Code Chapter 367, Building Emissions Performance - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe, to extend the 2024 reporting, exemption and extension deadlines under the Building Emissions Performance by-law, Chapter 367. The by-law requires owners of buildings 10,000 square feet and larger to report energy and water use annually, phased in from 2024. Council is asked to amend its earlier decision to extend the 2024 report deadline.

title: Maximizing Housing on the New Island - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, on maximizing housing on the new Port Lands island. The island opens in the fall with updated zoning in June proposing to raise affordable housing from 20 to 30 percent. Council is asked to request the Deputy City Manager, Development and Growth Services to report to the June 13, 2024 Planning and Housing Committee on any difficulties achieving 30 percent affordable housing on non-City owned lands.

title: Amending Item 2022.MM45.51 to Support the Kensington Market Community Land Trust to Acquire an Affordable Rental Housing Property - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: change, rental housing; amendments; conversion; modification, rental properties; rental units
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow, to amend the 2022 approval supporting the Kensington Market Community Land Trust's acquisition of an affordable rental housing property. The City's Multi-Unit Residential Acquisition program helps non-profits buy at-risk market rental buildings of six to sixty units. Council is asked to delete Part 4 of its earlier decision, which authorized up to $450,000 from the Capital Revolving Reserve Fund for Affordable Housing.

title: Requesting the Province to Protect Small Businesses and Support Vibrant, Affordable, and Successful Mainstreets - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: commercial properties, rent, small businesses; office real estate; retail space, rents
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asking the Province to protect small businesses on Toronto's main streets. Commercial retail rents rose 20 percent, and unlike residential rentals there is no rent control for small businesses, pushing out local shops in favour of chains. Council is asked to request the Province implement commercial rent control for small locally-owned businesses, create a dispute resolution tribunal, and require standardized leases.

title: Authority to Accept the Conveyance of Land at 57-77 Wade Avenue for the Protection of the Toronto Transit Commission Tunnel - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: land, public safety & protection (sc); property
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, to accept the conveyance of land at 57-77 Wade Avenue to protect the TTC tunnel. The 7-storey office redevelopment's site plan conditions require conveying a 3-metre sub-strata parcel surrounding the tunnel about 9 metres below grade. Council is asked to exempt the stratified parcel and support easement from the policy against accepting untested land so the conveyance can proceed.

title: Advancement of Professional Women’s Soccer in Toronto, and Seeking Proposals for Lamport Stadium - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Jaye Robinson
topics: soccer, sports clubs; badminton clubs; baseball associations; baseball leagues; bowling clubs; cross-country ski clubs; curling clubs; gymnastic clubs; hockey associations; hockey leagues; karate clubs; lacrosse clubs; lawn bowling clubs; ride clubs; rifle clubs; slo-pitch leagues; soccer clubs; soccer leagues; softball associations; softball leagues; swim clubs; tennis clubs; volleyball clubs
brief: This is a member motion from Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Jaye Robinson, on advancing professional women's soccer in Toronto and seeking proposals for Lamport Stadium. Council supported establishing a professional women's sports league in December 2023 and directed staff to explore opportunities including potential sites. Council is asked to direct Parks, Forestry and Recreation, with the FIFA World Cup 2026 Secretariat and Corporate Real Estate Management, to negotiate agreement terms to advance the initiative.

title: Partnering with Tennis Canada for Future Facilities - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: facilities, partnerships, tennis;
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside, on partnering with Tennis Canada for future facilities. Tennis Canada is seeking to donate up to $2 million toward community tennis bubbles and partner with the City; demand for tennis is high and the facilities master plan identifies a need for up to 20 new courts. Council is asked to have Parks, Forestry and Recreation explore a year-round, accessible and affordable tennis facility and identify sites.

title: Request for Review of Governance and Operations for Moss Park Arena - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: arenas; indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, requesting a review of governance and operations for Moss Park Arena. The 1974 arena at 140 Sherbourne Street must align its programming with City priorities and community needs while operating cost effectively. Council is asked to direct the City Manager, with Parks, Forestry and Recreation, to assess the impacts of transitioning the arena from a board of management to a City-operated facility.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Kensington Market Community Land Trust to Upgrade a Mural - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: development charges, funding, public art; financing, outdoor art; outdoor sculptures; outdoor statues
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, to release $7,000 in Section 37 funds to the Kensington Market Community Land Trust for a mural upgrade at 54-56 Kensington Avenue. The trust already received $6,500 and needs $7,000 more to finish the mural; the funds come from $150,000 in Section 37 money earmarked for area streetscape improvements from the 297 College Street development. Council is asked to increase the 2024 Non-Program operating budget by $7,000, fully funded by the Section 37 money.

title: Strengthening Our Cultural Event Investment Throughout the City - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: [events in culture], investment;
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, on strengthening cultural event investment across the city. Newer, denser neighbourhoods outside the downtown lack grandfathered festivals and need support to become vibrant places to live, work and play. Council is asked to direct Economic Development and Culture and Parks, Forestry and Recreation to report on the current distribution of City-funded cultural events and a plan to strengthen investment outside the core.

title: Equitable Funding and Distribution for Canada Day Events in All Community Council Areas for 2025 - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: festivals and special events, funding; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals, financing
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, on equitable funding for Canada Day events in 2025. The 15 City-run July 1 events in 2024 fall in only 12 of 25 wards, and neither event counts nor funding are equitably distributed. Council is asked to direct Parks, Forestry and Recreation and Economic Development and Culture to report back by the fourth quarter of 2024 with recommendations for equitable distribution.

title: The Future of Visitor Parking - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: parking, parking authorities, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, parking authority
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, on the future of visitor parking. New developments are increasingly approved with minimal visitor parking, a foreseeable problem in the suburbs without street parking or public lots. Council is asked to have the Chief Planner, with the Toronto Parking Authority president, consider the greater suburban need for visitor parking in the ongoing zoning review.

title: Requesting the Province to Create Safety Zones Around Places of Worship, Faith-Based Schools and Vulnerable Community Social Infrastructure - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: public safety & protection (sc);
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, asking the Province to create safety zones around places of worship, faith-based schools and vulnerable community infrastructure. Hate crimes in Toronto rose 93 percent since October 7, 2023, with 56 percent of incidents antisemitic. Council is asked to request the Attorney General introduce legislation modelled on Ontario's abortion clinic bubble zone law, permitting peaceful protest while creating protected zones.

title: Granting a Nominal Licence to the East York Historical Society for Space in the Basement of East York Civic Centre - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: community centres, licences; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, licenses; licensing
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, to grant the East York Historical Society a nominal licence for 132 square feet of basement space at the East York Civic Centre. The non-profit society needs a home for historical archives and artifacts, fitting for East York's 100th anniversary year. Council is asked to authorize a five-year licence with a five-year renewal option.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 1-25 Defries Street to Amend the 2024-2033 Capital Budget and Plan for Parks, Forestry and Recreation for Improvements to the Labatt Avenue Right-of-Way - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: agreements, improvement; enhancement; rehabilitation (property), tenancy agreements
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, to release Section 37 funds for streetscape improvements on the Labatt Avenue right-of-way between Defries Street and its eastern termination. The Section 37 agreement for 1-25 Defries Street requires the developer to design and cost the improvements for the planned vehicle closure and open space. Council is asked to amend the 2024-2033 capital budget and plan to create the $850,000 capital project.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds and Section 45 Funds to Enhance Access to Recreation at the Regent Park Athletic Grounds - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: funding, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, financing
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, to release Section 37 and Section 45 funds for a new storage shed and electrified zamboni storage hut at the Regent Park outdoor artificial ice rink. The project costs $433,655 gross and $0 debt in 2024, fully funded by developer funds from 88 Queen Street East and the Mutual Street developments. Council is asked to amend the 2024-2033 Parks, Forestry and Recreation capital budget and plan to create the new capital project.

title: Tie-Back Encumbrances - 245-285 Queen Street East, 348-412 Richmond Street East, 78-106 Ontario Street and 8-12 Brigden Place - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: parkland dedication, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, on tie-back encumbrances for the Queen Street East, Richmond Street East, Ontario Street and Brigden Place lands. Council accepted a 2018 settlement for a mixed-use development with three towers and 1,341 residential units. Council is asked to approve the acceptance of the on-site parkland dedication as previously authorized in the 2018 decision.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from Various Developments for Streetscape Improvements to Draper Street - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: funding, urban form; financing, streetscapes; urban landscape
brief: This is a member motion from Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, to release $500,000 in Section 37 funds for streetscape improvements on Draper Street between Front Street West and Wellington Street West. The Well development's Section 37 agreement secured funding for the area improvements. Council is asked to amend the 2024-2033 capital budget and plan, transferring $500,000 to Transportation Services for Vision Zero safety enhancements, sidewalk widening, decorative paving, curb extensions and planting.

title: Publicly Providing Receipts Before City Council Consideration of Expenses under the Members of Council Operations Policy - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: change, improvement; amendments; conversion; modification, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside, to require public receipts when Council approves expenses under the Members of Council Operations Policy. Recent events highlighted the need for continuous improvements to accountability processes. Council is asked to amend the policy so the City Clerk provides receipts and related documentation publicly as attachments to the agenda when reimbursement needs Council approval.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Essential Structural Work to the Community Non-Profit Affordable Rental Housing Building at 1501 Queen Street West - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: community & life (sc), development charges, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, to release $1,221,924.47 in Section 37 funds to the Parkdale Activity-Recreation Centre for structural restoration of its 38-unit affordable rental building at 1501 Queen Street West. Earlier City-funded repair work is underway, but serious structural issues not in the original scope were discovered. Council is asked to authorize the Housing Secretariat to provide the funding.

title: 1000 Mural Graffiti Removal Blitz
topics: arts and culture, graffiti, public art, vandalism; graffiti abatement; graffiti crime; graffiti eradication; graffiti vandalism; grafitti removal, outdoor art; outdoor sculptures; outdoor statues
brief: Councillor Mike Colle asks the Infrastructure and Environment Committee to recommend a graffiti removal strategy, including a 1000 Mural Graffiti Removal Blitz. Graffiti tagging has markedly increased over the last year, including hateful messages linked to global conflicts. Colle recommends Council ask the General Manager, Transportation Services, with the General Manager, Economic Development and Culture, to report on murals and removal approaches.

title: Prohibiting Distribution of Plastic Manufactured Items
topics: bulky plastics (waste), reduction, regulations;
brief: This is a confidential directions item: the City Solicitor asks City Council to direct that the confidential attachment remain confidential in its entirety, as it contains legal advice subject to solicitor-client privilege. The item concerns the legal feasibility of a by-law prohibiting retailers from giving customers the plastic manufactured items banned under federal regulations. No public decision on the by-law itself is in this item.

title: Update on Stage 2 of the Single-Use and Takeaway Items Reduction Strategy
topics: environmental programs, reduction, solid waste management; environmental initiatives; green living, solid waste management planning; swm; waste management
brief: This is an information item: the General Manager, Solid Waste Management Services updates Council on Stage 2 of the Single-Use and Takeaway Items Reduction Strategy. The new single-use by-law took effect March 1, 2024 for all Toronto retail businesses, following Council's December 2023 adoption. The recommendation asks Council to have the General Manager include further implementation updates in the Stage 3 report due in the first quarter of 2025.

title: Donation from High Park Initiatives for Outdoor Classroom
topics: city initiatives, donation, parks; bequest; toy drive, city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: The General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation asks City Council to accept a $75,000 donation from High Park Initiatives for an outdoor classroom and nature education space called the Outdoor Urban Restoration Space 2.0 in High Park. Council is also asked to amend the 2024-2033 Parks, Forestry and Recreation capital budget and plan and enter into a donor agreement. The council is asked to authorize the donation acceptance.

title: King Street Transit Priority Corridor Update
topics: projects, transit routes, transportation (sc); surface routes
brief: The General Manager, Transportation Services asks City Council to allow the Billy Bishop Airport shuttle bus to use the King Street Transit Priority Corridor between Bathurst Street and Jarvis Street. The corridor gives streetcars priority over private vehicles on the 504 King route, the city's busiest surface transit line. Council is asked to approve the related amendments to the traffic and parking by-law.

title: eglintonTOday Phase 1 Complete Street Project: Bicknell Avenue to Mount Pleasant Road
topics: light rail transit, road construction, traffic management; lrt, traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations
brief: The General Manager, Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize the eglintonTOday Complete Street Project on Eglinton Avenue from Bicknell Avenue to Mount Pleasant Road. With Eglinton Crosstown construction nearing completion, the project marks the end of over a decade of construction with wide sidewalks, raised bikeways, parking and rapid transit. Council is also asked to authorize related bikeway projects, including on Croham Road from Eglinton Avenue West to Bowie Avenue.

title: A Micromobility Strategy for Toronto
topics: pilot projects, safety, transportation; public safety, transportation services
brief: The General Manager, Transportation Services recommends that City Council continue to decline participating in the provincial electric kick-scooter pilot and instead opt in to the provincial low-speed vehicle pilot. The micromobility strategy addresses growing use of e-bikes, e-scooters, cargo bikes and other small vehicles and their safe operation. Council asked for the strategy in July 2023; staff reviewed other jurisdictions to inform the report. Council is asked to approve the pilot participation recommendations.

title: Yonge-Dundas Square Renaming Initiative
topics: attractions, facility naming, naming; cultural attractions; places of interest; tourist attractions; tourist sites, park naming
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor Stephen Holyday asks for information on the Yonge-Dundas Square renaming initiative. Council directed the square's board in December 2023 to adopt the new name Sankofa Square, selected by the Recognition Review Committee, as part of confronting the legacy of the transatlantic slave trade and the Henry Dundas name. The inquiry asks questions under the Council procedures by-law; no decision is attached.

title: Partnership for Healthy Cities - Seeking Authority to Receive External Funds for the 2024 Budget Year
topics: external services, health; consultants; consulting services; professional services, health coverage
brief: The Medical Officer of Health asks City Council to authorize an agreement with Vital Strategies Inc. to implement a public health surveillance initiative on health behaviours during extreme heat or wildfire smoke events. Toronto Public Health will lead the project with the Environment and Climate division, under the Partnership for Healthy Cities program supported by Bloomberg Philanthropies and the World Health Organization. Council has participated in the program since 2017.

title: Amendment to Various Purchase Orders and Blanket Contracts with Various Vendors for Corporate Learning Services Providers for People and Equity
topics: contracts, equity, purchasing, service delivery; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, employment equity; fair wage; pay equity
brief: This is a procurement item: the Chief People Officer and the Chief Procurement Officer ask City Council for a two-year extension to various purchase orders and blanket contracts with corporate learning services providers, beyond their original five-year term. The extension lets People and Equity finish work already started while it analyzes future corporate learning needs. No additional dollar value is requested.

title: 2900 Warden Avenue - Designation of a Portion of the Property Used by Toronto Employment and Social Services as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: agreements, by-laws, exemptions, taxes, zoning designations; bylaws, exceptions, levies, permitted use requests; permitted uses, tenancy agreements
brief: The Interim Controller asks City Council to pass a by-law designating part of 2900 Warden Avenue, used by Toronto Employment and Social Services, as a municipal capital facility. The designation of unit 225, about 34,658 square feet, would provide an exemption from municipal and education taxes. The agreement is with the landlord, Bridlewood Mall Management Inc., under section 252 of the City of Toronto Act.

title: Procurement Policy Updates Resulting from Amendments to Toronto Municipal Code, Chapter 195, Procurement
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, bylaws
brief: The Chief Procurement Officer asks City Council to direct administrative updates to procurement policies to align with the amended Procurement By-law, Chapter 195, taking effect July 1, 2024. The report also responds to Council's request to align procurement policies with the TransformTO Net Zero Strategy. The by-law amendments were adopted in December 2023 and reviewed through 2023. Council is asked to direct the updates.

title: Expropriation of Property Interests Near Old Mill Station for the Easier Access Phase III Project - Stage 2
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, expropriations, municipalities, property (sc); boroughs; cities; counties; regional municipalities; towns, compulsory purchase; eminent domain, ttc
brief: The Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management asks City Council to advance Stage 2 of expropriating property interests at 39 Old Mill Road, 2662 Bloor Street West and 21 Old Mill Road for elevators at Old Mill Station under the Easier Access Phase III project. Council authorized the expropriation in February 2022; the Ontario Land Tribunal held a hearing in September 2023 and reported in February 2024 that the takings are fair, sound and reasonably necessary. Council is asked to consider the Tribunal report and pay $200 in hearing costs to the expropriated owner.

title: Application for Approval to Expropriate 320-326 Bloor Street West for the Spadina Station Streetcar Platform Extension - Stage 1
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, applications, expropriations, streetcars; application process, compulsory purchase; eminent domain, street-cars, ttc
brief: The Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management asks City Council to start Stage 1 of expropriating permanent and temporary easement interests in part of 320-326 Bloor Street West. The land is needed to extend the Spadina Station streetcar platform to fit two low-floor light rail vehicles, part of the TTC's Line 2 Capacity Enhancement Program. If Council approves, staff will serve and publish the Notice of Application for Approval to Expropriate, and owners will have 30 days to request a hearing of necessity.

title: Award of Doc4328129808 to ASCO Construction (Toronto) Ltd., for the Scarborough Pump Station Rehabilitation and New Atmospheric Surge Tank Project
topics: construction, contracts, purchasing, taxes; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, building, levies
brief: This is a procurement item: the Chief Engineer, the General Manager of Toronto Water and the Chief Procurement Officer ask City Council to award the Scarborough Pump Station rehabilitation and new atmospheric surge tank project to ASCO Construction (Toronto) Ltd. for $39,320,590 net of taxes ($40,012,633 net of HST recoveries). ASCO was the lowest supplier meeting the solicitation requirements, with an 83-week construction period. Council is asked to grant authority to award.

title: New Non-Competitive Contracts and Amendments to Various Competitive and Non-Competitive Blanket Contracts to Maintain Shelter Services
topics: contracts, housing services, purchasing, taxes; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, levies
brief: This is a procurement item: the General Manager, Toronto Shelter and Support Services, the Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management and the Chief Procurement Officer ask City Council for authority to enter two new non-competitive contracts and amend multiple blanket contracts and purchase orders to maintain shelter services. The spending covers catering at hotel shelter sites, emergency accommodation for refugees and families, centralized intake, interpretation services and state of good repair. Suspending these services would harm the City's ability to run the shelter system.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contracts and Non-Competitive Procurement for the Supply of Paging and Mobile Devices, Accessories and Services
topics: contracts, mobile application software, purchasing, services, taxes; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, levies, mobile app; smartphone app
brief: This is a procurement item: the Chief Technology Officer and the Chief Procurement Officer ask City Council to authorize spending on paging and mobile devices while the City awaits a new provincial Vendor of Record. The City has used the Province's Vendor of Record since 2020, and the Province extended it to July 31, 2024. Council is asked to approve a $890,000 amendment with Rogers Communications Canada Inc. plus bridge contracts with existing vendors.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Blanket Contract 47022515 with Joe Johnson Equipment for Supply and Delivery of Original Equipment Manufacturer Parts and Specialized Services for Warranty and Non-Warranty Repair and Maintenance
topics: budgets, contracts, maintenance, repairs, taxes; budgets and accounts, levies
brief: This is a procurement item: the General Manager, Fleet Services and the Chief Procurement Officer ask City Council to amend the non-competitive blanket contract with Joe Johnson Equipment for fleet parts and repair services. The amendment extends the term from five to ten years and raises the target value from $1,761,067 to $4,504,274, an increase of $2,743,207 net of HST. Council is asked to authorize the amendment.

title: Permanent Closure of portions of Bloor Street West, Dundas Street West and Kipling Avenue
topics: [activities in environment], [locations in recreation and tourism], road closures; street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: The Deputy General Manager, Transportation Services asks City Council to permanently close portions of Bloor Street West, Dundas Street West and Kipling Avenue. Once closed, the former highway lands would transfer to Parks, Forestry and Recreation for the construction of Dunkip Park and the expansion of Six Points Park. Council approval is required for permanent highway closures. Council is asked to authorize the closures.

title: 417-419 Burnhamthorpe Road - Zoning By-law Amendment and Site Plan Control Applications - Appeal Report
topics: townhouses, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The Director, Community Planning recommends that City Council oppose the zoning amendment application for 417-419 Burnhamthorpe Road at the Ontario Land Tribunal. The 2022 application proposed a four-storey townhouse building with 10 residential units; the applicant appealed in January 2024 after Council missed the decision deadline. Council is asked to direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the hearing in opposition while continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: 2636-2654 Eglinton Avenue West and 1856 and 1856A Keele Street - Zoning By-law Amendment and Site Plan Control Applications - Appeal Report
topics: multi-unit dwellings, zoning bylaws; multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The Director, Community Planning recommends that City Council oppose the zoning and site plan applications for 2636-2654 Eglinton Avenue West and 1856 and 1856A Keele Street at the Ontario Land Tribunal. The 2022 application proposed a 33-storey building with 370 residential units and 324 square metres of non-residential space; the applicant appealed in January 2024. Council is asked to direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the hearing in opposition.

title: U-turn Prohibition - Aukland Road and St. Albans Road
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, turn prohibitions (traffic); ttc
brief: The Director, Traffic Management asks City Council to prohibit U-turns at all times on Aukland Road between Dundas Street West and St. Albans Road, and on St. Albans Road between Aukland Road and the access road from southbound Kipling Avenue. Transportation Services requested the prohibitions for traffic safety. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on both roads.

title: 135 Plunkett Road - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, rezoning; developing land; development (land); land development, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: The Director, Community Planning recommends that City Council amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 to permit a residential development at 135 Plunkett Road. The proposal is six blocks of stacked back-to-back townhouses, about 14.5 metres high, with 146 dwelling units, 13,057 square metres of floor area and 164 underground parking spaces. Staff find the proposal conforms with provincial and Official Plan policies. Council is asked to approve the amendment with a holding provision.

title: Review of Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee
topics: aboriginal services, advisory committees, governance; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups, governance structure; municipal governance
brief: The City Manager and City Clerk recommend that City Council adopt new Terms of Reference for the Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee so it can resume operation. During the 2018-2022 term, committee members raised concerns about the committee's structure and procedures. Council is also asked to have the City Clerk canvass councillors for interest in appointment, and to have the committee review its mandate by the end of 2025.

title: Toronto Water 2023 Year End Capital Budget and 2024-2033 Capital Plan Adjustments
topics: capital budgets, projects;
brief: This is a finance item: the General Manager, Toronto Water asks City Council to authorize cashflow reallocations in Toronto Water's capital budgets. The adjustments reallocate $33.877 million in 2023 for project accelerations and deferrals within the approved capital budget and plan. The adjustments have zero dollar impact on the approved budgets. Council is asked to approve the reallocations.

title: City of Toronto’s 2024 Corporate Asset Management Plan
topics: financial reports, investment, planning; annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is a finance item: the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends that City Council adopt the City of Toronto's 2024 Corporate Asset Management Plan. Much of the City's infrastructure dates from the post-war period and will need growing investment over time. Council is asked to adopt the plan and authorize the Executive Director, Financial Planning to make non-material amendments before the July 1, 2024 regulatory deadline.

title: Adjustments to Capital Budget, Carry Forward Funding and Future Year Commitments
topics: capital budgets, funding; financing
brief: This is a finance item: the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer asks City Council to approve an additional $519.9 million in carry-forward funding from unspent 2023 capital projects. The 2024-2033 capital budget already carried forward $1.157 billion based on earlier estimates; the closed 2023 actuals increased the request. The funding lets City programs and agencies continue previously approved capital projects in 2024 and beyond. Council is asked to approve the adjustment.

title: 3-5 Marina Avenue - Development Charges Complaint
topics: complaints, development charges;
brief: The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends that City Council dismiss the development charges complaint for 3-5 Marina Avenue in Etobicoke-Lakeshore. The complainant, Dan Iannetti, objects that charges for two semi-detached dwellings with secondary units were calculated at the singles and semis rate rather than the multiples rate. Staff recommend Council determine the Development Charges By-law was properly applied and dismiss the October 11, 2023 complaint.

title: Extending the Mandate of the City’s Chief Information Security Officer
topics: corporations, information and communication technology, information management, security; ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it, information handling; information processing
brief: The Chief Information Security Officer recommends that City Council extend the mandate of the City's cybersecurity office to cover all City agencies and corporations. The independent Office of the Chief Information Security Officer was created in 2020 on the Auditor General's recommendation. Council is asked to direct the officer to build a cyber security risk management partnership with agencies, fold their risks into the City's governance program, and conduct ongoing monitoring.

title: Ontario Line Pape Segment Advanced Works - Temporary Road Closures and Transportation Impacts
topics: construction, road closures, transportation; building, street closures; temporary highway closings, transportation services
brief: The General Manager, Transportation Services asks City Council to approve temporary long-term lane closures for Metrolinx's Ontario Line Pape segment advanced works. The work covers the Gerrard portal, Pape Station and Sammon crossover sites, plus Don Valley Parkway slope stabilization at the Minton Place portal. The closures include rescinding permit parking on the south side of Riverdale Avenue from June 1, 2024 to January 31, 2026. Council is asked to approve the closures and traffic by-law amendments.

title: 130th Edition of the Good Roads Conference April 21 - 24, 2024
topics: conferences, infrastructure, transportation; conference travel, transportation services
brief: This is an information item: Councillor Paul Ainslie, Toronto's appointee to the Ontario Good Roads Association board, reports on the 130th annual Good Roads conference held April 21-24, 2024. The conference theme was connecting global change to local impacts and solutions, with over 100 seminars on transportation infrastructure topics. Ainslie recommends Council receive the report for information.
