topics: boards of management, budgets, municipalities; boards of directors; boards of governors, boroughs; cities; counties; regional municipalities; towns, budgets and accounts

The meetings covered federal infrastructure funding, a municipal growth framework, community safety and support for asylum claimants. Ainslie recommends Council receive the report for information.

The report follows up on the General Government Committee's December 2023 consideration, which the Executive Committee took over in April 2024. Council is asked to approve the amendments.

The proposal includes 15 rental replacement units and a new 136 square metre open space along Irwin Avenue. An Official Plan amendment is needed for the tall building.

title: 34-42 Maitland Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment, and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, official plan amendments, rental housing, zoning bylaws; rental properties; rental units, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a 56-storey residential building with 532 dwelling units at 34-42 Maitland Street. The proposal includes 55 rental replacement units and a Tenant Relocation and Assistance Plan for residents of demolished rental housing. An Official Plan amendment is needed to allow the tall building on the site.

title: Establishing a Community Safety Zone on Blake Street
topics: safety, schools, transportation; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, public safety, transportation services
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher asks Council to designate a Community Safety Zone, in effect at all times, on both sides of Blake Street between Strathcona Avenue and Boultbee Avenue. Blake Street is a residential street with two schools and a community centre nearby, and residents are concerned about traffic volume and speeding. Council is also asked to have Transportation Services consider moving the automated speed camera from Strathcona Avenue west of Blake Street onto Blake Street once the zone is designated.

title: Ambassador Pizza (946 Bloor Street West) - Exemption of Polling Requirements under Chapter 742
topics: boulevard cafes; boulevard patios (restaurants); sidewalk cafes; sidewalk patios (restaurants)
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo asks Council to exempt Ambassador Pizza at 946 Bloor Street West from the polling and notice requirements of the sidewalk cafe bylaw when it applies for its 2024 summer cafe season permit. The restaurant expanded onto the connecting property and beautified an existing sidewalk cafe patio in place since 2014. The exemption covers the notice requirements in section 742-2.3 and the objection provisions in sections 742-3.2A(2) and 742-4.3B(2).

title: 931 Yonge Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, planning approvals, zoning bylaws; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a 32-storey mixed-use building with 250 dwelling units and ground-floor commercial space at 931 Yonge Street. The project is part of the ModernTO program, with at least 33 percent of units secured as affordable. City Council is asked to amend the zoning by-law to permit the building.

title: 171-175 Lowther Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve an 11-storey residential building with 64 dwelling units at 171-175 Lowther Avenue. The plan re-designates the lands from Neighbourhoods to Apartment Neighbourhoods and partly conserves the designated heritage building at 171 Lowther Avenue, integrating it into the new development. Three rental units in the heritage building would be demolished.

title: Pedestrian Crossing Protection - Front Street East and Scott Street
topics: pedestrian crossovers, pedestrian infrastructure; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, pedestrian network
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize traffic control signals at the intersection of Front Street East and Scott Street. Transportation Services assessed pedestrian crossing safety there and found the warrant criteria were met, concluding signals will make the intersection safer for all road users. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Front Street East.

title: Accessible Parking Space - Springhurst Avenue
topics: accessible permit parking; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled)
brief: Staff recommend that City Council designate an on-street accessible parking space on the north side of Springhurst Avenue, between a point 57 metres west of Dufferin Street and a point 5.5 metres further west. The space would be in effect at all times. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on the street.

title: 350 Bloor Street East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a 63-storey mixed-use building with 806 dwelling units at 350 Bloor Street East. The proposal includes at least 400 square metres of non-residential space and dedicates 1,300 square metres to new affordable housing. An Official Plan amendment is required for development within 10 metres of the top-of-bank of a ravine and to reduce office uses.

title: Douro Street (1071 King Street West) - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, road closures; building, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Hallmark is building a 14-storey residential building at 1071 King Street West, and staff recommend that City Council authorize closing the west sidewalk and the southbound and northbound vehicle lanes on Douro Street, south of King Street West, for 33 months from April 30, 2024 to January 31, 2027. The closure is for construction staging. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on King Street West.

title: 400-420 King Street West - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, transportation; transportation services, ttc
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council, needed because the TTC operates on King Street West, to extend the construction staging closure for TMG Builders' 49-storey mixed-use condominium at 400-420 King Street West. The closure covers the north sidewalk and westbound curb lane on King Street West between Charlotte Street and 66 metres east, with a temporary pedestrian walkway, and the east sidewalk on Charlotte Street was approved until December 31, 2026.

title: Road and Intersection Safety Review - Winona Drive at St. Clair Avenue West and Barrie Avenue
topics: road safety;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council prohibit westbound right turns on a red signal at all times at the intersection of St. Clair Avenue West and Winona Drive. Staff also recommend rescinding the existing 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. weekday parking prohibition nearby. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on St. Clair Avenue West.

title: 350-396 Queens Quay West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: improvement, zoning bylaws; enhancement; rehabilitation (property), zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the zoning amendment for 350-396 Queens Quay West to permit a 16-storey residential tower above the existing five-storey parkade at 396 Queens Quay West, for a total height of 21 storeys or 66 metres. The proposal adds 249 new dwelling units and 43 hotel suites, alters the existing buildings, and includes public realm enhancements along Queens Quay West.

title: 65-83 Raglan Avenue - Public Art Plan
topics: planning, public art; outdoor art; outdoor sculptures; outdoor statues
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the Public Art Plan for 65-83 Raglan Avenue. The plan sets out how the owner will commission public art in a new park next to the site, covering the vision, locations, and commissioning process. This is a Section 37 agreement item.

title: 68 Wellesley Street East - Refusal of Application for Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties Under Part IV, Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the proposed alterations to the designated heritage property at 68 Wellesley Street East under the Ontario Heritage Act. The proposal would build a new 28-storey mixed-use building tied to the property, and staff say the plans do not meet heritage requirements. City Council decides whether to refuse or approve the application.

title: 650 (650A and 652) and 664 Yonge Street - Alterations to Heritage Properties, Demolition of Attributes and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: development, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the alterations and demolition of attributes proposed for the heritage properties at 650 (650A and 652) and 664 Yonge Street in connection with a 75-storey mixed-use tower with mechanical penthouses. The proposal conserves the buildings by restoring the primary street-facing facades and demolishing other attributes.

title: 36-42 Maitland Street - Alterations to Heritage Properties, Demolition of Attributes and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: demolitions, easements, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the alterations and demolition proposed for the heritage properties at 36-42 Maitland Street under the Ontario Heritage Act, in connection with a 56-storey residential tower with mechanical penthouse and three levels of underground parking. The proposal conserves the primary south elevations of 36 and 42 Maitland Street in place and panelizes and reconstructs parts of the side elevations.

title: 346 Yonge Street, 7 Elm Street, 13 Elm Street and 34 - 52 River Street - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage properties, official plan amendments; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council add thirteen properties to the City's Heritage Register for their cultural heritage value: 346 Yonge Street, 7 and 13 Elm Street, and 34 to 52 River Street. The Elm Street properties include Georgian Revival houses and a Second Empire mixed-use building, and the River Street properties are north of Queen Street East.

title: 171 Lowther Avenue - Alterations to a Heritage Property and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage properties, official plan amendments, zoning; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the alterations proposed for the designated heritage property at 171 Lowther Avenue and grant authority to enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement. The property, built in 1901-1902 in the West Annex between Walmer Road and Dalton Street, would allow construction of an 11-storey residential building.

title: 2453-2469 Bloor Street West - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, zoning bylaws; developing land; development (land); land development, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the zoning amendment for 2453-2469 Bloor Street West in a modified form, permitting a 10-storey mixed-use building instead of the 13 storeys proposed. The modified approval better fits the area's context and preserves sunlight on the public realm along Bloor Street West; the proposal includes 91 dwelling units and 260 square metres of ground-floor retail.

title: 350 Bloor Street East - Demolition of a Designated Heritage Property with Conditions
topics: heritage properties, official plan amendments; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the demolition of the designated heritage property at 350 Bloor Street East, with conditions under Section 34(1)2 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The conditions require the replacement structure to commemorate the original building, including reinstating its precast concrete panels on the podium as part of a reconstruction strategy for the six-storey site.

title: 134 Carlton Street, 50 Richmond Street East and 860 Richmond Street West - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council add three properties to the City's Heritage Register for their cultural heritage value: 134 Carlton Street, 50 Richmond Street East, and 860 Richmond Street West. The properties include a three-storey apartment building on Carlton Street across from Allan Gardens and buildings in Ward 10 and Ward 13.

title: Liberty Village Public Realm Strategy - Final Report
topics: applications, development, transportation; application process, developing land; development (land); land development, transportation services
brief: Staff recommend that City Council adopt the Liberty Village Public Realm Strategy. The strategy sets a vision for high-quality streetscapes, open spaces, and right-of-way connections, with principles, guidelines, and an implementation plan to create a connected, walkable, attractive, and safe neighbourhood. It would guide development applications, road work, capital projects, and new parks.

title: 10 Huntley Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, planning;
brief: The applicant appealed City staff's decision on a 45-storey, 334-unit residential building proposed for 10 Huntley Street, sending it to the Ontario Land Tribunal. City Planning recommends that City Council direct staff and the City Solicitor to oppose the appeal at the tribunal while continuing talks with the applicant. City Council decides whether to fight the appeal.

title: 595 Bay Street and 306 Yonge Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, planning;
brief: The applicant appealed City staff's decision on a 34-storey, 317-unit mixed-use building proposed at 595 Bay Street and 306 Yonge Street, sending it to the Ontario Land Tribunal. The proposal would demolish part of the Atrium on Bay retail building while keeping the office towers. City Planning recommends that City Council direct staff and the City Solicitor to oppose the appeal at the tribunal.

title: 467-479 Wellington Street West and 33 Draper Street -Zoning Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal item: the applicant's 2022 zoning amendment for a 23-storey mixed-use building with 225 dwelling units at 467-479 Wellington Street West and 33 Draper Street was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after Council did not decide in time. Staff recommend Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the appeal in its current form while continuing discussions.

title: 68-78 Wellesley Street East and 505-509 Church Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the application for a 28-storey mixed-use building with 258 residential units at 68-78 Wellesley Street East and 505-509 Church Street. Staff say the building's form and massing do not fit the Church Street Character Area policies. If the decision is appealed, staff recommend using mediation to resolve the outstanding issues.

title: 70-86 Lynn Williams Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the zoning amendment application for 70-86 Lynn Williams Street in its current form. The proposal is a 43-storey mixed-use building with 588 rental units; staff found it does not meet Official Plan policies on public realm and built form, does not appropriately respond to heritage resources, and fails servicing requirements. If appealed, Council would direct the City Solicitor.

title: 1141 Bloor Street West, 980 Dufferin Street, and 90 Croatia Street - Official Plan Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council amend the Official Plan for 1141 Bloor Street West, 980 Dufferin Street, and 90 Croatia Street to correctly identify the interior floor space of the two lower floors of the former Kent School building, which will be conveyed to the City as a community hub including a child care facility. Council authority is also sought to correct the Section 37 provision's floor area.

title: 195-209 Shaughnessy Boulevard, Unit 609  - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 21 125986 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, committee meetings, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee will hear the appeal of a property standards order issued February 16, 2024 for 195-209 Shaughnessy Boulevard, Unit 609 (file 21 125986 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order. The appeal is the owner's chance to challenge the city's repair or maintenance requirements.

title: 30 Tuxedo Court - Application for a Clothing Drop Box Location permit
topics: clothing drop boxes, permits; clothes donation boxes; clothing bins, permit renewal
brief: Municipal Licensing and Standards refused a clothing drop box location permit at 30 Tuxedo Court, and the applicant has asked City Council to reconsider. Staff recommend that City Council either deny or approve the application. City Council makes the final decision on the permit.

title: 10 Tuxedo Court - Application for a Clothing Drop Box Location Permit
topics: clothing drop boxes, permits; clothes donation boxes; clothing bins, permit renewal
brief: Municipal Licensing and Standards refused a clothing drop box location permit at 10 Tuxedo Court, and the applicant has asked City Council to reconsider. Staff recommend that City Council either deny or approve the application. City Council makes the final decision on the permit.

title: Temporary Use Zoning By-law for Public Spaces on Private Property - Wexford Pilot Project
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council enact a temporary use zoning by-law for three years, under Section 39 of the Planning Act, to let the non-profit PlazaPOPS turn underused parking lots and spaces in the Wexford Heights BIA into free, safe, accessible public gathering places. The current zoning by-law does not allow reducing lawfully existing parking spaces for these public spaces.

title: 1125 to 1137 Markham Road and 2141 Ellesmere Road - Zoning Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: redevelopment, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the zoning amendment and draft plan of subdivision for 1125 to 1137 Markham Road and 2141 Ellesmere Road to permit three towers of 18, 33, and 37 storeys plus an eight-storey mid-rise, with a new public park and two new public roads dedicated to the City. Existing structures would be demolished; the proposal conforms to the Growth Plan.

title: 2771 and 2773 Victoria Park Avenue - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the zoning amendment for 2771 and 2773 Victoria Park Avenue in an amended form to permit a four-storey stacked and back-to-back townhouse building with 62 dwelling units and 31 surface parking spaces. Staff reviewed the applicant's original proposal and support the amended version.

title: Port Union Road Widening Project
topics: road operations, road reconstruction; road alterations; road narrowing; road widening, road services
brief: With construction on the Port Union Road widening project underway, Councillor Jennifer McKelvie recommends that City Council designate a two-way centre left-turn-only lane on Port Union Road between 58 metres south of Island Road and Dear Gate, and prohibit eastbound right turns on red at all times at Lawrence Avenue East and Port Union Road, to enhance safety and operations.

title: Intersection Safety Review - Kingston Road and Collinsgrove Road
topics: intersections, road safety;
brief: This is an information item: Scarborough Community Council asked Transportation Services to review safety and operations at the intersection of Kingston Road and Collinsgrove Road. Staff recommend that City Council receive the safety review report for information. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Kingston Road.

title: 567 Scarborough Golf Club Road - Application for a Clothing Drop Box Location Permit
topics: clothing drop boxes, permits; clothes donation boxes; clothing bins, permit renewal
brief: Municipal Licensing and Standards refused a clothing drop box location permit at 567 Scarborough Golf Club Road, and the applicant has asked City Council to reconsider. Staff recommend that City Council either deny or approve the application. City Council makes the final decision on the permit.

title: 370 McCowan Road - Application for a Clothing Drop Box Location permit
topics: clothing drop boxes, permits; clothes donation boxes; clothing bins, permit renewal
brief: Municipal Licensing and Standards refused a clothing drop box location permit at 370 McCowan Road, and the applicant has asked City Council to reconsider. Staff recommend that City Council either deny or approve the application. City Council makes the final decision on the permit.

title: 215 Markham Road - Application for a Clothing Drop Box Location permit
topics: clothing drop boxes, permits; clothes donation boxes; clothing bins, permit renewal
brief: Municipal Licensing and Standards refused a clothing drop box location permit at 215 Markham Road, and the applicant has asked City Council to reconsider. Staff recommend that City Council either deny or approve the application. City Council makes the final decision on the permit.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council reviews the Order Paper, the formal record of Council's agenda business. The review is part of the regular order of business at the April 17, 2024 Council meeting. No decision is attached.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions, and announcements will be made at the City Council meeting. These are ceremonial or informational items with no decision attached.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council may file petitions at the meeting. Petitions are formal requests from the public or councillors brought to Council's attention.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council declare their interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act. Declarations of interest ensure councillors do not take part in decisions where they have a personal stake.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from the Mayor and City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council introduces the committee reports and new business from the Mayor and City officials at the start of the meeting. The reports come from the Executive Committee, Economic and Community Development Committee, General Government Committee, Infrastructure and Environment Committee, and Planning and Housing Committee. Mayor Olivia Chow submits the Executive Committee report.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will confirm the minutes from the regular meeting held on March 20 and 21, 2024. Confirming the minutes makes them the official record of the meeting.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council opens the meeting with O Canada and a moment of silence. The call to order is the formal start of the council session.

title: Short-Term Rental By-law Implementation Update
topics: by-laws, rental housing; bylaws, rental properties; rental units
brief: This report updates City Council on implementation of the short-term rental by-law, which requires operators to register and companies to be licensed with the City. Staff recommend that City Council amend the by-law to require applicants, on request, to provide at least two extra documents beyond government-issued identification to prove their principal residence. Only owners and tenants renting their principal residence for less than 28 consecutive days may register.

title: RentSafeTO Program Update Report
topics: [activities in property], [organizations in property], buildings, property maintenance, tenant organizations; grounds maintenance; groundskeeping
brief: This report updates City Council on RentSafeTO, the program enforcing maintenance and operational standards for rental apartment buildings of three or more storeys and ten or more units. Staff recommend that City Council amend the Apartment Buildings chapter of the municipal code, including removing COVID-19 measures and requiring notification board information to be posted so each piece is readable. The program aims to strengthen bylaw compliance and proactive maintenance in rental buildings.

title: Improvements to the Sign By-law Amendment and Sign Variance Process
topics: change, improvement; amendments; conversion; modification, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: This report responds to a 2023 committee direction to review the Sign By-law amendment and variance process. The Chief Building Official recommends that City Council amend the Signs chapter of the Municipal Code to streamline and clarify how sign by-law amendments and variances are processed, and delegate authority to the Chief Building Official so amendment applications are not used as a substitute for the variance process.

title: Technical Amendments to Zoning By-law 569-2013
topics: urban planning, zoning bylaws; city planning; community planning; regional planning, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This report proposes technical amendments to Zoning By-law 569-2013 to correct typographical errors, clarify wording and regulations, and adjust zoning and overlay map boundaries. Staff recommend that City Council enact the amendments and authorize the City Solicitor to make stylistic and technical changes as needed. The amendments also respond to a Planning and Housing Committee motion about incorporating low-rise residential lands into the by-law.

title: Support for Habitat for Humanity Housing Development
topics: housing, rental housing; homes; residences, rental properties; rental units
brief: The Executive Director, Housing Secretariat, recommends that City Council approve financial support for an affordable home ownership development by Habitat for Humanity Greater Toronto Area. Affordable homeownership is part of the HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan, since households unable to buy add demand to the rental market. The instructions are in confidential attachments to the April 2, 2024 report, which would be released publicly at the Executive Director's discretion.

title: Taking Action to Accelerate Modular and Rapid Build Construction in Toronto
topics: affordable housing, construction; affordable homes; housing projects, building
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford recommends that City Council accelerate modular and rapid-build construction to increase housing supply and restore affordability. The recommendation asks City Council to direct staff to issue a follow-up pre-qualification by the fourth quarter of 2024 to expand the City's existing pre-qualified vendors for rapid-build housing. The report cites the modular supportive housing site at 540 Cedarvale, built within days, as an example of the technology's benefits.

title: 6 and 8 Cawthra Square - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the properties at 6 and 8 Cawthra Square under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The properties, between Jarvis and Church Streets near Barbara Hall Park, are recognized for their cultural heritage value. Statements of Significance set out the reasons for designation.

title: Our Plan Toronto: Official Plan Chapter One - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning
brief: Staff recommend that City Council adopt Official Plan Amendment 718, which sets out Chapter One of the Official Plan. Chapter One contains the vision-based statements that guide how Toronto will grow over the next 30 years, balancing the needs of current residents with those of future generations. The Official Plan is Toronto's roadmap for growth, and Chapter One is its compass.

title: 322 La Rose Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 322 La Rose Avenue, known as the La Rose Farmhouse, under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property is on the north side of La Rose Avenue, east of Islington Avenue, and is recognized for its cultural heritage value. A Statement of Significance sets out the reasons for designation.

title: 294, 306 and 318 Lawrence Avenue East and 101 Mildenhall Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the properties at 294, 306, and 318 Lawrence Avenue East and 101 Mildenhall Road under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The properties on the north side of Lawrence Avenue East, between Mildenhall Road and Bayview Avenue, are recognized for their cultural heritage value. Statements of Significance set out the reasons for designation.

title: 24 Mason Boulevard - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 24 Mason Boulevard under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The North York property, southwest of Yonge Street and York Mills Road, contains the late-19th-century Denison/Mason Farmhouse, a vernacular Ontario farmhouse recognized for its cultural heritage value. A Statement of Significance sets out the reasons for designation.

title: 111 and 115 Berkeley Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the properties at 111 and 115 Berkeley Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The properties anchor the southeast corner of Berkeley and Richmond Street East in the King-Parliament community and are recognized for their cultural heritage value. Statements of Significance set out the reasons for designation.

title: 1 Heritage Place - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 1 Heritage Place under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The property in Etobicoke's Humber Heights-Westmount neighbourhood contains a two-storey detached house form building recognized for its cultural heritage value. A Statement of Significance sets out the reasons for designation.

title: 64 Woodlawn Avenue West - Refusal of Repeal of Designating By-law under Section 32 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Proposed Amendment to Designating By-law under Part IV, Section 30.1 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the application to repeal heritage designation By-law 606-2018 for 64 Woodlawn Avenue West under the Ontario Heritage Act. The property contains a 2½-storey house built in 1906, designed by architect Eden Smith. Staff also recommend that City Council state its intention to amend the designating by-law.

title: 1111 Danforth Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 1111 Danforth Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The property contains a two-storey buff brick building on a basement, built in 1931 in the Neo-Gothic style, on the south side of Danforth Avenue between Byron and Greenwood Avenues.

title: Etobicoke Creek Watershed Plan
topics: land use, watersheds; subwatersheds
brief: Staff recommend that City Council endorse the Etobicoke Creek Watershed Plan, a non-statutory document guiding land use decisions, natural heritage restoration, and flood remediation. The plan was developed by the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority with City, Peel, Mississauga, Brampton, Caledon, Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation, and airport authority staff. Council is also asked to direct staff to advise the conservation authority of the City's ongoing commitment.

title: Response to Including New Approval Conditions for Rental Demolition Applications
topics: demolitions, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: This report responds to City Council's request to review the City's approval conditions for rental housing demolition applications under Chapter 667 of the Toronto Municipal Code. It addresses matters such as requiring additional purpose-built market rent units as a condition of approval. Staff recommend that City Council ask the Chief Planner to publish updated implementation practices for rental demolition and conversion applications on the City's website.

title: Housing Now - Bloor-Islington and Islington Bus Terminal - City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment and Plan of Subdivision - Decision Report - Approval
topics: redevelopment, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve City-initiated zoning changes and a plan of subdivision for the Bloor-Islington Housing Now site and the new Islington bus terminal. The City-owned lands at 3326 and 3330 Bloor Street West and 1240 and 1226 Islington Avenue are one of 22 Housing Now sites approved for redevelopment. The zoning changes would permit a multi-tower development concept and set standards for the relocated TTC bus terminal.

title: 26-38 Hounslow Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a 26-storey residential building with 305 units at 26-38 Hounslow Avenue. The building would have 19,384.5 square metres of gross floor area, at 8.98 times the site area, with 1,310 square metres of indoor and outdoor amenity space. Parking would be in two levels of underground parking accessed from Hounslow Avenue.

title: 680 and 688 Sheppard Avenue East - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, applications, demolitions, rental housing, zoning bylaws; application process, rental properties; rental units, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the rental housing demolition application to demolish 47 existing rental units at 680 and 688 Sheppard Avenue East and replace them with 47 new rental units of the same types and sizes at similar rents. The related Official Plan and zoning amendment was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, which approved it in a February 2023 decision.

title: 390-400 Woodsworth Road - Official Plan, Zoning By-law Amendment, Site Plan Control, and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Appeal Report
topics: Official Plans, applications, demolitions, official plan amendments, rental housing, site plan control, zoning bylaws; application process, rental properties; rental units, site plan approvals, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The applicant appealed City staff's decision on a proposal for 8, 9, and 10-storey residential buildings and stacked townhouses at 390-400 Woodsworth Road, sending it to the Ontario Land Tribunal. The proposal has 603 units, including replacement of 80 demolished rental townhouses with new rental units. City Planning recommends that City Council direct staff and the City Solicitor to oppose the appeal at the tribunal.

title: 278 - 280 Viewmount Avenue - Zoning Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, applications, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal item: the applicant's 2022 zoning amendment for a 33-storey, 107-metre residential building with 342 units and 296 square metres of ground-floor retail at 278-280 Viewmount Avenue was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in December 2023 after Council did not decide in time. The proposal has about 22,360 square metres of floor area at a density of 15.5 times the site. Staff recommend Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the appeal while continuing discussions.

title: 379-381 Wilson Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: multi-unit dwellings, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the zoning amendment for 379-381 Wilson Avenue to permit a 13-storey, 41.10-metre mixed-use building with 261 dwelling units, 19,172 square metres of gross floor area including 481 square metres of non-residential space, at a density of 4.58 times the lot area.

title: Naming 125 Consumers Road in North York to David Caplan Park
topics: community development, equity, naming; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development, employment equity; fair wage; pay equity
brief: Councillor Shelley Carroll recommends that North York Community Council approve naming 125 Consumers Road as David Caplan Park and placing a plaque honouring his contributions. David Caplan was a Toronto-born public servant from North York who served as a school trustee, including vice-chair of the North York Board of Education, and was elected Member of Provincial Parliament for Oriole in 1997. North York Community Council is the decision body for the naming.

title: Parkwoods Village Drive and Combermere Drive - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic control systems, traffic management, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council, needed because the TTC operates on Parkwoods Village Drive, to authorize traffic control signals at the intersection of Parkwoods Village Drive and Combermere Drive. Staff's assessment supports the signals to enhance safety for all road users.

title: 461 Sheppard Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments for 461 Sheppard Avenue East to permit a 44-storey, 144-metre mixed-use building with 513 dwelling units and 29,151 square metres of gross floor area, including 372 square metres of ground-floor retail, at a density of 13.07 times the lot area.

title: 18-28 Athabaska Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments for 18-28 Athabaska Avenue to permit a 43-storey, 135.15-metre mixed-use building with 516 residential units and 31,983 square metres of gross floor area, at a density of 10.81 times the lot area. The proposal conforms to the Growth Plan.

title: Portlands Energy Centre: Request for Environmental Assessment - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: energy, environmental assessments; ea; ecological assessment; environmental assessment; environmental evaluation, energy resources; energy use
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe, on the proposed 50-megawatt expansion of the 550-megawatt Portlands Energy Centre natural gas plant in the Port Lands. The final Screening Report released in March 2024 did not address the City's comments and questions on the draft. Council is asked to request the Minister of Environment, Conservation and Parks to elevate Atura Power's expansion proposal to a comprehensive environmental assessment.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2023.TE7.91- Altering Turning Restrictions at Old Forest Hill Road and Eglinton Avenue West - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: traffic regulations, traffic signal timing; advanced green; amber light phase; coordination of traffic signals; left turn arrow phase; left turn phase; pedestrian crossover timing; signal timing; traffic light timing; traffic signal operations; traffic signal phases; traffic signal synchronization
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, to re-open and amend Council's October 2023 decision on turning restrictions at Old Forest Hill Road and Eglinton Avenue West. The incomplete Eglinton Crosstown construction has pushed heavy traffic onto local roads, making the northbound left-turn prohibition (7 a.m. to 7 p.m. weekdays) unbearable for residents. Council is asked to delete Parts 4 and 5 of its earlier decision, which set the turn prohibitions.

title: Re-opening and Amending Items 2023.MM12.18 and 2023.MM12.25 - Revising Temporary Adjustments to Parking Regulations on St. Clair Avenue West - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: parking, transportation; transportation services
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow, to re-open and amend earlier decisions setting temporary parking restrictions on St. Clair Avenue West during streetcar right-of-way construction. The motion clarifies when the temporary regulations expire by replacing the phrase about resumed TTC streetcar service with the fixed date of June 19, 2024 in Part 19. Council is also asked to restore pre-construction conditions along the corridor.

title: Amending Item 2022.EY33.8 - 337-349 Queens Drive - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Final Report - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: by-laws, site plan control, zoning; bylaws, site plan approvals
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, to amend Council's 2022 approval of the zoning by-law amendment for 337-349 Queens Drive. The approval allowed 20 townhouses and eight semi-detached homes, but staff found two regulations were inadvertently omitted from the draft by-law during site plan review. Council is asked to delete and replace Parts 1 and 2 of its earlier decision with a corrected by-law.

title: Transforming the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence River Basin into a Thriving Blue-Green Economic Corridor While Safeguarding Our Freshwater Resources - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: environmental impacts, environmental policies, environmental programs, environmental projects; environmental effects; environmental footprint; environmental impact, environmental initiatives; green living, environmental policy; environmental standards; sewer use bylaws
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, on turning the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence River Basin into a blue-green economic corridor while safeguarding freshwater resources. The Cities Initiative is launching a Mayors Commission on Economic Transformation at its May 2024 conference in Montreal, which will develop a 2025-2035 action plan. Council and the Mayor are asked to affirm their commitment to work with the Cities Initiative and guide the Commission's mission.

title: Metrolinx Eglinton Crosstown Light Rail Transit - New Traffic Control Signals - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: light rail transit, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, lrt
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, to authorize new traffic control signals for the Eglinton Crosstown Light Rail Transit project. Metrolinx built a bus terminal at Eglinton Avenue East and Don Mills Road, with new signals at Eglinton and Gervais Drive, Gervais Drive and the bus terminal entrance, and Don Mills Road and the bus terminal exit. Council approval is needed to inspect, accept and activate the signals for efficient TTC bus operations.

title: Cancellation of the Vacant Home Tax Program - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: property taxes, taxes; levies, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday, to immediately cancel the Vacant Home Tax program after more than 60,000 complaints and hundreds of residents wrongly billed thousands of dollars. The motion also asks Council to direct the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer and the Executive Director, Housing Secretariat to report by the fourth quarter of 2024 on innovative alternatives for addressing vacant homes. The motion says the program is invasive and disruptive beyond repair.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds to Amend the 2024-2033 Capital Budget and Plan for Parks, Forestry and Recreation for the L’Amoreaux Kidstown Waterpark Redevelopment - By Councillor Nick Mantas, Seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: parks, recreational facilities; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, recreation facilities; recreational amenities
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, to release Section 42 funds for the L'Amoreaux Kidstown Waterpark redevelopment. The waterpark, the City's only owned and operated free waterpark, opened in 1988 and is beyond its serviceable lifespan, closing for the 2024 season. Council is asked to amend the 2024 Capital Budget and 2025-2033 Capital Plan with $5 million for the improvements sub-project, with the redesigned park planned to reopen for summer 2025.

title: 30 Lakeside Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: appeals, motions; council decisions; decisions (council)
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, on the Toronto Local Appeal Body appeal for 30 Lakeside Avenue. The Committee of Adjustment refused the owner's application for variances to demolish a two-storey dwelling and build a new three-storey home with a pool and rear cabana on March 6, 2024, and the owner appealed on March 25. Council is asked to authorize the City Solicitor to attend the appeal body to uphold the refusal and retain outside counsel.

title: Supporting Domestic Post-Secondary Tuition Fees for Ukrainian Students Residing in Ontario under the Canada-Ukraine Authorization for Emergency Travel Program - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: students, travel; conference travel; seminar travel
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers, supporting Ukrainian students under the Canada-Ukraine Authorization for Emergency Travel program. Their non-refugee status blocks them from domestic post-secondary tuition rates, a difference of more than $20,000 per year, leaving some students unable to apply for school. Council is asked to request the Government of Ontario extend the international tuition fee exemption and the Ontario Student Assistance Program to these students before September 2024.

title: Heroes' Way Ceremonial Street Name - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
topics: ceremonies, memorials; ceremonial, monuments; permanent memorials
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, for a ceremonial street name honouring the first responders of the April 23, 2018 Yonge Street van attack. The motion asks the City Manager to review naming Canterbury Place in North York — a local street running parallel to Yonge Street between Ellerslie Avenue and Horsham Avenue — as "Heroes' Way". The City Manager is asked to report back in the fourth quarter of 2024 under the City's ceremonial naming rules.

title: Naming Rights Agreement with MLSE Foundation for Dixon Park Outdoor Basketball Courts and Refurbishment  - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: basketball, parks and open space areas; green spaces; open spaces
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday, for a naming rights agreement with the MLSE Foundation for the Dixon Park outdoor basketball courts. To mark their 30th season, the Toronto Raptors and MLSE Foundation will refurbish three basketball courts and two 3v3 pads at Dixon Park, building on a 2003 Vince Carter Court investment. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation to negotiate the naming rights agreement.

title: Amending Items 2020.TE16.9 and 2022.MM45.44 - 1071 King Street West - Rezoning Application - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: parkland dedication, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: This is a member motion from Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, to amend earlier decisions on the rezoning of 1071 King Street West. The Ontario Land Tribunal approved the rezoning in August 2022, including an on-site parkland dedication of at least 230 square metres to be transferred to the City free of encumbrances. Council is asked to amend the lead paragraph of Part 4 of its earlier decision regarding that parkland dedication.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2024.TE10.37 - Turn Prohibitions - Bloor Street West and Perth Avenue - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: traffic control systems, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, to re-open and amend the earlier decision on turn prohibitions at Bloor Street West and Perth Avenue. Residents and businesses raised access concerns after new traffic signals and turn prohibitions were installed. Council is asked to amend Part 4 of its earlier decision by deleting the words "and southbound", so the prohibition applies to northbound through movements at all times, bicycles excepted.

title: Improving the Vacant Home Tax Program for Seniors - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
topics: taxes; levies
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, to improve the Vacant Home Tax program for seniors after hundreds expressed frustration with the process. The motion asks Council to direct the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer and the Executive Director, Housing Secretariat to report in January 2025 on the number of vacant homes in 2022 and 2023 and the program's effectiveness. The Vacant Home Tax was implemented in 2022 to push vacant units back onto the market.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2023.NY8.11 - 2135 Sheppard Avenue East, 325 Yorkland Boulevard, 125 Consumers Road, 15 Smooth Rose Court, and 55 Smooth Rose Court - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, to re-open and amend the November 2023 approval of an 11-storey mixed-use building at 2135 Sheppard Avenue East, 325 Yorkland Boulevard, 125 Consumers Road, 15 Smooth Rose Court and 55 Smooth Rose Court. The approval included a maximum unit count and minimum unit mix intended for the draft zoning by-law that were not properly carried through. Council is asked to amend its earlier decision to fix the by-law provisions.

title: Waiving Permit Fee Charges for the 2024 Bum Run in Support of Colon Cancer Awareness - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: fees, permits; administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees, permit renewal
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, to waive the permit fee for the 2024 Bum Run colon cancer awareness event. The Bum Run is a Toronto-hosted, 100 percent non-profit volunteer event raising funds for early diagnosis clinics; 90 percent of colon cancer deaths are preventable through early diagnosis. Council is asked to direct Transportation Services to waive the permit fee under the fees and charges bylaw.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from Various Developments for a Permanent Memorial to the Yonge Street Tragedy - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
topics: funding, memorials; financing, monuments; permanent memorials
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, to authorize $118,452 in Section 37 funds from various developments to commission a permanent memorial to the 2018 Yonge Street Tragedy. The City consulted bereaved families and the injured, who envisioned a place of quiet contemplation honouring those lost and recognizing the North York community's resilience. Council is asked to amend the 2024 Capital Budget for Economic Development and Culture with $50,000 cash flow in 2024 and a $68,452 future-year commitment in 2025.

title: Businesses Operating without a Licence - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: business licences, businesses; business licensing; business permits; municipal licenses, commercial waste collection customers
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, on businesses operating without a licence. The City currently cannot close a business solely for lacking a licence; it can only temporarily suspend an existing licence for up to 14 days in cases of immediate danger to health or safety. Council is asked to direct the Executive Director, Municipal Licensing and Standards, with the City Solicitor, to identify actions including by-law amendments to address unsafe activity at both licensed and unlicensed premises.

title: Commemorative Tree and Bench Program Review - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: commemorative benches, commemorative trees;
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, to review the Commemorative Tree and Bench Program, which since 2000 has let residents dedicate a park bench or tree to a loved one. Donors and councillors have raised concerns about response and installation timelines, unclear eligible locations, and maintenance of benches and trees. Council is asked to direct the Acting General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation to review the program and report to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee by the first quarter of 2025.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2024.MM14.15 - King Street West Watermain and Track Renewal - Bus and Streetcar Rerouting along Queen Street West - Temporary Adjustments to Parking Regulations - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: light rail transit, parking regulations; lrt, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, to re-open and amend the February 2024 decision on temporary parking regulations for the King Street West watermain and track renewal project. Staff found technical amendments are needed to the bylaws to fix signage inconsistencies along the Queen Street West bus and streetcar reroute. Council is asked to delete Parts 19, 29, 30 and 33 of its earlier decision.

title: Use of Nathan Phillips Square - Doors Open Toronto and Pride Toronto - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: festivals and special events, public realm; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals, public spaces
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, for a one-time exemption to the facility usage policies at City Hall and Nathan Phillips Square for Doors Open 2024 and Pride Toronto 2024. The exemption would allow covering ground-level windows west of the main doors for the Doors Open Photo Laureate art exhibition. These exemptions were left out of the March 2024 Nathan Phillips Square events approval because the Photo Laureate details were still being developed.

title: Appointment of a Member of Council to the Toronto Police Service Board - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
brief: This is a member motion from Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, to appoint a member of Council to the Toronto Police Service Board. The new provincial Community Safety and Policing Act came into force April 1, 2024, making Councillor Jon Burnside ineligible to serve on the board as a former member of the Toronto Police Service. Council is asked to remove Burnside effective immediately and waive the requirement to canvass members for interest before appointing his replacement.

title: Renaming of Tiverton Avenue Parkette - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: commemorative benches, commemorative trees, naming;
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, to rename Tiverton Avenue Parkette as Caroline Huebner Parkette. Caroline Huebner immigrated to Canada from Poland in 1988, was raised in Scarborough, and became an educator who taught in Toronto, Egypt and Turkey. Council is asked to approve the renaming despite the provisions of the City of Toronto Property Naming Policy.

title: Accepting an In-Kind Donation from Banbury and Thorncliffe Park Tennis Clubs to Resurface the Tennis Courts at Banbury Park and to Reconstruct Court 6 at Leaside Park - by Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: reconstruction, tennis; rebuilding
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, to accept in-kind donations from community tennis clubs for court repairs in 2024. Council is asked to authorize Parks, Forestry and Recreation to accept up to $150,000 from the Banbury Tennis Club to resurface the courts at Banbury Park, plus a donation from the Thorncliffe Park Tennis Club to reconstruct Court 6 at Leaside Park. Community tennis clubs maintain capital reserve funds for court repairs under the City's 2004 tennis policy.

title: Fixing the Vacant Home Tax - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: taxes; levies
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, to fix the Vacant Home Tax rollout after residents declared online but still received tax bills, with no proper receipting or confirmation process. The motion asks Council to suspend the $21.24 late fee for the 2024 Vacant Home Tax and have the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer refund residents who already paid. It also directs the City Manager to improve the annual declaration process.

title: Project Design Changes to Superior Avenue Based on New Public Feedback
topics: cycling, low speed vehicles, on-street parking; bicycling, curb parking; curbside parking; street parking
brief: Councillor Amber Morley recommends that City Council ask the General Manager of Transportation Services to adjust the design of the Superior Avenue road project between Lake Shore Boulevard West and Stanley Avenue, based on new public feedback. Residents petitioned with concerns about the design and consultation process. The requested changes should continue to support reducing motor vehicle speeds on the Mimico Neighbourhood Mobility Plan project.

title: 55-65 Broadway Avenue - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: construction, curb extensions, development; building, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Times Group Corporation is building two 45-storey residential towers at 55-65 Broadway Avenue, with the south sidewalk and part of the eastbound curb lane on Broadway closed for construction staging. Staff recommend that City Council extend the closure from March 28, 2024 to December 31, 2025. This is a construction staging time extension.

title: Under Gardiner Public Realm Plan
topics: emergency plans, heritage properties, parks; building evacuation plans; business continuity plans; fire escape plans; fire safety plans, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Bentway Conservancy and the City have developed a vision for underused public space under and near the Gardiner Expressway in downtown Toronto. Staff recommend that City Council endorse, in principle, the Under Gardiner Public Realm Plan. The plan supports the Central Waterfront Secondary Plan and the Downtown Parks and Public Realm Plan, including improving north-south connections.

title: Cycling Network Plan: 2024 Cycling Infrastructure Installation - Second Quarter Update and Missing Sidewalk Program - 2024 Local Road Sidewalk Installations
topics: cycling maps, delegation of authority, zoning designations; permitted use requests; permitted uses, signing authorities
brief: Staff seek City Council authority to install new bikeway projects from the Cycling Network Plan, plus new sidewalks under the Missing Sidewalk Program. Proposed bikeways include cycle tracks and contra-flow bike lanes on Ferrand Drive and Rochefort Drive near Eglinton Avenue East. The Cycling Network Plan aims to connect gaps in the network and grow cycling into new parts of the city.

title: Toronto's Climate Change Readiness: Updates on commitments and a refreshed mandate for coordinating resilience activities
topics: climate change, greenhouse effect, weather; atmospheric phenomena; meteorological conditions; weather conditions, climate protection, greenhouse gas emissions
brief: This report gives City Council an update on Toronto's climate change work, highlighting progress toward net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2040 through the TransformTO plan. It proposes a renewed, coordinated approach to climate resilience as the city faces hotter, wetter, and wilder weather. Staff recommend that City Council receive the TransformTO Net Zero Progress and Accountability Report for information and confirm support for the renewed resilience focus.

title: Organics Processing Facilities Update
topics: organics processing facilities, solid waste management; solid waste management planning; swm; waste management
brief: Toronto owns and operates two anaerobic digestion organics processing facilities: the Disco Road facility, designed for 75,000 tonnes of organics per year, and the Dufferin facility. Staff recommend that City Council authorize the General Manager of Solid Waste Management Services to amend a purchase order with GHD Limited for detailed design and construction oversight to expand the facilities. The Green Bin program serves about 460,000 houses plus apartments, schools, and City buildings.

title: Post-Transition of the Blue Box Program to Extended Producer Responsibility and Results of District 2 Service Delivery Options Review
topics: bag tags, in-unit recycling containers, material recovery facilities; recycling plants; resource recovery centres; single-stream recycling facilities
brief: This report updates City Council on the transition of the Blue Box recycling program to Extended Producer Responsibility and staff's talks with Circular Materials about curbside collection after the transition. Those talks ended in early 2024 over cost-of-service timing requirements. Staff recommend that City Council direct staff to competitively procure daytime curbside collection in District 2 before the current agreement expires on August 2, 2026.

title: Increase in Penalty Amounts for Parking Offences and Establishment of New Electric Vehicle Parking Offences for Off-Street Parking Facilities
topics: parking enforcement, parking fines, parking infractions; blocked driveway; illegal parking; parking offences; parking violations; vehicle blocking driveway
brief: Staff recommend that City Council increase administrative penalty amounts for parking offences and establish new electric vehicle parking offences for off-street parking facilities, with an implementation date to come. The review, requested by the Infrastructure and Environment Committee, compared Toronto's penalties with other Canadian municipalities through a jurisdictional scan.

title: The Implementation of the Vacant Home Tax in 2024
topics: housing, public inquiries, taxes; homes; residences, judicial inquries, levies
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor Brad Bradford asks for information on the 2024 implementation of the Vacant Home Tax, after thousands of residents reported receiving demands for thousands of additional dollars in taxes. The inquiry seeks details on how the second year of the program was administered. No decision is attached; the inquiry asks questions rather than proposing action.

title: Award of Request of Proposal Doc3580308056 to Safedesign Apparel Ltd. for the Supply and Delivery of Station Wear (Trousers and Shirts) for Toronto Fire Services Division
topics: proposals, purchasing, suppliers; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, bids; request for proposal; rfp
brief: Staff report the proposal results and ask City Council for authority to award a contract to Safedesign Apparel Ltd., the highest-scoring supplier meeting all specifications, for the supply and delivery of station wear trousers and shirts for Toronto Fire Services. The contract is for one year with options to renew for six additional one-year periods.

title: Permanent Road Closure - Eglinton Avenue West, West of Croham Road
topics: highways, transportation infrastructure management, utility corridors; freeways; motorways; parkways, hydro corridors; hydro rights of way; rail corridors; rail rights of way, road management; transportation operations
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council to permanently close an unused portion of the public road in the northwest quadrant of Croham Road and Eglinton Avenue West, to support new infrastructure for the Caledonia GO station on the Barrie rail corridor. The closure would let the land be nominally transferred for the station project.

title: Expropriation of Properties for the St. Clair Avenue West Transportation Master Plan - Stage 2
topics: Master Plans, [transportation management], expropriations; compulsory purchase; eminent domain
brief: Staff ask City Council, as approving authority under the Expropriations Act, to approve the expropriation of property interests for the St. Clair Avenue West Transportation Master Plan, which aims to improve the multi-modal transportation network in the area. This is the second stage of the expropriation process, following notices served in the first stage.

title: Application for Approval to Expropriate Easements for the Construction of the Black Creek Sanitary Trunk Sewer Relief System - Stage 1
topics: expropriations, sanitary sewers, trunk sewers; compulsory purchase; eminent domain, main sewers; sewer mains
brief: Staff ask City Council for authority to start expropriation proceedings for permanent easements on parts of seven properties and a temporary easement on part of 2090 Jane Street, to facilitate phase one of Toronto Water's Black Creek Sanitary Trunk Sewer Relief System. This is stage one of the expropriation process; staff will continue negotiating to acquire the property interests.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Esri Canada Limited for Proprietary Geographic Information System Software Licences, Cloud Subscriptions and Related Maintenance
topics: geographic information systems, maintenance, software licences; geospatial layers; gis, software licenses
brief: Staff ask City Council for authority to negotiate and enter a one-year, non-competitive contract with Esri Canada Limited for proprietary geographic information system software licences, cloud subscriptions, and related maintenance, for $1,052,851 net of taxes. The additional Esri licences for existing products support anticipated City needs.

title: 12 Hillside Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the application for a two-storey detached dwelling with an integral garage at 12 Hillside Road. The site is designated Natural Areas, lies within the Natural Heritage System and the conservation authority's regulated area, and is subject to the ravine protection by-law. Staff say the proposal conflicts with provincial planning policy and the provincial Growth Plan.

title: 630 The East Mall - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report

City Council must adopt the municipal levy, education levy, and claw-back rates each year so the City can issue final property tax bills. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends adoption of the rates for school purposes.

title:
New Island, New Beginnings: 
Furthering Reconciliation and an Indigenous Cultural Framework for the Port Lands

title: Supporting potential city-building opportunities on Toronto District School Board lands
topics: buildings, school boards, schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums

The Toronto District School Board stewards over 5,000 acres of land, and the amendment would let school boards request a ministerial exemption from the requirement to obtain fair market value for surplus lands. This could unlock city-building initiatives on surplus school board lands, such as the Davisville Community and Aquatic Centre model.

topics: food, nutrition, students; diet; dieting; healthy eating, menus

topics: churches, refugees;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize reimbursement of $1,440,401 to churches and community organizations that provided emergency shelter to refugee claimants. The organizations already received partial reimbursement, and this covers the remaining eligible expenses.

Staff recommend that City Council make personal alcohol consumption permanent in the 27 pilot parks, with health and safety restrictions, by amending the Parks chapter of the municipal code.
