title: Selection of Candidates for Interview for the Committee of Adjustment
topics: appointments, committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel - Committee of Adjustment selects candidates to interview for appointment by City Council to the Committee of Adjustment. The City Clerk recommends selecting 9 candidates from the confidential list; the panel will interview them and recommend three candidates to City Council. Confidential attachments stay sealed.

title: Notice of Member Absences on Committee of Adjustment, Scarborough District
topics: appointments, public appointments;
brief: This is an information item: the City Clerk advises the Nominating Panel - Committee of Adjustment that a Scarborough District member has been absent from three consecutive hearings without permission. The City Clerk recommends the panel review the attachment from the Director of Zoning and take appropriate action.

title: 2024 Board of Health Self-Evaluation
topics: boards of health;
brief: This is an information item: the Medical Officer of Health presents the results of the Board of Health's 2024 self-evaluation, required under the Ontario Public Health Standards. The Board of Health is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Implementation Panel for Our Health, Our City: A Mental Health, Substance Use, Harm Reduction and Treatment Strategy for Toronto
topics: boards of health;
brief: The Medical Officer of Health recommends that the Board of Health approve the terms of reference for the Our Health, Our City Implementation Panel and appoint a Board of Health director as its chair for the rest of the 2022-2026 term. The panel implements the November 2023 mental health, substance use, harm reduction, and treatment strategy, which takes a city-wide, population-level approach.

title: Toronto Public Health Update on Measles Prevention and Management
topics: boards of health;
brief: This is an information item: the Deputy Medical Officer of Health gives a presentation on Toronto Public Health's measles prevention and management update. No decision is attached.

title: 2023: A Year-in-Review of Toronto Public Health
topics: boards of health;
brief: This is an information item: the Medical Officer of Health presents a 2023 year-in-review of Toronto Public Health's main accomplishments, programs, innovative strategies, and key priorities for 2024 and beyond. The Board of Health is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Compliance Audit Application by Kevin Wiener for the Election Campaign Finances of Giorgio Mammoliti
topics: audits, compliance, elections; auditors; auditors, polls (elections); voting
brief: This is a procedural item: a compliance audit application was received on February 26, 2024 from Kevin Wiener concerning the election campaign finances of mayoral candidate Giorgio Mammoliti. The Compliance Audit Committee will consider the application.

title: Resignation from Property Standards Committee, Scarborough Panel
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Clerk's Office has received notice that Ryan Hardy resigned from the Property Standards Committee's Scarborough Panel effective March 14, 2024. The Public Appointments Secretariat plans to run a recruitment and selection process to fill the vacancy in the coming months.

title: 400 Sewells Road - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 24 103794 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, inspection, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws, site inspection; viewing
brief: This is a procedural item: the tribunal hears the appeal of a property standards order issued January 16, 2024 for 400 Sewells Road. The tribunal can confirm, change, or cancel the order, which is the owner's chance to challenge the city's repair or maintenance requirements.

title: 4 Wickson Trail - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 24 100781 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the tribunal hears the appeal of a property standards order issued January 4, 2024 for 4 Wickson Trail. The tribunal can confirm, change, or cancel the order, which is the owner's chance to challenge the city's repair or maintenance requirements.

title: 363-391 Yonge Street - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300) - Decision Report - Approval
topics: noise, zoning bylaws; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council classify the lands at 363-391 Yonge Street as a Class 4 Noise Area under the provincial noise guideline NPC-300. The designation allows higher daytime and night-time sound level limits for the residential development, with noise control measures built into the design to mitigate the impact.

title: 929 Queen Street East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; developing land; development (land); land development, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments for 929 Queen Street East to permit a 10-storey mixed-use building with 70 rental dwelling units and 213.5 square metres of retail and commercial space at grade. The proposal conforms to the Official Plan, including Site and Area Specific Policy 469.

title: Toronto Metropolitan University (TMU) Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: parking, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the zoning amendment bringing the entire Toronto Metropolitan University campus into the city-wide Zoning By-law 569-2013 and extending the campus-wide approach to parking requirements to include loading spaces and bicycle parking. No development is proposed; the change addresses the complex area-specific zoning rules that had excluded post-secondary institutions like TMU from the by-law.

title: 211-219 Gerrard Street East - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the zoning amendment for 211-219 Gerrard Street East to permit a seven-storey mixed-use building with 39 dwelling units and 250 square metres of non-residential gross floor area.

title: 2161 Yonge Street - Official Plan Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: minor variances, official plan amendments; variance
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the Official Plan amendment for 2161 Yonge Street to permit a reduction in the required office replacement in a 38-storey mixed-use building currently under construction. The application includes a minimum of 4,000 square metres of office uses and expanded permissions for home occupation.

title: 1365-1375 Yonge Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments for 1365-1375 Yonge Street to permit a 50-storey mixed-use building of 159.9 metres with 714 dwelling units and 450 square metres of ground-floor commercial space. The proposal includes landscaped open space at the south end and a pedestrian path along the laneway to the east.

title: Construction Staging Area Time Extension - 1 Bloor Street West (Balmuto Street)
topics: construction; building
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council, needed because the TTC operates on Yonge and Bloor and the recommendations do not comply with City policy, to authorize a temporary closure on Balmuto Street for construction at 1 Bloor Street West, the Mizrahi mixed-use development known as The One. The closure covers a five-metre-wide portion of the northbound curb lane and the east sidewalk on Balmuto Street south of Bloor Street West.

title: Royal Ontario Museum - Revolving Doors and a Protective Canopy
topics: energy, museums (facilities); energy resources; energy use
brief: The Royal Ontario Museum asks for permission to install energy-saving revolving doors and a protective canopy over its entrance at 100 Queen's Park Crescent to protect patrons and passersby from ice and snow falling from the Crystal. The current zoning by-law does not allow protrusions from the building envelope, so Council is asked to have the Chief Planner work with the ROM to permit the work.

title: 50-64 Merton Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: heritage properties, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments for 50-64 Merton Street to permit a 157-metre, 45-storey mixed-use building with 581 dwelling units and 1,700 square metres of office floor area. The approvals reduce the required office replacement and change the unit mix, and the proposal partially retains the facade of the two-storey designated heritage building.

title: Use of Nathan Phillips Square for Various Events - May 1, 2024 - August 31, 2024
topics: [events in culture];
brief: Staff ask City Council to grant exemptions from the public squares by-laws to permit events on Nathan Phillips Square from May 1 to August 31, 2024. The events are proposed by organizations including the Canadian Polish Congress, Rugby Ontario, and the Taste of the Middle East festival committee, among others.

title: Pay-and-Display Parking - Various Streets (Non-Delegated)
topics: parking authorities, parking spaces; parking authority, parking spots
brief: This is a routine delegated item: because the TTC operates on the subject streets, City Council approval is needed to authorize new on-street pay-and-display parking locations in Wards 4, 9, 12, and 19. The Toronto Parking Authority and Transportation Services identified the new paid spaces to encourage turnover and support local businesses.

title: 950 King Street West - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, transportation; building, transportation services
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council, needed because the TTC operates on King Street West, to authorize a 35-month construction staging closure on Strachan Avenue for the 14-storey residential building by Verdiroc Construction Corporation at 950 King Street West. From February 29, 2024 to January 31, 2027, the east sidewalk and both bicycle lanes on Strachan Avenue between King Street West and 38 metres north would close.

title: Inclusion of 10 Properties on the Heritage Register - 143, 155, 161,167 Main Street, 154 and 164 Main Street and 2201- 2207 Gerrard Street East
topics: heritage properties, urban design; civic improvements, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council add ten properties at the intersection of Main Street and Gerrard Street East to the City's Heritage Register. The properties, including 143, 155, 161, 167, 154, and 164 Main Street and 2201 to 2207 Gerrard Street East, are early-twentieth century Main Street commercial buildings anchoring the historic core of the former municipality of East Toronto.

title: 50 Merton Street - Alterations and Demolition of a Heritage Attribute to a Designated Heritage Property and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: easements, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage property at 50 Merton Street and authorize a Heritage Easement Agreement. The report also recommends approving the demolition of heritage attributes, namely the three-storey rear wing and the northern half of the front wing's east elevation, to allow a 45-storey mixed-use building under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act.

title: 2681 Danforth Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning Amendment Applications - Appeal
topics: Official Plans, zoning;
brief: This is an appeal item: the applicant's 2022 applications for a 44- and 33-storey tower development at 2681 Danforth Avenue were appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal. The proposal includes 905 residential units, 79,854 square metres of gross floor area, Canadian Tire retail space, a 958-square-metre park dedication, and a new north-south public street. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition and keep negotiating.

title: 1437-1455 Queen Street West - Zoning Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal item: the applicant appealed a zoning amendment for a 12-storey mixed-use building at 1437-1455 Queen Street West to the Ontario Land Tribunal after Council did not decide in time. The proposal has ground-floor retail, one level of underground parking, and 249 residential units. Staff recommend Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the appeal at the Tribunal while continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: 2079-2111 Yonge Street, 9-11, 21, and 31 Hillsdale Avenue East and 12-18 Manor Road East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the Official Plan and zoning amendment applications for 2079-2111 Yonge Street, 9-11, 21, and 31 Hillsdale Avenue East, and 12-18 Manor Road East in their current form. The proposal is a 29-storey mixed-use building with 486 residential units and 2,000 square metres of non-residential floor area, partially retaining a heritage building at 2111 Yonge Street. The site contains 31 rental dwelling units, with a related rental housing demolition application.

title: 3474 Yonge Street - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 23 238046 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the tribunal hears the appeal of a property standards order issued December 28, 2023 for 3474 Yonge Street. The tribunal can confirm, change, or cancel the order, which is the owner's chance to challenge the city's repair or maintenance requirements.

title: 3464 Yonge Street - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 23 238064 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the tribunal hears the appeal of a property standards order issued December 28, 2023 for 3464 Yonge Street. The tribunal can confirm, change, or cancel the order, which is the owner's chance to challenge the city's repair or maintenance requirements.

title: 7 Carscadden Drive - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 23 198565 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the tribunal hears the appeal of a property standards order issued September 6, 2023 for 7 Carscadden Drive. The tribunal can confirm, change, or cancel the order, which is the owner's chance to challenge the city's repair or maintenance requirements.

title: Council Member Appointments to the Canadian National Exhibition Association, Municipal Section and Board of Directors
topics: appointments, committees of council; council committees
brief: This is a procedural item: the Striking Committee considers members' preferences and recommends to City Council the appointment of five Council members to the Canadian National Exhibition Association's municipal section and board of directors, for a term from the spring 2024 annual meeting to the spring 2025 annual meeting.

title: Council Member Appointment to Fill a Vacancy on the Service Excellence Committee
topics: appointments, committees of council; council committees
brief: This is a procedural item: the Striking Committee considers members' preferences and recommends to City Council the appointment of one Council member to fill the Service Excellence Committee vacancy left by Councillor Jaye Robinson's resignation, for a term until December 31, 2024.

title: Council Member Appointments to the City of Toronto Long-Term Care Committee of Management
topics: appointments, committees of council; council committees
brief: This is a procedural item: the Striking Committee considers members' preferences and eligibility and recommends to City Council the appointment of a Council member to the City of Toronto Long-Term Care Committee of Management for a term until November 14, 2026.

title: 4151 to 4155 Sheppard Avenue East and 5 Lamont Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment applications for 4151 to 4155 Sheppard Avenue East and 5 Lamont Avenue in their current form. The proposal is a 46-storey, 152.9-metre mixed-use building with 726 dwelling units, 43,946 square metres of residential floor area, 520 square metres of non-residential floor area, a density of 11.72 times the lot area, and 232 underground parking spaces.

title: 4566 and 4568 Kingston Road - Zoning Amendment, Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the zoning amendment for 4566 and 4568 Kingston Road to permit a 12-storey mixed-use building with 131 residential units, 9,276.39 square metres of gross floor area, 105 vehicle parking spaces, and 116 bicycle parking spaces. The proposal supports the Official Plan direction for Avenues and mixed-use areas.

title: 3060 Eglinton Avenue East, Zoning Amendment Application,  Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the zoning amendment to permit an 80-unit townhouse development at 3060 Eglinton Avenue East, including 10 affordable housing units. The development is four-storey stacked townhouses in six blocks, with about 10,040 square metres of gross floor area, a density of 0.72 times the lot area, and 92 parking spaces including 12 for visitors.

title: Scarborough Civic Centre 2025 - Strategic Plan
topics: civic centres, community & life (sc); ccs
brief: Councillor Myers recommends that City Council direct the City Manager to assess the use of space at Scarborough Civic Centre and explore a strategic plan by 2025 for the centre, aligned with the City's Workplace Modernization Program. The plan would address local needs as the centre marks fifty years as Scarborough's civic hub.

title: Assumption of Services, St. Magnus Subdivision, Chiavatti Developments Limited, Plan 66M-2482, Subdivision File: 06 198723 ESC 44 SB
topics: assumption of services, municipal services; city services
brief: This is a routine delegated item: staff recommend that City Council formally assume the municipal services installed under the subdivision agreement for Plan 66M-2482, the St. Magnus subdivision by Chiavatti Developments Limited, including St. Magnus Drive, Lawson Road, and Brumwell Road.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2461,  Portia Street Subdivision, Scarborough (90 Morningside Avenue)
topics: assumption of services, municipal services; city services
brief: This is a routine delegated item: staff recommend that City Council formally assume the municipal services, including the road, installed under the subdivision agreement for Plan 66M-2461, the Portia Street subdivision at 90 Morningside Avenue, and release the developer's performance guarantee.

title: Right Turn Prohibition at Military Trail and Ellesmere Road
topics: traffic regulations, turn prohibitions (traffic);
brief: Councillor Ainslie recommends that City Council prohibit westbound right turns from 7:00 to 9:00 a.m., Monday to Friday, except public holidays, on Ellesmere Road at Military Trail and Orton Park Road, and amend the existing eastbound left-turn prohibition for the same hours. The changes align the turn rules with the other existing restrictions at the intersection.

title: Old Finch Avenue - Heavy Truck Prohibitions
topics: heavy truck prohibitions, traffic regulations;
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council, needed because the TTC operates on Old Finch Avenue, to prohibit heavy trucks at all times on Old Finch Avenue between Morningside Avenue and Morningview Trail. The ban reduces heavy truck activity in the Morningside Heights residential neighbourhood and on the Sewells Road bridge and underpass, and allows enforcement by the Toronto Police Service under the Highway Traffic Act.

title: Metrolinx Scarborough Subway Extension - Time Extension of Temporary Sidewalk Closure on McCowan Road
topics: public transit, sidewalks; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council, needed because the TTC operates on McCowan Road, to extend the temporary closure of the east sidewalk on McCowan Road between Sheppard Avenue East and Nugget Avenue from April 1, 2024 to December 31, 2025. The closure keeps pedestrians away from tunnel boring work by Metrolinx's contractor Strabag for the Scarborough Subway Extension.

title: 2157 to 2183 Lawrence Avenue East - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the zoning amendment for 2157 to 2183 Lawrence Avenue East to permit a 24-storey tower and a 21-storey tower on a shared 6-storey podium. The development includes 526 residential units, 35,555 square metres of gross floor area, ground-floor commercial uses, 264 vehicle parking spaces, and 395 bicycle parking spaces.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council reviews the Order Paper, which lists the items for the meeting's consideration. No decision is attached.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions, and announcements are made at the City Council meeting. No decision is attached.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council may file petitions. No decision is attached.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council declare any interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act. No decision is attached.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from the Mayor and City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: the Mayor and City officials introduce committee reports and new business, including reports from the Executive, Audit, Civic Appointments, and Economic and Community Development committees. No decision is attached.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council confirms the minutes from the regular meeting held February 6 and 7, 2024 and the special meeting held February 14, 2024. No other decision is attached.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Council meeting is called to order, including the singing of O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is attached.

title: 78, 80 and 86 Mimico Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the properties at 78, 80, and 86 Mimico Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for their cultural heritage value. Built between 1920 and 1929 on the north side of Mimico Avenue at Station Road, the three main-street commercial buildings have residential or office uses above and share a remarkable visual cohesion.

title: 80-86 Lynn Williams Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 80-86 Lynn Williams Street, the A. R. Williams Machinery Company Warehouse in Liberty Village, under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value, as set out in the report's Statement of Significance.

title: Update Downsview - Authorization to Enter into Agreements for Resourcing
topics: agreements, development, planning & development (sc); developing land; development (land); land development, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize the Deputy City Manager, Development and Growth Services, to enter into agreements with Canada Lands Company Ltd. and Northcrest Developments to secure resources for continued planning of the Downsview Secondary Plan area. A 2022 memorandum of understanding funded a dedicated City staff team that will bring deliverables to Council in May, and the work continues with master planning for 15 district plans and further environmental assessment phases.

title: New Multi-Tenant Houses Renovation Program to Preserve and Improve Affordable Rental Homes
topics: improvement, rental housing, rooming houses; boarding houses; lodging homes; lodging houses, enhancement; rehabilitation (property), rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize the Housing Secretariat, with Toronto Building, Fire Services, and Municipal Licensing and Standards, to establish a new Multi-Tenant Houses Renovation Program to preserve and improve affordable rental homes. Multi-tenant houses, or rooming houses, house students, seniors, newcomers, low-income residents, and people exiting homelessness, and the new regulatory framework takes effect March 31, 2024.

title: Eliminating Education Development Charges on Missing Middle Housing Forms
topics: fees, second suites, urban planning; accessory apartments; granny flats; in-law suites, administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees, city planning; community planning; regional planning
brief: Councillor Bradford recommends that City Council ask the Province of Ontario to amend the Education Act to exempt secondary dwelling units, such as laneway suites and garden suites, from education development charges. The Toronto Catholic District School Board reinstated these charges in November 2023, and households building missing-middle homes are now asked to pay about $3,600.

title: Technical Corrections to the Multi-tenant Housing Zoning By-law
topics: change, residential tenants, tenants; amendments; conversion; modification, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: Councillor Gord Perks recommends that the City Solicitor and Chief Planner report directly to the March 20-22, 2024 Council meeting on technical, non-substantive corrections and clarifications needed in the multi-tenant house Zoning By-law 156-2023, which takes effect March 31, 2024. Staff have identified items to fix since the framework was adopted in December 2022.

title: Supporting New Long-Term Care Beds in North York
topics: [locations in health], [objects in health], seniors; elderly; geriatric; older adults; senior citizens
brief: Councillor Carroll recommends that City Council ask the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing to enact an Enhanced Minister's Zoning Order for the lands at 4000 Leslie Street, next to North York General Hospital, to permit a mixed-use building as part of a long-term care development with 528 licensed long-term care beds. North York has the highest percentage of residents aged 65 and older in Toronto and growing seniors' health care needs.

title: Evaluation of Ontario Building Code Requirements for Multi-Tenant Houses
topics: building codes, evaluation, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, review; reviewing
brief: This is an information item: Toronto Building and Toronto Fire Services evaluated the Ontario Building Code requirements for multi-tenant houses, also known as rooming houses, ahead of the new zoning and licensing framework taking effect March 31, 2024. City Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: 290 Sheppard Avenue West - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: community councils, official plan amendments, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the zoning amendment for 290 Sheppard Avenue West to permit a six-storey hotel with 32 rooms and six surface parking spaces. The proposal conforms to the Official Plan and the Sheppard Lansing Secondary Plan.

title: 48, 50, 56, 58 and 60 Avondale Avenue and 17 and 19 Bales Avenue and 25, 35, 37, 39, 41, 43, 45, 51, 53, 55, 57, 61 and 63 Glendora Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: community councils, demolitions, rental housing, tenants; rental properties; rental units, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the rental housing demolition application for 48 to 60 Avondale Avenue, 17 and 19 Bales Avenue, and 25 to 63 Glendora Avenue, allowing demolition of 16 detached dwellings containing 20 rental units. The demolition would facilitate three new residential buildings of 45, 39, and 26 storeys with 1,040 dwelling units; the related Official Plan and zoning amendment was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 1053 Don Mills Road, 2, 4, 4R, and 6 The Donway East Zoning By-law Amendment, Plan of Subdivision, and Site Plan Applications - Appeal Report
topics: applications, buildings, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal item: the applicant appealed the zoning amendment, plan of subdivision, and site plan applications for 1053 Don Mills Road and 2, 4, 4R, and 6 The Donway East to the Ontario Land Tribunal. The proposal has four residential buildings of 32, 28, 24, and 16 storeys with 1,185 units, including 160 rental replacement units, plus a public park, a public road, and a privately-owned public space. Staff recommend Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the appeals while continuing discussions.

title: 1802 Bayview Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment and Site Plan Control Applications - Appeal Report
topics: applications, community councils, site plan control, zoning bylaws; application process, site plan approvals, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal item: the applicant appealed the zoning amendment and site plan applications for a 46-storey, 148.6-metre residential building with 419 units at 1802 Bayview Avenue to the Ontario Land Tribunal after Council did not decide in time. The proposal has 28,576 square metres of residential floor area, 384 square metres of ground-floor retail, and a density of 20.5 times the lot area. Staff recommend Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose the appeals while continuing discussions.

title: 405 and 415 Mount Pleasant Road and 323, 323R, 325, 327 and 329 Balliol Street - Zoning By-Law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, community councils, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the zoning amendment to permit an outdoor sports and recreation field at 405 and 415 Mount Pleasant Road and 323 to 329 Balliol Street for Greenwood College School at 443 Mount Pleasant Road. The proposal conforms to the Official Plan and the Yonge Eglinton Secondary Plan.

title: 3 Leila Lane, 5 Leila Lane, and 31-109 Bagot Court - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report
topics: applications, community councils, demolitions, rental housing; application process, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the rental housing demolition application to demolish 102 social housing units in two three-storey rental buildings at 3 and 5 Leila Lane and townhouses at 31-109 Bagot Court, as part of the Lawrence Heights revitalization by Toronto Community Housing. The demolition accommodates a new City community recreation centre; the City has applied for federal Green and Inclusive Community Building Fund support, which would require the centre to meet its criteria.

title: 72 Church Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, planning approvals, rezoning, zoning bylaws; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments for 72 Church Avenue to permit a four-storey rental residential building with 14 units at 13.9 metres high. The building has 1,508 square metres of gross floor area, a density of 2.4 times the lot area, and 8 vehicle and 17 bicycle parking spaces in a below-grade garage.

title: 1408-1420 Bayview Avenue - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: community councils, construction; building
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council, needed because Bayview Avenue is a major arterial, to extend the construction staging closure on Bayview Avenue for the eight-storey condominium with ground-floor retail being built at 1408-1420 Bayview Avenue. The closure covers the west sidewalk and southbound curb lane between Balliol Street and Merton Street, with a 1.5-metre-wide covered pedestrian walkway provided.

title: 26-34 Nipigon Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: applications, community councils, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the Official Plan and zoning amendment applications for 26-34 Nipigon Avenue in their current form. The proposal is a 50-storey, 165.3-metre mixed-use building with 569 residential units and 38,099.89 square metres of residential floor area, at a density of 17.0 times the lot area, which does not conform to the Official Plan or the Council-adopted Yonge Street North Secondary Plan.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Toronto District School Board for Improvements to the Schoolyard and Running Track at Jesse Ketchum Junior and Senior Public School - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: funding, schools, sports; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, financing
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside, asks City Council to release $300,000 in Section 37 funds to the Toronto District School Board and the ABC Residents Association to upgrade the outdoor running track and schoolyard at Jesse Ketchum Junior and Senior Public School, which is open to the community outside school hours. The funds come from developments at 1-11 Bloor Street West, 768-784 Yonge Street, and 760-762 Yonge Street.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Developments at 104-110 Bartley Drive and 1185 Eglinton Avenue East to Amend the 2024-2033 Capital Budget and Plan for Parks, Forestry and Recreation for Capital Projects in Ward 16 - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: funding, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, financing
brief: Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng, asks City Council to amend the Parks, Forestry and Recreation 2024-2033 capital budget to create sub-projects for Bartley Park Improvements at $925,000 and a second Ward 16 park project, advancing design and engagement in 2024 with construction in 2025. Both are fully funded by Section 37 community benefit funds from developments at 104-110 Bartley Drive and 1185 Eglinton Avenue East.

title: Exploring Innovative Adaptive Reuse of the Scarborough Rapid Transit Elevated Guideway and Assets - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: light rail transit, public transit, reuse; freecycle network; internet recycling, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, lrt
brief: Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, asks City Council to affirm Council's 2013 and 2022 decisions to explore adaptively reusing the decommissioned Scarborough Rapid Transit's 6.4-kilometre right-of-way and six station assets. The motion frames converting the elevated portions into a linear public park and active transportation corridor as a major city-building opportunity for Scarborough, whose residents have the longest TTC commute times.

title: Bloor Bedford Safe Rear Access - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: driveways, expropriations, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, compulsory purchase; eminent domain
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asks City Council to direct the General Manager of Transportation to report to Toronto and East York Community Council in the second quarter of 2024 with a plan and timetable for converting the City-owned driveway just west of Avenue Road and north of Bloor Street West, which runs south from Prince Arthur Avenue toward Bedford Road behind the Royal Sonesta Hotel site. Building owners hold non-exclusive easements on part of it.

title: Pursuing Parkland Acquisition in Leslieville - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: land acquisition, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, land acquisitions; park acquisition; parkland acquisition; parks acquisitions; property acquisition; property acquisitions
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, asks City Council to direct Corporate Real Estate Management, with Parks, Forestry and Recreation and the local councillor, to pursue expanding Maple Leaf Forever Park through City acquisition of properties. Leslieville has low parkland provision, and the Parkland Strategy identifies high need just west of the park between Queen Street East and Eastern Avenue.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item MM14.16 - Summit to Solve the Epidemic of Criminal Break-and-Enters Against Small Business in the City of Toronto - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: security, small businesses;
brief: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, asks City Council to amend the earlier decision on a summit to solve the epidemic of criminal break-and-enters against small businesses, directing Economic Development and Culture to include additional measures in its report. Small businesses face an unprecedented wave of break-ins while still recovering from COVID.

title: Support for the Canadian Independent Music Association - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: economy, funding, music; financing
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, asks City Council to support the Canadian Independent Music Association and the Canadian Live Music Association in their request that the federal government increase its annual contribution to the Canada Music Fund to $50 million by 2024-2025.

title: Establishing a community safety hub at Shoreham Court - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: community safety;
brief: Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, asks City Council to direct the Housing Secretariat to expedite releasing a unit at Shoreham Court for an IHELP Community Resource Centre, establishing a community safety hub. Shoreham Court is a Toronto Community Housing neighbourhood where residents, after a recent spring incident involving gun violence, have demanded action for a safer community.

title: Urgent Action on the Auto Theft Crisis - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: automobiles, theft; cars; used automobiles; used cars
brief: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, asks City Council to request that the Premier and the provincial Minister of Transportation impose lifetime driver's licence bans on anyone convicted of motor vehicle theft under the Criminal Code. The motion cites a 106 percent increase in carjackings so far in 2024, with 68 reported, and over 12,200 auto thefts in 2023.

title: Extending 2024 Application Due Dates for Property Tax and Utility Relief programs for Low-Income Seniors and Low-Income Disabled Persons - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: low income groups, persons with a disability, property taxes, tax reduction, utilities; disabled; disabled persons; handicapped persons; people with disabilities; persons with disabilities; persons with special needs; physical disabilities; physically challenged; physically disabled; physically impaired; special needs; the physically disabled, in need; low income; low income families; low income households; low income individuals; low income residents, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts, power utilties, tax assistance; tax decrease; tax rebate; tax refunds; tax relief
brief: Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, asks City Council to extend the 2024 application deadline for property tax, water, and solid waste relief programs for low-income seniors and low-income disabled persons from August 31 to October 31, 2024. Council has extended the deadline to the end of October in each year from 2020 to 2023.

title: Establishing a Stakeholder Advisory Committee to Optimize the use of Mel Lastman Square - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: community & life (sc), community partners, neighbourhoods (planning);
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, asks City Council to have Parks, Forestry and Recreation convene a stakeholder advisory committee to optimize the use of Mel Lastman Square. The committee would include North York Arts, local arts organizations, the local Business Improvement Area, and local businesses, engaging the community on planned events to better activate the square.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 15, 19 and 21 Holmes Avenue for Improvements to the Schoolyard at St. Cyril Catholic School - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: catholic schools, funding; financing
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, asks City Council to release $500,000 in Section 37 funds from the development at 15, 19, and 21 Holmes Avenue for improvements to the schoolyard at St. Cyril Catholic School. The City bought part of the schoolyard in 2005 and committed to a playing field, but the grass failed under heavy use and the school paved the yard; the funds would improve it for the 400-plus children who use it.

title: Amendment to Toronto Public Health’s 2024 Operating Budget - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik
topics: operating budgets, public health;
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, asks City Council to increase Toronto Public Health's 2024 operating budget by $900,000 gross, $0 net, conditional on receiving funding from another order of government, for programming outlined in a confidential attachment. Council authority is needed to reflect the external funding.

title: Purchase Order Amendment on Contract with Midome Construction Services Limited for the New Streetcar Tracks on Adelaide Street - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: construction, light rail transit; building, lrt
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, asks City Council to amend the purchase order and contract with Midome Construction Services Limited for installing new streetcar tracks and related infrastructure on Adelaide Street between York Street and Victoria Street. The work is part of the planned streetcar detour around the Ontario Line's Queen Street station construction.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 390 to 440 Dufferin St and 41 Alma Avenue to the Neighbourhood Land Trust to support the development of affordable rental housing at 128 Havelock Street - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: funding, rental housing; financing, rental properties; rental units
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, asks City Council to authorize $800,000 from the Capital Revolving Reserve Fund for Affordable Housing to the Neighbourhood Land Trust to redevelop 128 Havelock Street. The Land Trust acquired the derelict former rooming house in 2022 and proposes turning the five-room house into 10 new self-contained affordable rental units; the funds come from Section 37 funds from developments at 390 to 440 Dufferin Street and 41 Alma Avenue.

title: Re-opening and amending Item 2023.EX4.9 - Metrolinx Ontario Line - Temporary Lane Closures on the Don Valley Parkway and F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Temporary Delegation of Authority - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: highways, road closures; freeways; motorways; parkways, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe, asks City Council to revise the 2023 timelines for temporary lane closures on the Don Valley Parkway needed for the Ontario Line's Lower Don and Leaside bridges. Delays in contractor procurement prevented Metrolinx from starting work on schedule, so the by-law sections on the closures are amended.

title: Advancing Justice Centres in Toronto - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: courts, social services;
brief: Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng, asks City Council to authorize the Executive Director of Social Development, Finance and Administration to extend agreements with the Ministry of the Attorney General and receive $412,000 to support Toronto's Justice Centres. The centres are community courts that co-locate justice, health, and social services to provide wrap-around support for vulnerable accused people and reduce recidivism.

title: Night Economy Manifesto - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: economy, safety; public safety
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to express its support for the Nighttime Manifesto and have the Mayor sign it on behalf of the City. As Night Economy Champion, he is working with Economic Development and Culture to modernize rules for nighttime businesses with appropriate oversight for nuisance and public safety.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Amend the 2024-2033 Capital Budget and Plan for Parks, Forestry and Recreation to Advance the Davisville Community Aquatic Centre Project in Ward 12 - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: [activities in planning and development], community centres; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, asks City Council to add $9,835,000 to the Parks, Forestry and Recreation 2024-2033 capital budget for the Davisville Community Aquatic Centre, raising the total project cost from $58,520,000 to $68,355,000 to advance the construction contract award. The three-storey accessible facility will sit on the Spectrum Alternative School site near Yonge and Davisville, connected to an underground parking lot.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 871 to 899 College Street for Lakeview Avenue Parkette Improvements - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: capital budgets, parks, planning & development (sc); conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, asks City Council to release $200,000 in Section 37 funds from the development at 871 to 899 College Street to the Little Portugal Toronto Business Improvement Area for the Lakeview Avenue Parkette redesign, with $60,000 in 2024 and $140,000 in 2025. The BIA needs the funds released urgently so the project can proceed before costs rise.

title: 60 Sudbury Street - Liquor Licence Application - Lyla - Licence 2504417 - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, asks City Council to advise the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that the liquor licence application for Lyla at 60 Sudbury Street is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing community concerns are attached. The premises are near residential units.

topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, asks City Council to advise the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that the liquor licence application for Sansa Bakery and Grill at 350-352 Oakwood Avenue is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing community concerns are attached. The premises are near residential units.

title: 118 Havelock Street - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: appeals, committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, asks City Council to authorize the City Solicitor to appeal and attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of variances at 118 Havelock Street. The applicant sought variances for a one-storey side addition and four-storey side and rear additions to convert the house into a residential care home providing supportive housing.

title: 1174 St. Clair Avenue West - Liquor Licence Application - Ja Tequila Imperial Inc. - Licence 2365491 - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, asks City Council to advise the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that the liquor licence application for Ja Tequila Imperial Inc. at 1174 St. Clair Avenue West is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing community concerns are attached. The premises are near residential uses.

title: 103 Roncesvalles Avenue - Liquor Licence Application - Bossanova Wine and Beer - Licence 2464251 - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: applications, liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, application process
brief: Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, asks City Council to advise the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that the liquor licence application for Bossanova Wine and Beer at 103 Roncesvalles Avenue is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing community concerns are attached to the licence. The premises are near sensitive uses.

title: Authorization to Install a Curb Lane CaféTO Patio - 17 St. Nicholas Street, Bar Volo - Waiving requirement to operate in a public laneway - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: street occupation permits; curblane permits; road use permits; street closure permits; streets and sidewalks
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, asks City Council to exempt Bar Volo, the family-owned Italian restaurant at 17 St. Nicholas Street, from the requirement that curb lane cafes not operate in a public laneway. Bar Volo fronts directly onto a laneway with no sidewalks and held successful CafeTO permits in 2021, 2022, and 2023.

title: Request for Updates on Northern Segment of the Ontario Line - by Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: construction, public transit; building, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside, asks City Council to direct the Chief Planner, with the Executive Director of Transit Expansion, to report to North York Community Council with regular updates on the northern segment of the Ontario Line. The 15.6-kilometre provincial subway project spans 15 stations from Exhibition Place to the Ontario Science Centre, with work beginning on the elevated guideway and Thorncliffe Park, Flemingdon Park, and Ontario Science Centre stations.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Ward 13 2023 Participatory Budgeting Projects for the Bay Cloverhill, Bloor East, Church Wellesley and Upper Jarvis Neighbourhoods - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, asks City Council to amend Transportation Services' 2024-2033 capital budget to create a sub-project for Ward 13 participatory budgeting projects in the Bay Cloverhill, Bloor East, Church Wellesley, and Upper Jarvis neighbourhoods. In 2023, residents crowdsourced and voted on ideas for spending community benefit funds; this item includes $150,000 gross, $0 debt, fully funded by Section 37 funds.

title: Request the Province of Ontario Undertake a Comprehensive Review of the Cannabis Control Act, 2017 - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: legislation, licences; acts, licenses; licensing
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to request that the Province of Ontario undertake a comprehensive review of the Cannabis Control Act, 2017, in consultation with municipalities. The motion cites challenges with unlicensed cannabis establishments and the need to clarify roles, responsibilities, funding, and enforcement.

title: Analysis of Costs: Removal of Elevated Portions of the Scarborough Rapid Transit Structure, and Detailed Feasibility for Reuse - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: costs, public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, asks City Council to have the City Manager, with the CFO, TTC, and Parks, Forestry and Recreation, analyze the costs and financial implications of any detailed feasibility work on the adaptive reuse or removal of the elevated Scarborough Rapid Transit structure and assets. The analysis would cover viability, costs, and impacts as part of capital prioritization, noting the 2024 budget's Scarborough Busway allocation.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Revitalize Trans Flag-Coloured Pedestrian Crossings in the Village - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: funding, lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgendered; financing, gay community; glbt; homosexual; lgbt; queer; transexual; transgendered; two spirited
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, asks City Council to release $40,000 in Section 37 community benefit funds from the development at 355 Church Street to revitalize the trans flag-coloured pedestrian crosswalks at Hayden Street and Church Street and Wood Street and Church Street. The crossings were painted in 2019 for the Trans Day of Visibility anniversary and the decriminalization anniversary.

title: Right-sizing Regent Park - Providing Adequate Affordable Housing to Under-housed Families - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: housing, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, homes; residences
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, asks City Council to have Toronto Community Housing's board direct its CEO, with the Housing Secretariat, to review housing needs for under-housed families in Regent Park. Household composition has changed since the 2007 revitalization, and residents face conditions that don't fit their family sizes, with an internal transfer waitlist discontinued unresolved.

title: Mandating Human Rights, Equity, and Diversity Training for City of Toronto Arena Boards - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: arenas, human rights; indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, asks City Council to require all members of the City's eight arena boards to complete human rights, equity, and diversity training each Council term. The training covers Indigenous learning, human rights responsibilities, and combating anti-Black racism, plus an orientation on City policies.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds to Amend the 2024-2033 Capital Budget and Plan for Parks, Forestry and Recreation to Advance Hanlan’s Beach Priority Initiatives in Ward 10 - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: funding, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, financing
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, asks City Council to amend the Parks, Forestry and Recreation 2024-2033 capital budget and plan to create new sub-projects for Hanlan's Beach priority initiatives, including bike parking and other service improvements. The Toronto Islands Master Plan process has run since 2022, with advocacy from groups like Friends of Hanlan's on enhancing and protecting the beach important to queer communities.

title: Authority to Accept an In-Kind Donation and Enter into an Agreement with Pride Toronto for Hanlan's Point Rainbow Road - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: budgets, operating budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, asks City Council to authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to accept an in-kind donation of up to $200,000 from Pride Toronto for upgrades to Beach Road near Hanlan's Point Beach on the Toronto Islands. The donation supports work to safeguard and celebrate the historically significant queer community hub at Hanlan's Point.

title: Strengthening Compliance and Closing Loopholes in Parking Permit and Enforcement Systems - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: parking, parking enforcement;
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside, asks City Council to direct the General Manager of Transportation Services to report back by the end of the third quarter of 2024 with amendments to the accessible parking by-law to close loopholes. The motion cites complaints about a large recreational vehicle persistently blocking streets under the protection of an accessible parking permit.

title: Continuing City Support for Hugh’s Room - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: arts and culture, music;
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, asks City Council to have Economic Development and Culture review all supports offered to live music venues and help Hugh's Room at 296 Broadview Avenue access them. Hugh's Room was driven out of its west-end location by rent increases and is moving into 296 Broadview, and Council has previously acted to preserve the venue.

title: Trans-Inclusive Benefits: Expanding Health Benefits for Toronto Employees to Include Gender-Affirming Care - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: health, transgender, treatment (health); health coverage, health treatments; therapeutics; therapy
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, asks City Council to direct the Executive Director of Pension, Payroll and Employee Benefits to review options for adding gender-affirming health care benefits not covered by OHIP to City employee benefit plans and report back to the General Government Committee. The motion notes the federal government approved such benefits for its employees last year.

title: Supporting the Government of Canada's Proposed Online Harms Act - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: federal governments;
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to express its support in principle for the federal government's Bill C-63, the Online Harms Act, introduced February 26, 2024 to promote online safety and reduce harms from harmful content. The motion also asks the City Manager to review the bill and report back to the Executive Committee on opportunities.

title: Support Bill 152, Chad’s Law (Enforcing Safer Passing) 2023 - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: highways, provincial legislation, traffic; freeways; motorways; parkways, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to support Bill 152, Chad's Law (Enforcing Safer Passing) 2023, a provincial bill by MPP Guy Bourgouin aimed at discouraging risky passing on highways, especially where double solid yellow lines are marked. The bill passed first reading on November 21 and was ordered for second reading; the motion would forward Council's support to the Premier, MPP Bourgouin, Toronto MPPs, and the Good Roads Association.

title: Authority to Donate Surplus Vehicles - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: emergency vehicles, police services; police; policing
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to authorize donating up to five more surplus vehicles at no cost to the Ukrainian government for humanitarian purposes, following seven vehicles donated in 2022 and 2023. The request follows a meeting with Ukraine's Consul General about the humanitarian crisis in Kyiv, Toronto's friendship city since 1991.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 and Section 42 Funds to Amend the 2024-2033 Capital Budget and Plan for Parks, Forestry and Recreation to Advance Capital Projects in Ward 18 - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: funding, projects; financing
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside, asks City Council to amend the Parks, Forestry and Recreation 2024-2033 capital budget to create sub-projects for two Ward 18 projects: the Glendora Park off-leash area design at $100,000 and a park study, with $50,000 in 2024 and $50,000 in 2025, fully funded by Section 42 funds.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 and Section 42 Funds to Amend the 2024-2033 Capital Budget and Plan for Parks, Forestry and Recreation to Advance Capital Projects in Ward 11 - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
topics: funding, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, financing
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, asks City Council to amend the Parks, Forestry and Recreation 2024-2033 capital budget to advance two Ward 11 park projects with Section 37 and Section 42 funds. The Huron Washington Parkette improvements would rise from $556,273 to $956,273, an additional $400,000, to advance construction of the community's preferred design.

title: An Equitable Distribution of Canada Day Celebrations Throughout the City - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: equity, public holidays; bank holidays; holidays; holidays (public), employment equity; fair wage; pay equity
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, asks City Council to direct Economic Development and Culture and Parks, Forestry and Recreation to review all City-run and funded Canada Day events for equitable distribution across the City. Willowdale residents used to gather for fireworks at the North York Civic Centre, but City fireworks there stopped after COVID; Willowdale has 83,000 visible minority residents and 74,000 residents whose mother tongue is neither English nor French.

title: Clarification on Municipal Licensing and Standards Poster Enforcement Policies and By-laws - Rules Governing Affixing and Removing of Posters - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: licences; licenses; licensing
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, asks City Council to direct the City Manager and the Executive Director of Municipal Licensing and Standards to review and clarify the rules for affixing and removing community posters on utility poles, kiosks, and other structures, and report back to the Economic and Community Development Committee. The motion says the current by-law leaves unclear whether compliant posters can still be removed.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2023.IE7.4 on Updates on Vision Zero Road Safety Initiatives to Allow Optional Polling for Traffic - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: local roads, service delivery, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to reopen and amend the 2023 Vision Zero item to allow optional polling for traffic calming. The 2023 policy changes lowered the warranted speed threshold and used posted speeds, which qualifies more streets for speed humps; the motion would let the optional polling approach apply.

title: Authorization to Amend Section 37 Agreement on Timing of Obligations in Response to Committee of Adjustment Application Regarding 3450 Dufferin Street - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: committees of adjustment, funding; committee of adjustment, financing
brief: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, asks that if the Committee of Adjustment decision on 3450 Dufferin Street is not appealed or is upheld, City Council require the owner to enter into an amending Section 37 agreement on the timing of obligations. The site was approved by the Tribunal in 2019 for three tall buildings with a child care facility, and the Committee of Adjustment is considering changes affecting the agreement's timing.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Ward 13 2023 Participatory Budgeting Projects for the Canary District, Corktown and Distillery District Neighbourhoods - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: funding, projects; financing
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, asks City Council to amend Transportation Services' 2024-2033 capital budget for Ward 13 participatory budgeting projects in the Canary District, Corktown, and Distillery District neighbourhoods. In 2023, residents crowdsourced and voted on how to spend community benefit funds; this item is $80,000 gross, fully funded by Section 37 funds.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Ward 13 2023 Participatory Budgeting Projects for the St. Lawrence Neighbourhood - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: funding, projects; financing
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, asks City Council to amend Transportation Services' 2024-2033 capital budget for Ward 13 participatory budgeting projects in the St. Lawrence neighbourhood. In 2023, residents crowdsourced and voted on how to spend community benefit funds; this item is $2,400 gross, fully funded by Section 37 funds.

title: Upgrades to Paul Martel Park - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: funding, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, financing
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers, asks City Council to direct the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to report to Toronto and East York Community Council in the second quarter of 2024 on the feasibility, timing, and potential funding for upgrades to Paul Martel Park behind the Spadina subway station, including renaming and continuing Indigenous uses of the park. The park was designed by architect Paul Martel and renamed in his honour in 2014.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Developments at 666 Spadina Avenue and 192A, 194, and 200 Bloor Street West for Production and Installation of Two Heritage Plaques in Ward 11 - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow

title: Local Improvement Charges and Ridgewood Road Sanitary Sewer Installation

title: Requiring Fair Payment from For-Profit Gas Utilities for Use of City Property
topics: financial reports, natural gas, utilities; annual financial reports; financial statements, power utilties
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe recommends that City Council ask the Province of Ontario to amend its regulations so municipalities can charge fair fees to for-profit gas utilities for their use of public property. The motion argues that current rules give gas utilities free use of City property without compensation, even for damage from utility cuts, and that the City needs new revenue tools as provincial responsibilities have been downloaded.

title: Rouge Park Bridges Transportation Master Plan Environmental Assessment

title: Authority to Accept Metrolinx Funding for Road Rehabilitation on Eglinton Avenue

Construction of the Eglinton Crosstown LRT has degraded pavement along Eglinton; while Metrolinx's contractor restores sections at tunnelled and at-grade stations, the City is responsible for sections between stations that deteriorated from heavy construction traffic and maintenance delays.

Allen Road, as part of the citywide approach to dogs off-leash areas. Residents and trail users have said the area needs a fenced place for dogs.

Tinsley among the broader list of names, as part of the Dundas renaming work.

title: No More Subsidies for New Gas Pipelines that Drive Up Torontonians’ Energy Costs
topics: energy costs, fuels;
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, asks City Council to support the Ontario Energy Board's decision to stop forcing existing customers to subsidize new methane gas pipelines effective 2025, and to ask the Ontario government to let the decision stand. The motion argues fossil fuel subsidies are bad for consumers, air pollution, climate pollution, and human health, and would be forwarded to the Premier and provincial ministers.

title: Tax Fairness for All: An Equitable Approach to the Residential Property Tax Rate on Toronto Island
topics: property tax rates, residential properties; residential real estate
brief: Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, asks City Council to direct the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer to report back by the end of the second quarter of 2024 on the feasibility of area rating the residential property tax rate for Toronto Island properties. The motion notes Island homeowners own their houses but lease the land from the City, and pay some of the lowest residential property tax bills in the City while receiving full municipal services and the year-round ferry.

title: Implementation of a Commercial Parking Levy
topics: development, parking; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Following Council's 2023 direction to develop a levy on commercial parking, the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer asks City Council to endorse the guiding design principles for a commercial parking levy for consultation, ahead of implementation in 2025. The report covers a recommended tax, collection and enforcement design, estimated revenues, and timelines.

title: Vehicle-for-Hire and Private Transportation Industries Update Request
topics: drivers, transportation; transportation services
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow recommends that the City Manager include analysis and consideration of driver wages in the forthcoming report on options for vehicle-for-hire licensing, and report to the Executive Committee by the fourth quarter of 2024. The motion follows a December 2023 Council request for a report on the local impact of the vehicle-for-hire and private transportation industries.

title: Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee - Request for Accessibility Considerations in Our Plan Toronto: Chapter One Review
topics: feedback, implementation;
brief: The Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee asks the Planning and Housing Committee to have the Chief Planner, in consultation with the Housing Secretariat, study how to build more accessible housing as part of the Chapter One Official Plan review and implementation work. The goal is stronger accessibility considerations in the City's housing policies.

title: Improvements to the Sign By-law Amendment and Sign Variance Process
topics: change, improvement; amendments; conversion; modification, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: This report responds to a 2023 committee direction to review the Sign By-law amendment and variance process. The Chief Building Official recommends that City Council amend the Signs chapter of the Municipal Code to streamline and clarify how sign by-law amendments and variances are processed, and delegate authority to the Chief Building Official so amendment applications are not used as a substitute for the variance process.

title: 1111 Danforth Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 1111 Danforth Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The property contains a two-storey buff brick building on a basement, built in 1931 in the Neo-Gothic style, on the south side of Danforth Avenue between Byron and Greenwood Avenues.

title: Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods - Garden Suites Monitoring Program - Update
topics: housing, residential properties, rezoning; homes; residences, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: This is an information item: staff update the Planning and Housing Committee on the Garden Suites monitoring program. City Council approved garden suites across most residential zones in 2022 through Official Plan Amendment 554 and Zoning By-law Amendment 101-2022; appeals to the Ontario Land Tribunal were dismissed. The committee is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Housing Action Plan: Avenues Policy Review - Proposals Report
topics: housing, official plan amendments, public consultation; community consultation; consultation; public hearing, homes; residences
brief: Under the Housing Action Plan, staff propose reviewing the Official Plan's Avenues policies to enable more housing along Toronto's major transportation thoroughfares. The Interim Chief Planner recommends that the Planning and Housing Committee direct broad public and stakeholder consultation on the proposed policy directions, with recommended Official Plan changes to come back later.

title: Renovictions By-Law
topics: affordable housing, building permits, eviction; affordable homes; housing projects, building records; commercial xpress service; residential fastrack service
brief: Councillors Paula Fletcher, Mike Colle, Frances Nunziata, and Parthi Kandavel recommend that the Planning and Housing Committee direct the deputy city managers to include analysis of Hamilton's Renovation Licence By-law in their upcoming report on renovictions. The renovictions subcommittee heard from tenants and advocates about landlords using N-13 notices to push tenants out for renovations.

topics: Master Plans, baseball, recreational facilities; recreation facilities; recreational amenities
brief: Following Council's 2021 approval of the updated Centennial Park Master Plan, Councillor Stephen Holyday recommends that the Infrastructure and Environment Committee ask the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation, in consultation with the community, to consider amenities for the new baseball hub as part of its phased implementation. Space opened up when the privately operated Mini Indy amusement complex closed in late 2023, with pickleball and play areas also planned.

title: Morgan Avenue and Penhurst Avenue - Parking Amendments
topics: loading zones, parking, parking regulations; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Transportation Services asks Etobicoke York Community Council to swap parking designations near a school: the existing 10-minute maximum parking on the east side of Morgan Avenue would become a school bus loading zone, and the existing school bus loading zone on the west side of Penhurst Avenue would become 10-minute parking. The change moves the loading zone closer to the school's main doors.

title: Longbourne Drive - Introduction of Overnight On-Street Permit Parking Area 11
topics: on-street parking, parking; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking
brief: Transportation Services asks City Council, needed because the TTC operates on Longbourne Drive, to introduce overnight on-street permit parking on Longbourne Drive between Willowridge Road and Redgrave Drive from 12:01 a.m. to 7:00 a.m. daily, in a newly created Permit Parking Area 11. Residents requested the change to accommodate long-term parking needs.
