topics: speed humps, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: Transportation Services asks Etobicoke York Community Council to authorize the installation of speed bumps in the public lane south of Eglinton Avenue West, west of Scott Road, at the locations shown in the report's attachment.

title: Kingsway Crescent between Bannon Avenue and Government Road - Speed Humps
topics: speed humps, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: This is a follow-up to the January 19, 2024 decision authorizing traffic calming on Kingsway Crescent. Staff ask Etobicoke York Community Council to direct the City Solicitor to prepare a by-law to alter the roadway for the installation of one speed hump on Kingsway Crescent between Bannon Avenue and Government Road.

title: 47 Westpoint Lane - Application to Remove a Private Tree
topics: tree maintenance, tree removal;
brief: This is a procedural item: the owner of 47 Westpoint Lane appeals the denial of a permit to remove one private littleleaf linden tree, 39 cm in diameter, requested over concerns that roots could damage the foundation, plumbing, and pavers. The tree is healthy and maintainable, so the by-law does not support removal. Staff recommend Etobicoke York Community Council deny the permit.

title: 31 Central Street - Application to Remove a Private Tree
topics: privately-owned trees, tree removal; private owned trees; private trees; privately owned trees; trees on private property
brief: This is a procedural item: the owner of 31 Central Street appeals the denial of a permit to remove one private black walnut tree, 56 cm in diameter, requested to mitigate a severe walnut allergy. The tree is healthy and maintainable, so the by-law does not support removal. Staff recommend Etobicoke York Community Council deny the permit.

topics: [rules in transportation], speed limits, traffic regulations, transportation (sc);

The signage would be placed under the attached conditions, as the by-law does not allow variances for charitable and community event signage.

brief: This is a routine delegated item: Etobicoke York Community Council is asked to make changes to the Weston Village Business Improvement Area Board of Management, appointing a nominated director as required by the BIAs chapter of the Municipal Code.

brief: Transportation Services asks Etobicoke York Community Council to rescind the eastbound stop control on Tarragona Boulevard at Gunns Road and install a stop control for northbound traffic on Gunns Road instead. The change would more clearly define right-of-way and improve traffic management at the intersection.

title: Jane Finch Secondary Plan and Urban Design Guidelines - Final Report
topics: official plan amendments, transportation infrastructure; transportation network; transportation networks
brief: Staff recommend that City Council adopt the Jane Finch Secondary Plan and associated Urban Design Guidelines as an Official Plan Amendment, creating a comprehensive planning framework for the area around Jane Street and Finch Avenue West. The plan leverages the Finch West LRT investment by directing development to appropriate locations, supporting walking, cycling, and transit use, and identifying public realm improvements and community facilities.

topics: applications, official plan amendments, zoning, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse the Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment applications for 1800 Sheppard Avenue East. If the applications are appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, Council is asked to direct the City Solicitor.

body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking regulations, service delivery, signs; parking by-laws; parking bylaws, signage
brief: This motion responds to a produce business on Alma Avenue west of Dufferin seeking better delivery truck access on the narrow street. It asks Toronto and East York Community Council to prohibit parking at all times on both sides of Alma Avenue between Dufferin Street and a point 43.5 metres west, formalizing a prohibition that existed before construction.

body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: affordable housing, commercial areas; affordable homes; housing projects, commercial districts; retail areas
brief: This motion asks Toronto and East York Community Council to direct Transportation Services to report back by June 11, 2024 on a plan for the stop-up and closure of part of Sumach Street, the dead-end section north of Eastern Avenue, to accommodate the Block Developments proposal at 1, 2-16 Sumach Street. Allowing the developer to build on or cantilever over the street would make the site feasible for new affordable housing and potential retail in Corktown.

body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations, standing prohibitions; no parking, no standing, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: This motion responds to resident safety concerns on Sterling Road, where construction trucks standing in a no-parking zone on the west side create a bottleneck for delivery trucks and near-misses with pedestrians. It asks Toronto and East York Community Council to instead prohibit standing at all times on the west side of Sterling Road between Dundas Street West and Perth Avenue.

topics: parking regulations, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits, parking by-laws; parking bylaws

It asks Toronto and East York Community Council to rescind the existing parking prohibition and instead prohibit stopping at all times on the east side of Abell Street between Queen Street West and Sudbury Street, reducing confusion for vehicles loading and unloading at nearby buildings.

topics: Toronto Transit Commission, subway stations, transportation; transportation services, ttc
brief: This motion asks Toronto and East York Community Council to direct Transportation Services to make Shaftesbury Avenue one-way westbound between Yonge Street and Tacoma Avenue until December 31, 2025 or completion of the TTC's elevator project at Summerhill Station. TTC construction has blocked a westbound lane, leaving Summerhill residents with no way to exit their neighbourhood except via Yonge Street, which is hard to cross without a traffic light.

The motion asks Transportation Services, with the Toronto Police Service as needed, to report back in the second quarter of 2024 on traffic, cyclist, and pedestrian safety at the intersection with recommendations to make it safer.

brief: This is a procedural item: the City Council meeting is called to order, including the singing of O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is attached.

title: 2024 Operating and Capital Budgets
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: Under the City of Toronto Act, the Mayor presents the proposed City budget to City Council for consideration. Mayor Olivia Chow's 2024 operating budget protects services, invests in housing, transit, community safety, and basic repairs like roads and parks, while responsibly addressing a $1.8 billion opening pressure. The budget includes, for example, a Children's Services operating budget of $1,103.5 million gross and $93.6 million net. City Council will debate and vote on the budget.

title: Response to Ontario Regulation 286/09 Budget Matters - Expenses
topics: budgets, financial reports, regulations; annual financial reports; financial statements, budgets and accounts
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer report on how Ontario Regulation 286/09 on budget matters applies to the City's annual balanced budget. Because the City uses cash-basis accounting, the regulation lets it exclude amortization, post-employment benefits, and solid waste landfill closure and post-closure expenses from the budget. City Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Budget Implementation Including Property Tax Rates, User Fees and Related Matters
topics: budgets, property tax rates; budgets and accounts
brief: This report brings forward the approvals needed to put the 2024 budget into effect. It asks City Council to enact the by-law setting 2024 property tax rates and tax ratios, approve annual property tax policy decisions, and approve adjustments to user fees through the annual budget process.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council introduces general bills and confirming bills, the by-laws that give legal effect to decisions made at the meeting. No separate decision is attached.

brief: The Board of Health's Strategic Plan Development Committee recommends that the Board of Health ask the Medical Officer of Health to develop a new strategic plan for Toronto Public Health. brief: The Chief Executive Officer recommends the Board of Management of the Toronto Zoo approve establishing a Strategic Planning Committee and appoint three board members to guide development of the 2024-2027 Strategic Plan. The confidential attachments stay sealed because they contain personal applicant information.

topics: appointments, corporations;
brief: This is an information item: the Manager of the Public Appointments Secretariat presents the Nominating Panel - Corporations' 2024 work plan. The panel is asked to receive the presentation for information. No decision is required.

title: Increasing Equity and Access: Social Policy Strategies and Initiatives at The City of Toronto
brief: This presentation highlights the City of Toronto's social policy strategies and initiatives aimed at advancing equity and access, with a focus on current work impacting Black communities in Toronto. It complements the City's anti-Black racism work. No decision is attached.

title: Confronting the Legacy of the Transatlantic Slave Trade: Renaming Civic Assets Bearing the Henry Dundas Name - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: This is a member motion from Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, relating to City Council's December 2023 adoption of the Dundas renaming item. It asks that the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee include candidates such as Dudley Laws, a Canadian civil rights icon, among those considered for honouring in the Dundas renaming process and in the next Confronting Anti-Black Racism Action Plan.

title: Our Plan Toronto: Chapter One Review
brief: This is an information item: the Manager of the Official Plan and Legislation Team will present an overview of the draft Our Plan Toronto: Chapter One Review, including Indigenous planning perspectives, the 2051 vision statement, priorities, principles and next steps. No decision is attached.

title: Economic Development and Culture’s 2024 Strategic Planning: An Overview of Three Key Strategic Plans
brief: Economic Development and Culture staff present an overview of three strategic plans being developed for fall 2024: the divisional strategy for 2024 to 2028, an action plan for Toronto's culture sector, and an action plan for Toronto's economy. The overview covers each plan's public engagement process, and the committee can give early feedback.

title: An Overview and Discussion of the 2024-2026 Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee Workplan
brief: This is an information item: staff from the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Unit will present an overview of the process for developing the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee's 2024-2026 workplan. The presentation covers the issues and desired impacts the committee will consider during its term and considerations for future meeting agendas. No decision is attached.
