brief: The Chief Procurement Officer recommends the Bid Award Panel authorize awarding RFP Doc4038115970 to West 8 Urban Design & Landscape Architecture B.V. for design and construction contract administration of a new park at 229 Richmond Street West for Parks, Forestry and Recreation. The solicitation, issued June 20, 2023 and closed September 29, 2023, drew five bids after five addenda.

title: 69 Yonge Street and 3 King Street East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve Official Plan and zoning amendments for 69 Yonge Street and 3 King Street East to conserve the 15-storey designated heritage building and convert its offices to residential on levels 2 to 15. The proposal adds six storeys on top, infills the southeast corner, and includes 127 homes plus 1,361 square metres of ground-floor retail and restaurant space.

title: 83-89 Queen Street East and 119-127 Church Street - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, multi-residential properties, rental housing, zoning; rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment and rental housing demolition for 83-89 Queen Street East and 119-127 Church Street to allow a 59-storey, 194-metre mixed-use building with 690 homes, including 17 replacement rental units. The existing 2- to 4-storey buildings with 17 rental units would be demolished under a tenant relocation and assistance plan.

title: 147-153 Vaughan Road - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: building permits, demolitions, rental housing; building records; commercial xpress service; residential fastrack service, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the rental housing demolition application for 147-153 Vaughan Road, allowing demolition of 20 rental units to be replaced with 20 new rental units of the same types, sizes and similar rents, plus a tenant relocation and assistance plan, within a new 12-storey, 80-unit building. The Committee of Adjustment approved the related minor variance in December 2023.

title: Parking Amendment - Russell Yard and Queen Street East
topics: parking;
brief: Councillor Fletcher recommends City Council approve parking amendments on Queen Street East related to the removal of the TTC stop at Connaught Avenue. The changes would prohibit stopping at all times on the south side of Queen Street East near Connaught Avenue to improve sight lines for streetcar operators using the TTC Russell Yard driveway and provide safe parking near the tracks.

title: Recipient of the 2024 Agnes Macphail Award
topics: awards;
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher recommends City Council approve Susan Scandiffio as the 2024 Agnes Macphail Award recipient and thank the selection committee for its ongoing work. The award, established by the former Borough of East York, annually recognizes an outstanding volunteer within the former borough's boundaries; the committee unanimously selected Scandiffio on January 18, 2024. This is the same award approval also moved by Councillor Robinson as item NY10.29.

title: Traffic By-Law changes in Forest Hill Village
topics: traffic regulations;
brief: Councillor support is requested for traffic by-law changes in Forest Hill Village to give effect to the BIA's 2020 streetscape redesign, which has largely completed physical changes such as curb bump-outs and expanded sidewalks for pedestrian safety. The recommendations include rescinding a standing prohibition on the north side of Lonsdale Road between Spadina Road and 15 metres west and amending a parking prohibition on the same side. Council is asked to endorse the listed by-law changes.

title: 111 and 141 Davisville Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 111 and 141 Davisville Avenue to permit a 33-storey, 109.1-metre residential building with 24,369 square metres of residential floor area. The existing 20-storey building with 313 units at 141 Davisville Avenue would be maintained, and the proposal adds a 3-metre mid-block connection and landscaped open space.

title: 33 Davisville Avenue and 60 Balliol Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve Official Plan and zoning amendments for 33 Davisville Avenue and 60 Balliol Street to permit a 41-storey, 131.9-metre residential infill building at 60 Balliol Street. The Official Plan change would redesignate the privately owned Balliol Parkette from Parks to Apartment Neighbourhoods to allow the residential use.

title: 759-763 Queen Street East Permit Parking Realignment
topics: on-street parking, permit parking; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher recommends City Council ask Transportation Services to review and report on excluding the development at 759-763 Queen Street East from the on-street permit parking program. The local permit parking area is already in high demand and the development provides off-street parking.

title: 316 Bloor Street West - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body
topics: appeals, hearings;
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe recommends City Council authorize the City Solicitor to appeal and attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to review whether the variances the Committee of Adjustment approved for 316 Bloor Street West were appropriate. The applicant sought variances to height, floor area and amenity space beyond the site-specific by-law permitting a 29-storey, 98-metre mixed-use building, proposing a 121.4-metre building; the panel approved them on December 13, 2023.

title: Metrolinx's Ontario Line Construction within the Toronto and East York District - First Quarter Update
topics: construction, transportation; building, transportation services
brief: This is an information item: the Q1 2024 update on Metrolinx's Ontario Line construction within the Toronto and East York district, covering project status, timelines, construction mitigation plans and community engagement milestones. Council adopted consolidated city recommendations for the Ontario Line in July 2023. The community council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: 914 Bathurst Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve Official Plan and zoning amendments for 914 Bathurst Street to permit a 12-storey mixed-use building with 155 homes and a minimum of 30 square metres of ground-floor commercial space.

title: Turn Prohibitions - Bloor Street West and Perth Avenue
topics: turn prohibitions (traffic);
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council rescind the eastbound and northbound left-turn prohibitions at Bloor Street West and Perth Avenue, now that traffic signals authorized in July 2022 are being installed. The prohibitions (weekday peak periods, bicycles excepted) are no longer needed given the signals, the close spacing to the Sterling Road/Symington Avenue signals, and the offset intersection. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Bloor West.

title: Parking Amendments - Donlands Avenue
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council rescind the alternate-side parking rules on Donlands Avenue between Mortimer Avenue and Sammon Avenue and allow parking on both sides, in response to a resident petition. Several existing permit parking and stopping regulations on nearby blocks would also be rescinded. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Donlands Avenue.

title: Accessible Parking Space - January 2024 (Non-Delegated)
topics: accessibility, parking; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize removing an on-street accessible parking space on the east side of Donlands Avenue, as listed in the report's attachment. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Donlands Avenue.

title: Accessible Loading Zone - Kingston Road
topics: accessibility, loading zones; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council designate an on-street accessible loading zone on the south side of Kingston Road between Beech Avenue and Balsam Avenue, operating at all times except 3:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. weekdays. The zone would give Wheel-Trans users and accessible permit holders unimpeded curbside access. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Kingston Road.

title: Accessible Loading Zone - Dundas Street West
topics: accessibility, loading zones; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council designate an on-street accessible loading zone on the south side of Dundas Street West between Keele Street and Indian Grove, operating at all times except 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. weekdays. The zone would give Wheel-Trans users and accessible permit holders unimpeded curbside access. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Dundas Street West.

title: Honda Indy Toronto Race 2024 - Temporary Street Closures
topics: road closures; street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize entering a new one-year agreement with Green Savoree Toronto ULC to hold the 2024 Honda Indy Toronto race, and approve temporarily closing Lake Shore Boulevard West between Strachan Avenue and Ontario Drive and Strachan Avenue between Fleet Street and Lake Shore Boulevard West from July 17 to July 22, 2024. If the July 21 race is delayed or cancelled, the final race would be held July 22.

title: 440, 444, 450 and 462 Front Street West; 425, 439, 441 and 443 Wellington Street West; 6-18 Spadina Avenue and 1 and 19 Draper Street - The Well - Extension of Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Approval
topics: exemptions, part lot control; exceptions
brief: Staff recommend City Council amend By-law 227-2020 to extend the Part Lot Control Exemption for The Well lands (440-462 Front Street West, 425-443 Wellington Street West, 6-18 Spadina Avenue, 1 and 19 Draper Street) for an additional 4 years. The exemption, enacted February 2020, facilitates the approved seven-building mixed-use development with public parkland and privately-owned public spaces.

title: 980 Dufferin Street / 1141 Bloor Street West - TTC Tunnel Construction (Stage 1 and 2) - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction; building
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize lane and bicycle lane closures on Bloor Street West near Dufferin Street for construction of an underground pedestrian tunnel connecting the Dufferin TTC station to a proposed 33-storey building (Tower C) at 980 Dufferin Street. The tunnel would run north-south on Bloor Street West just west of the Dufferin intersection. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Bloor and Dufferin.

title: Designation of the Cabbagetown Southwest Heritage Conservation District under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage districts; historic areas
brief: Staff recommend City Council designate the Cabbagetown Southwest area as a Heritage Conservation District under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act and adopt its conservation district plan by by-law. The designation would manage change in the district to conserve its cultural heritage value.

title: 7 Laxton Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve Official Plan and zoning amendments for 7 Laxton Avenue to allow a new 6-storey residential building with 19 rental homes. The proposal is described as consistent with provincial policy and the Growth Plan and an appropriate scale for the site.

title: 69 Yonge Street And 3 King Street East - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: agreements, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage property at 69 Yonge Street and 3 King Street East, the 1911-13 Canadian Pacific Railway Building designed by Darling and Pearson, to allow construction of a new 21-storey tower on the lands. The board is also asked to authorize a heritage easement agreement.

title: 127 (121-123) Church Street and 89 Queen Street East - Alterations to Heritage Properties and 119 Church Street - Removal of a Heritage Building; Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve alterations to the heritage properties at 127 (121-123) Church Street and 89 Queen Street East, and approve the full removal and partial reconstruction of the building at 119 Church Street, in connection with the site's development. Council adopted the staff report recommending designation of these properties in December 2023. The board is also asked to authorize a heritage easement agreement.

title: Demolition of Heritage Properties with Conditions - 938, 944 and 950 King Street West and 95, 97 and 99 Strachan Avenue
topics: demolitions, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the demolition of the designated heritage properties at 938, 944 and 950 King Street West and 95, 97 and 99 Strachan Avenue, on condition the replacement structure is built to the approved plans, as part of a reconstruction strategy for the site. The properties are all designated under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act.

title: 45, 57-93 Balliol Street - Community Benefits Charge In-kind Offer
topics: community benefits;
brief: Staff recommend City Council allow the owner of 45 and 57-93 Balliol Street to convey an additional 174.44 square metres of open space as part of the development, free and clear of easements and encumbrances. Council approved the 40-storey, 477-unit building with 19 replacement rental units in July 2023; the proposal already includes a 906 square metre open space with 435 square metres of parkland dedication.

title: 8 Dawes Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: applications, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing to oppose the appealed zoning amendment application for 8 Dawes Road and continue discussions with the applicant. The proposal was a 38-storey mixed-use building with ground- and second-floor commercial uses and 399 homes; the applicant appealed September 15, 2023.

title: 2575 and 2625 Danforth Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application, Rental Housing Demolition and Conversion Application and Site Plan Control - Appeal
topics: rental housing, site plan control, zoning; rental properties; rental units, site plan approvals
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the appealed zoning, site plan and rental demolition applications for 2575 and 2625 Danforth Avenue and continue discussions with the applicant. The proposal had five mixed-use buildings from 15 to 55 storeys as infill on a site with four rental buildings of 9 to 29 storeys; new public streets would be required.

title: 15-17 Elm Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the appealed zoning amendment application for 15-17 Elm Street and continue discussions with the applicant. The revised proposal was a 30-storey mixed-use building with 216 homes; the existing heritage building at 15 Elm Street would be demolished. The applicant appealed September 25, 2023.

title: 1728 Bloor Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal to oppose the appealed zoning amendment application for 1728 Bloor Street West and continue discussions with the applicant. The proposal was a 19-storey mixed-use building with ground-floor retail and 99 homes; the applicant appealed October 4, 2023 after Council did not decide in time.

title: 40 Walmer Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council refuse the zoning amendment application for 40 Walmer Road in its current form. The proposal was a 35-storey residential building with 365 homes including 33 replacement rental units; the existing building has 33 rental units and a related rental demolition application is under review. Staff also recommend opposing any appeal to the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 1134 Queen Street East - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 1134 Queen Street East to permit a 6-storey mixed-use building with 29 condo homes and 274.7 square metres of ground-floor retail and commercial space. The proposal is described as consistent with provincial policy, the Growth Plan and the Official Plan.

title: 743 Warden Avenue - Proposed Amendment to Section 37 Agreement
topics: planning, provincial legislation;
brief: The City Planning Division recommends City Council authorize amending the December 2015 Section 37 agreement for 743 Warden Avenue to adjust construction phasing terms, a legal convenience to allow timely construction of the previously approved residential development. The community benefits secured in the agreement are not affected. A related application to lift the holding symbol for Blocks 6-8 on Plan 66M-2549 was also received.

title: 54-62 Glen Everest Road - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the rental housing demolition application for 54-62 Glen Everest Road, allowing demolition of three 3-storey buildings with 68 rental units, to be replaced within a new 12-storey building of 414 homes. The related zoning amendment was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, which approved it in principle in an August 2023 written decision.

title: 5855, 5865, 5875, 5945, 5951, and 5955 Steeles Avenue East - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 5855-5955 Steeles Avenue East to permit a one-storey warehouse of about 35,752 square metres with 268 surface parking spaces and three driveway entrances. An enhanced landscaped area would be created at the northwest corner, two designated heritage buildings would be restored for retail or office reuse, and Staines Road would be extended (truncated).

title: 2031 Kennedy Road - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 2031 Kennedy Road to permit additional commercial uses in the existing at-grade commercial spaces while keeping the current parking ratio. New uses would include restaurants, take-out restaurants, personal service shops, a convenience store, medical and dental offices and offices. The proposal is described as consistent with provincial policy and the Growth Plan.

title: 2683 Lawrence Avenue East - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 2683 Lawrence Avenue East to permit demolishing the existing multi-tenant retail plaza and building a new L-shaped 11-storey mixed-use building with 206 homes and 589 square metres of ground-floor retail and commercial space. The proposal has a gross floor area of 19,168 square metres, a floor space index of 2.66, and 249 parking spaces (truncated).

title: 150 Clonmore Drive - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: City Council referred the 150 Clonmore Drive zoning amendment back to Scarborough Community Council for further consideration at its December 2023 meeting. The proposal is a 12-storey residential building with 290 homes; Council's referral asks the community council to consider the amendment and any bills before they return to Council.

title: Tapscott Road and Passmore Avenue - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic regulations, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize installing traffic control signals at Tapscott Road and Passmore Avenue, replacing the existing all-way stop, to improve safety for all road users. The signals are justified by the assessment undertaken. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on both roads.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will review the Order Paper.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions and announcements will be made at the City Council meeting.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council may file petitions.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council will declare interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council receives the introduction of committee reports and new business from city officials, including reports from the Executive, Civic Appointments, Economic and Community Development, General Government and Infrastructure and Environment Committees.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will confirm the minutes from its regular meeting held December 13, 14 and 15, 2023.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council opens its meeting with O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is attached.

title: 505 University Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Interim Chief Planner recommends City Council state its intention to designate the property at 505 University Avenue (including entrance at 136 Edward Street) under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The property, on the northeast corner of University Avenue and Edward Street, contains the Shell Oil Building designed by the prominent firm Marani.

title: 309 Cherry Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council state its intention to designate the property at 309 Cherry Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The Port Lands property at Cherry and Villiers Streets is bounded by Cherry Street, Villiers Street and Commissioners Street.

title: Ready, Set, Midtown: Zoning Review - City Initiated Zoning By-law Amendments for Select Lands Designated Apartment Neighbourhoods - Decision Report - Approval
topics: apartment neighbourhoods, land use designations, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve city-initiated zoning amendments for select Apartment Neighbourhood lands to implement Official Plan Amendment 405, the Yonge-Eglinton Secondary Plan, as part of the Ready, Set, Midtown program. This Midtown Zoning Review is one of three initiatives alongside infrastructure and public realm strategies, and by-laws have already been adopted in phases for other character areas. Council is asked to amend city-wide By-law 569-2013 for the areas in Attachment 3.

title: 202 Sheppard Avenue West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve Official Plan and zoning amendments for 202 Sheppard Avenue West to permit a 6-storey mixed-use building with medical offices and residential uses, up to 19.6 metres high. The project has 1,350 square metres of floor area (2.86 times the lot area) with seven surface parking spaces at the rear. Staff say the proposal is consistent with provincial policy and the Growth Plan.

title: 3 Swift Drive - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, community councils, demolitions; application process
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment and rental housing demolition for 3 Swift Drive to allow demolishing an existing 4-storey building with 61 rental units and building 35- and 31-storey towers on a 7-storey podium. The proposal includes a 518.9 square metre public park dedication and a 268 square metre privately-owned publicly-accessible space.

title: 3374 Keele Street - Zoning Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing in opposition to the appealed zoning amendment for 3374 Keele Street in its current form, and continue discussions with the applicant. The revised application proposes a 29-storey residential building with 296 homes and 20,761 square metres of floor area, up from an earlier 12-storey, 158-unit plan.

title: 3736, 3742, 3748, 3750 Bathurst St and 11-15 Richelieu Road - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 3736, 3742, 3748 and 3750 Bathurst Street and 11-15 Richelieu Road to permit a mixed-use development with a 10-storey (34.1-metre) building fronting Wilson Street and a 32-storey (100.5-metre) residential building on a shared 6-storey base. The project has 479 homes, 853 square metres of ground-floor retail and 37,540 square metres of floor area at 7.24 times the lot area, subject to conditions including sanitary servicing holds.

title: Susan Scandiffio - Recipient of the 2024 Agnes Macphail Award
topics: awards;
brief: Councillor Robinson recommends City Council approve Susan Scandiffio as the 2024 Agnes Macphail Award recipient. The award, established by the former Borough of East York, annually recognizes an outstanding volunteer living within the former borough's boundaries who upheld the values and causes of Agnes Macphail. The selection committee unanimously chose Scandiffio at its January 18, 2024 meeting.

title: 1350 Sheppard Avenue West - Subdivision Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, land use, subdivision (land), zoning bylaws; subdivision of land, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff advise City Council that the Chief Planner intends to approve the draft plan of subdivision for 1350 Sheppard Avenue West under delegated authority. The plan would create three residential development blocks, three woodlot blocks, two public park blocks, a 22-metre new public road from Keele Street to Sheppard Avenue, road widenings and reserve blocks, with one block retained by the applicant under a public access easement. Staff say the proposal is consistent with provincial policy.

title: Going with the Snow - Returning Tobogganing to 45 Hills Across Toronto - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: parks, recreation policies; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, recommends City Council direct the Acting General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation, to remove the signs prohibiting tobogganing and install warning signs instead, returning tobogganing to 45 hills across Toronto. The motion says families have tobogganed at parks like East Lynn and Christie Pits for generations and were dismayed to find the hills posted off-limits.

title: Review of City of Toronto Ice time and Cricket Field Allocation and Booking Policy - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: facility booking, recreation policies; book a room; booking centre; booking space; civic centre public space booking; elevator postings; event booking; event space booking; facilities booking; facilities rental; facility rental; hall booking; meeting room booking; promotional space booking; rental space; room booking; room rates; room rental; space booking
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council direct the Parks, Forestry and Recreation general manager to review the booking and allocation policies for ice time, cricket fields and other sports assets. The motion notes established groups hold most long-standing bookings, while newer leagues formed by women and girls struggle to get fair access to indoor arenas, outdoor rinks and fields.

title: Examining the Feasibility of Piloting an Operational Base in North York for the North York Municipal Licensing and Standards By-Law Enforcement Team - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: by-laws, enforcement; bylaws
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends City Council direct the Municipal Licensing and Standards executive director to study the feasibility of piloting an operational base in North York for its by-law enforcement team. There are 47 officers from the by-law enforcement, investigation and rental standards teams assigned to North York investigations, currently operating out of Markham Road, Eastern Avenue or The West Mall.

title: Report on Addition of ITM Thai Massage Alumni Association to Appendix L, Chapter 545, Licensing, List of Professional Holistic Associations - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: business associations, licences, municipal codes; industry associations; marketing alliances; trade associations, licenses; licensing
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, recommends City Council direct the Municipal Licensing and Standards executive director to report to the Economic and Community Development Committee in the third quarter of 2024 on adding the ITM Thai Massage Alumni Association to the list of professional holistic associations under the licensing by-laws. The listing would let the association issue holistic practitioner licences; the new school will train workers in traditional Thai massage.

title: 199 Thirtieth Street - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: appeals, hearings, municipal officials; city officials
brief: Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body with city staff to oppose the appeal of a Committee of Adjustment decision at 199 Thirtieth Street. The applicant sought variances from city-wide Zoning By-law 569-2013 for side and rear yard setbacks and loading spaces (A0277/23EYK) to build a new warehouse; a previous application (A0251/20EYK) had approved related variances.

title: Tax Fairness for All:  An Equitable Approach to the Residential Property Tax Rate on Toronto Island - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: property taxes, taxes; levies, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends City Council direct the Chief Financial Officer to report back by the end of the second quarter of 2024 on the feasibility of applying a more equitable residential property tax rate on Toronto Island. The motion notes Island homeowners own their houses but lease the land from the City, and pay some of the lowest residential tax bills while enjoying full municipal services and year-round ferry service.

title: Amending Item 2018.CC36.5 - 4000 Eglinton Avenue West - Timing of Parkland Conveyance - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: parkland dedication, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, recommends City Council amend its 2018 decision on item 2018.CC36.5 regarding 4000 Eglinton Avenue West by adding new instructions on the timing of the parkland conveyance. The original decision accepted a without-prejudice settlement offer for the zoning appeal to the former Ontario Municipal Board under confidential city solicitor instructions.

title: Restoring In-Person Landlord and Tenant Board Hearings - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: hearings, landlords, tenants; renters; tenancy agreements
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council request the Government of Ontario to make in-person hearings the default format at the Landlord and Tenant Board while still offering virtual options. Council previously raised this in motion PH22.12 in May 2021 over concerns about the negative impacts of the Board's virtual-only hearings on tenants. The motion asks the province to take mitigation steps.

title: 1-25 Defries Street - Amendment to Section 37 Agreement - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: accessibility, funding; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, financing
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends City Council authorize the City Solicitor to amend the Section 37 agreement registered on title for 1-25 Defries Street, to the satisfaction of the Interim Chief Planner. The agreement was registered after the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal's October 23, 2020 order approving a 37-storey residential building, securing financial contributions, facilities and services.

title: 717 - 733 Mount Pleasant Road - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Ontario Land Tribunal - by Councillor Jaye Robinson, Seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal with staff or outside consultants over the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of a minor variance at 717-733 Mount Pleasant Road (A0237/23NY). The applicant, Rockport (MPE) Inc., sought to modify its zoning to permit the proposal.

title: Summit to Solve the Epidemic of Criminal Break-and-Enters Against Small Business in the City of Toronto - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: crime, small businesses; illegal activity
brief: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, recommends City Council request the Economic Development and Culture general manager, in consultation with the Toronto Association of Business Improvement Areas and Toronto Police, to convene a summit on the wave of criminal break-and-enters hitting Toronto small businesses. The motion says owners already struggling to recover post-COVID face an unprecedented wave of break-ins threatening main street communities.

title: King Street West Watermain and Track Renewal - Bus and Streetcar Rerouting along Queen Street West - Temporary Adjustments to Parking Regulations - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, parking, parking regulations, watermains; mains; water mains, parking by-laws; parking bylaws, ttc
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, recommends City Council temporarily adjust parking regulations on Queen Street West and Shaw Street during the King Street West watermain and track renewal construction. The motion extends peak-hour parking restrictions to keep over 106,000 daily TTC riders moving on the 504 King, 508 Lake Shore and 501 Queen streetcar routes.

title: No More Subsidies for New Gas Pipelines that Drive Up Torontonians’ Energy Costs - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: energy, subsidies and grants; energy resources; energy use, financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council express support for the Ontario Energy Board's decision to end the subsidy that forces existing gas customers to pay for new methane gas pipeline construction, and ask the Ontario government to let the decision stand effective 2025. The motion calls fossil fuel subsidies bad for consumers, air pollution, climate and health, and opposes the Ford government's contemplated override.

title: Technical Amendments to Bloor West Complete Street Extension - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: commercial properties, loading zones; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, office real estate; retail space
brief: Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, recommends City Council make technical amendments to the Bloor West Complete Street Extension approved June 14, 2023, based on a supplementary review with stakeholders. The changes include adding a commercial loading zone on the east side of Jane Street north of Bloor Street West and rescinding traffic and parking provisions listed under Municipal Code Chapter 950, Schedule XV.

title: Supporting the Learning Enrichment Foundation (LEF) in Continuing to Deliver Community and Social Services in York South-Weston - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: community outreach, social services; awareness programs; community engagement; outreach; promotion (communication); public outreach
brief: Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, recommends City Council direct city real estate, social development and finance staff regarding the Learning Enrichment Foundation's continued occupancy at 116 Industry Street in Mount Dennis. The foundation has served York South-Weston with holistic community and social service programs for 45 years and has leased its current location for over 30 years.

title: Supporting New Indigenous Affordable Rental Housing at 537 Broadview Avenue - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: First Nations, affordable housing, rental housing; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples, affordable homes; housing projects, rental properties; rental units
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, recommends City Council authorize up to 12 affordable rental units at 537 Broadview Avenue to be eligible for waivers of parkland dedication fees and development charge exemptions. The motion supports capital renovations by Na-Me-Res (Native Men's Residence), an Indigenous non-profit housing provider, aligning with the HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan's focus on Indigenous affordable housing.

title: Community Safety Zone - Driftwood Avenue - Technical Amendment - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: community safety, safety; public safety
brief: Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends City Council adjust the Community Safety Zone on Driftwood Avenue, rescinding the designation between Wilmont Road and Niska Road and designating it between Jane Street and Grandravine Drive. Driftwood Avenue is a 40 km/h collector road fronting residential properties and three elementary and middle schools, and also carries TTC service.

title: Approval of the Allocation of Canada-Ontario Community Housing Initiative Funding for Affordable Housing at 128 Havelock Street - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: affordable housing, emergency housing, housing; affordable homes; housing projects, emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless), homes; residences
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends City Council authorize the Executive Director, Housing Secretariat, to make budget adjustments to allocate Canada-Ontario Community Housing Initiative funding for affordable housing at 128 Havelock Street. In 2022 the Neighbourhood Land Trust took ownership of the vacant derelict rooming house there as part of a portfolio of 81 properties acquired from Toronto Community Housing through the city's Tenants First project.

title: Highway 401 Overpass Safety
topics: highways, overpasses, provincial highways; freeways; motorways; parkways
brief: Councillor James Pasternak recommends the Infrastructure and Environment Committee ask staff to report directly to the February 6-8, 2024 City Council meeting on existing safety policies and enforcement measures for protests and rallies on Highway 401 overpasses. Recent protests have included flag-waving, posters and noise amplification in what the motion calls a dangerous location intended to distract drivers. No Council decision is attached yet; this asks for a staff report.

title: Delivering Improved Accessibility: Bike Share Toronto's Modernized Rate Structure Update
topics: parking, parking fees, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws, parking charges; parking rates
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority board seeks City Council authority to have Social Development, Finance and Administration administer Bike Share Toronto reduced-fare annual memberships to eligible Fair Pass Program clients on the authority's behalf, as part of a modernized Bike Share rate structure. The board referred the item to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee after its November 2023 meeting.

title: Endangered Species Habitat Replacement on Public Lands
topics: conservation, environmentally sensitive areas, natural habitat; environmental conservation; environmental improvements; environmental management; environmental protection; environmental stewardship; greening, environmental sensitivity; environmentally sensitive lands; environmentally-sensitive areas
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe recommends City Council direct Parks, Forestry and Recreation, with other departments or the Conservation Authority, to require high-quality replacement habitat whenever city property is used to create replacement habitat under the Endangered Species Act. Replacement habitats typically have poor success rates, and the Environmental Commissioner recommended building at least two high-quality replacements before destroying original habitat.

title: Bike Lanes that are Safe and Passable for Bikes
topics: bike lanes, city initiatives, snow management; bicycle lanes; on street bike lanes, city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, de-icing; snow clean-up; snow plans
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe recommends City Council direct Transportation Services to take all reasonable steps to make designated bike lanes safe and passable for bicycles during winter. The minimum 'safe and passable' standard works for cars, but bike lanes need clearing to bare pavement; layers of snow and slush that cars can pass quickly turn icy and unsafe for bikes.

title: Cycling Network Plan: 2024 Cycling Infrastructure Installation - First Quarter Update
topics: bikeway networks, cycling, cycling maps; bicycle facilities; bicycle routes; bike routes; bikeway routes; bikeways; cycling routes; shared roadways; signed routes, bicycling
brief: The General Manager, Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize installing near-term bikeway projects from the Cycling Network Plan adopted in December 2021, for which design and consultation are complete. Projects include uni-directional cycle tracks on Champagne Drive from Chesswood Drive to Finch Avenue West, Alness Street from Finch Avenue West to the Finch Hydro Corridor, and University Avenue (truncated).

title: Administrative Penalty System for Red Light Camera and Automated Speed Enforcement Violations
topics: penalties, red light cameras, traffic management; red light monitoring, traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations
brief: Staff recommend City Council establish a system of administrative penalties for red light camera and automated speed enforcement violations effective November 1, 2024, under the Highway Traffic Act and Ontario Regulation 355/22. The report sets out the governance and administrative requirements to expand the city's administrative penalty system to camera-detected violations.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Tacel Ltd. for the Supply and Delivery of Polara Accessible Pedestrian Signals System Components and Central Control Units
topics: pedestrian signals, transportation; crosswalk lights; pedestrian displays, transportation services
brief: The General Manager, Transportation Services and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend City Council authorize a non-competitive agreement with Tacel Ltd. for Polara accessible pedestrian signal components and central control units, for $4,172,841 through July 31, 2025, with three one-year renewal options. A contract was originally awarded to Tacel in 2013.

title: Expropriation of Properties for the Extension of Beecroft Road - Stage 2
topics: expropriations, property (sc); compulsory purchase; eminent domain
brief: The Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management recommends City Council, as approving authority under the Expropriations Act, consider the Ontario Land Tribunal's report for the Stage 2 expropriation of properties at 2, 4, 6, 18, 22 and 24 Greenview Avenue, 36, 38 and 41 Hendon Avenue and 5754 Yonge Street for the Beecroft Road extension. Council authorized starting the expropriations in June 2022.

title: Expropriation of 1430 Gerrard Street East for Permanent Affordable Rental Housing - Stage 2
topics: affordable housing, expropriations, rental housing; affordable homes; housing projects, compulsory purchase; eminent domain, rental properties; rental units
brief: The Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management recommends City Council, as approving authority under the Expropriations Act, consider the Ontario Land Tribunal's report and approve the Stage 2 expropriation of 1430 Gerrard Street East for permanent affordable rental housing. Council authorized starting the expropriation in March 2022; the Tribunal's December 2023 report found the taking fair, sound and reasonably necessary.

title: Expropriation of Property Interests at 2 Bloor Street East and 90 Bloor Street East for the Bloor Yonge Capacity Improvement Project - Stage 2
topics: development, expropriations; compulsory purchase; eminent domain, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: The Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management recommends City Council, as approving authority under the Expropriations Act, consider the Ontario Land Tribunal's report and authorize paying $200 in hearing costs to the expropriated owner for the Stage 2 expropriation of property interests at 2 Bloor Street East and 90 Bloor Street East for the TTC's Bloor-Yonge station capacity improvement project. Council authorized starting the expropriations in May and July 2022.

title: 4884-4896 Dundas Street West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments, rezoning, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the appealed Official Plan and zoning amendment application for 4884-4896 Dundas Street West, and continue discussions with the applicant. The proposal was revised in June 2023 from a 12-storey building with 225 units to a 29-storey building with 395 units; the heritage building would be retained and relocated.

title: 2, 7 and 10 Queen Elizabeth Boulevard, 506, 514, 516, 520 and 522 Royal York Road and 3, 5 and 15 Sinclair Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: mid rise buildings, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the appealed zoning amendment application for 2, 7 and 10 Queen Elizabeth Boulevard, 506-522 Royal York Road and 3, 5 and 15 Sinclair Street. The proposal includes a 10-storey mid-rise and 17- and 35-storey towers on the north parcel with 5,000 square metres of employment space, and a 20-storey mixed-use building with 220 homes on the south parcel.

title: 251-285 The West Mall - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: buildings, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal to oppose the appealed zoning amendment application for 251-285 The West Mall, and continue discussions with the applicant. The proposal had three 13-storey buildings with 610 homes including 66 rental replacement units; a rental demolition application was also submitted. The applicant appealed August 1, 2023.

title: 3350 Weston Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: apartment neighbourhoods, apartments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 3350 Weston Road to permit a 15-storey apartment building (14 storeys plus a mechanical penthouse and amenity storey) with 190 homes, 50.8 metres tall, a gross floor area of 15,268 square metres and 153 vehicle parking spaces.

title: Parking Regulation Amendments - St Clair Avenue West
topics: parking, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Councillor Frances Nunziata recommends City Council amend the parking prohibition on the north side of St. Clair Avenue West between Scarlett Road and Florence Crescent, changing the 7:00-9:00 a.m. and 4:00-6:00 p.m. weekday prohibition to apply between Scarlett Road and Florence Crescent. Her office received complaints about illegal parking of plated and unplated vehicles belonging to auto repair shops and used car lots.

title: 801 The Queensway - Construction Staging Area
topics: condominium housing, construction permits (right-of-way), residential properties; condominiums; condos, curb cut permits; driveway paving permits; driveway resurfacing permits; driveway widening permits; landscaping permits (right-if way), residential real estate
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize closing the south sidewalk on The Queensway between Taymall Avenue and a point 68 metres east, from February 29 to December 31, 2024, to accommodate construction staging for Marlin Spring Developments' 10-storey condo with ground-floor retail at 801 The Queensway. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on The Queensway.

title: Application for a Clothing Drop Box Location permit located at 9 Milvan Drive
topics: [objects in community and life], clothing drop boxes; clothes donation boxes; clothing bins
brief: Municipal Licensing and Standards refused to issue a clothing drop box location permit for 9 Milvan Drive. Staff recommend City Council either deny the application or approve it; the report presents both options for Council's decision.

title: 2 and 10 East Mall Crescent - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 2 and 10 East Mall Crescent to permit a mixed-use development with a 33-storey tower and a nine-storey mid-rise building connected by a four-storey base. The proposal includes 606 homes, 350 square metres of ground-floor retail, a total gross floor area of 40,550 square metres and a floor space index of 4.3.

title: Advancing the George Street Revitalization Project - Update and Next Steps
topics: construction, facilities; building
brief: Staff provide an update on the George Street Revitalization project and recommend City Council adopt confidential instructions in Confidential Attachment 1 and authorize release of the attachments on the stated timing. In 2013 Council approved the project to replace the Seaton House men's shelter and co-locate a long-term care home, shelter services, affordable housing and a community service hub. The recommendations cover the next phase of procurement and construction.

title: RapidTO: Surface Transit Network Plan
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, ttc
brief: Staff recommend City Council endorse in principle the RapidTO: Surface Transit Network Plan and direct Transportation Services to use it as the basis for planning and programming surface transit priority projects. The report notes 70 percent of TTC journeys include a surface transit trip and that bus and streetcar reliability supports the city's priority of keeping Toronto moving.

title: Finch West Light Rail Transit: Train Operating and Services Term Sheet
topics: light rail transit, public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, lrt
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize the Deputy City Manager, Infrastructure Services, in consultation with the TTC CEO, to finalize and execute a Train Operating and Services Agreement for the Finch West Light Rail Transit. The 11-kilometre line will run along Finch Avenue West between Finch West Subway Station and Humber College Station with 18 stops linking Line 1, TTC buses, GO, MiWay, Viva and Zum; the Province owns the line through Metrolinx and is funding its construction.

title: Review of the Imagination, Manufacturing, Innovation and Technology Property Tax Incentive Program
topics: business incentives, planning & development (sc), science & technology (sc); commercial facade improvement program; commercial festivals and special events program; commercial research program; community grant allocations; employment area revitalization; employment revitalization areas; facade improvement; financial incentives; mural program; streetscape improvement program
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the Chief Planner, in consultation with Economic Development and Culture and the Chief Financial Officer, on next steps from a review of the Imagination, Manufacturing, Innovation and Technology (IMIT) financial incentive program and its Local Employment Requirement points-based pilot. The review weighed the city's planning and economic development priorities and financial position, including directions from the Updated Long-Term Financial Plan. The report presents findings for Council's direction.

title: Applications to the Imagination, Manufacturing, Innovation and Technology Property Tax Incentive Program
topics: applications, property taxes; application process, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: Staff recommend City Council refuse Imagination, Manufacturing, Innovation and Technology (IMIT) property tax incentives for three Cadillac Fairview applications in East Harbour, at 21 Don Roadway (Buildings 1A and 1B). The applications, submitted August 11, 2020, fall under the South of Eastern Community Improvement Plan, By-law 1324-2012, in effect at the time. The report provides recommendations on the three applications for Council's decision.

title: Donation from Private Giving Foundation to City of Toronto’s Robertson House Emergency Shelter
topics: donation, women; bequest; toy drive, shelters for women
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize accepting a donation of $92,675.88 from the Private Giving Foundation to the City for Toronto Shelter and Support Services' Robertson House emergency shelter, which serves women and children experiencing homelessness. The donation would enhance the programming area, including a welcoming client-centred space for children's programming.

title: Development Charges Complaint - 615 Kennedy Road
topics: complaints, development charges;
brief: The Chief Financial Officer recommends City Council determine that the Development Charges By-law was properly applied to the 10-storey, 215-unit residential building at 615 Kennedy Road in Scarborough and dismiss the complaint filed July 12, 2023 by 615 Kennedy Road Inc. under Section 20 of the Development Charges Act, 1997. The complainant, which applied for a building permit December 21, 2021, objects to the amount of development charges determined at permit issuance.

title: Toronto Police Services Board response to MM11.37 - Keeping Toronto Safe from Hate
topics: police services boards; police boards
brief: This is an information item: the Toronto Police Services Board forwards an extract from its October 19, 2023 public meeting minutes responding to City Council's decision MM11.37, Keeping Toronto Safe from Hate. The Board agreed to send the minute to the Executive Committee for information. No decision is attached.

title: Municipal Non-Resident Speculation Tax on Foreign Buyers of Residential Property
topics: residential properties, taxes; levies, residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a new Municipal Non-Resident Speculation Tax on foreign buyers of certain residential property in Toronto, effective January 1, 2025, at a rate of 10% of the purchase price. The tax follows Council's September 2023 direction to develop an implementation plan for a land transfer tax on foreign buyers as part of the Updated Long-Term Financial Plan. Its stated aim is to safeguard and enhance the availability of residential housing supply.

title: Implementation Review of the Noise By-law
topics: by-laws, noise, noise control; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise, bylaws, noise barriers; sound barriers
brief: The Executive Director, Municipal Licensing and Standards recommends City Council amend the noise by-law, adding a definition of exemption permit screening criteria and other changes, following the directed implementation review. The by-law balances the city's vibrancy with residents' needs through time restrictions and sound level limits for various noise types.

title: Homelessness Services Capital Infrastructure Strategy: Real Estate Strategy and Lease Extensions
topics: emergency housing, homelessness, properties (real estate); emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless), property; real estate
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize negotiating and approving real estate actions to implement the Homelessness Services Capital Infrastructure Strategy, approved November 2023, including lease extensions. The strategy takes a long-term, proactive approach to stabilizing the shelter system amid unprecedented demand for shelter beds, focusing on developing purpose-built shelters.

title: Changes to Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
topics: appointments, business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: The General Manager, Economic Development and Culture recommends City Council remove directors Kozeta Izeti from The Eglinton Way BIA board and Yacov (Jacob) Aboudi from the Upper Village BIA board, under the Business Improvement Areas by-law. Both BIAs fall within two community council boundaries.

title: Business Improvement Areas - 2024 Operating Budgets - Report 1
topics: budgets, business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations, budgets and accounts
brief: The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends City Council adopt and certify the 2024 operating budgets and levy requirements for the city's Business Improvement Areas, as required by the City of Toronto Act, 2006. Council approval lets the city collect the levy from commercial and industrial properties in each BIA; for example, Albion Islington Square's budget is $352,230 with $187,415 in levy funds required.

title: Balanced Approach to Distributing Legislative Meeting Materials - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: costs, council meetings, ecological footprint, environmental conditions, printing and distribution; circulation; copying; mailing list; photocopying; printing; subscriptions, environmental footprint; zero footprint cities; zerofootprint cities, environmental health; environmental quality; environmental sensitivity; state of the environment
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, asks City Council to direct the City Clerk to consult and survey councillors on their interest in receiving paper copies of legislative meeting materials and report back with findings, a proposal, budget implications and implementation options. The motion says the technology-only approach since the pandemic-era end of printing has left members overwhelmed and does not work for everyone.

title: Reimbursement of Cities Forum 2023 Conference Expenses, Torino, Italy - by Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: refund; reimbursement
brief: Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to approve reimbursement of travel expenses for himself and his Chief of Staff for the Cities Forum 2023 conference in Torino, Italy, to be paid from his Constituency Services and Office Budget. As the city's Advocate for Technology and Innovation, he attended with additional meetings with Torino officials; a missed return flight raised the total trip cost above $7,000. Reimbursement requires Council approval under the councillor expense policy.

title: 683 - 685 Warden Avenue - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment and Plan of Subdivision - Ontario Land Tribunal Appeal - Request for Direction
topics: by-laws, zoning; bylaws
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council to adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 for the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal at 683-685 Warden Avenue, covering Official Plan amendment, zoning amendment and plan of subdivision applications. The proposal is 2 mixed-use and 4 residential buildings from 13 to 36 storeys; the applicant appealed all three applications on April 5, 2022, with a 10-day hearing scheduled.

title: 141 Roehampton Avenue - Request for Directions
topics: by-laws, zoning; bylaws
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council to adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 for the zoning amendment matter at 141 Roehampton Avenue. The revised application proposes a 58-storey, 179.6-metre residential building with 614 homes, up from an earlier 48-storey, 152-metre proposal.

title: 1265 Wilson Avenue - Request for Directions
topics: zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council to adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 for the Ontario Land Tribunal matter at 1265 Wilson Avenue. The application proposes an 11-storey residential building fronting Wilson Avenue with a 25-storey residential building at the south end, connected by building elements of varying heights. The recommendation asks Council to adopt the solicitor's advice and authorize its release.

title: 46, 46R, 48, 50, 52 and 52R Laing Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: by-laws, zoning bylaws; bylaws, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council to adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 for the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing into the appealed Official Plan, zoning and site plan applications for 46, 46R, 48, 50, 52 and 52R Laing Street. The applicant appealed on May 8, 2023 after Council failed to decide; the original proposal was two apartment buildings of four and seven storeys, later revised after the applicant acquired more land.

title: 2-20 Glazebrook Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application- Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council to adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 for the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of the 2-20 Glazebrook Avenue zoning amendment. The applicant appealed on December 8, 2022 after Council failed to decide; the proposal is a 34-storey, 109-metre mixed-use building with 434 homes and 29,600 square metres of floor area. The abutting landowner, 1840 Bayview LP, joined at the April 14, 2023 case management conference.

title: 133 and 141 Erskine Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council to adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 for the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing into the appealed zoning amendment for 133 and 141 Erskine Avenue. The applicant appealed to the Tribunal because Council did not decide within the Planning Act timeframe; the hearing is scheduled to begin July 15, 2024 for two weeks.

title: 561 Jarvis Street and 102-120 Earl Place - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Request for Direction Report
topics: Official Plans, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: On August 4, 2022, applications were submitted for a 58-storey mixed-use building with 690 homes and 154.34 square metres of non-residential space at 561 Jarvis Street and 102-120 Earl Place. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on March 31, 2023 after Council did not decide in time. The City Solicitor asks Council to adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 for the hearing scheduled to begin March 11, 2024, and authorize their release if adopted.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Local Appeal Body
brief: The Nominating Panel - Toronto Local Appeal Body recommends City Council appoint candidates to the Toronto Local Appeal Body. The panel considered the item at its January 29, 2024 meeting after conducting interviews, and the City Clerk transmits the panel's decision letter. City Council makes the final appointments.

title: 1117 Queen Street West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: The Interim Chief Planner recommends City Council refuse the Official Plan and zoning amendment applications (23 210259 STE 09 OZ) for 1117 Queen Street West in their current form. The proposal is a 29-storey mixed-use building with 272 condominium homes and 919 square metres of community space, retaining the existing 2-storey Postal Station C building.

title: 710 The West Mall - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The Interim Chief Planner recommends City Council refuse the zoning amendment application for 710 The West Mall in its current form. The proposal is a 22-storey residential building with 282 homes; staff say it has inappropriate zoning standards for height, base building height and tower floorplates and does not conform to city policies. If the applicant appeals, staff also recommend opposing the appeal at the Tribunal.

title: 509 Parliament Street - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
topics: by-laws, heritage properties, planning; bylaws, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend City Council affirm its October 11, 2023 decision (PH6.7) stating its intention to designate the property at 509 Parliament Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The City received an objection to the designation notice on November 14, 2023 from the property owner's representative, within the statutory timeframe ending November 16, 2023. The property is on the east side of Parliament Street between Winchester and Carlton Streets.

title: 3585 and 3595 St. Clair Avenue East, 636 to 646 and 641 to 663 Danforth Road, and 411 and 415 Kennedy Road - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning Amendment, Draft Plan of Subdivision - Request for Direction
topics: planning, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: The City Solicitor asks City Council to adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 for the Ontario Land Tribunal matter at 3585 and 3595 St. Clair Avenue East, 636 to 646 and 641 to 663 Danforth Road, and 411 and 415 Kennedy Road. The applications propose redeveloping the lands for 6,600 homes in up to 17 high-rise towers from 14 to 48 storeys; the applicant appealed all applications on September 21, 2022.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Multi-Tenant House Licensing Tribunal
brief: The Nominating Panel - Multi-Tenant House Licensing Tribunal recommends City Council appoint six candidates to the Multi-Tenant House Licensing Tribunal. The panel considered item NH2.1 at its January 23, 2024 meeting after interviews, and the City Clerk transmits the panel's decision letter. City Council makes the final appointments.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Yonge-Dundas Square Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Civic Appointments Committee will conduct interviews and recommend three candidates, including one as Chair, to City Council for appointment to the Yonge-Dundas Square Board, for terms ending February 7, 2028. City Council makes the final appointments.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Parking Authority Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Civic Appointments Committee will conduct interviews and recommend three candidates, including one as Chair, to City Council for appointment to the Toronto Parking Authority Board, for terms ending February 7, 2028. City Council makes the final appointments.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Civic Appointments Committee will recommend one candidate, from those interviewed December 4, 2023, to City Council to fill a vacancy on the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority Board, for a term ending December 15, 2027. City Council makes the final appointment.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Preservation Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: The City Clerk recommends City Council appoint the seven candidates listed in a confidential attachment to the Toronto Preservation Board, at pleasure of Council, for terms ending February 9, 2028. Council is asked to keep the balance of the attachment confidential.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will introduce General Bills and Confirming Bills. The brief motion is part of the meeting's standard legislative business and carries no policy decision beyond enacting the listed by-laws.

title: Strategic Planning Resource for Community Organizations
body: Board of Health - Strategic Plan Development Committee
topics: boards of health, public consultation, public health, strategic plans; community consultation; consultation; public hearing, strategic planning; strategy
brief: Councillors Alejandra Bravo and Amber Morley recommend the Board of Health ask the Medical Officer of Health to develop a resource for community organizations to consult on and participate in the Toronto Public Health Strategic Plan, and share it online, with stakeholders and with councillors. Community organizations across every neighbourhood help deliver public health's vision of a healthy city for all.

title: Review of Toronto Public Health to inform Strategic Planning
body: Board of Health - Strategic Plan Development Committee
topics: boards of health, public health, strategic plans; strategic planning; strategy
brief: This is an information item: the Deputy Medical Officer of Health and Toronto Public Health's Director will give a presentation reviewing Toronto Public Health to inform strategic planning. No decision is attached.

title: Storefront Entry Ramps on the Public Right-of-Way
topics: wheelchair ramps; handicapped ramps
brief: This is an information item: Transportation Services staff will present on temporary storefront entry ramps on the public right-of-way, as directed by the Infrastructure and Environment Committee, covering the reporting history, consultation findings and placement guidelines for ramps used by storefronts with stepped entrances. No decision is attached.

title: Cycling, Sidewalks and Accessibility: 2023 Highlights and 2024 Goals
topics: sidewalks;
brief: This is an information item: Transportation Services staff will present 2023 highlights and 2024 goals for cycling, sidewalks and accessibility, covering the expansion of cycling and pedestrian infrastructure with an emphasis on safety and comfort for seniors, people with disabilities and other vulnerable road users. No decision is attached.

title: Economic Development and Culture Division Upcoming 2024 Strategies - Accessibility Feedback
topics: economic development; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: This is an information item: Economic Development and Culture staff will present the division's upcoming 2024 strategies and seek the committee's accessibility feedback. No decision is attached.
